The two sentences should be logically related in the same direction; avoid combining opposite directions (good → bad).
The subjects can differ, but the topics should be closely related to avoid sounding disjointed.
Add a comma after そのうえ to make the rhythm of the sentence clear. ⏐ examples: 1. この店は安い。そのうえ、品質もいい。
This shop is cheap. On top of that, the quality is good too.
2. 彼は親切だ。そのうえ、仕事も早い。
He is kind. In addition, he works fast too.
3. 昨日は寒かった。そのうえ、風も強かった。
Yesterday was cold. Moreover, the wind was strong too.
4. 彼女は遅刻した。そのうえ、宿題も出していない。
She was late. On top of that, she hasn't handed in her homework either.
5. この薬はよく効く。そのうえ、副作用が少ない。
This medicine works well. Moreover, it has few side effects. ⏐ comparison: Pattern | Nuance | Difference | Short example
そのうえ | moreover (formal) | Reinforces in the same direction | 安（やす）い。 そのうえ、便利（べんり）。
それに | besides (neutral) | More colloquial, lighter | 安（やす）い。 それに 便利（べ explain: Usually used when you want to add one more characteristic of a thing, matter or person.
Usually used with an implication of praise, raising it even higher. ⏐ examples: 1. この店の料理はおいしい。その上値段も安い。
The food at this restaurant is delicious. On top of that, the prices are low too
2. 彼は、頭がいい。その上スポーツも何でもできる。
He is smart. On top of that, he can do any sport too

examples.jp: 厳しい規制が導入された。その結果、排出量が大幅に減った。
examples.tr: Strict regulations were introduced. As a result, emissions fell sharply.

examples.jp: 十分な準備ができなかった。その結果、試験は不合格だった。
examples.tr: I couldn't prepare enough. As a result, I failed the exam.

examples.jp: 調査を続けた。その結果、原因が特定できた。
examples.tr: We continued the investigation. As a result, we were able to identify the cause.

examples.jp: その結果は次の会議で共有する。
examples.tr: Those results will be shared at the next meeting.

examples.jp: 新しい戦略を採用した。その結果として、利益が回復した。
examples.tr: We adopted a new strategy. As a result, profits recovered.

677.explain:
Formal; suited to academic writing and business reports.
Usually placed at the beginning of a sentence with a comma: "その結果、～"。
Used as a noun meaning "that result": attaches to は/が/を…
Can be used with "として" to emphasize the consequential relationship: その結果として～。

• "As a result/Therefore" emphasizes the cause-and-effect relationship and the final outcome after a process.
• Usually used in written language, reports and theses; the nuance is more formal than それで/だから.
• The premise (cause, process) must be clear in the preceding sentence/paragraph so that "その結果" has an accurate reference.
• Can be used for positive, negative or neutral results.

rows: <ruby>改善<rt>かいぜん</rt></ruby>。その<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby><ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>事故<rt>じこ</rt></ruby>。そのため<ruby>遅延<rt>ちえん</rt></ruby>。
Implies "in the end/looking at the whole picture"
<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>として<ruby>残<rt>のこ</rt></ruby>った。

mistakes: No clear premise before "その結果" → the reader doesn't know "the result of what."
Confusing it with "そのために" (purpose) in reading comprehension questions; pay attention to the context of result vs purpose.
Repeating "その結果" too often in the same paragraph → alternate with そのため／したがって／結果として.
Using "結果は" when you actually mean "経過/要因は" → identify correctly what you need to state.
677.notes:
• In a long paragraph, use "この/その/前述の結果" to keep the reference clear.
• "～の結果" (the result of N/V): 交渉の結果／調査した結果、～（a very common pattern）.
• In argumentation, combine it with "一方で／しかし／つまり" to create a tight logical flow. explain: Used when something that happened in the past is the reason leading to the consequence of the next event. Used as a connective linking two sentences. ⏐ examples: 1. 父は、人の何倍も努力した。その結果、仕事で成功した。
My father worked many times harder than other people. As a result, he succeeded in his career
2. 3ヶ月ダイエットを続けた。その結果、5キロやせた。
I stayed on a diet for 3 months. As a result, I lost 5 kilos

examples.jp: パン、それとコーヒーをください。
examples.tr: Bread, and a coffee too, please.

examples.jp: 住所それと電話番号を教えてください。
examples.tr: Please tell me your address and phone number.

examples.jp: それと、明日の会議は中止です。
examples.tr: Oh, and also, tomorrow's meeting is canceled.

examples.jp: この色はいいね。それと、値段も手頃だ。
examples.tr: This color is nice. And the price is reasonable too.

examples.jp: それとこれとは話が別だ。
examples.tr: That and this are two different matters.

678.explain:
Casual and natural in everyday conversation.
Used at the beginning of a sentence to add information that just came to mind, gently shifting the topic.
In formal documents, replace it with そして/または/および/ならびに depending on the context.

• A colloquial conjunction meaning "and/besides," used to add the next item or piece of information.
• Conversational nuance, softer than そして; can be used as a light shift, "oh, and also…."
• When listing nouns, "それと" separates relatively independent items; it does not emphasize temporal order like それから.

rows: Adds something, light shift of topic
More formal than それと; continues the flow of content
<ruby>朝<rt>あさ</rt></ruby>ご<ruby>飯<rt>はん</rt></ruby>。それから<ruby>仕事<rt>しごと</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>安<rt>やす</rt></ruby>い。それに<ruby>便利<rt>べんり</rt></ruby>。
Close in meaning to それと, very casual

mistakes: Using それと to express cause and result: ×雨。それと中止になった → use それで/そのため.
Using it in formal documents such as reports/regulations → inappropriate; replace with および/ならびに/また.
Confusing it with それから (temporal order) and それに (addition with a positive evaluation); the JLPT often tests this nuance.
678.notes:
• In a long list, "A、B、それとC" highlights the last item, like "and also C."
• It can carry the nuance of "just remembering" a secondary piece of information in conversation.
• When legal/technical precision is needed, avoid それと and use および/並びに.

679.meaning:
「～が原因だ。 ・～が原因で…という結果になる。」 …には普通希望・意向・相手への働きかけなどの文は来ない。少し硬い言い方。
~ is the cause./ ~ is the cause that leads to the result …
Sentences expressing a desire, an intention, or an appeal to the listener to do something are not used in the … part. It is a somewhat formal expression.
679.connection: V/A plain form + ためだ・ため(に)… / Nの + ため(に)（cause）

examples.jp: 報告書にミスが多かったのは、よく見直しをしなかったためだろう。
examples.tr: The many mistakes in the report were probably because it wasn't checked carefully.

examples.jp: この村には医者がいないために、病気のときはとなりの町まで行かなければならない。
examples.tr: Because there is no doctor in this village, people have to go all the way to the neighboring town when they are sick.

examples.jp: 出張のため、明日の会議は欠席させていただきます。
examples.tr: Owing to a business trip, I will be absent from tomorrow's meeting.

679.notes:
meaning_vi: Expresses a cause. 「～から」、「（のは）～ためだ」 has the same meaning as 「（・・・のは）～からだ」
examples: 1. ①　雪が降ったため
Because it snowed
2. ②　雪が降ったため（に）、電車が遅れた。
Because it snowed, the train was late.
3. ③　会議が延期されたのは、社長の体調が悪いためだ。
The meeting was postponed because the company president is not feeling well.

680.meaning: Expresses a result that is the opposite of what one would generally expect.

examples.jp: 乗ったら、かえって
examples.tr: When I took it, it actually…

examples.jp: 急いでいたのでタクシーに乗ったら、かえって時間がかかってしまった。
examples.tr: I was in a hurry, so I took a taxi, but it actually ended up taking longer.

examples.jp: ダイエットしようと思って昼ごはんとか食べなかったら、かえって太ってしまった。
examples.tr: I skipped things like lunch to lose weight, but I actually ended up gaining weight.

681.meaning: The casual way of saying 「～てはいけません」

examples.jp: 買ったらだめ／買ってはだめ／買っちゃだめ
examples.tr: You mustn't buy it

examples.jp: そんな高い服を買ったら／買っちゃ、お金がなくなるよ。
examples.tr: If you buy such expensive clothes, you'll run out of money.

examples.jp: ちゃんと朝ご飯を食べなきゃ／食べなく（っ）ちゃ（＝食べなければ／食べなくては）だめだよ。
examples.tr: You have to eat a proper breakfast, you know.

682.meaning:
「～するのがいいですよ。」 助言や忠告の気持ちで相手にある行為を軽く進めるときに使う。④のように、その行為をしないことを非難する言い方にもある。
It would be good to do ~.
Used when gently suggesting, encouraging or advising the listener to do something.
As in example ④, it is also a way of criticizing the listener for not doing it.

examples.jp: 体のことが心配なら、一度健康診断を受けたらどうでしょうか。
examples.tr: If you're worried about your health, why don't you get a medical checkup once?

examples.jp: 疲れているみたいですね。少し休んだらどうですか。
examples.tr: You look tired. Why don't you take a little rest?

examples.jp: 迷惑メールが多いの？じゃ、アドレスを変えたらどう？
examples.tr: You're getting a lot of spam? Then why not change your address?

examples.jp: 悪いのはそっちですよ。一言謝ったらどうですか。
examples.tr: You're the one at fault. Why don't you at least apologize?

682.notes: An idiomatic expression of suggestion or recommendation. It is often used in the form 「Ｖ－てみたらどうか」. It is almost synonymous with 「てはどうか」, but 「たらどうか」 is more typical of spoken language. In casual speech, 「たらどうなの／どうかしら（女性）」「たらどうなんだ（男性）」「たらどう（男女）」 are used, and in polite speech, 「たらいかがですか／いかかでしょうか」 and so on. ③④ are used in situations where the listener does not readily follow the speaker's advice or recommendation, and carry the speaker's irritation. ⑥ has the latter part omitted and is pronounced with rising intonation.（２１３）

683.meaning: Presents something small and expresses the feeling “just that is fine”

examples.jp: 見るだけでいい
examples.tr: Just looking is enough

examples.jp: この宿題だけでいいから、教えてくれない？
examples.tr: Just this homework is fine, so won't you help me with it?

examples.jp: ぼくのそばに君がいるだけでいい。
examples.tr: Just having you by my side is enough for me.

684.name: ～って（I heard）
684.meaning: Spoken language for passing on to others what you have heard from someone.

examples.jp: 参加しないって
examples.tr: (I heard) they're not coming

examples.jp: 木村さんはパーティーに参加しないって。
examples.tr: I heard Kimura isn't coming to the party.

examples.jp: 明日は雪だって。
examples.tr: They say it'll snow tomorrow.

685.meaning: Spoken form of the structures「～というのは」、「～と」. The structure「「N1～ってN2 in example ⑤ is the spoken form of the structure「N1 というN2」, and indicates the name of N2.
685.connection: N/[sentence/clause] + って（= というのは/と）

examples.jp: 手伝うって何を？
examples.tr: Help with what?

examples.jp: 「ちょっと手伝ってよ」「手伝うって何を？」
examples.tr: “Give me a hand, will you?” “Help with what?”

examples.jp: 「デジカメって何ですか」「デジカメっていうのは、デジタルカメラのことですよ」
examples.tr: “What's a デジカメ?” “A デジカメ is a digital camera.”

examples.jp: 「ここに『禁煙』って書いてありますよ」「あ、気づきませんでした」
examples.tr: “It says 『No Smoking』 here.” “Oh, I didn't notice.”

examples.jp: 「隣のクラスの山田って人、知ってる？」「知らない」
examples.tr: “Do you know a guy called Yamada in the class next door?” “No.”

686.meaning: Spoken form of the structure 「～ても／でも」

examples.jp: 走ったって
examples.tr: Even if (you) run

examples.jp: 今から走ったって間に合わない。
examples.tr: Even if you run now, you won't make it.

examples.jp: いくら広くたって、駅から遠い部屋には住みたくない。
examples.tr: No matter how spacious it is, I don't want to live in an apartment far from the station.

examples.jp: この料理は簡単だから、子供だって作れる。
examples.tr: This dish is simple, so even a child can make it.

689.meaning: Intended to… but (it did not happen)

examples.jp: 明日は早く起きるつもりでしたが、寝坊してしまいました。
examples.tr: I meant to get up early the next day, but I overslept.

examples.jp: そのメールはもう送ったつもりでしたが、下書きに残っていました。
examples.tr: I thought I had already sent that email, but it was still in my drafts.

examples.jp: 今日は出かけないつもりでしたが、急用ができました。
examples.tr: I wasn't planning to go out today, but something urgent came up.

examples.jp: 冗談のつもりでした。気に障ったらごめんなさい。
examples.tr: It was meant as a joke. I'm sorry if it offended you.

examples.jp: 学生時代、留学するつもりでしたが、資金が足りませんでした。
examples.tr: When I was a student, I intended to study abroad, but I didn't have enough money.

689.explain:
The polite form; often used to explain, together with “が／けど”, a result contrary to expectation.
Vた + つもりでした often goes with “が／のに／けど” to signal a gap with reality.
Talking about someone else's intention: use ～つもりだったようだ／と言っていた to be polite and accurate.
Apologizing/correcting: “～したつもりでしたが…” is a very natural pattern in emails and at work.

• Past intention: “intended/planned to …” at a point in time in the past. Whether it was carried out depends on the context that follows.
• False belief/misunderstanding: “thought I had already …” used with Vた, usually followed by a contrary result and an apology/correction.
• Negative intention: Vない + つもりでした = “intended not to …”.
• The subject is usually the speaker; for other people, quote them or use an indirect expression.

rows: Speaker's subjective view; may differ from reality
<ruby>出張<rt>しゅっちょう</rt></ruby>の<ruby>予定<rt>よてい</rt></ruby>だった
Adverbial of purpose for the main action
<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>するつもりで<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>た

mistakes: Using it for another person without quoting: “彼は行くつもりでした” can sound like a subjective guess; better to use “と言っていました/だったようです”.
Confusing it with ～はずだった: “つもり” is a personal intention; “はず” is a grounded expectation.
Confusing “thought I had V-ed” with “intended to V”: you must use Vた + つもり to express “thought I had”.
Omitting the contrasting clause afterwards: with Vた + つもりでした, you usually need to state the different reality to make the meaning clear.
689.notes:
• The present negative form “～つもりはない” (have no intention) is different from the polite past “～つもりでした”.
• In business emails, “送ったつもりでしたが、確認が足りませんでした” is a tactful way to apologize.
• With N: “冗談のつもり” is a common set phrase when explaining a misunderstanding.

691.connection: 「Vてくれ」 + と + 頼む/言う（quoting a request）

examples.jp: 彼は私にもう一度説明してくれと頼んだ。
examples.tr: He asked me to explain it once more.

examples.jp: 上司に明日までに報告書を出してくれと言われた。
examples.tr: My boss told me to submit the report by tomorrow.

examples.jp: 友達にもっと連絡してくれって言われた。
examples.tr: My friend told me to keep in touch more.

examples.jp: 警備員にここで写真を撮らないでくれと言われた。
examples.tr: A security guard told me not to take pictures here.

examples.jp: 母が早く帰ってくれと言っている。
examples.tr: My mother is telling me to come home early.

691.explain:
Direct nuance; can be rude if used as a direct request; usually used to report a request.
“くれ” implies that the benefit goes to the person making the request. For a neutral/polite request, use “～てくださいと” or “～ように言う”.
Subject/target: AはBにVてくれと頼む → B is the one who does V for A's benefit.
The contracted spoken form “～てくれって” is common in conversation, not used in formal writing.

• Quotes the content of a request “please V for me/us” using ～てくれと + 言う/頼む/頼まれる.
• “くれ” shows that the benefit goes to the speaker/the speaker's group; it has a somewhat rough nuance of asking/commanding when used directly.
• Negative form “～ないでくれと” = “told not to …”.
• Often used with verbs of speaking/requesting: 言う・頼む・注意する・命じる（strong, rarely used with くれ）.

rows: Tell/ask someone to do V for oneself
Direct; somewhat rough when used directly
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>ってくれと<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>ってくださいと <ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う
Expresses a desire; softer than くれ
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>ってほしいと <ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う
Tell/remind someone to do/not to do
<ruby>早<rt>はや</rt></ruby>く<ruby>来<rt>く</rt></ruby>るように <ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う

mistakes: Forgetting the quotation particle “と”: it must be “Vてくれと 言う”.
Getting the direction of benefit wrong: “くれ” means doing something for me/us. For a neutral statement, use “ください”.
Using it with superiors: impolite. Switch to “～ていただけますか／～てください”.
Confusing it with “Vてくる”: “～てくれと” is a request, not a compound verb.
691.notes:
• When reporting at work or in emails, prefer “～てくださいと（依頼されました）／～ように言われました” to stay polite.
• With superiors/customers, never use “～てくれ” directly, as it is rude.
• “～てくれと言われた” can be understood as a command or a request depending on the power relationship.
examples: 1. 友達に、田中さんの電話番号を教えてくれと頼まれた。
A friend asked me to give them Tanaka's phone number.
2. 大家に、玄関の前に自転車を置かないでくれと言われた。
The landlord told me not to leave my bicycle in front of the entrance.

692.meaning:
「～という事実（または仮定の状況）だと、 …というよくない結果になる。」 …はマイナスの意味の文で、話者の希望・意向を表す文や働きかけの文は来ない。
If the fact (or hypothetical situation) is ~, it leads to the bad result …
… is a sentence with a negative meaning; it cannot be a sentence expressing the speaker's desire or intention, or one urging the other person to do something.
692.connection: Vては / Aくては / N・Naでは + [bad result] / V plain form + のでは

examples.jp: 山田さんは手術したばかりだから、お見舞いに行ってはかえって迷惑だろう。
examples.tr: Yamada has just had surgery, so going to visit would probably be more of a bother than a help.

examples.jp: そんな無責任な態度ではみんなにきらわれますよ。
examples.tr: With such an irresponsible attitude, everyone will dislike you.

examples.jp: 今から家を建て始めるのでは年内にはでき上がらない。
examples.tr: If you start building the house now, it won't be finished within the year.

examples.jp: 運動をしてみたらどうですか
examples.tr: Why don't you try exercising?

examples.jp: 「毎晩、寝られなくて困っています」「昼間、運動をしてみたらどうですか」
examples.tr: “I'm having trouble because I can't sleep every night.” “Why don't you try exercising during the day?”

examples.jp: この本、面白いから、読んでみたら（どう）？
examples.tr: This book is interesting, so why don't you try reading it?

694.name: ～てる（contracted Vている）
694.meaning: Spoken contracted form of Vている
694.connection: Vている → Vてる / Vていた → Vてた（spoken language）

examples.jp: 持ってる／忘れちゃう／書いとく
examples.tr: Have / end up forgetting / write in advance

examples.jp: このビール、冷蔵庫に入れといて。
examples.tr: Put this beer in the fridge, will you?

examples.jp:
「あそこで新聞読んでる人、知ってる？」
「ああ、吉(よし)田(だ)さんだよ」
examples.tr:
“Do you know the person reading the newspaper over there?”
“Oh, that's Yoshida.”

examples.jp:
「このジュース、全部飲んじゃっていい？」
「ええ、いいですよ」
examples.tr:
“Is it OK if I drink all of this juice?”
“Sure, go ahead.”

694.explain: Spoken form of the structures「～ている／～てしまう／～ておく」

695.meaning: Expresses a strong emotional or physical state that cannot be controlled.

examples.jp: （のどが）かわいてしょうがない
examples.tr: (I'm) unbearably thirsty

examples.jp: 眠くてしょうがない。
examples.tr: I'm so sleepy I can't stand it.

examples.jp: ああ、試合の結果が気になってしょうがない。
examples.tr: Oh, I can't stop worrying about the result of the game.

696.meaning:
「～の動作をすることで、…という事実に気がついた。」… は前から続いている状態を表す文で、少し意外感がある内容。「…ていた」の形がよく使われる。～と…の主語は違う。
By doing action ~, one noticed the fact that …
… is a sentence expressing a state that existed beforehand, with somewhat surprising content.
The ていた form is often used.
The subjects of ~ and … are different.
696.connection: Vると/Vたら、～ていた・～た / Vていると/Vていたら、～た（discovery, surprise）

examples.jp: プレゼントを開けると、人形が入っていた。
examples.tr: When I opened the present, there was a doll inside.

examples.jp: 玄関を出ると、そこに大男が数人いた。
examples.tr: When I stepped out the front door, there were several large men there.

examples.jp: 窓の外を見たら、真っ白な雪景色だった。
examples.tr: When I looked out the window, it was a pure white snowy landscape.

examples.jp: 夜１２時ごろテレビを見ていると、アメリカの友だちから電話がかかってきた。
examples.tr: While I was watching TV around midnight, I got a call from a friend in America.

examples.jp: コーヒーショップでマキさんのうわさをしていると、偶然マキさんが入ってきた。
examples.tr: While we were gossiping about Maki at the coffee shop, Maki happened to walk in.

examples.jp: 庭の掃除をしていたら、突然大雨が降り出した。
examples.tr: While I was cleaning the garden, it suddenly started pouring.

696.notes: Vると、(すぐに)Vた — both clauses have the same subject; a sequence of actions

697.connection: V/A plain form + といいなあ

examples.jp: 明日、晴れるといいなあ。
examples.tr: I hope it's sunny tomorrow.

examples.jp: このプレゼント、喜んでくれるといいなあ。
examples.tr: I hope they'll like this present.

examples.jp: 試験、受かるといいなあ。
examples.tr: I hope I pass the exam.

examples.jp: 今日は早く帰れるといいなあ。
examples.tr: I hope I can go home early today.

examples.jp: 連絡が早く来るといいなあ。
examples.tr: I hope I hear back soon.

examples.jp: 席が空いているといいんだけど。
examples.tr: I hope there are seats available.

697.explain:
Used with the present/future; the past is rare, only when hoping that something already happened in a good way (result not yet known): ちゃんと届いていた といいなあ。
For an action someone else does for you: ～てくれるといいなあ.
Avoid in formal writing; replace with ～ことを願っております／～だと幸いです。
といいなあ is a personal wish; it does not carry the nuance of advising someone to do something.

• Expresses a personal wish/hope about the future or about something currently unknown: “If only/I hope…”.
• Often used when the speaker has no control over the matter (exams, weather, replies…).
• Casual nuance; talking to oneself or sharing a mild feeling with the listener.
• Adding なあ makes it more of a monologue; な replaces なあ in some regions/in spoken language.

rows: Monologue, personal; usually beyond one's control.
<ruby>合格<rt>ごうかく</rt></ruby>するといいなあ。
Directed at the listener; a suggestion/recommendation.
もっと<ruby>安<rt>やす</rt></ruby>ければいいのに。
Equivalent meaning, casual; emphasizes the hypothetical condition.
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>がやんだらいいなあ。
Soft, hesitant; slightly more polite than なあ.
<ruby>間<rt>ま</rt></ruby>に<ruby>合<rt>あ</rt></ruby>うといいんだけど。

mistakes: Confusing it with ～といい (advising others) in multiple-choice questions: if the subject is “you” → it is advice, not a wish.
Using it in formal writing → inappropriate; choose ～と幸いです／～ことを願っております.
Wrong tense/adjective ending: Aだといいなあ (dropping だ is accepted in casual speech, but keep the correct form in exams).
Confusing it with something the subject can control: if the speaker can decide, use ～ばいい instead of ～といいなあ (meaning “should”).
697.notes:
• When you want to be polite with a business partner: 「ご検討いただけると幸いです」 instead of ～といいなあ.
• On social media/in diaries, ～といいなあ expresses a sincere, natural wish.
• Emotional range: lengthen なぁ to emphasize the feeling: ～といいなぁ (informal writing, spoken language).
meaning_vi: If only…, I hope
explain: Used to express a personal desire or wish. It is a type of exclamation sentence
examples: 1. もっと日本語がうまく話せたらいいなあ。
I wish I could speak Japanese more fluently.
2. 明日、雨が降らないといいなあ。
I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.

698.meaning: Has a meaning similar to the structure 「～のに」, but expresses more surprise than 「～のに」
698.connection: V/A plain form + というのに / N/Naだ + というのに

examples.jp: 旅行に行くというとのに
examples.tr: Even though (I'm) going on a trip

examples.jp: 明日から旅行に行くというとのに、まだ準備が終わっていない。
examples.tr: Even though I'm leaving on a trip tomorrow, I still haven't finished getting ready.

examples.jp: もう夜の１時だというとのに、父はまだ帰ってこない。
examples.tr: Even though it's already one o'clock at night, my father still hasn't come home.

examples.jp: 料理をしているところに
examples.tr: Just when I was cooking

examples.jp: 料理をしているところに、電話がかかってきて困った。
examples.tr: Just when I was cooking, I got a phone call, which was annoying.

examples.jp: デートをしているところを友達に見られてしまった。
examples.tr: A friend saw me while I was on a date.

examples.jp: 会社に行こうとして電車に乗ったところで、今日が祝日だと気づいた。
examples.tr: Just as I got on the train to go to work, I realized that today was a holiday.

700.name: ～ところだ・～ところ（＋particle）…
700.meaning:
「～の直前だ（①）・進行中だ（②）・直後だ（③④）。」文中では、後に来る動詞によって「ところを・ところで・ ことろへ」などの形になる。
Just before ~ (①)/ In the middle of ~ (②)/ Right after (③④).
Within a sentence, the accompanying particle changes depending on the verb that follows, taking forms such as "ところを／ところで／ところへ／etc. ".
700.connection: Vる + ところだ（about to）/ Vている + ところだ（in the middle of）/ Vた + ところだ（just finished）( + particle を/で/に…)

examples.jp: ロケットは間もなく飛び立つところです。緊張の瞬間です。
examples.tr: The rocket is about to take off. It is a tense moment.

examples.jp: 試験中、となりの人の答えを見ているところを先生に注意された。
examples.tr: During the exam, the teacher warned me when I was looking at the answers of the person next to me.

examples.jp: 楽しみにしていたテレビドラマが始まったところで電話が鳴った。
examples.tr: Just as the TV drama I had been looking forward to started, the phone rang.

examples.jp: ケーキが出来上がったところへ子どもたちが帰ってきた。
examples.tr: The children came home just as the cake was finished.

701.connection: [sentence/clause] + などと/なんて + 言う/思う

examples.jp: 彼が犯人だなんて信じられない。
examples.tr: I can't believe he's the culprit.

examples.jp: 子どもが親に暴力をふるうなど、昔は考えられなかった。
examples.tr: In the past, it was unthinkable that children would be violent toward their parents.

examples.jp: 「試験まであと１週間あるから大丈夫なんて思っていると、また失敗するよ」
examples.tr: “If you think you're fine because there's still a week until the exam, you'll fail again.”

examples.jp: あの政治家はいつも「国民のために働く」などと言っていたが、実は自分の利益のことしか考えていなかったのだ。
examples.tr: That politician always said things like “I work for the people,” but in fact he was only thinking of his own interests.

701.explain: Often used to evaluate, mock, or deny what someone else says or thinks.
701.notes:
1) Easy to confuse with simple など (giving examples).
→ ～などと（なんて）言う／思う is often used for evaluation, sarcasm, surprise, or denial.
2) Often used with the verbs “say/think”.
→ Common structure: 普通形＋などと＋言う／思う.
3) If you only want to list things, do not use this pattern.
→ This pattern emphasizes the speaker's attitude, not just giving an example.

702.meaning:
Spoken language expressing surprise. What follows「なんて」is sometimes omitted.
［ふつう］　+　なんて
702.connection: V/A plain form + なんて / N/Na(だ) + なんて（surprise）

examples.jp: こんなにやさしかったなんて
examples.tr: (I never knew) they were this kind

examples.jp: この本を一日で全部読んだなんて、信じられません。
examples.tr: I can't believe you read this whole book in one day.

examples.jp: オリンピックに出たことがあるなんて、すごい。
examples.tr: You've been in the Olympics? That's amazing.

examples.jp: あの話がうそだったなんて。
examples.tr: To think that story was a lie.

703.meaning: Spoken language expressing a feeling of making light of something.

examples.jp: うわさなんて
examples.tr: Rumors and such

examples.jp: うわさなんて、みんなすぐに忘れるよ。
examples.tr: Rumors? Everyone will forget them soon enough.

examples.jp: 「どれにしようかなあ」「これなんて、どう？」
examples.tr: “Which one should I choose?” “How about this one?”

examples.jp: ケーキを作るなんて、簡単だよ。
examples.tr: Making a cake? That's easy.

704.connection: V plain form / N / Na + にしては ・ V plain form / N の / Na な / Aい + わりに

examples.jp: 学生にしては
examples.tr: For a student

examples.jp: 田中君は学生にしてはいいマンションに住んでいる。きっと親が金持ちなんだろう。
examples.tr: Tanaka lives in a nice apartment for a student. His parents must be rich.

examples.jp: 川田さんは、毎日３時間勉強しているにしては、あまり成績がよくない。
examples.tr: Kawata doesn't get very good grades for someone who studies three hours every day.

examples.jp: このアパートは駅から近いわりに、家賃が安い。
examples.tr: This apartment is cheap considering how close it is to the station.

examples.jp: ホームページで、商品に対する質問を受け付けている。
examples.tr: We accept questions about our products on our website.

examples.jp: 森先生は、遅刻した学生に対して厳しく注意する。
examples.tr: Mr. Mori strictly reprimands students who come late.

705.explain: ◎ An expression indicating the target of actions such as "giving a present"
705.notes: Expresses the meaning 「それに向けての」 (directed toward it) or 「それに関しての」 (concerning it), and modifies the noun that follows. The form 「ＮにたいしてのＮ」 is also sometimes used, as in 「その問に対しての解答」.

examples.jp: 人口が増えるにともなって、さまさまな問題も起きている。
examples.tr: Along with the increase in population, various problems are also arising.

examples.jp: 引っ越しにともなういくつかの手続きは、もう済ませました。
examples.tr: I have already finished the procedures that come with moving.

706.explain: ◎ Describes something that happens simultaneously with, or immediately after, something else.

708.name: ～には（purpose）
708.meaning: Expresses a purpose and what is necessary to achieve that goal.
708.connection: Vる + には / N(サ変) + には（purpose）

examples.jp: 上手になるには
examples.tr: To become good at

examples.jp: 日本語が上手になるには、どうしたらいいですか。
examples.tr: What should I do to become good at Japanese?

examples.jp: コンサート会場に行くには、バスが便利です。
examples.tr: To get to the concert venue, the bus is convenient.

708.notes: Expresses the meaning 「そうするためには」 (in order to do so) or 「そうしたいと思うのなら」 (if you want to do so).

709.meaning: On the basis of …, based on …

examples.jp: この映画は実際にあった事件に基づいて作られた。
examples.tr: This movie was based on an incident that actually happened.

examples.jp: データに基づいて仮説を立てる。
examples.tr: We form a hypothesis based on the data.

examples.jp: 法律に基づき、当店では２０歳未満の方には酒の販売をいたしません。
examples.tr: In accordance with the law, this store does not sell alcohol to anyone under 20.

examples.jp: 今回の知事の発言は、正しい知識に基づいたものではない。
examples.tr: The governor's recent remarks were not based on accurate knowledge.

examples.jp: 今後とも、お客様のご意見に基づいた商品を開発していくつもりです。
examples.tr: We intend to continue developing products based on our customers' opinions.

709.explain: Used to state the basis or grounds for a decision or evaluation. Often used in written language.
709.notes:
1) Easy to confuse with ～によって.
→ ～にもとづいて／もとづき means “based on/in accordance with” standards, data, laws, or regulations.
2) Often used in written language (laws, newspapers, research).
→ Has a formal nuance.
3) Not used for means.
→ For “by doing…”, use ～によって／～を通じて…

examples.jp: 試合は、国際ルールに基づいて行われます。
examples.tr: The match will be held according to international rules.

examples.jp: この売り上予想は、去年のデータに基づいています。
examples.tr: This sales forecast is based on last year's data.

710.explain: ◎ Expresses taking something as the basis when acting on or making a judgment about something.

711.meaning: Depending on the case, ~ (there are cases where ~)

examples.jp: 国によって習慣が違う。
examples.tr: Customs differ from country to country.

examples.jp: 感じ方は人によってさまざまだ。
examples.tr: The way people feel varies from person to person.

examples.jp: わたしの帰宅時間は毎日違う。日によっては夜中になることもある。
examples.tr: My time getting home differs every day. Some days it's even the middle of the night.

examples.jp: 場合によっては今年の文化祭は中止になるかもしれない。
examples.tr: Depending on circumstances, this year's school festival may be canceled.

711.explain:
「～が違えば…。」 …は一定ではないことを表す文（さまざまだ・変えるなど）。「～によっては…」の…は、いろいろな場合のうちの一つの例を言う文。
If ~ differs, then …
… is a sentence expressing that something is not fixed ( 様々だ／変える etc.)
The … in ~ によっては… is a sentence giving an example from among various cases.

712.meaning:
「～が原因で…という結果が起こる。」 …には状態を表す文は来ない。また、希望・意向・相手への働きかけなのでの文は来ない。少し硬い言い方。
~ is the cause that brings about the result …
… is not used to express a state, and it is not a sentence expressing a desire, an intention, or urging the other person to do something. A somewhat formal expression.

examples.jp: 外国語を学ぶことによってその国の人たちの考え方も知ることができる。
examples.tr: By learning a foreign language, you can also learn how the people of that country think.

examples.jp: クレジットカードによるお支払いを希望される方は、次の注意をお読みください。
examples.tr: Those wishing to pay by credit card, please read the following notes.

examples.jp: うちの工場では、材料不足によってたたみの生産はもうできなくなった。
examples.tr: At our factory, we can no longer produce tatami mats due to a shortage of materials.

examples.jp: 今年のインフルエンザは、今までにない型のウイルスによるものである。
examples.tr: This year's flu is caused by a type of virus never seen before.

712.notes: meaning_vi: By…, due to…, depending on… (によって/による)

713.meaning: ~ Depending on…, there are cases where

examples.jp: この注射をすると、ひとによっては熱が出ることもある。
examples.tr: With this injection, some people may get a fever.

examples.jp: 天気によっては、試合が中止になることもある。
examples.tr: Depending on the weather, the match may be canceled.

713.explain: ◎ Such things can happen under certain conditions and circumstances.

714.meaning: Expresses that there are many different cases.

examples.jp: 人によって違う
examples.tr: It differs from person to person

examples.jp: 店によって値段が違います。
examples.tr: Prices differ from store to store.

examples.jp: 夕食を食べる時間は、人によっていろいろだ。
examples.tr: The time people eat dinner varies from person to person.

examples.jp: 休みの日の過ごし方は、その日の気分による。
examples.tr: How I spend my days off depends on how I feel that day.

716.meaning:
Gives the source of information
ニュースに　+　よれば／よる

examples.jp: 医者によると
examples.tr: According to the doctor

examples.jp: 天気予報によると、明日は雨らしい。
examples.tr: According to the weather forecast, it looks like it will rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: 統計によるば、この市の人口は２０年間減り続けている。
examples.tr: According to statistics, the population of this city has been decreasing for 20 years.

717.name: ～に対して（target）
717.meaning: Indicates the other party or the target toward which an action is directed
717.connection: Nに + 対して（target toward which the action is directed）

examples.jp: 目上の人に対して
examples.tr: Toward one's superiors

examples.jp: 目上の人に対して、敬語を使うようにしている。
examples.tr: I make a point of using honorific language toward my superiors.

examples.jp: 発表に対して、質問がある方はどうぞ。
examples.tr: Anyone with questions about the presentation, please go ahead.

examples.jp: 発表に対する質問は、この紙に書いてください。
examples.tr: Please write your questions about the presentation on this sheet of paper.

examples.jp: パーティーのこと
examples.tr: About the party

examples.jp: パーティーのことは、田中さんがよく知っているよ。
examples.tr: Tanaka knows a lot about the party.

examples.jp: 先生、すみません。試験のことで、ちょっとご相談があるんですが。
examples.tr: Excuse me, sir. I'd like to consult you about the exam.

examples.jp: 来週のテストのことで、質問があります。
examples.tr: I have a question about next week's test.

examples.jp: 田中さんが入院したことを知っていますか。
examples.tr: Do you know that Tanaka was hospitalized?

718.notes: Original meaning: About the matter of

719.meaning:
「～が事実だから、当然…。」 ～には相手が知っているはずの事実を表す文、 …には話者の判断・希望・意向や相手への働きかけなどの文が来る。
Since ~ is a fact, naturally…
~ is a sentence expressing a fact the other person surely knows as well.
… is a sentence expressing the speaker's judgment, desire, or intention, or urging the other person to do something.

examples.jp: 世界は広いのだから、いろいろな習慣があるのは当然だ。
examples.tr: The world is a big place, so it's only natural that there are various customs.

examples.jp: あなたはけがをしているんだから、無理をしてはいけませんよ。
examples.tr: You're injured, so you mustn't overdo it.

examples.jp: 笑わないでください。真剣にやっているんですから。
examples.tr: Please don't laugh. I'm doing this seriously, after all.

719.notes: Takes a clause, acknowledges that what is stated there is a fact, and expresses that this fact serves as the cause or reason from which what is stated next is derived. For example, in ①, after acknowledging that the person is a child, the judgment that it cannot be helped if they do not understand is derived on that basis. In contrast, in 「まだ子供だから分からないのだろう」, the speaker is conjecturing the reason, i.e., that they do not understand probably because they are a child. In spoken language, it often becomes 「…んだから」.（４６６）

720.connection: V/A plain form + のではないだろうか / N・Na + なの

examples.jp: はっきりと自分の意見を述べることが大切なのではないだろうか。
examples.tr: Isn't it important to state your own opinion clearly?

examples.jp: 田中さんは、実はこの方法に反対なのではないだろうか。
examples.tr: Isn't Tanaka actually against this method?

720.explain: ◎ 「だろうか」(could it be, isn't it) is attached after the negative ending「のではない」; this is a construction that takes the form of a question but actually emphasizes an assertion, like 「～のだ」.
720.notes: Variant: ～(の)ではないかと思う; spoken language: ～んじゃない？

721.meaning: Compares two things that contrast with each other.
721.connection: V/A plain form + のに対して / Naな(である)/Nである + のに対して（contrast）

examples.jp: 怒りっぽいのに対して
examples.tr: In contrast to being quick-tempered

examples.jp: 東京ではそばが人気があるのに対して、大阪ではうどんが人気がある。
examples.tr: In Tokyo soba is popular, whereas in Osaka udon is popular.

examples.jp: 父が短気で怒りっぽいのに対して、母はのんびりしている。
examples.tr: While my father is short-tempered and gets angry easily, my mother is easygoing.

722.name: ～のに（purpose）
722.meaning: Expresses a purpose and what is needed to achieve that goal.
722.connection: Vる + のに + 使う/便利だ/かかる…（purpose・function）

examples.jp: 調べるのに使う
examples.tr: use (something) to look things up

examples.jp: ことばの意味を調べるのに、インタネットを使っている。
examples.tr: I use the internet to look up the meanings of words.

examples.jp: 髪を切るのに、はさみが必要だよ。
examples.tr: You need scissors to cut hair.

723.name: ～のに（contrast）
723.meaning: Expresses a connection contrary to expectation
723.connection: V/A plain form + のに / Nな/Naな + のに（contrary to expectation）

examples.jp: 約束したのに
examples.tr: Even though (someone) promised...

examples.jp: 来ると約束したのに、彼は来なかった。
examples.tr: He promised he would come, but he didn't.

examples.jp: まだ昼の２時だというのに、夕方のように暗い。
examples.tr: Even though it's still only 2 in the afternoon, it's as dark as evening.

724.connection: V plain form + のは + ～(こと)だ

examples.jp: 最近、頑張っているのは、毎朝ウォーキングをすることです。
examples.tr: What I've been working hard at lately is walking every morning.

examples.jp: 私がさっき電話で話していたのは、田中さんです。
examples.tr: The person I was talking to on the phone a moment ago was Mr. Tanaka.

724.explain: ◎ Expresses a firm judgment about something.

examples.jp: 友達の話では、チケットはまだ残っているようです。
examples.tr: According to my friend, it seems there are still tickets left.

725.explain: ◎ Indicates the source of information. 「～の話によると」 is a similar expression.

726.meaning: Expresses acknowledgment that something is only natural.

examples.jp: 怒るのも当然だ
examples.tr: It's only natural to get angry

examples.jp: そんなひどいことをしたなら、かれが怒るのも当然だ。
examples.tr: If he did something that awful, it's only natural that he's angry.

examples.jp: ３０年も前のことだから、覚えていないのも無理はない。
examples.tr: It happened 30 years ago, so it's no wonder you don't remember it.

727.meaning:
～によくにている
Very similar to ~
727.connection: Nの + ようだ / N + みたいだ（very similar）

examples.jp: ここから見える景色は絵のようだ。
examples.tr: The view from here is like a painting.

examples.jp: このパンはケーキみたいに甘くて軟らかい。
examples.tr: This bread is sweet and soft, like cake.

examples.jp: ガラスみたいな氷を靴で踏んで遊んで。
examples.tr: Step on the glass-like ice with your shoes and play.

727.explain: Used in spoken language to describe a person or thing as having a certain look or appearance that the other person can compare to something
727.notes:
meaning_vi: よく似ているものに例えて言う
used to liken something to a thing with similar features
examples: 1. 今日は暖かくて、まるで春が来たかのようだ。
It's warm today, as if spring has come.
2. 朝から晩までロボットのように働いた。
I worked like a robot from morning till night.
3. バケツをひっくり返したような雨だった。
It was pouring, as if someone had turned a bucket upside down.
meaning_vi: A figurative expression likening something to something similar. 「まるで」 emphasizes the comparison.
春　+　のようだ／春　+　みたいだ
春　+　のようなN／春　+　みたいだなN
春　+　のように～／春　+　みたいに～
examples: 1. ①　（まるで）母親のようだ／母親みたいだ
(Just) like a mother.
2. ②　今日は暖かくて、（まるで）春のようだ／みたいだ。
It's warm today, (just) like spring.
3. ③　今日は暖かくて、（まるで）春のような／みたいな日だ。
Today is a warm day, (just) like a spring day.
4. ➃　今日は（まるで）春のように／みたいに暖かい。
Today is warm, (just) like spring.
meaning_vi: Like, looks like
examples: 1. 彼の話し方は、女みたいだ。
His way of talking is like a woman's
2. ここの砂は星みたいな形をしている。
The sand here is shaped like stars.
3. このアパートはだれも住んでいないみたいだ。
It seems nobody lives in this apartment
4. 明日は雨みたいね。
It looks like it'll rain tomorrow
5. リンさんみたいに日本語がうまくなりたい。
I want to get good at Japanese like Lin

728.meaning:
「が」 in a noun-modifying clause changes to 「の」
父が作ったN　＝　父の作ったN
728.connection: N1の/が + V + N2（の replacing が in a modifier clause）

examples.jp: 不動産屋のすすめる部屋
examples.tr: the room the real estate agent recommends

examples.jp: 母の作った料理が食べたい。
examples.tr: I want to eat the food my mother made.

examples.jp: あの背の高い人はだれですか。
examples.tr: Who is that tall person?

examples.jp: 景色のきれいなところに住みたいです。
examples.tr: I want to live somewhere with beautiful scenery.

729.meaning: There is no way ~ (a negative judgment made with certainty)
729.connection: V/A plain form + はずがない / Naな(である)・Nの(である) + はずがない

examples.jp: ちゃんと約束したんだから、彼が来ないはずがない。どうしたのかなあ。
examples.tr: We made a firm promise, so there's no way he won't come. I wonder what happened.

examples.jp: あの店が今日休みのはずはありません。電話で確認したんですから。
examples.tr: There's no way that shop is closed today. I checked by phone.

examples.jp: 国家試験なのだから易しいはずがない。頑張らなくては…。
examples.tr: It's a national exam, so there's no way it's easy. I have to work hard...

examples.jp: こんなに大きい家、私に買えるわけがないでしょう。
examples.tr: A house this big? There's no way I could buy it.

examples.jp: 試合に勝つために練習しているのだ。練習が厳しくないわけがない。
examples.tr: We practice in order to win matches. There's no way the practice wouldn't be tough.

729.explain:
「絶対～ない。」 話者が強い確信を持って否定する言い方。
Definitely not ~.
A way of negating with the speaker's strong certainty.

730.name: ～はずだ（naturally）
730.meaning:
No wonder … (so that's why)
Should have… (but in reality…)
I'm sure that … but in reality it's different

examples.jp: ドアが開かないはずだ。かぎが違っていた。
examples.tr: No wonder the door won't open. It was the wrong key.

examples.jp: 体がだるいはずだ。熱が３８度もある。
examples.tr: No wonder I feel so sluggish. I have a fever of 38 degrees.

examples.jp: 汽車は３時に発車するはずだったが、急病人が出たために１０分ほど遅れた。
examples.tr: The train was supposed to depart at 3, but it was delayed about 10 minutes because someone suddenly fell ill.

examples.jp: 「変だなあ。このボタンを押せば動くはずなのに。。。」
examples.tr: "That's strange. It should work if I press this button..."

examples.jp: 日本へ来れば日本語なんかすぐに話せるようになると思っていた。こんなはずではなかった。
examples.tr: I thought that once I came to Japan, I'd soon be able to speak Japanese. It wasn't supposed to be like this.

examples.jp: はさみが見あたらない。さっき見たときは、机の上にあったはずなのに。
examples.tr: I can't find the scissors. I'm sure they were on the desk when I saw them earlier...

730.explain:
Reasoning logically from a cause to reach the conclusion “naturally…”.
Expresses a result different from the original prediction or expectation.
Expresses something the speaker is sure they remember correctly, but in reality it is different.
730.notes:
1) The meanings of ～はずだ are easy to confuse.
→ It means “naturally (logical inference)”, can mean “should have…”, and also means “I'm sure that…”.
2) Look at the context.
→ If there are grounds for inference: the meaning “naturally”.
→ If the result is contrary to expectation: the meaning “should have…”.
3) Easily confused with ～に違いない.
→ ～はずだ is based on logical inference; ～に違いない is a more certain judgment based on intuition/evidence.

examples.jp: 学生はもちろん、先生も参加してください。
examples.tr: Students, of course, and teachers too, please take part.

examples.jp: この料理は味はもちろん、見た目も美しい。
examples.tr: This dish is delicious, of course, and it looks beautiful too.

examples.jp: 漢字はもちろん、ひらがなも練習が必要だ。
examples.tr: You need to practice kanji, of course, and hiragana too.

examples.jp: 彼は平日はもちろん、週末も働いている。
examples.tr: He works on weekdays, of course, and on weekends too.

examples.jp: 時間がないのはもちろん、予算も足りない。
examples.tr: We don't have time, of course, and the budget isn't enough either.

examples.jp: 喫煙はもちろん、飲酒も校内で禁止です。
examples.tr: Drinking, as well as smoking, is prohibited on campus.

731.explain:
N1 must be something obvious/natural in the context; N2 is an addition.
The original particle at N1 is usually replaced with は to emphasize the topic:日本語 は もちろん（を/が is not used here）.
When N1 is a clause, remember to nominalize it with の: ～のはもちろん.
The second clause has も/まで/さえ to mark the addition; まで/さえ give the nuance “even”.
Style: neutral → formal; the variant ～はもとより is more formal.

- Meaning: “N1, of course, and N2 too…”. The N1 part is something obvious, naturally true; the N2 part is additional information that is less obvious.
- Nuance: Emphasizes the “obviousness” of N1. Compared with ～だけでなく, marking the topic with は makes N1 stand out more.
- Can be used with both a positive nuance and a negative nuance; often appears in announcements, rules and introductions.

rows: Not only A but B too
Neutral, does not emphasize “obviousness”; widely used
<ruby>学生<rt>がくせい</rt></ruby>だけでなく<ruby>先生<rt>せんせい</rt></ruby>も<ruby>参加<rt>さんか</rt></ruby>。
Not only A but also B
Stronger nuance of “beyond expectation/surprise” than ～はもちろん
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>ばかりか<ruby>風<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>も<ruby>強<rt>つよ</rt></ruby>い。
In addition to A, also B
Leans toward listing, little nuance of “obviousness”
<ruby>経験<rt>けいけん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>加<rt>くわ</rt></ruby>えて<ruby>資格<rt>しかく</rt></ruby>も<ruby>必要<rt>ひつよう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもはもとより<ruby>大人<rt>おとな</rt></ruby>も<ruby>歓迎<rt>かんげい</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Keeping the original particle at N1 (× 日本語をもちろん) → it must change to は: 日本語はもちろん.
Leaving out も in the second clause weakens the sense of addition: ～も/まで/さえ is needed.
Confusing it with ～ばかりか when the question calls for “unexpected/beyond expectation” → choose ～ばかりか.
Forgetting to nominalize with の when N1 is a clause: × 時間がないはもちろん → 時間がないのはもちろん.
731.notes:
• With long noun phrases, using のはもちろん keeps the sentence coherent: 安全に配慮するのはもちろん、…
• In advertising/introductions: “品質はもちろん、価格も…” is a stock phrase.
• Put the newer/more appealing information in N2 to communicate effectively.
• “もちろん” can also be used as an independent adverb at the beginning of a sentence: もちろん、参加します。 (a different structure from the one discussed here).
meaning_vi: Not only … but also …
explain: Expresses that the first item is obvious and further emphasizes the following item to a higher degree: “not only… but also…”.
examples: 1. 会社の経営が悪化して、ボーナスはもちろん給料も出ない状態だ。
Because the company's business has deteriorated, we aren't even getting our salaries, let alone bonuses.
2. 「今度のパーティーには、君はもちろん、奥さんにも出席してもらいたい。」
For the next party, I'd like not only you but also your wife to attend.
3. コンビニでは日用品の販売はもちろん、宅配便の受け付けもするし、公共料金の支払いもできる。
Convenience stores not only sell daily necessities, of course, but also accept parcel deliveries and let you pay utility bills.
4. 彼はスポーツマンで、自分でするのはもちろん、見るのも大好きだそうだ。
He's a sportsman; apparently he loves not only playing sports himself but also watching them.
5. 日本へ留学するなら、言葉はもとより文化や習慣も学んでほしい。
If you're going to study abroad in Japan, I want you to learn not only the language but also the culture and customs.
6. アメリカ大統領選挙の結果は、国内はもとより国外にも大きな影響を与える。
The result of the US presidential election has a big impact not only domestically but also abroad.
meaning_vi: (Noun) goes without saying, but also (Noun')
explain: Used to show that a thing also has a (good) characteristic similar to another obvious characteristic.
Often expresses praise or surprise
examples: 1. 彼は勉強はもちろんスポーツもよくできる。
He's good at studying, of course, and at sports too
2. キャベツは炒めて食べるはもちろん、生で食べてもおいしいです。
Cabbage is tasty stir-fried, of course, but it's also delicious raw

732.meaning:
「もし～の場合、…という結果になるはずだが、実際にはそうではない。」～も…も実際とは違うことを言う。…は「～た・～のだが・～のに」などの文が多い。
In the case of “if ~”, it would surely lead to the result …, but in reality that is not the case.
~ and … are conditions that differ from the facts.
… is mostly in the form ～た／～のだが／～のに／etc.
732.connection: Vば…/Vたら…/N・Naなら…（counterfactual supposition; the second clause is often ～のに/んだけど）

examples.jp: お金とひまがあればわたしも海外旅行するんだけど…。
examples.tr: If I had money and free time, I'd travel abroad too, but...

examples.jp: もし寝坊していたらこの飛行機には乗れなかった。間に合ってよかった。
examples.tr: If I had overslept, I couldn't have caught this flight. Good thing I made it in time.

examples.jp: ああ、残念だ。学生なら学生割引でチケットが買えたのに…。
examples.tr: Oh, what a shame. If I were a student, I could have bought the ticket with a student discount...

732.notes: Common endings for the second clause: ～たい・～のに・～(ば)よかった

733.meaning: The structure 「～ばいい」 expresses the speaker's desire. The structure 「～ばいいのに」 expresses regret that the present situation differs from what one wants.

examples.jp: 新しい部屋があればと思う
examples.tr: I wish I had a new room.

examples.jp: 誰かいい人と出会えればと思って、パーティーに行った。
examples.tr: I went to the party hoping I might meet someone nice.

examples.jp: あんなすてきな人が恋人ならな。
examples.tr: If only such a wonderful person were my partner.

examples.jp: このかばん、ほしいけど高いなあ。もっと安ければいいのに。
examples.tr: I want this bag, but it's expensive. I wish it were cheaper.

734.connection: V + [sentence/clause] + のに / N + なら / Na + なら / Aい + い ければ

examples.jp: もう少し早く出れば、間に合ったのに。
examples.tr: If I had left a little earlier, I would have made it in time.

examples.jp: お金があれば、旅行できたのに。
examples.tr: If I'd had money, I could have traveled.

examples.jp: 彼に聞けばよかったのに。
examples.tr: I should have asked him.

examples.jp: 雨でなければ、行けたのに。
examples.tr: If it hadn't been raining, I could have gone.

examples.jp: 連絡してくれれば、迎えに行ったのに。
examples.tr: If you had let me know, I would have come to pick you up.

examples.jp: 静かにすればいいのに。
examples.tr: I wish you'd just be quiet.

734.explain:
Used for regret about a condition that did not happen; has a complaining nuance when directed at someone else.
The second clause is usually in the past: ～たのに, expressing a desired result that did not happen.
When expressing regret, a command/volition is not combined in the second clause; for a suggestion, use ～ばいいのに.
With Aな/N, ～なら is the most natural; in formal style ～であれば can be used.

- Meaning: “If only A, then B…”, expressing regret, mild criticism, or regret about a condition that did not happen (counterfactual).
- The second clause ～のに shows a desired result that was not achieved; the past is often used: ～たのに／～だったのに.
- Nuance: May imply criticism of oneself/the other person; for a mild suggestion, use ～ばいいのに.

rows: Does not need the ば condition; states a contrasting fact
If only (I) had…, it would have been good
Close in meaning to ～ばよかったのに; たら has a more conversational nuance
As long as A, then B
Minimum condition, no implication of regret
<ruby>時間<rt>じかん</rt></ruby>さえあれば、<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>ける。
I wish/If only (you would do) A
Suggestion/mild complaint, not describing a result already missed
<ruby>早<rt>はや</rt></ruby>く<ruby>寝<rt>ね</rt></ruby>ればいいのに。

mistakes: Using the present in the second clause when expressing regret: ～たのに should be used to make “already missed” clear.
Confusing it with ～のに (concession): if the sentence expresses “counterfactual + regret”, the first clause must have the ば condition.
Incorrect use with Aな/N: choose ～なら/～であれば instead of using ば directly.
Inversion of the natural order: the condition should be something controllable/hypothetical; the second clause is the desired result.
734.notes:
• Tense pattern: [ば condition] + [desired result in the past] + のに is the standard pattern for regret.
• With い形容詞: 高ければ買ったのに／安ければよかったのに.
• With negative N/Aな: Nでなければ／Aでなければ is used when the actual condition is negative.
• In spoken language, the subject can be omitted and the sentence broken off to emphasize emotion: もっと早く出れば……（ため息）……間に合ったのに。
meaning_vi: Supposes something contrary to fact, then expresses a complaint about reality or a wish to do that thing.
examples: 1. ①　時間があれば行ったのに
If I'd had time, I would have gone.
2. ②　「昨日どうしてカラオケに行かなかったの？」
「忙いそがしかったんだ。時間じかんがあれば行いったのに」
"Why didn't you go to karaoke yesterday?"
"Because I was busy. If I'd had time, I would have gone"
3. ➂　昨日のカラオケ、楽しかったよ。リーさんも行ったらよかったのに。
Karaoke yesterday was fun. You should have come too, Lee.
4. ➃　この荷物、重くなければ、一人で運べるのに。
If this luggage weren't heavy, I could carry it by myself.

735.meaning: Contracted form of the structure 「～ば～ほど」
735.connection: Vる/Aい + ほど（contracted form of Vば Vるほど: 短いほどいい）

examples.jp: 短いほど
examples.tr: the shorter (the better)

examples.jp: 結婚式のスピーチは短いほどいいと、よく言われます。
examples.tr: It is often said that the shorter a wedding speech, the better.

examples.jp: たばこをよく吸う人ほど病気になりやすい。
examples.tr: The more someone smokes, the more prone they are to illness.

examples.jp: 子どものとき、母からよく本を読むように言われた。
examples.tr: When I was a child, my mother often told me to read books.

examples.jp: 美術館では写真を撮らないように注意された。
examples.tr: At the art museum, I was warned not to take photos.

736.explain: ◎ An expression indicating an intention toward a certain state. Used when conveying instructions or setting a goal …

rows: Direct to the listener; ～ように<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う is reported/indirect.
<ruby>命令<rt>めいれい</rt></ruby><ruby>形<rt>けい</rt></ruby>／～なさい
Strong/stiff. ように<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う is softer, suited to written language/instructions.
Expresses the speaker's effort; a different function from “conveying a request”.
<ruby>静<rt>しず</rt></ruby>かにするようにする。
Emphasizes the speaker's desire. てくれるように<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う adds the nuance of “asking someone to do it for me”.
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>ってほしいと<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>う。

mistakes: Wrong “に” marking the recipient: × 彼を早く来るように言った → ○ 彼に早く来るように言った。
Dropping ように leads to a different, direct meaning: × 静かにすると言った → “said that I would be quiet”, not “told (someone) to be quiet”.
Confusing it with ～てください in reported speech involving a third party: when conveying a request to a third party, ～ように言う is more natural.
Using an adjective/noun directly is incorrect: × 静かだように言う → ○ 静かにするように言う。
736.notes:
meaning_vi: Tell (someone) to do…
explain: Politeness is adjusted by the accompanying verb:言う（neutral）,頼む（request）,注意する（reminder）,指示する（command）,依頼する（formal request）.
Vないように言う is used to forbid something/remind someone to avoid it; Vてくれるように言う asks someone to do something for you.
The passive is used to emphasize the rule/instruction rather than the person giving the order: ～ように言われている。
examples: 1. ①　買うように言う。
Tell (someone) "buy it"
2. ②　先生はみんなにもっと勉強するように言った。
The teacher told everyone to study harder.
3. ③　医者にお酒を飲まないように言われた。
I was told by the doctor "don't drink alcohol"
──────
1. 先生は学生に、毎日復習するように言った。
The teacher told the students to review every day.
2. 部長に、資料を明日までに提出するように言われました。
I was told by the department manager to submit the documents by tomorrow.
3. 子どもに、危ないから川に近づかないように言う。
I tell my child not to go near the river because it's dangerous.
4. 受付に、着いたら電話してくれるように言っておきます。
I'll ask the reception desk to call you when you arrive.
5. 会議では、携帯はマナーモードにするように言われています。
In meetings, everyone is asked to put their phones on silent mode.
6. 医者は彼に、酒を控えるように言った。
The doctor told him to cut down on alcohol.

737.connection: V plain form + ように感じる / 思う / N の / Na な

examples.jp: 彼が言っていることは間違っているように思う。
examples.tr: I think what he's saying seems to be wrong.

examples.jp: この店は、最近、サービスが悪くなったように感じる。
examples.tr: I feel that this shop's service has gotten worse lately.

737.explain: ◎ Unlike 「～と感じた／思った」, which states an evaluation or impression directly, this expression conveys an impression when one cannot be completely sure.

examples.jp: この活動を通して、彼女を知り合いました。
examples.tr: I got to know her through this activity.

examples.jp: 私の場合、仕事を通して日本語を覚えました。
examples.tr: In my case, I learned Japanese through work.

738.explain: ◎ Something becomes a means or intermediary that is useful for something.

rows: <ruby>仲介<rt>ちゅうかい</rt></ruby><ruby>会社<rt>かいしゃ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>通<rt>つう</rt></ruby>じて<ruby>契約<rt>けいやく</rt></ruby>
<ruby>活動<rt>かつどう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>通<rt>とお</rt></ruby>して<ruby>成長<rt>せいちょう</rt></ruby>
Broad meaning; includes the passive and cause
<ruby>研究<rt>けんきゅう</rt></ruby>によって<ruby>明<rt>あき</rt></ruby>らかになった
<ruby>香港<rt>ほんこん</rt></ruby><ruby>経由<rt>けいゆ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>帰国<rt>きこく</rt></ruby>
<ruby>蚊<rt>か</rt></ruby>を<ruby>介<rt>かい</rt></ruby>して<ruby>感染<rt>かんせん</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Confusing it with ～によって (cause or reason/passive): “TVによって伝えられた” can be ambiguous; “TVを通じて” is more natural.
Using “通して” when you want to emphasize “the entire period”: choose “通じて” for a consistently formal nuance in the JLPT.
Attaching it to a verb that requires a specific agent: “先生を通じて教える” is ambiguous; it should be “先生を通じて知らせる/紹介される”.
738.notes:
meaning_vi: Through…, throughout…
explain: Used for a channel of communication (人・媒体・制度・経験) or an entire period of time (日・年・季節).
Nuance ranges from neutral to formal; often used in articles and news.
“を通じて” leans toward a result achieved via a channel; “を通して” leans toward experience/process.
examples: 1. インターネットを通じて情報を集める。
Gather information through the internet.
2. 留学を通して多くのことを学んだ。
I learned many things through studying abroad.
3. 一年を通じてこの地域は湿度が高い。
This area is humid all year round.
4. テレビを通じて最新ニュースが伝えられた。
The latest news was conveyed through TV.
5. 仕事を通して彼と知り合った。
I got to know him through work.
6. 四季を通じて楽しめる公園だ。
It's a park you can enjoy throughout all four seasons.
meaning_vi: Through, by means of …
Throughout…
explain: Expresses the means, intermediary or method for carrying out an action: “through…”.
Expresses something happening throughout an entire period of time.
examples: 1. 彼女とサークルの先輩を通して知り合った。
I got to know her through a senior member of my club.
2. 子どもは学校の勉強だけではなく、いろいろな経験を通して成長していく。
Children grow not only through schoolwork but also through various experiences.
3. むかし読書を通して得た知識が、今役に立っている。
The knowledge I gained through reading long ago is useful now.
4. 紅白歌合戦は衛星放送を通じて海外でも見られる。
The Kohaku Uta Gassen song contest can also be watched overseas via satellite broadcasting.
5. 佐藤教授はあらゆる機会を通じて環境保護を訴えている。
Professor Sato appeals for environmental protection at every opportunity.
6. 京都には年間（／四季）を通じて観光客が訪れる。
Tourists visit Kyoto all year round.
7. 私は高校３年間を通して無遅刻無欠席だった。
Throughout my three years of high school, I was never late or absent.
8. 彼女は一生を通して恵まれない子どもたちのために働いた。
She worked all her life for underprivileged children.
meaning_vi: Means “through ~”, “throughout ~”
examples: 1. ①　スポーツを通じて
Through sports
2. ②　子供たちはスポーツを通じて、いろいろなことを学ぶことができます。
Children can learn many things through sports.
3. ③　彼女は、先輩を通して知り合いました。
I got to know her through a senior.
4. ➃　この国は一年を通して暑い。
This country is hot all year round.
meaning_vi: through ～; throughout ～
explain: Used when talking about establishing a relationship or conveying information or contact that is achieved via an intermediary.
When referring to a continuous, uninterrupted period of time.
examples: 1. 友人を通じて彼と知り合った。
I got to know him through a friend.
2. テレビのニュースを通じてその事件を知った。
I learned of that incident through the TV news.
3. ここでは一年を通じて美しい花が見られます。
Here you can see beautiful flowers all year round.

739.connection: V volitional form + と思っている

examples.jp: 今度の花火大会で浴衣を着ようと思っている。
examples.tr: I'm thinking of wearing a yukata to the next fireworks festival.

examples.jp: 子どもたちが大きくなったら、妻と二人で田舎に住もうと思っている。
examples.tr: When the children have grown up, I'm thinking of living in the countryside with my wife.

739.explain: ◎ Expresses the speaker's volition or intention over a certain period of time. Similar to the expression 「～つもりだ」.

740.meaning: The same state continues without any change.

examples.jp: 会わないままになる
examples.tr: to end up never meeting

examples.jp: 彼と会う約束をしたけれど、結局、会わないままになってしまった。
examples.tr: I promised to meet him, but in the end we never did meet.

examples.jp: 洗濯物が、ずっと外に干したままになっている。
examples.tr: The laundry has been left hanging outside the whole time.

741.connection: まるで + Nの / V plain form + よう(だ)

examples.jp: 合格した！まるで夢のようだ。
examples.tr: I passed! It's just like a dream.

examples.jp: 彼の日本語はまるで日本人が話しているみたいに聞こえる。
examples.tr: His Japanese sounds just as if a Japanese person were speaking.

examples.jp: あなたの言うことはまるで理解できない。
examples.tr: I can't understand what you're saying at all.

741.explain: Used when you want to compare a thing or action to a high degree, equivalent to something others could hardly imagine or believe.

742.connection: Aい (drop い) + み / Na + み

examples.jp: 丸みを帯びた形・青みを帯びた白・厚みのある板
examples.tr: a rounded shape, white tinged with blue, a board with some thickness

examples.jp: 校長は入学式で毎年同じことを言っている。ぜんぜん新鮮味がない。
examples.tr: The principal says the same thing at the entrance ceremony every year. There's nothing fresh about it at all.

examples.jp: 「お会いできる日を楽しみにしています」
examples.tr: "I'm looking forward to the day I can meet you."

742.explain: Turns certain adjectives into nouns with ～み to express the degree, feeling or nuance of a quality. It cannot be used with every adjective.
742.notes:
1) It is easy to misread ～み as "try doing" (～てみる).
→ Here ～み turns an adjective into a noun to talk about a "feeling/degree..."; it has nothing to do with ～てみる.
2) Not every adjective can take ～み.
→ Only certain fixed adjectives are commonly used (such as 痛み, 苦み...); do not make up your own forms in the exam.
3) Easily confused with ～さ.
→ ～さ is usually used to measure/quantify (height, length...); ～み leans toward perception/sensory quality.

746.connection: V plain form + かも かもしれない かもしれません / N / Na / Aい

examples.jp: もしかすると彼の話はうそかもしれない。
examples.tr: His story might possibly be a lie.

examples.jp: もしかしたら、明日行けないかもしれません。
examples.tr: I might not be able to go tomorrow.

746.explain: Used to describe the speaker's conjecture, often based on intuition

748.meaning: Giving a reason (often like "because...", common among women/children)
748.connection: V plain form + ものだから ものですから もんだから (spoken) / N + な / Na / Aい

examples.jp: 「なぜ遅刻したのですか」「すみません、事故で電車が止まってしまったものですから」
examples.tr: "Why were you late?" "I'm sorry, the train stopped because of an accident."

examples.jp: ふだん健康なものだから、つい過信して過労で倒れてしまった。
examples.tr: Because I'm usually healthy, I was overconfident and ended up collapsing from overwork.

examples.jp: 「父が病気なものですから、いろいろとお金が必要なんです」
examples.tr: "My father is ill, you see, so I need money for all sorts of things."

examples.jp: 「先生とは知らなかったもので、大変失礼いたしました」
examples.tr: "I didn't know you were a teacher, so I'm terribly sorry for being rude."

748.explain: Used to give a subjective reason, as an explanation or excuse. 「もので」 is more polite than 「ものだから」.
748.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～から／～ので.
→ ～ものだから／もので is an explanation that sounds like a justification or excuse; it is subjective.
2) Distinguishing ものだから and もので.
→ もので is usually more neutral/polite; ものだから leans toward spoken language.
3) Not used for objective, formal causes.
→ If the reason is "because of the rules / because of the figures," use ～ため／～ので.

749.meaning: Spoken language expressing an excuse and a reason.

examples.jp: 不便なものですから
examples.tr: because it's inconvenient

examples.jp: 「昨日、来なかったでしょう？」「すみません、急用があったものですから」
examples.tr: "You didn't come yesterday, did you?" "Sorry, something urgent came up."

examples.jp: 友達が遊びに来たものだから、勉強しないで遊んでしまった。
examples.tr: My friend came over to hang out, so I ended up playing instead of studying.

752.name: ～ようだ／～みたいだ（conjecture）
752.meaning:
Expresses conjecture based on what one feels or sees.
［ふつう］　+　ようだ／みたいだ
［N：雨な／N：雨の　+　ようだ」
元気／N：雨　+　みたいだ］
752.connection: V/A plain form + ようだ・みたいだ / Nの/Naな + ようだ / N/Na + みたいだ（conjecture）

examples.jp: 具合が悪いようだ／みたいだ
examples.tr: seems to be unwell

examples.jp: 田中さんは今日は具合が悪いようだ／みたいだ。
examples.tr: Mr. Tanaka seems to be unwell today.

examples.jp: 隣の部屋がうるさい。パーティーをしているようだ／みたいだ。
examples.tr: The room next door is noisy. It looks like they're having a party.

753.meaning: Tried to / was about to... but
753.connection: V volitional form + とした(ら/ところ)（just as one was about to do..., ...）

examples.jp: 家を出ようとしたところ、上司から電話がかかってきた。
examples.tr: Just as I was about to leave the house, I got a call from my boss.

examples.jp: ドアを開けようとしたが、鍵が壊れていて開かなかった。
examples.tr: I tried to open the door, but the lock was broken and it wouldn't open.

examples.jp: 彼に本当のことを言おうとしたが、言えなかった。
examples.tr: I tried to tell him the truth, but I couldn't.

examples.jp: 電車に乗ろうとしたら、財布を忘れたことに気づいた。
examples.tr: Just as I was about to get on the train, I realized I had forgotten my wallet.

examples.jp: 寝ようとした瞬間、隣の部屋がうるさくなった。
examples.tr: The moment I was about to fall asleep, the room next door got noisy.

examples.jp: 帰ろうとしていたところに、急な依頼が入った。
examples.tr: Just as I was about to go home, an urgent request came in.

753.explain:
Used to describe an immediate intention at a past point in time, often together with an interrupting event or an unsuccessful result.
V-ようとしたら／ところ／途端(に): emphasizes surprise, right at the moment of the intended action.
V-ようとしたが／ものの: emphasizes effort that failed.
The form V-ようとしていた: provides the background of "was about to" lasting for a short while.
Not used for long-term plans; use ～つもりだった for plans.

• Meaning 1: "Was about to do ... when ..." — emphasizes the moment just before carrying out the action, with another event intervening.
• Meaning 2: "Tried to do ... (but did not succeed)" — connected with が／ものの to show a result contrary to expectation.
• Meaning 3: The nuance of being "on the verge" — the action almost happened but in the end did not take place or was prevented.
• Analysis: とした is the past of とする, describing an intention at a point in time that has passed; it is often followed by a second clause expressing an obstacle, a contrary result or an unexpected event.
• The subject is usually the speaker or an agent with volition; it is rarely used with inanimate subjects.

rows: Was about to / tried (but did not succeed)
<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>かけようとしたが、<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>。
Not past; the action is ongoing
About to / in the middle of / just did
Three tenses: ところだ／ところに／ところで
Long-term intention, no emphasis on the moment
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くつもりだったが、<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>けなかった。

mistakes: Using it with a non-volitional verb: ×雨が降ろうとした → 〇雨が降り出した／降りそうだった。
Confusing it with ～つもりだった: ～ようとした means "about to, right at that moment," not a plan made in advance.
Omitting the second clause: many sentences need a result/obstacle clause after ～とした to be complete.
Wrong tense: to say "is about to," use ～ようとしている, not ～ようとした.
JLPT: often tests the distinction between としたら (surprise) and としたが (result contrary to expectation).
753.notes:
• With verbs that do not express volition (rain, happen), avoid ～ようとした; use ～ところ／～直前など instead.
• Attaching としたら gives a stronger nuance of surprise than としたところ.
• In narrative writing, ～ようとした瞬間／矢先(に) often appears to build a climax.

examples.jp: 私は赤いやピンクのような、明るい色が好きだ。
examples.tr: I like bright colors like red and pink.

examples.jp: 私も早くリンさんのように、上手に日本語が話せるようになりたい。
examples.tr: I also want to be able to speak Japanese well like Lin soon.

examples.jp: 「私もあなたが着ているようなセーターがほしい」
examples.tr: "I want a sweater like the one you're wearing, too."

examples.jp: アメリカのような大きな国では、国内にも時差があって当然だ。
examples.tr: In a big country like America, it's only natural that there are time differences within the country.

754.explain: Used to compare, give examples or express similarity: like..., similar to.... Often used when describing an image, a situation or a way of doing something.
754.notes:
1) It is easy to confuse the functions of ～ような and ～ように.
→ ～ような comes before a noun; ～ように usually modifies a verb or a clause.
2) Easily confused with ～みたいだ.
→ ～ような／ように is neutral and can be used in written language; ～みたいだ leans toward spoken language.
3) Do not take it to mean "exactly the same."
→ This pattern usually indicates similarity or gives examples. | Also used to give typical examples (例示)

755.name: ～ように（introductory remark・as is known）
755.meaning:
…の内容がすでに知られていると前置きする
An introductory remark saying that the content of ... is already known.

examples.jp: 人間のように、植物にも栄養が必要だ。
examples.tr: Like humans, plants also need nutrients.

examples.jp: 母親が明るい人だったように、その娘たちも性格が明るい。
examples.tr: Just as their mother was a cheerful person, her daughters also have cheerful personalities.

examples.jp: わたしたちはあなたが想像しているような関係ではありませんよ。
examples.tr: We're not in the kind of relationship you're imagining.

examples.jp: 前にも話したように、来週はわたしは日本にいません。
examples.tr: As I told you before, I won't be in Japan next week.

examples.jp: 今朝の新聞に書いてあったように、今年は米のできがいいらしい。
examples.tr: As it said in this morning's paper, the rice harvest seems to be good this year.

examples.jp: ご存じのように、日本は台風が多い国です。
examples.tr: As you know, Japan is a country with many typhoons.

755.notes:
It is also used when instructing others to do something ⏐ examples: 1. 皆様ご存じのように、試験の内容が変わります。
As you all know, the content of the exam will change
2. ここに書いてあるように、今度の木曜日、授業は午前中だけです。
As written here, this coming Thursday there will be classes only in the morning.
3. 前にお話ししたように、来年から授業料が値上がりします。
As I said before, tuition will go up from next year

examples.jp: 健康のために、よく噛んで食べるようにしましょう。
examples.tr: For your health, try to chew your food well when you eat.

examples.jp: エレベーターでは騒がないようにしましょう。
examples.tr: Let's try not to make noise in the elevator.

examples.jp: 約束の時間は守るようにしましょう。
examples.tr: Let's make sure to be on time for appointments.

examples.jp: 目を休めるため、1時間に1回は立ち上がるようにしましょう。
examples.tr: To rest your eyes, try to stand up at least once an hour.

examples.jp: 夜更かしをしないようにしましょう。
examples.tr: Let's try not to stay up late.

examples.jp: 大きな声で挨拶するようにしましょう。
examples.tr: Let's make a point of greeting people in a loud, clear voice.

757.explain:
Has a gentle, polite nuance; more of a guideline/instruction than a command.
Suitable for contexts such as: announcements at a company or school, information signs, speeches.
For an immediate action, "～ましょう/～てください" is more natural. For a long-term habit, use "～ようにしましょう".
The subject is usually an implied "みなさん/私たち" and does not need to be stated.

• The pattern "～ようにしましょう" expresses an appeal/advice to make a steady effort together or build a habit: "Let's try to .../let's be careful to ...".
• Unlike "～ましょう" (just an invitation to do something right now), "～ようにしましょう" focuses on maintaining/paying attention to a principle or repeated behavior.
• The negative form can be used to advise avoiding a behavior: "～ないようにしましょう".
• Often appears in public announcements, rules, health/safety recommendations, classrooms and instruction manuals.

rows: <ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れないようにしてください。
<ruby>早<rt>はや</rt></ruby>く<ruby>寝<rt>ね</rt></ruby>るようにする。
A specific decision, no emphasis on habit
<ruby>明日<rt>あした</rt></ruby>は<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>むことにしましょう。

mistakes: Attaching it directly to a noun is wrong: ×健康ようにしましょう → ○健康に気をつけるようにしましょう。
Using it for an immediate action sounds awkward: ×ドアを閉めるようにしましょう（right now） → ○ドアを閉めましょう。
Confusing it with "～ようにする": the latter describes one's own habit, not an appeal to others.
757.notes:
• The negative form "～ないようにしましょう" is very common in safety/work contexts: 転ばないようにしましょう。
• When the goal is "to become able to do," use the potential form: 毎日少しずつ読んで、新聞が読めるようにしましょう。
• In long-term guidance, add "～ていきましょう" to emphasize the process: 省エネを続けていくようにしましょう。

759.connection: Vる/V potential form + ようになった

examples.jp: 毎日練習して、ピアノが弾けるようになった。
examples.tr: I practiced every day, and now I can play the piano.

examples.jp: 年を取って、早起きするようになった。
examples.tr: As I've gotten older, I've started getting up early.

examples.jp: スマホを見ながら歩かないようになった。
examples.tr: I no longer walk while looking at my smartphone.

examples.jp: 自動で電気が消えるようになっている。
examples.tr: The lights are designed to turn off automatically.

examples.jp: この町は観光客が増えるようになってきた。
examples.tr: This town has gradually come to see more tourists.

examples.jp: 眼鏡を替えて、小さい文字も読めるようになった。
examples.tr: After changing my glasses, I can now read even small print.

759.explain:
More natural and objective than "～ようにする" (intentional action). Emphasizes the result of a change that has taken place.
Used to report growth, progress or a change of habit.
For natural phenomena/designs, use "～ようになっている" instead of "～ようになった".

• Expresses a "change of state" over time: from not doing → starting to do; from not being able → being able.
• Emphasizes the result achieved after a process, often due to circumstances/practice/outside influence.
• Negative form: "Vないようになった" = stopped/no longer does (change of habit).
• "～ようになっている" describes a mechanism/design that leads to a certain result.

rows: An effort; the state may not have changed yet
<ruby>毎日<rt>まいにち</rt></ruby><ruby>走<rt>はし</rt></ruby>るようにする。
<ruby>毎日<rt>まいにち</rt></ruby><ruby>走<rt>はし</rt></ruby>るようになった。
<ruby>転勤<rt>てんきん</rt></ruby>することになった。
Natural/degree, no emphasis on a goal
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>降<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>らなくなった。
Change of habit due to awareness/circumstances
<ruby>酒<rt>さけ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>飲<rt>の</rt></ruby>まないようになった。

mistakes: Confusing it with "～ようにする": that one is effort; "～ようになった" is the result of a change.
Using it for unconscious natural phenomena: prefer ～なくなった over ～ないようになった when there is no element of control.
Do not attach it directly to adjectives: ×きれいようになった → ○きれいになった。
759.notes:
• Ability: 走れる/話せる/見られる + ようになった expresses "have become able to ..." after practice.
• With devices/procedures: ～ように（自動で）なる/なっている states the intended mechanism/design.
• Avoid attaching it directly to adjectives to say "became ...ようになった": use ～く/～に なってきた/なった. Example: ×暑いようになった → ○暑くなってきた。

760.meaning:
Expresses what one perceives. Also used to state one's own opinion gently.
［ふつう］　+　ように　+　感じる／見える／思う
［Na：元気な　N：子供の］
760.connection: V/A plain form + ように感じる

examples.jp: これ以上の部屋はないように感じた
examples.tr: I felt there couldn't be a better room than this.

examples.jp: 彼は大学を卒業してから少し変わったように感じる。
examples.tr: I feel he has changed a little since graduating from college.

examples.jp: この服を着ると、太っているように見える。
examples.tr: When I wear these clothes, I look fat.

examples.jp: こちらの色のほうがいいように思いますが．．．。
examples.tr: I think this color might be better...

761.name: ～ように（like／as）
761.meaning: So that..., in order to... (achieve a state/purpose)

examples.jp: 子どもは親の思うようにはならないのがふつうだ。
examples.tr: It's normal for children not to turn out the way their parents want.

examples.jp: 「皆さん、今から私が言うように体を動かしてください。」
examples.tr: "Everyone, please move your body as I tell you from now on."

examples.jp: 「この本にも書いてあるように、世界のあちこちで水不足が大きな問題になっています」
examples.tr: "As this book also says, water shortages are becoming a serious problem in many parts of the world."

examples.jp: 「先日お話しましたように、佐藤さんが転勤することになったので、来週、送別会を開きたいと思います」
examples.tr: "As I mentioned the other day, Mr. Sato is being transferred, so I'd like to hold a farewell party next week."

examples.jp: ９時の新幹線に間に合うように、８時に家を出た。
examples.tr: I left home at 8 so that I would make the 9 o'clock shinkansen.

examples.jp: 母は家族が快適に暮らせるよう、いろいろと気を配っている。
examples.tr: My mother takes care of all sorts of things so that the family can live comfortably.

761.explain:
Used to compare or to cite content: "like..., as...".
Expresses a purpose of achieving some result: "so that...".

Like / as ...
In order to achieve a purpose ...
761.notes:
1) It is easy to confuse the many meanings of ～ように.
→ It has the meaning "like/as" and the meaning "so that (purpose)".
2) Look at the second clause to decide.
→ If the second clause is an action/instruction: it is usually the purpose meaning.
→ If it is a comparison/citation of content: it is the "like/as" meaning.
3) Easily confused with ～ために.
→ ～ように is often used when the purpose concerns an ability/result to be achieved; ～ために is usually more direct.

764.connection: Vる → V passive form + た (噛まれた・褒められた)

examples.jp: 犬に手を噛まれた。
examples.tr: I was bitten on the hand by a dog.

examples.jp: 先生に褒められた。
examples.tr: I was praised by my teacher.

examples.jp: 昨日はぐっすり寝られた。
examples.tr: I was able to sleep soundly last night.

examples.jp: 社長が会議に来られた。
examples.tr: The company president came to the meeting. (keigo)

examples.jp: 急な雨に降られた。
examples.tr: I got caught in a sudden rain shower.

examples.jp: となりの人にずっと話しかけられた。
examples.tr: The person next to me kept talking to me the whole time.

764.explain:
Passive: neutral or with a nuance of disadvantage/annoyance depending on the context.
Past potential: only natural with Group 2 verbs and 来る（来られた）; Group 1 verbs use ～えた (書けた,行けた), not ～られた.
Passive keigo: formal, used for superiors/customers. Consider using special honorific forms:召し上がった, いらっしゃった.

• Past passive: The action has happened; the subject is the person/thing affected. Example: 先生に注意された。
• Past potential (Group 2/来る): Expresses "was able to ..." (could sleep, could see). Example: よく見られた（=見える/見られるの過去）.
• Passive keigo: Shows respect for the person doing the action. Example: 部長はもうお帰りになられた／帰られた。
• Adversative passive: Expresses annoyance caused by a behavior/phenomenon. Example: 隣で大声で歌われた。

rows: <ruby>先生<rt>せんせい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>叱<rt>しか</rt></ruby>られる。
Formal; avoids ambiguity with the passive
<ruby>社長<rt>しゃちょう</rt></ruby>はお<ruby>帰<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>りになった。
<ruby>残業<rt>ざんぎょう</rt></ruby>させられた。

mistakes: Confusing the Group 1 potential: ×行られた → ○行けた.
Missing the agent marker に in the passive: ×先生を叱られた → ○先生に叱られた.
Confusing it with keigo: "来られた" can be keigo, not passive. Use the subject to tell them apart.
Using から to mark the agent: ×先生から褒められた → ○先生に褒められた（によって is also correct but more formal/academic）.
764.notes:
• The agent in the passive is usually marked with に; when emphasizing the means/cause, use によって/で: 風に吹かれた／台風によって家が壊された。
• "見られた" can mean "was seen" (passive) or "was able to see" (potential of 一段). Context is needed to tell them apart.
• The adversative passive can be used with natural phenomena: 雪に降られた, 風に吹かれた.

765.name: ～れる／られる（spontaneous）
765.connection: Group 1: V (a-row) + れる / Group 2: Vます(drop ます) + られる / する → される / 来る → こられる

examples.jp: この歌を聞くと、子どものころのことが思い出される。
examples.tr: Whenever I hear this song, I can't help remembering my childhood.

examples.jp: 国から送られてきた荷物を見ると、母のことが思われる。
examples.tr: When I see the package sent from home, I find myself thinking of my mother.

examples.jp: 田舎で一人暮らしをしている祖母のことが案じられる。
examples.tr: I can't help worrying about my grandmother, who lives alone in the countryside.

examples.jp: 妹の病気は現代医学では治すことが難しいそうだ。新薬の完成が待たれる。
examples.tr: I hear my younger sister's illness is hard to cure with modern medicine. Everyone is eagerly awaiting the completion of a new drug.

765.explain: Expresses emotions, thoughts or actions that arise naturally, unintentionally.
765.notes:
1) Easily confused with the ordinary passive (someone has something done to them by someone).
→ Here ～れる／られる expresses emotions/thoughts that arise naturally (spontaneously), with no emphasis on the agent.
2) Often used with verbs such as 思われる・思い出される.
→ It means "can't help feeling/remembering/worrying...".
3) Not used to describe a specific harm suffered.
→ If there is a clear agent (A does B), use the ordinary passive.

examples.jp: 彼は年齢のわりには若く見える。
examples.tr: He looks young for his age.

examples.jp: 初めてのわりには、うまくできたね。
examples.tr: You did well for a first time.

examples.jp: この店は安いわりには量が少ない。
examples.tr: For a cheap restaurant, this place gives small portions.

examples.jp: 日本に長く住んでいるわりには、漢字が読めない。
examples.tr: For someone who has lived in Japan for a long time, I can't read kanji.

examples.jp: 静かな場所であるわりには、集中できない。
examples.tr: Even though it's a quiet place, I can't concentrate.

766.explain:
Place the "standard of comparison" before ～わりには, then give a result/evaluation contrary to expectation in the second clause.
Suitable for both spoken and written language; "であるわりには" is more formal.
Often carries a slight nuance of criticism/surprise; avoid putting a command/volitional expression (～しなさい、～ましょう) right after it.
The sense of contrast can be emphasized with a following connective: ～わりには、意外と／案外／思ったより…

- Expresses an evaluation that is "out of proportion/different from expectation" based on a stated standard. Translation: "considering...", "for...", "and yet".
- Nuance: normally standard A would be expected to lead to B, but in reality it is C (different, or lower/higher than expected). Often implies surprise, contrary to common sense.
- Mainly used in comments and evaluations. Not used with a direct command/volition right after ～わりには.

rows: Judging by standard A, B is surprising
Close in meaning; ～にしては is usually for a "clear, specific standard"
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもにしてはよく<ruby>頑張<rt>がんば</rt></ruby>った。
Compared with A, the result differs from expectation
The standard can be subjective or based on common sense; used widely
<ruby>値段<rt>ねだん</rt></ruby>のわりには<ruby>質<rt>しつ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>い。
<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているくせに<ruby>教<rt>おし</rt></ruby>えない。
Opposite nuance: the result matches expectations
<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>いだけあって<ruby>品質<rt>ひんしつ</rt></ruby>がいい。

mistakes: Wrong "助詞": writing 子どもわりには × correct: 子どものわりには.
Confusing it with ～だけあって (meets expectations). The JLPT often sets traps by reversing the praise/criticism nuance.
Using it with a command: ～わりには、行きなさい × (avoid). Use a different structure.
Forgetting "な" with な-adjectives: 静かわりには × correct: 静かなわりには.
766.notes:
• Nouns indicating age/experience very often go with ～のわりには: 年齢のわりには／初心者のわりには.
• In conversation, the second part can be omitted if the context is clear: この値段のわりには…（いいね）.
• With quantities: 量／価格／点数／頻度 のわりには…
explain: Expresses a result that differs from the normal degree or way of thinking: "considering..., ...".
examples: 1. 「山田さんは留学経験がないわりに英語の発音がきれいですね」
Yamada has never studied abroad, but his English is good.
2. この仕事は大変なわりに給料が安い。
This job is hard, and yet the pay is low.
3. あのレストランは値段のわりに（＝値段が安いわりに）おいしくて量も多い。
That restaurant is cheap, yet the food is good and the portions are large too.
4. 彼女はやせているわりには丈夫で力も強い。
She is thin but healthy.
5. ＊今度の試験はあまり勉強しなかった。そのわりには成績がまあまあでほっとした。
I didn't study much for this exam. Even so, my results were fairly good, which was a relief. meaning_vi: Even though, despite ⏐ explain: Used when describing or showing a case where a thing or event runs contrary to common sense or what is natural.
Expresses a feeling of surprise, something unexpected ⏐ examples: 1. 年のわりには若く見える。
Despite his age, he still looks young
2. お金がない（と言っている）わりに、よく買い物をするね。
You have no money, and yet you shop a lot

767.connection: V/A plain form + んだもん（spoken language, giving a reason）

examples.jp: 今日は行かない。疲れてるんだもん。
examples.tr: I'm not going today. I'm tired, okay?

examples.jp: 泣いてないよ。目にゴミが入ったんだもん。
examples.tr: I'm not crying. I just got something in my eye.

examples.jp: 遅れちゃった。電車が遅延したんだもん。
examples.tr: Sorry I'm late. The train was delayed, that's why.

examples.jp: いいじゃん、欲しかったんだもん。
examples.tr: So what? I wanted it, okay?

examples.jp: 私、初心者なんだもん。
