examples.tr: I'm a beginner, you know.

767.explain:
Used in casual conversation; avoid it in formal speech or with superiors (except “～んですもの”).
Expresses emotion, sometimes in a childish way; suitable for explaining personal, minor reasons.
Can be combined with “だって” at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize the reason: だって、忙しい んだもん。

- Gives an emotional, casual reason or excuse: “because…”, “it's just that…”.
- Nuance: whiny, defensive, making excuses; often used by women/children, or when the speaker wants to downplay their responsibility.
- Usually comes at the end of a sentence; rarely followed by another clause.

rows: <ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しいから<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>けない。
Neutral; adding “もの” gives a softer nuance

mistakes: Using it with superiors or in formal writing: inappropriate. Switch to ～ので／～から／～んです.
Forgetting “な” with N/na: 便利んだもん × correct: 便利なんだもん。
Confusing its nuance with ～から: the JLPT sets traps with options that do or do not carry a whiny, emotional nuance.
767.notes:
• “もん” is the spoken form of “もの”; “～んだもの” sounds more polite than “～んだもん”.
• When emphasizing annoyance: ～んだもん！ (rising intonation at the end of the sentence).
• In a dialogue, the previous sentence is often a question or reproach; the reply uses ～んだもん to justify oneself. explain: Used to explain a reason with an unhappy, annoyed or disappointed feeling
Common in casual speech ⏐ examples: 1. 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、まずいんだもん。」
“Why aren't you eating?” “Because it tastes awful, that's why.”
2. 今日の試験、できなかった・・・。勉強しなかったんだもん、仕方がない。
I couldn't do today's exam… well, I didn't study, so there's nothing I can do about it.

examples.jp: 今日は残業してください。そのかわり、明日は早く帰っていいですよ。
examples.tr: Please work overtime today. In exchange, you can go home early tomorrow.

examples.jp: 兄は勉強はできない。そのかわりに、スポーツは得意だ。
examples.tr: My older brother isn't good at studying. Instead, he's good at sports.

examples.jp: この店は値段が高い。そのかわり、味は保証できる。
examples.tr: This restaurant is expensive. In return, the taste is guaranteed.

769.explain: A sentence-initial conjunction: it takes the whole first clause as the premise, and the second clause states something that replaces or compensates for it to an equal degree. In meaning it corresponds to ～かわりに, but it stands on its own at the beginning of the following sentence, usually followed by 「、」.

770.name: ～ことだ（advice）
770.meaning: That is to say; you should

examples.jp: 暖かくして、ゆっくり休むことだ。
examples.tr: Keep warm and get plenty of rest.

examples.jp: 無理をしないことです。
examples.tr: You shouldn't overdo it.

770.explain: Used when giving advice about something

772.name: ～ますように（praying for）
772.connection: Vます・Vません・Vれます + ように（praying for）

examples.jp: 合格しますように。
examples.tr: I hope I pass.

examples.jp: 母の病気が治りますように。
examples.tr: I pray my mother recovers from her illness.

examples.jp: インフルエンザにかかりませんように。
examples.tr: I hope I don't catch the flu.

772.explain: Usually used to express hope or a prayer for something

774.meaning: Not even a little, not at all

examples.jp: あの人が話す英語は少しもわからない。
examples.tr: I can't understand that person's English at all.

examples.jp: スタイルのことは、少しも気にならない。
examples.tr: I don't worry about my figure at all.

examples.jp: 日本語は少ししか話せません。
examples.tr: I can only speak a little Japanese.

examples.jp: ピアノは、弾けることは弾けますが、うまくありません。
examples.tr: As for the piano, I can play it, but I'm not good at it.

examples.jp: このバッグ、高いことは高いけれど、すごく使いやすいです。
examples.tr: This bag is expensive, sure, but it's really easy to use.

775.explain: Used when you want to explain or state that the reality is lower, not to the degree the other person thinks

examples.jp: 日本文化について勉強する。
examples.tr: To study Japanese culture.

examples.jp: 「受験についての注意」を読む。
examples.tr: To read "Notes on Taking the Entrance Exam."

778.explain: Used when talking about an action or matter focused on a certain topic

779.name: ～ように（desired result）

examples.jp: ここでたばこを吸わないように。
examples.tr: Do not smoke here.

examples.jp:
「明日はもっと早く来るように。」
「わかりました。」
examples.tr:
"Come earlier tomorrow."
"Understood."

779.explain: Used to request or instruct another person (of lower status) to do something

780.name: ～まで（until）

examples.jp: 映画が始まるまで30分あります。
examples.tr: There are 30 minutes until the movie starts.

examples.jp: 連絡があるまで待っています。
examples.tr: I'll be waiting until I hear from you.

780.explain: Used to describe the end point of something

781.name: ～らしい（typical）

examples.jp: 今日は、春らしい暖かい日でした。
examples.tr: Today was a warm, spring-like day.

examples.jp: 私は女性らしい洋服はあまり着ない。
examples.tr: I don't often wear feminine clothes.

781.explain: Used in spoken language. Used when you want to describe a characteristic you sense in a thing or situation

782.name: ～とく・どく（contracted Vておく）
782.meaning: Do something in advance, do something beforehand

examples.jp: テストで間違ったところを、ノートに書いとこう。
examples.tr: I'll write down in my notebook the parts I got wrong on the test.

examples.jp: これ洗濯しといて。
examples.tr: Wash this for me, will you?

examples.jp: トイレットペーパーがもうすぐなくなるから、買っとかないと。
examples.tr: We're almost out of toilet paper, so I need to buy some.

782.explain:
This is the contracted form of Vておく.
Vておく has 3 meanings:
Preparing something in advance. Taking care of a task. Leaving things as they are.
See also the grammar points that use Vておく: See

783.name: ～(ら)れている（passive）

examples.jp: この本には、くわしい説明は書かれていません。
examples.tr: This book does not contain a detailed explanation.

examples.jp: 入学式は、このホールで行われます。
examples.tr: The entrance ceremony will be held in this hall.

examples.jp: これは、世界でいちばん大きいダイヤモンドだと言われています。
examples.tr: This is said to be the largest diamond in the world.

examples.jp: 昔は、その考えが正しいと思われていた。
examples.tr: In the past, that idea was believed to be correct.

783.explain:
Used to report something that is done by another agent (the agent is hidden)
Talks about things that are widely known.
See also:
Review the conjugation of verbs in the passive form (受身形）：See
Review the grammar points that use the passive form (受身形）：See

784.name: ～上げる・～上がる（completion）

examples.jp: やっとレポートを書き上げた。
examples.tr: I finally finished writing the report.

examples.jp: ケーキが焼き上がりましたよ。
examples.tr: The cake has finished baking.

784.explain: Used to talk about completely finishing or ending a task. Can be used with both intransitive and transitive verbs
784.notes: Distinguish it from あげる for giving and receiving (the ～上げる line)

787.meaning: Tell (someone), ask (someone) to do / not to do something

examples.jp: 田中さんに、私の部屋に来るよう（に）言ってください。
examples.tr: Please tell Tanaka to come to my room.

examples.jp: 妻に、家ではたぼこを吸わないよう（に）言われています。
examples.tr: My wife has told me not to smoke at home.

787.explain:
Used when you want to ask someone to pass on your command to a third party
Or used when relaying a command passed on by someone else

791.name: ～たところ（result・discovery）

examples.jp: 先生に今度のテストの範囲を聞いたところ、10課までだと言われた。
examples.tr: When I asked the teacher what the next test would cover, I was told it goes up to Lesson 10.

examples.jp: 歯が痛いので歯医者さんに行ったところ、ひどい虫歯になっていると言われた。
examples.tr: My tooth hurt, so I went to the dentist, and I was told I had a bad cavity.

791.explain: Used when you want to talk about surprise or the seriousness of a problem after trying to do something

examples.jp: みんなに聞こえるようにもっと大きな声で話してください。
examples.tr: Please speak in a louder voice so that everyone can hear.

examples.jp: 忘れないように、手帳に書いておこう。
examples.tr: I'll write it in my planner so I don't forget.

examples.jp:
家を買うようにために貯金をしている。
働くようにために学校をやめた。
examples.tr:
I'm saving money to buy a house.
I quit school to work.

793.explain:
Used to indicate the purpose of the action performed afterward
Cannot be used with transitive verbs or verbs expressing deliberate action. Usually used with verbs in the potential form or intransitive verbs

794.meaning: Intended to do / not to do something

examples.jp: 昨日は買い物に行きつもりでしたが、頭が痛かったのでずっと家にいました。
examples.tr: I was planning to go shopping yesterday, but I had a headache, so I stayed home the whole time.

examples.jp: お菓子を食べないつもりでしたが、つい食べてしまいました。
examples.tr: I meant not to eat any sweets, but I ended up eating some anyway.

794.explain: Used to talk about a plan or intention to do something in the past that was not carried out afterward

795.meaning: Want someone to do / not to do something for you

examples.jp: あのう、教科書を見せてほしいんですが・・・。
examples.tr: Um, I'd like you to show me the textbook...

examples.jp: あなたに教えてもらいたいことがあります。
examples.tr: There's something I'd like you to teach me.

795.explain: Used when you want to ask someone to do something for you; usually used in the plain form, not formal

798.meaning:
最後まで～し続ける
Do ~ to the end
798.connection: Vます(drop ます) + 通す (やり通す・読み通す)

examples.jp: 自分で決めたことは最後までやり通そう。
examples.tr: Let's see through to the end what we decided ourselves.

examples.jp: 彼は何を聞かれても黙り通した。
examples.tr: No matter what he was asked, he stayed silent throughout.

798.notes: Attaches to verbs expressing a volitional action and expresses the meaning 「最後まで－．する」 (do all the way to the end). (316)

799.meaning: Apparently, it means that, the fact is
799.connection: V plain form + ということだ とのことだ / N + (だ) / Na + (だ) / Aい

examples.jp: 田中さんから電話があって、少し遅れるれるということです。
examples.tr: Tanaka called, and he says he'll be a little late.

examples.jp: 試験の結果は70％、つまり合格ということだ。
examples.tr: The exam result was 70%, which means a pass.

799.explain:
Has 2 main meanings:
– Reporting something heard or read
– Stating a meaning, fact or result that is drawn
The verb can be in the volitional or imperative form

801.meaning:
「～の状態が続いているとき、ずっと…する・ずっと…の状態だ。」～は継続的なことを表す言葉。…継続的なことを表す文。
While state ~ continues, state … is carried out / takes place throughout that time.
~ is a word expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
… is also a sentence expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
「～の状態が続いているとき、 …する・…が起こる。」 ～は継続的なことを表す言葉。…は瞬間的なことを表す文。
While state ~ continues, … is done / … happens.
~ is a word expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
… is a sentence expressing something that happens in a short moment.
801.connection: Vている/Vる/Vない/Nの + 間、…（throughout the period）/ 間に、…（at a point within the period）

examples.jp: お母さんが昼寝をしている間、子供たちはテレビを見ていた。
examples.tr: While their mother was taking a nap, the children were watching TV.

examples.jp: 私が旅行で留守番の間、うちの犬の世話をお願いできないでしょうか。
examples.tr: Could you possibly take care of our dog while I'm away on a trip?

examples.jp: お母さんが昼寝をしている間に、子供たちは遊びに出かけた。
examples.tr: While their mother was taking a nap, the children went out to play.

examples.jp: 私が旅行で留守番の間に、庭に草がたくさん生えてしまった。
examples.tr: While I was away on a trip, a lot of weeds grew in the garden.

802.name: ～の（nominalization）
802.connection: V/Aい plain form + の / Na + な + の（nominalization: いいのを、元気なのが…）

examples.jp: 田中さんに電話するのをすっかり忘れていました。
examples.tr: I completely forgot to call Tanaka.

examples.jp: 日曜日に混んだところへ行くのは、あまり好きではありません。
examples.tr: I don't really like going to crowded places on Sundays.

802.explain:
Used to turn nouns, verbs, adjectives and phrases into a noun phrase
Used in casual, concise contexts

804.meaning: (Verb) all the way… / can't… all; do completely, thoroughly

examples.jp: ご飯の量が多くて、食べ切れないよ。
examples.tr: There's so much rice that I can't eat it all.

examples.jp: 長い小説を、2日間で読み切った。
examples.tr: I read the long novel all the way through in two days.

examples.jp: 疲れ切ったようす。
examples.tr: Looking completely exhausted.

804.explain:
Used when using up something completely, with nothing left over
Conversely, the negative form expresses that the action does not end, or that the action or quality of something goes on
804.notes:
meaning_vi: Do to the finish, completely finish ⏐ examples: 1. この小説はおもしろくて、１日で読み切った。
This novel was so interesting that I read it all in one day.
2. 彼は疲れ切った顔をしている。
He looks completely exhausted.

806.meaning: Be told / be warned / be scolded / be yelled at to do / not to do something
806.connection: V imperative form・Vるな + と + 言われる・注意される・しかられる・怒られる

examples.jp: 医者に酒を飲むなと言われた。
examples.tr: The doctor told me not to drink alcohol.

examples.jp: 先生に、もっと勉強しろと言われた。
examples.tr: My teacher told me to study harder.

examples.jp: 父に、もっと早く帰れと注意された。
examples.tr: My father warned me to come home earlier.

806.explain: Used when reporting a command someone else gave you

807.name: ～まで（even）

examples.jp: この魚は骨まで食べられますよ。
examples.tr: You can eat this fish, bones and all.

examples.jp: あなたまで私を疑うのですか。
examples.tr: Even you doubt me?

807.explain: Used to express surprise at how great or excessive something is

808.meaning: Asking permission to do something yourself.
808.connection: V causative form て + ほしい

examples.jp: 休ませてほしい
examples.tr: I'd like you to let me rest.

examples.jp: この仕事、ぜひ私にやらせてください。
examples.tr: Please do let me handle this job.

examples.jp: 昨日課長に、新しいプロジェクトの仕事をやらせてほしいと訴えた。
examples.tr: Yesterday I appealed to the section chief to let me work on the new project.

examples.jp: 頭が痛いので、今日は会社を休ませてほしいんですが。
examples.tr: I have a headache, so I'd like to take the day off work today, if that's all right.

809.meaning:
「passive」＋「causative」(使役受身) Expresses an unpleasant feeling when you end up in an unwanted situation because of someone's actions or words. Can also express a feeling brought about by some occasion.
【「～される／～（さ）せられる」の作り方】
読まない+　される／せられる→読まされる／読ませられる
見ない+　させられる→見させられる
こない+　させられる→こさせられる
する→させられる
809.connection: Vる → V causative-passive form (待つ→待たされる; group II: 見る→見させられる)

examples.jp: 待たされる
examples.tr: To be made to wait

examples.jp: 兄の下手な歌を聞かされた。
examples.tr: I was made to listen to my older brother's terrible singing.

examples.jp: 子供のときは、毎日、部屋を掃除させられた。
examples.tr: When I was a child, I was made to clean my room every day.

examples.jp: その映画によって、戦争の怖さに気付かされた。
examples.tr: That movie made me realize how frightening war is.

examples.jp: 先生の講演を聞いて、環境問題について考えさせられました。
examples.tr: Listening to my teacher's lecture made me think about environmental issues.

809.explain:
「受身」＋「使役」Expresses an unpleasant feeling when you end up in an unwanted situation because of someone's actions or words. Can also express a feeling brought about by some occasion.
【「～される／～（さ）せられる」の作り方】
V-u：読まない+　される／せられる→読まされる／読ませられる
V-ru：見ない+　させられる→見させられる
V-irr（不規則）：こない+　させられる→こさせられる
する→させられる

810.meaning:
「～という情報を受けて、…。」～はほかの人の話や様子などから分かったこと、…は話者の判断・意志・相手への働きかけの文など。
On receiving information ~ , …
~ is something the speaker has learned from what someone else said or from the actual situation.
… is a sentence expressing the speaker's judgment or intention, or urging the listener to do something.
810.connection: V/A plain form + (の)なら / N/Na + なら（receiving information, then making a judgment）

examples.jp: その箱、もう使わないんですか。使わないなら私にください。
examples.tr: You're not using that box anymore? If you're not using it, please give it to me.

examples.jp: ああ、あしたは雨か。雨ならサイクリングには行けそうもないね。
examples.tr: Oh, it's going to rain tomorrow? If it rains, it doesn't look like we'll be able to go cycling.

examples.jp: その本、読んでしまったのなら私に貸してくれませんか。
examples.tr: That book—if you've finished reading it, could you lend it to me?

examples.jp: この薬は6時間ごとに飲んでください。
examples.tr: Please take this medicine every 6 hours.

examples.jp: オリンピックは4年ごとに開かれる。
examples.tr: The Olympics are held every 4 years.

examples.jp: 会う人ごとに同じ質問をされる。
examples.tr: Everyone I meet asks me the same question.

examples.jp: 困ったときは助け合いましょう。
examples.tr: Let's help each other when we're in trouble.

examples.jp: 二人は将来について話し合った。
examples.tr: The two of them talked together about the future.

examples.jp: 遠慮しないで、意見を出し合ってください。
examples.tr: Don't hold back; please share your opinions with each other.

813.meaning: Does nothing but… (negative description, ばかりで…ない)
813.connection: V plain form + ばかりで / Na / Aい

examples.jp: 彼は文句を言うばかりで、何もしません。
examples.tr: He does nothing but complain and never does anything.

examples.jp: この仕事は大変なばかりで、給料が安い。
examples.tr: This job is nothing but hard work, and the pay is low.

examples.jp: 息子はゲームをするばかりで、手伝ってくれない。
examples.tr: My son does nothing but play games and won't help me.

814.meaning: Not particularly…, not especially… (別に～ない)

examples.jp: 別に用事はありません。
examples.tr: I don't have anything in particular to do.

examples.jp: その映画は別におもしろくなかった。
examples.tr: That movie wasn't particularly interesting.

examples.jp:
A: 怒ってる？
B: 別に怒っていないよ。
examples.tr:
A: Are you mad?
B: No, I'm not particularly mad.

815.meaning: For the first time in (period of time)… (3年ぶりに)
815.connection: [period of time] + ぶりに (3年ぶりに)

examples.jp: 10年ぶりに高校の友だちに会いました。
examples.tr: I met my high school friends for the first time in 10 years.

examples.jp: 3日ぶりに雨がやみました。
examples.tr: The rain stopped for the first time in 3 days.

examples.jp: 1か月ぶりに国の料理を食べました。
examples.tr: I ate food from my home country for the first time in a month.

816.meaning: In the middle of…, throughout… (N中: ちゅう/じゅう)

examples.jp: 会議中ですので、後でかけ直します。
examples.tr: I'm in a meeting, so I'll call you back later.

examples.jp: 今日中にレポートを出してください。
examples.tr: Please submit the report by the end of today.

examples.jp: 夏休み中、ずっとアルバイトをしていました。
examples.tr: I worked part-time throughout the summer vacation.

examples.jp: のどが渇いたので、お茶か何か飲みたいです。
examples.tr: I'm thirsty, so I'd like to drink some tea or something.

examples.jp: ペンか何か書くものはありますか。
examples.tr: Do you have a pen or something to write with?

examples.jp: 週末は映画か何か見に行きませんか。
examples.tr: Would you like to go see a movie or something this weekend?

examples.jp: いろいろ考えたが、結局行かないことにした。
examples.tr: I thought about it a lot, but in the end I decided not to go.

examples.jp: 結局、会議は何も決まらなかった。
examples.tr: In the end, nothing was decided at the meeting.

examples.jp: 急いで行ったが、結局間に合わなかった。
examples.tr: I hurried there, but in the end I didn't make it in time.

examples.jp: 川に飛び込まないでください。
examples.tr: Please don't jump into the river.

examples.jp: 彼は黙って考え込んでいます。
examples.tr: He is silent, lost in thought.

examples.jp: 知らない人が家に入り込んだ。
examples.tr: A stranger got into the house.

820.meaning: Perhaps…, maybe… (もしかしたら～かもしれない)
820.connection: もしかしたら もしかすると + [sentence/clause] + かもしれない

examples.jp: もしかしたら明日は雪が降るかもしれません。
examples.tr: It might snow tomorrow.

examples.jp: もしかしたら彼はもう帰ったのかもしれない。
examples.tr: Maybe he has already gone home.

examples.jp: もしかすると来月日本へ行けるかもしれません。
examples.tr: I might be able to go to Japan next month.

examples.jp: もしも宝くじが当たったら、世界旅行がしたいです。
examples.tr: If I won the lottery, I'd want to travel around the world.

examples.jp: もしも明日雨が降ったら、試合は中止です。
examples.tr: If it rains tomorrow, the game will be canceled.

examples.jp: もしも困ったことがあったら、いつでも連絡してください。
examples.tr: If you ever have any trouble, please contact me anytime.

822.meaning: Re-… (do again one more time: Vます+直す)

examples.jp: 作文の間違いを書き直しました。
examples.tr: I rewrote the mistakes in my composition.

examples.jp: もう一度考え直してください。
examples.tr: Please reconsider it once more.

examples.jp: 電話が遠いので、かけ直します。
examples.tr: I can't hear you well, so I'll call you back.

823.meaning: Try to…, as much as possible (なるべく早く)

examples.jp: なるべく早く返事をください。
examples.tr: Please reply as soon as possible.

examples.jp: なるべく毎日運動するようにしています。
examples.tr: I try to exercise every day if I can.

examples.jp: 甘いものはなるべく食べないでください。
examples.tr: Please avoid eating sweets as much as possible.

824.meaning: Get used to…, be used to…

examples.jp: 日本の生活にもう慣れましたか。
examples.tr: Have you gotten used to life in Japan yet?

examples.jp: 新しい仕事にだんだん慣れてきました。
examples.tr: I've gradually gotten used to my new job.

examples.jp: 朝早く起きるのに慣れていません。
examples.tr: I'm not used to getting up early in the morning.

825.meaning: …, I wonder? (polite question, softens the question)
825.connection: V plain form + のでしょうか んでしょうか / N + な / Na / Aい

examples.jp: この電車は東京駅に止まるのでしょうか。
examples.tr: Does this train stop at Tokyo Station?

867.explain:
Neutral nuance, analytical/objective evaluation.
Suitable for written language, reports and presentations; also natural in conversation when comparing two sides.
Not used with a command/volition in the second clause; focuses on describing facts/characteristics.

• Expresses two opposite sides/a trade-off of the same thing/matter: “on the other hand / conversely”.
• Usually states one advantage together with one disadvantage (or vice versa), keeping the evaluation balanced.
• The subject A of both clauses should be the same, to ensure “two sides of the same target”.

rows: Can compare two different targets; broader scope.
<ruby>都市<rt>とし</rt></ruby>は<ruby>人口<rt>じんこう</rt></ruby>が<ruby>増<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>える<ruby>一方<rt>いっぽう</rt></ruby>で、<ruby>地方<rt>ちほう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>減<rt>へ</rt></ruby>っている。
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>うかわりに、<ruby>夕飯<rt>ゆうはん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>奢<rt>おご</rt></ruby>って。
Contrast between two subjects/aspects; also used in the sense of “toward”.
<ruby>兄<rt>あに</rt></ruby>は<ruby>無口<rt>むくち</rt></ruby>なのに<ruby>対<rt>たい</rt></ruby>して、<ruby>弟<rt>おとうと</rt></ruby>はよく<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>す。
Two sides of the same target
Pros/cons of the same thing, balanced evaluation.
<ruby>便利<rt>べんり</rt></ruby>な<ruby>反面<rt>はんめん</rt></ruby>、<ruby>危険<rt>きけん</rt></ruby>もある。

mistakes: Using it for two different subjects: X 東京は便利な反面、田舎は不便だ → use ～に対して/～一方で instead.
Second clause is a request/volition: X 便利な反面、我慢しましょう → does not fit the descriptive nuance.
Confusing the sequence with a simple “but”: ～が/けれども does not necessarily mean “two sides”.
867.notes:
• When the subjects are different, prefer ～一方で/～に対して over ～反面.
• In formal writing, Nである反面 makes the sentence concise and precise.
• Softer alternatives in conversation: その一方で/でも.
meaning_vi: 「～だが、逆に…の面もある。」あることの対比的な両面を言うときに使う。
~ but conversely there is also the side of…
Used to express two opposite sides of a certain issue.
examples: 1. 都会の生活は面白いことが多い反面、ストレスも多い。
City life has many interesting things, but there is also a lot of stress.
2. 一人旅は気楽な反面、何でも一人でやらなければならないので、不便だ。
Traveling alone is carefree, but it is inconvenient because you have to do everything by yourself.
3. 仕事を辞めて自由な時間が増えた反面、緊張感もなくなってしまった。
Quitting my job gave me more free time, but on the other hand, I also lost the sense of tension I needed. | Also written 半面

examples.jp: 時間さえあれば、手伝います。
examples.tr: As long as I have time, I'll help.

examples.jp: 君さえいれば、怖くない。

868.explain:
Emphasizes a minimum condition, with a slight feeling of “that's enough”.
The original particle of N (が/を/は) is usually omitted before さえ: お金 さえ あれば (you do not say お金 がさえ …).
B can be a command/volition/advice:早く連絡し さえすれば、間に合うよ。
Avoid using it when A and B are logically contradictory (A is the minimum sufficient condition, yet B is a total negation).

• “As long as … then …”; emphasizes a minimum condition; when it is met, the desired result will occur.
• “さえ” means “even/only need”; combined with “～ば” it forms a minimum sufficient condition.
• V-てさえいれば emphasizes a state that has been secured in advance or throughout a period of time.
• Used in inference, advice and stating principles; B usually does not contradict A.

rows: As long as A, then B
<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>さえすれば<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>する。
Describes a means, not a condition
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>降<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>れば<ruby>中止<rt>ちゅうし</rt></ruby>。
～さえあれば vs ～さえすれば
N when the condition is existence; V when the condition is an action
<ruby>時間<rt>じかん</rt></ruby>さえあれば／<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>さえすれば

mistakes: Keeping the original particle: お金がさえあれば × → お金さえあれば ✓
Confusing it with “さえ” meaning “even”, which does not go with “ば”: 彼さえ来た（even he came）≠ a condition.
Using it with an adjective without “ある/状態”: 高いさえあれば × → 安くさえあれば（with ある）.
B contradicts A: お金さえあれば、買わない × (illogical) → お金さえあれば、買える ✓
868.notes:
• Irregular verbs: する→しさえすれば；来る→来さえすれば（きさえすれば）.
• V-てさえいれば is suitable when the condition needs to be maintained over time: 連絡してさえいれば安心だ。
• If you want to emphasize “it is very unlikely to happen without A”, you can add さえ: これさえあれば十分だ。
meaning_vi: Indicates that if a condition is met, that alone is enough.
examples: 1. ①　熱さえ下がれば
As long as the fever goes down...
2. ②　恋人の声さえ聞ければと思って、電話をした。
I called just to hear my partner's voice.
3. ③　あの問題さえわかれば、合格したと思う。
I think I would have passed if only I had understood that question.
4. ➃　だれかに道を聞きさえすれば、間に合ったのに。
If only I had asked someone the way, I would have made it in time.
meaning_vi: 「～が実現すれば、それだけで…が実現する。」「～さえ～ば（なら）」は…が成り立つための必要最低限の条件を示す。
If ~ is realized, then with that alone … will be realized.
～さえ～ば（なら） indicates the minimum condition that needs to be met…
examples: 1. 太郎は漫画さえ読んでいれば退屈しないようだ。
Taro seems not to get bored as long as he is reading manga.
2. 体さえ丈夫ならどんなことにも挑戦できる。
As long as you are physically healthy, you can take on any challenge.
3. 一言「ごめんなさい。」と言いさえすれば、相手は許してくれるだろう。
As long as you just say 「I'm sorry.」, the other person will probably forgive you.
meaning_vi: それだけで→後(うし)ろのことが成立(せいりつ)する
As long as, if only
examples: 1. あとは肉さえ焼けば、夕食の準備は終わりだ。
Now all that's left is to grill the meat, and dinner will be ready.
2. あの子は暇さえあればいつも本を読んでいる。
That child is always reading whenever there is free time.
3. 元気さえ良かったら、山頂までいきたっかたのだが・・・・・。
If only the weather had been good, I would have wanted to go up to the summit...
4. この国では、まじめに働きさえすれば生活に困ることはない。
In this country, as long as you work hard, you will not have trouble making a living.
5. あなたと私が黙ってさえいれば（/黙っていさえすれば）、このことはだれにもわからないだろう。
As long as you and I keep quiet, no one will find out about this.
6. 道が込んでさえいなければ10分ぐらいで着くだろう。
As long as the roads aren't congested, we'll get there in about 10 minutes.
7. 「あまり辛いさえなければ何でもいただきます」
As long as it isn't too spicy, I can eat anything.
8. 「体が丈夫でさえあれば、もっと働きたいですが」
If only I were physically healthy, I would like to work more, but...
9. このコンテストは、２０歳以上でさえあればだれでも参加できる。
Anyone can enter this contest as long as they are 20 or older.
explain: Expresses that as long as there is ～, the following state will be established.
examples: 1. 携帯電話を買った。これさえあれば、時計もカメラもいらない。
I bought a cell phone. As long as I have this, I need neither a watch nor a camera.
2. この薬を飲みさえすれば、すぐに治ります。
As long as you take this medicine, you'll get better right away.

869.meaning: Perhaps because…, probably due to… (せいか)
869.connection: V/A plain form + せいか / Nの/Naな + せいか

examples.jp: 年のせいか、最近疲れやすい。
examples.tr: Maybe it's my age, but I get tired easily these days.

examples.jp: 寝不足のせいか、頭が痛い。
examples.tr: Probably from lack of sleep, I have a headache.

examples.jp: 雨が降ったせいか、今日は客が少ない。
examples.tr: Perhaps because it rained, there are few customers today.

870.meaning: If you ask whether… (actually, not necessarily); the reason is that

examples.jp: 日本人はみんな漢字が得意かというと、そうでもない。
examples.tr: If you ask whether all Japanese people are good at kanji, that's not really the case.

examples.jp: なぜ彼が選ばれたかというと、経験が豊富だからだ。
examples.tr: The reason he was chosen is that he has a lot of experience.

examples.jp: 高いものがいつもいいかというと、そうとは限らない。
examples.tr: If you ask whether expensive things are always good, that is not necessarily so.

871.meaning: On a par with…, along with…

examples.jp: 京都は奈良と並んで、古い歴史のある町だ。
examples.tr: Kyoto, along with Nara, is a city with a long history.

examples.jp: 富士山は桜と並んで、日本の象徴と言われている。
examples.tr: Mount Fuji, along with cherry blossoms, is said to be a symbol of Japan.

examples.jp: サッカーは野球と並んで人気のあるスポーツです。
examples.tr: Soccer, along with baseball, is a popular sport.

examples.jp: 相手のレベルに合わせて話し方を変えます。
examples.tr: I change the way I speak to match the other person's level.

examples.jp: 音楽に合わせて踊りましょう。
examples.tr: Let's dance to the music.

examples.jp: 自分に合った仕事を見つけたい。
examples.tr: I want to find a job that suits me.

873.meaning: Corresponds to…, is… (彼は私のおじに当たる)

examples.jp: 彼は私の母の弟、つまりおじに当たります。
examples.tr: He is my mother's younger brother, which makes him my uncle.

examples.jp: 今年は創立50年に当たる。
examples.tr: This year marks the 50th anniversary of the founding.

examples.jp: 彼が合格したのは言うまでもない。
examples.tr: Needless to say, he passed.

examples.jp: 健康が大切なのは言うまでもありません。
examples.tr: It goes without saying that health is important.

examples.jp: 練習が必要なのは言うまでもないことだ。
examples.tr: It goes without saying that practice is necessary.

875.connection: N + となっている / [rule・state] + となっている

examples.jp: この建物では、館内は禁煙となっています。
examples.tr: In this building, smoking is not permitted on the premises.

examples.jp: 申し込みの締め切りは今月末となっています。
examples.tr: The application deadline is the end of this month.

examples.jp: 入場料は大人500円となっております。
examples.tr: Admission is 500 yen for adults.

examples.jp: 電車とバスでは、前者は速いが、後者は安い。
examples.tr: Of trains and buses, the former are fast, while the latter are cheap.

examples.jp: AプランとBプランがあるが、前者は料金が高く、後者はサービスが少ない。
examples.tr: There are Plan A and Plan B; the former is expensive, and the latter offers fewer services.

examples.jp: 漢字とひらがなでは、前者は中国から伝わり、後者は日本で作られた。
examples.tr: Of kanji and hiragana, the former came from China, and the latter was created in Japan.

877.connection: 必ずしも + V/A/N plain form + ～ない（とは限らない・わけではない）

examples.jp: 高いものが必ずしもいいとは限らない。
examples.tr: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

examples.jp: 有名な大学を出ても、必ずしも成功するわけではない。
examples.tr: Even if you graduate from a famous university, it doesn't necessarily mean you will succeed.

examples.jp: 彼の意見が必ずしも正しいとは言えない。
examples.tr: You can't say that his opinion is necessarily right.

878.meaning: …point, in terms of… (この点, ～という点で)
878.connection: V plain form + 点 / Nの点 / Naな点 / Aい点 / ～という点で

examples.jp: その計画は費用の点で問題がある。
examples.tr: That plan has problems in terms of cost.

examples.jp: 安全だという点で、この車は評価が高い。
examples.tr: In terms of safety, this car is highly rated.

examples.jp: 二つの案は、時間がかかる点が同じだ。
examples.tr: The two proposals are the same in that they both take time.

examples.jp: まず第一に、健康が大切だ。
examples.tr: First of all, health is important.

examples.jp: 第一に安全、第二にスピードを考えてください。
examples.tr: Please think about safety first and speed second.

examples.jp: 行きたくないし、第一、お金がない。
examples.tr: I don't want to go, and besides, I have no money.

880.meaning: Suffix 型: type, form, size… (最新型)

examples.jp: 最新型のスマホを買いました。
examples.tr: I bought the latest model of smartphone.

examples.jp: 私の血液型はA型です。
examples.tr: My blood type is A.

examples.jp: この工場では小型の機械を作っている。
examples.tr: This factory makes small machines.

881.meaning: Has… (classical Japanese, old form of ある in written language/advertisements)
881.connection: N + あり（classical Japanese: 経験あり・条件あり）

examples.jp: 「経験あり」の人を募集しています。
examples.tr: We are looking for people with "experience".

examples.jp: このアパートは駐車場ありで便利だ。
examples.tr: This apartment is convenient because it has parking.

examples.jp: 条件ありのセールなので、よく読んでください。
examples.tr: This sale has conditions, so please read carefully.

examples.jp: 天気が試合の結果を左右することもある。
examples.tr: Sometimes the weather influences the outcome of a game.

examples.jp: 第一印象がその後の関係を左右する。
examples.tr: First impressions determine the relationship that follows.

examples.jp: この決断が会社の将来を左右するだろう。
examples.tr: This decision will probably determine the company's future.

883.meaning: To be careful of…, watch out for…

examples.jp: 車に気をつけてください。
examples.tr: Please watch out for cars.

examples.jp: 健康に気をつけて、頑張ってください。
examples.tr: Take care of your health and do your best.

examples.jp: 言葉づかいに気をつけなさい。
examples.tr: Watch your language.

884.meaning: I'm afraid ~, there is a risk of ~ | Indicates the possibility that something bad may happen

examples.jp: 明日は午後から激しい雨が降るおそれがあります。
examples.tr: There is a risk of heavy rain from tomorrow afternoon.

examples.jp: 火事になるおそれがあるので、窓のそばにペットルを置かないでください。
examples.tr: There is a risk of fire, so please do not put plastic bottles by the window.

examples.jp: この薬は副作用のおそれがあるので注意しなければならない。
examples.tr: This medicine may cause side effects, so you must be careful.

examples.jp: 出席率が悪いと、ビザの更新ができない恐れがある。
examples.tr: If your attendance rate is poor, there is a risk you won't be able to renew your visa.

examples.jp: 風が強く、火事が広がる恐れがあったので、付近の住民は避難した。
examples.tr: The wind was strong and there was a risk of the fire spreading, so residents in the area evacuated.

examples.jp: 警察は、犯人はすでに国外へ逃亡した恐れがあると見ている。
examples.tr: The police believe the criminal may have already fled the country.

884.explain: Expresses the possibility that a bad result may occur in the future; usually used in written language or announcements.

rows: <ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>中止<rt>ちゅうし</rt></ruby>の<ruby>恐<rt>おそ</rt></ruby>れがある。
Vます<ruby>語幹<rt>ごかん</rt></ruby>+かねない; subjective, also used in conversation
そんな<ruby>発言<rt>はつげん</rt></ruby>は<ruby>誤解<rt>ごかい</rt></ruby>を<ruby>招<rt>まね</rt></ruby>きかねない。
Not necessarily negative, little warning nuance
<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>する<ruby>可能<rt>かのう</rt></ruby><ruby>性<rt>せい</rt></ruby>がある。
<ruby>延期<rt>えんき</rt></ruby>の<ruby>恐<rt>おそ</rt></ruby>れはない。

mistakes: Using it for a positive result → Wrong nuance. Use 可能性がある for neutral/positive.
Attaching it directly to an adjective → Incorrect. It must be Vる or Nの.
Using it in casual speech → Sounds too stiff. Change to ～かもしれない when appropriate.
Confusing it with ～かねない: ～恐れがある is more formal/objective; ～かねない carries a subjective, emotional evaluation.
884.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～かもしれない.
→ ～おそれがある means “I'm afraid/there is a risk of”, a more serious degree.
2) Usually used in written language, announcements and warnings.
→ Often seen in news and safety documents.
3) Not used for minor matters or mild personal feelings.
→ If it is just a subjective worry, use another pattern depending on the context.
meaning_vi: There is a possibility that…, I'm afraid that…
explain: Formal style, used a lot in official announcements, newspapers, warning signs and safety instructions.
The second clause is usually a warning, request or advisory: ～ので注意してください／～を控えてください／～が見込まれます など.
Not used in everyday small talk; instead use ～かもしれない to talk about possibility in a neutral, casual way.
Can be combined with degree adverbs:十分に/強く/大いに +恐れがある (strong emphasis).
Negating the risk: ～恐れはない (affirming there is nothing to worry about).
examples: 1. 大雨の影響で、川が氾濫する恐れがある。
Due to heavy rain, there is a risk of the river flooding.
2. この薬は眠気を催す恐れがあるため、運転は控えてください。
This medicine may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving.
3. 個人情報が第三者に漏れる恐れがあるため、速やかにパスワードを変更してください。
There is a risk of personal information leaking to third parties, so change your password immediately.
4. 設備の老朽化により、稼働を続けると事故の恐れがある。
Due to aging equipment, there is a risk of an accident if operation continues.
5. 地震の際は、落下物でけがをする恐れがあるので、机の下に避難してください。
During an earthquake, there is a risk of injury from falling objects, so take shelter under a desk.
6. 今回の遅れは全体のスケジュールに影響を及ぼす恐れがある。
This delay may affect the entire schedule. meaning_vi: There is a worry that　～, I'm afraid ～ ⏐ explain: Expresses that a situation is heading in a bad direction.
Formal sentence. ⏐ examples: 1. 地震の際には、窓ガラスが割れたり壁が倒れたりする恐れがある。
During an earthquake, I'm afraid window glass may break and walls may collapse.
2. 台風１９号は今夜、四国に上陸の恐れがあります。
I'm afraid Typhoon No. 19 may make landfall on Shikoku tonight.

examples.jp: 今週はいつものテストに加えてレポート提出もあり、とても忙しい。
examples.tr: This week, in addition to the usual test, I also have a report to hand in, so I'm very busy.

examples.jp: キムさんの作文は文法の間違いが少ないことに加え、主張がはっきりしていて読みやすい。
examples.tr: Kim's essay has few grammar mistakes, and on top of that, its argument is clear, so it's easy to read.

examples.jp: 日本経済は原油の値上がりに加え、急激な円高で低迷している。
examples.tr: In addition to rising crude oil prices, the Japanese economy is stagnating due to the sudden rise of the yen.

examples.jp: ３月に電車賃が値上がりしたが、それに加え、４月からはバス代が値上がりするそうだ。
examples.tr: Train fares went up in March, and in addition to that, I hear bus fares will go up from April.

examples.jp: アルバイトに加えて
examples.tr: In addition to my part-time job

examples.jp: 土曜日は、アルバイトに加えて、ボランティア活動もしている。
examples.tr: On Saturdays, in addition to my part-time job, I also do volunteer work.

885.explain: Expresses "besides A, there is also B". Usually used to add one more element; common in written language.
885.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～だけでなく／～ばかりでなく.
→ ～に加えて means "on top of that", with the nuance of adding an element; often used in written language.
2) Order of meaning.
→ State A first, then "B as well" (B is the added part).
3) Not "increasing over time".
→ It only adds one more element; it does not express change.
meaning_vi: In addition, on top of… (に加えて)

886.meaning:
Conjecture about the actions of a person you know well.
彼女　+　のことだから

examples.jp: 「春木さんがまだ来てないです」「まあ、彼女のことだから、心配ないよ」
examples.tr: "Haruki hasn't come yet." "Well, knowing her, there's nothing to worry about."

examples.jp: 「これ、原さんに訳してもらったら？」「こうだね。英語が得意な彼女のことだから、1時間もあれば、できるだろうね」
examples.tr: "Why not have Hara translate this?" "Good idea. She's good at English, so she could probably do it in an hour."

examples.jp: 健太君のことだから
examples.tr: Knowing Kenta, ...

examples.jp: まじめな田中さんのことだから、宿題はきちんとやってくるだろう。
examples.tr: Tanaka is a serious person, so he'll probably do his homework properly.

examples.jp: 健太君のことだから、また約束を忘れちゃったんじゃないかな。
examples.tr: Knowing Kenta, I bet he forgot his promise again.

886.explain:
Position: almost always at the beginning of the sentence, stating the basis.
Target: a noun referring to a person, group of people or organization the speaker is familiar with.
Nuance: conjecture based on someone's nature; can be praise, criticism or tolerance.
Not used with a clause/verb directly before のことだから; it must be a noun.
Usually not used in affirmative sentences about a past event already known for certain; better suited to conjecture/characterization.

rows: <ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby><ruby>家<rt>か</rt></ruby>だけに、<ruby>期待<rt>きたい</rt></ruby>も<ruby>大<rt>おお</rt></ruby>きい。
Praise based on what has actually been seen
プロだけあって、<ruby>上手<rt>じょうず</rt></ruby>だ。
やるからには<ruby>最後<rt>さいご</rt></ruby>まで。
A conclusion; can follow のことだから
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>のことだから、<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>するに<ruby>違<rt>ちが</rt></ruby>いない。
<ruby>来週<rt>らいしゅう</rt></ruby>の<ruby>予定<rt>よてい</rt></ruby>のことだ。

mistakes: Used for an event already confirmed: × 彼のことだから、昨日来た。 → ◯ 彼のことだから、昨日も来たに違いない。
Attached to a verb: × 来るのことだから → ◯ 彼が来る人柄を前提に言うなら別表現。
Applied to inanimate things: × 天気のことだから → Unnatural; use 〜ので／〜から。
Missing the conjecture clause after it: a main clause expressing evaluation/conjecture is needed.
886.notes:
meaning_vi: Because (of their character/traits)…
examples: 1. 田中さんのことだから、きっと間に合うだろう。
Knowing Tanaka, he'll surely make it in time.
2. 子どものことだから、これくらいのけんかはすぐ忘れるよ。
They're children, so they'll soon forget a little quarrel like this.
3. 彼女のことだから、準備はもう終わっているに違いない。
Knowing her, she must have finished preparing already.
4. あの会社のことだから、対応も迅速だと思う。
Knowing that company, I think they'll respond quickly too.
5. 彼のことだから、言い訳なんてしないさ。
Knowing him, he won't make excuses.
6. 新入社員のことだから、最初は失敗して当然だ。
They're new employees, so it's natural to make mistakes at first.
7. あの二人のことだから、また仲直りするはずだよ。
Knowing those two, they'll surely make up again.

887.meaning: Has a certain…, there is something…

examples.jp: 彼の演説には人を引きつけるものがある。
examples.tr: There is something captivating about his speeches.

examples.jp: あの映画には心に響くものがある。
examples.tr: There is something about that movie that touches the heart.

examples.jp: その判断にはどこか納得しがたいものがある。
examples.tr: There is something about that decision that is hard to accept.

examples.jp: この写真には懐かしいものがある。
examples.tr: There is something nostalgic about this photo.

examples.jp: 最近のAIの進歩には目を見張るものがある。
examples.tr: The recent progress of AI is truly remarkable.

examples.jp: 彼の物言いには冷たいものがある。
examples.tr: There is something cold about the way he talks.

887.explain:
Emphasizes a subjective impression that still has an intuitive basis; suited to mildly objective commentary.
Often paired with emotion-evoking phrases:心に響く/胸を打つ/考えさせられる/印象深い/重みがある/迫力がある.
Rarely used for intention/future; it mainly describes an existing quality/impression.

• Expresses an impression/evaluation that is hard to put clearly, like "there is something …; somewhat …; has a … quality".
• Often used in commentary, reviews and news: 〜には目を見張るものがある, 〜には疑問を感じさせるものがある.
• Sounds neutral to positive, but can also be used for mild criticism.

rows: <ruby>切<rt>せつ</rt></ruby>なさのある<ruby>映画<rt>えいが</rt></ruby>だ＝<ruby>切<rt>せつ</rt></ruby>なさを<ruby>感<rt>かん</rt></ruby>じさせるものがある
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>頑固<rt>がんこ</rt></ruby>なところがある
Mild degree, leans toward a temporary state
<ruby>損<rt>そん</rt></ruby>したような<ruby>気<rt>き</rt></ruby>がする

mistakes: Confused with "〜ところがある": ものがある is more abstract; test questions set traps by swapping in abstract adjectives.
Wrong form of the na-adjective: × 静かなものがある → ✓ 静かなものがある.
Used for volition/commands → does not fit: × 早く行くものがある.
887.notes:
• Common collocations: 説得力があるものがある, 奥深いものがある, 無理がある（note: "無理がある" is a different fixed pattern; ものがある is not used here）.
• In headlines/articles: 「〜には〜ものがある」 creates a nuance of expert commentary.

888.meaning: On the occasion of…, thanks to…

examples.jp: 彼女とは、同じパーティーに出たのをきっかけに知り合いました。
examples.tr: I got to know her when we both went to the same party.

examples.jp: たまたま古本屋で本を買ったのをきっかけに、彼の所説を読むようになりました。
examples.tr: Buying a book by chance at a secondhand bookstore was what got me started reading his theories.

888.explain:
◎ A way of talking about something that was started by another event.

Explained in detail in block 411.
mistakes: Explained in detail in block 411.
888.notes:
Explained in detail in block 411.
meaning_vi: Thanks to …, from …
explain: Expresses an event or occurrence acting as the trigger that leads to a subsequent change or development.
examples: 1. 大学入学をきっかけに、一人暮らしを始めた。
When I entered university, I started living on my own.
2. 留学をきっかけに、自国の文化について考えるようになった。
Studying abroad made me start thinking about my own country's culture.
3. 大統領の来日をきっかけにして、日本人の米国に対する関心が深まった。
The president's visit to Japan deepened Japanese people's interest in the United States.
4. ちょっとした事件をきっかけとして、やがて死者が出る暴動へと発展した。
A minor incident soon developed into a riot in which people died.
meaning_vi: On the occasion of…, taking… as a starting point (をきっかけに)
meaning_vi: Taking the opportunity of some event.
explain: Indicates that something started or changed from a chance event.
＊「契機に、契機として、契機にして」　are formal ways of saying 「をきっかけに」
examples: 1. 大学入学をきっかけに引っ越す。
I'm moving when I enter university.
2. 病気をきっかけに酒をやめた。
I quit drinking when I got sick.
3. 卒業を契機に特立する。
I will take my graduation as the opportunity to live independently
4. 昨年の事故を契機として、安全対策が強化された。
Following last year's accident, safety measures were strengthened.

889.meaning: Means "on the basis of ~, based on ~"

examples.jp: この映画は実際にあった事件をもとに作られた。
examples.tr: This movie was made based on a real incident.

examples.jp: 試験の結果をもとに合否を決める。
examples.tr: Pass or fail is decided based on the exam results.

examples.jp: これは１０年前のデータをもとにしたグラフなので、現状とは違っている。
examples.tr: This is a graph based on data from 10 years ago, so it differs from the current situation.

examples.jp: 考古学者は一つの土器の破片をもとにして、古代人の生活を推理する。
examples.tr: Archaeologists infer the lives of ancient people from a single fragment of pottery.

examples.jp: 父の遺産をもとにして商売を始めた。
examples.tr: I started a business with my father's inheritance.

examples.jp: 昔話をもとに（して）
examples.tr: Based on an old folk tale

889.explain: Emphasizes taking an event, data or information as the basis for development.

mistakes: Confused with ～のもとで (under). When a person/organization acts as an "umbrella/supervisor" → you must use ～のもとで/～のもとに.
Choose ～に基づいて when the question has keywords like 規則/法律/基準/指針; if it is data/opinions/素材 → prefer ～をもとに(して).
Dropping "して" in a style that requires clear procedures may be seen as substandard (depending on the administrative context).
889.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～にもとづいて.
→ ～をもとに(して) means "taking … as a basis/material", emphasizing the source used to create/develop something.
2) Often used with creative activities.
→ Example: データをもとに分析する (analyze using data as a basis).
3) Not necessarily "strictly according to rules".
→ If the basis is a rule/standard, ～にもとづいて fits better.
meaning_vi: Based on…, on the basis of…
explain: Used when you want to emphasize the method: "take N as the basis and then proceed…".
Slightly more formal than ～をもとに; often seen in technical, academic and legal texts.
The modifier form 「NをもとにしたN」 is very common in titles, product descriptions and methods.
Not used for the meaning "under (someone's …)/under the condition" (distinguish from ～のもとで/～のもとに).
examples: 1. 衛星画像をもとにして被害範囲を推定した。
The extent of the damage was estimated based on satellite images.
2. 顧客の声をもとにしてサービスを改善する。
Improve services based on customer feedback.
3. 過去の事例をもとにしてガイドラインを作成した。
Guidelines were drawn up based on past cases.
4. 地震記録をもとにして耐震基準が見直された。
Earthquake-resistance standards were revised based on seismic records.
5. 古文書をもとにして当時の暮らしを再現した。
Life at that time was recreated based on old documents.
6. この映画は実在の事件をもとにして制作された。
This movie was produced based on a real incident.

896.explain:
Casual, natural; often used for invitations and suggestions.
Suited to outdoor activities/going somewhere. Rarely used for stationary indoor activities (e.g. 勉強がてら sounds unnatural).
Can combine with volition/suggestion: 〜ましょう/ませんか.

• Meaning: "while doing A, take the opportunity to do B". A is the main activity or the reason for going out; B is the side task.
• Common in conversation; a more natural, everyday nuance than 「かたがた」.
• A is usually an activity of going somewhere/going out: 散歩, 買い物, ドライブ, お茶, 花見, 見物; or Vます expressing an activity: 歩き, 出かけ.
• Implicit order: A takes priority; B is "on the side". For a more neutral expression, use 「ついでに」.

ご<ruby>挨拶<rt>あいさつ</rt></ruby>かたがた<ruby>伺<rt>うかがう</rt></ruby>う
Does not emphasize which one is main

mistakes: Used with a stationary activity (勉強がてら) → unnatural. Use ついでに instead.
Misunderstanding the focus: with 「がてら」 A is primary and B secondary; choosing A/B wrongly easily skews the meaning.
Confusing the style with 「かたがた」: 「がてら」 is not suitable for formal letters.
Forgetting the Vます form when using a verb: you need to drop ます before 「がてら」.
896.notes:
• Choose an N/V expressing an activity of "going out/moving around" so the sentence sounds natural.
• To be polite at work, switch to 「〜かたがた」 or keep 「〜ついでに」.
• If B is as important as A, consider 「ついでに」 to avoid seeming to downplay B.

900.explain:
Placed at the beginning of a sentence of inference; often paired with endings such as ～ということだ／わけだ／ことになる／のね／よね.
Used politely to confirm: "ということは、～という理解でよろしいでしょうか。"
Not used to state a cause; it is used to draw a consequence from information already given.

• "In that case/That means": draws a tentative conclusion based on the information just before.
• Two steps: state the facts (S1) → match a pattern → draw the conclusion (S2).
• Logical nuance; can be used to confirm the speaker's understanding with the listener.

rows: Inference from the facts just before
<ruby>満席<rt>まんせき</rt></ruby>。ということは、<ruby>予約<rt>よやく</rt></ruby><ruby>必須<rt>ひっす</rt></ruby>だ。
Restates the same content; not necessarily a new inference
<ruby>要点<rt>ようてん</rt></ruby>はつまり、<ruby>三<rt>みっ</rt></ruby>つだ。
Emphasizes a transition/end of a section
<ruby>時間切<rt>じかんぎ</rt></ruby>れ。というわけで、<ruby>今日<rt>きょう</rt></ruby>はここまで。
Assumes a condition in order to consider it
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>とすると、<ruby>中止<rt>ちゅうし</rt></ruby>だ。
If that's the case (condition stated by the listener)
<ruby>急<rt>いそ</rt></ruby>ぎということなら、<ruby>今<rt>いま</rt></ruby>やります。

mistakes: Used as a connective of cause → incorrect; it expresses inference/consequence, not a direct reason.
Confused with つまり: if a reading question asks you to "summarize", choose つまり; if it asks you to "infer", choose ということは.
Ignoring the degree of certainty: when the facts are uncertain, だろう／かもしれない is needed after S2.
900.notes:
• Useful in meetings to confirm: "Aということは、Bですね。" to avoid misunderstandings.
• In written language, ということは is usually followed by a general conclusion: ～ということだ／ことになる.
• The certainty of S2 depends on how reliable S1 is; you can add かもしれない／だろう to lower the certainty. explain: Begins a sentence containing a judgment based on grounds from the previous sentence (a). ⏐ examples: 1. 「彼は、まだ来ませんね。ということは、欠席ということですね。」
He still hasn't come, has he? That means he's absent, right?
2. 「私はもうお酒を飲めます。」
「ということは二十歳を過ぎてるんだね。」
I can already drink alcohol. That means you're over 20, right?

902.explain:
The sense of "hardship" is heightened with adverbs:散々／さんざん, いろいろ,長時間,何度も.
It can also be used in spoken language, but suits narrative/argumentative writing.

- Emphasizes that the "long, hard" process contributes to a sense of wasted effort when the outcome is not as hoped.
- Rhetorical effect: evokes feelings of discouragement and fatigue, and adds weight to the conclusion.

905.explain:
Placed after Vます to predict a bad consequence: ～Vます＋ かねない .
Formal style, leaning toward written language/speeches/reports.
Often used with risk-related vocabulary:誤解を招く,問題になる,批判される,破綻する,失う,危険だ.
Not used for the speaker's own volition or own future plans.
Not used for positive results (avoid:成功し かねない ), unless the sentence is ironic.

• Expresses a risk or high possibility of something happening (usually a bad, undesirable result) based on the speaker's judgment.
• Nuance of warning/reminder: “It could lead to…, you know”. It does not mean “cannot” like ～かねる.
• More subjective than おそれがある; it involves evaluation and consideration of the situation.
• Often used in analyses, news and reports: “～しかねない”, “～になりかねない”.
• Not used to talk about one's own ability (it does not mean “can/cannot do”).

There is a possibility/risk of it happening
<ruby>大雨<rt>おおあめ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>土砂<rt>どしゃ</rt></ruby><ruby>災害<rt>さいがい</rt></ruby>のおそれがある

mistakes: Confusing it with ～かねる (cannot do) — the two patterns have opposite meanings and very different pragmatics.
Using it for positive results: wrong nuance. Avoid “この案は成功しかねない”.
Using it for purely objective possibility: choose おそれがある or うる instead.
Subject “I” with the speaker's own volition/action: inappropriate (the pattern evaluates consequences).
905.notes:
• Common phrases: ～になりかねない, ～を招きかねない, ～を失いかねない, ～に見られかねない (could easily be seen as…).
• Often combined with つい, このままでは, 安易に, 軽率な, 不適切な to emphasize the risk.
• The past form is rare (～かねなかった) and sounds stiff; the present ～かねない is preferred for general statements.

906.explain:
Used when you want to refuse/decline politely while saving face.
Often used with verbs of perception/decision:判断する,了承する,承認する,受け入れる,対応する,許可する.
Keigo form: ～いたし かねます (very polite); neutral: ～し かねる .
When giving a reason, it is often combined with ため,都合上,規定により,個人情報につきましては…
If you want to be direct/objective: use できない; if something is merely hard to do: ～にくい／づらい.

• Expresses “cannot/can hardly do” for reasons of circumstances, rules, ethics, authority, or insufficient information.
• Soft nuance that avoids saying “できない” directly; more polite, especially in refusals.
• It does not negate ability. Instead of “don't know how to do it”, it means “it is not convenient/not appropriate/not permitted to do it”.
• The form しかねます is keigo used when dealing with customers/business partners.

<ruby>誤解<rt>ごかい</rt></ruby>を<ruby>招<rt>まね</rt></ruby>きかねない

mistakes: Using ～かねる to mean “not capable”: incorrect. It is a refusal based on one's position, not on ability.
Confusing it with ～かねない (risk): completely different meaning and direction.
Using ～しかねます in casual speech sounds stiff; use できない/むずかしいです in everyday conversation.
Leaving out the accompanying reason/circumstances makes the sentence sound abrupt: give the reason with ので／ため／都合上…
906.notes:
• Common polite phrases: お受けしかねます／ご対応いたしかねます／ご希望に添いかねます。
• The progressive form expresses hesitation: 決めかねている, 断りかねて（hesitating to refuse）.
• Within a company/organization it is often used to avoid taking direct responsibility: 「弊社といたしましては…いたしかねます」。 explain: The sentence pattern is affirmative in form but negative in meaning.
You want to do something but cannot; doing something is difficult.
Formal sentence. Stiff style. ⏐ examples: 1. 申し訳ありませんが、私にはわかりかねます。
I'm sorry, but it is hard for me to understand.
2. そのようなご依頼は、お引き受けしかねます。
We can hardly accept a request like that.

908.connection: V (plain form) + かのようだ かのような N かのように / N (である)

examples.jp: 彼女はまるで、何でも知っているかのように説明を始めた。
examples.tr: She began explaining as if she knew everything.

examples.jp: 彼は何事もなかったかのように振る舞っていた。
examples.tr: He was behaving as if nothing had happened.

908.explain: ◎ Expresses that something looks or feels that way even though in reality it is not so. Often used with adverbs such as 「まるで」「いかにも」and「あたかも」.

examples.jp: 金持ちの彼女は持ち物からして私たちとは違う。
examples.tr: She's rich, and even her belongings are different from ours.

examples.jp: あの子は口のきき方からして反抗的だ。
examples.tr: That kid is defiant, starting with the way they talk.

examples.jp: 「君の論は前提からして間違っている」
examples.tr: "Your argument is wrong right from its premise."

examples.jp: そのホテルは大理石のロビーからして豪華だった。
examples.tr: That hotel was luxurious, starting with its marble lobby.

examples.jp: この店は雰囲気からして高級だ。
examples.tr: This shop feels upscale from its atmosphere alone.

examples.jp: 彼は服装からしてだらしない。
examples.tr: He is sloppy, starting with the way he dresses.

909.explain:
Takes N as a “clue” and then gives an intuitive conclusion/evaluation.
Often used with negative words:変だ／怪しい／無理がある／失礼だ／安っぽい など。
Not used for clear objective causes; it leans toward subjective impressions.
Position: usually at the start of the clause or before the judgment: Nからして、～。

• A judgment based on a small sign: “Just looking at/judging only from N, you can tell…”. Example: 見た目からして高そうだ。
• Gives a typical example, “right from/even N…”, often implying something negative or unusual: 彼は挨拶からしてできていない。
• Emphasizes the “starting point” to infer the whole: a small part already shows the big picture.
• Nuance: subjective and more intuitive than からすると; often used to criticize, complain, or doubt whether something is right.

rows: Judging only from N, you can tell (intuitive, often negative)
<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>た<ruby>目<rt>め</rt></ruby>からして<ruby>怪<rt>あや</rt></ruby>しい。
N＋からすると／からすれば
データからすると<ruby>増加<rt>ぞうか</rt></ruby><ruby>傾向<rt>けいこう</rt></ruby>だ。
N＋から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ると／から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>れば
<ruby>本人<rt>ほんにん</rt></ruby>から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>れば<ruby>大<rt>だい</rt></ruby><ruby>問題<rt>もんだい</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>遅刻<rt>ちこく</rt></ruby>が<ruby>多<rt>おお</rt></ruby>いことから<ruby>評価<rt>ひょうか</rt></ruby>が<ruby>下<rt>さ</rt></ruby>がった。

mistakes: Using it for an objective cause → Incorrect. Use ので／ため／ことから instead.
Attaching it to a verb clause → Incorrect. からして mainly attaches to nouns.
Confusing it with からすると: JLPT questions often test the nuance “negative vs neutral”.
Using it for excessive praise → Unnatural. からして usually leans negative or conveys a strong impression.
909.notes:
• Often seen in spoken language, reviews and criticism because of its strong evaluative nuance.
• When N is something “overall” (雰囲気, 見た目, タイトル, 値段), からして is more natural.
• If you need to emphasize “even N…”, you can use: Nからして～ない／違う。

examples.jp: この名前からすると、たぶん日本人だな。
examples.tr: Judging from this name, this person is probably Japanese.

examples.jp: 彼からすると、どれも簡単すぎる問題だろう。
examples.tr: From his point of view, they are probably all questions that are too easy.

examples.jp: この足跡からすると、鹿ではなく熊だ。
examples.tr: Judging from these footprints, it's a bear, not a deer.

examples.jp: 症状からすると、インフルエンザの可能性が高い。
examples.tr: Judging from the symptoms, it is very likely influenza.

examples.jp: 彼の性格からすると、そんな嘘はつかないはずだ。
examples.tr: Given his personality, he wouldn't tell a lie like that.

examples.jp: 親からすると、子どもの安全が一番だ。
examples.tr: From a parent's point of view, a child's safety comes first.

910.explain:
Takes N as the basis and then makes an inference; often used in reports, analyses and news.
When it indicates a “standpoint”, the subject is usually a person/group:学生からすると／経営者からすると.
Moderate certainty; the conclusion often comes with an adverb/conjecture ending.
More formal than からして when used in logical reasoning.

• Inference: “Based on N, one can infer…”. Example: 症状からすると風邪だろう。
• Standpoint/viewpoint: “Seen from N's side…”. Example: 消費者からすると値上げは痛い。
• Neutral nuance, more rational than からして; can be used for both positive and negative conclusions.
• Often accompanied by uncertain judgments: ～だろう／～と思われる／～ようだ。

rows: <ruby>数値<rt>すうち</rt></ruby>からすると<ruby>改善<rt>かいぜん</rt></ruby><ruby>傾向<rt>けいこう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>雰囲気<rt>ふんいき</rt></ruby>からして<ruby>高級<rt>こうきゅう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>外部<rt>がいぶ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ると<ruby>不透明<rt>ふとうめい</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>騒音<rt>そうおん</rt></ruby>が<ruby>多<rt>おお</rt></ruby>いことから<ruby>苦情<rt>くじょう</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Taking it as a direct cause → Incorrect. It is a basis for inference, not an actual reason.
Concluding too definitely (断定) → Unnatural. Use ～だろう／～と思われる.
Confusing it with からして in nuance questions: the JLPT often tests “negative impression” vs “neutral inference”.
910.notes:
• In written language, からすると suits conclusion clauses with a clear basis (データ、症状、状況、結果).
• からすれば sometimes implies “speaking from that position…”, with a more subjective nuance than からすると.
• With “people/groups”, both からすると and からすれば are natural: 消費者／親／専門家 など.

examples.jp: 高いからといって、品質がいいとは限らない。
examples.tr: Just because something is expensive doesn't mean its quality is good.

examples.jp: 日本人だからといって、みんな寿司が好きなわけではない。
examples.tr: Just because people are Japanese doesn't mean they all like sushi.

examples.jp: 忙しいからといって、連絡しないのは失礼だ。
examples.tr: Not getting in touch just because you're busy is rude.

examples.jp: 寒いからといって、運動をやめるべきではない。
examples.tr: You shouldn't stop exercising just because it's cold.

examples.jp: 子どもだからといって、何をしても許されるわけではない。
examples.tr: Just because someone is a child doesn't mean they'll be forgiven no matter what they do.

examples.jp: 安いからといって、むやみに大量購入するな。
examples.tr: Don't go buying things in bulk thoughtlessly just because they're cheap.

911.explain:
The first clause states a “seemingly sufficient reason”, and the second clause negates or adjusts the expectation.
Common in debates, education, and rules of conduct.
In spoken language からって is used; in written, formal language からといって is used.
It usually avoids a strongly affirmative conclusion that accepts that reason.

• “Just because… (not necessarily/shouldn't)…”: negates mechanical thinking based on the preceding reason.
• Often combined with partial negation expressions: ～とは限らない／わけではない／とは言えない.
• Also used to warn about or criticize behavior based on an inadequate reason.
• Nuance: challenging prejudices, advising moderation and not making excuses.

rows: <ruby>有名<rt>ゆうめい</rt></ruby>だからといって<ruby>正<rt>ただ</rt></ruby>しいとは<ruby>限<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>らない。
<ruby>料理<rt>りょうり</rt></ruby><ruby>人<rt>じん</rt></ruby>といっても<ruby>家庭<rt>かてい</rt></ruby><ruby>料理<rt>りょうり</rt></ruby>だけ。
Equivalent to からといって (formal/archaic)
<ruby>若<rt>わか</rt></ruby>いからとて<ruby>侮<rt>あなど</rt></ruby>るな。
Emphasizes concession, not rebutting a reason
<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しいにしても<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>は<ruby>必要<rt>ひつよう</rt></ruby>だ。

mistakes: Second clause is a strong affirmative “should/is allowed” → Usually unnatural. This pattern leans toward negation/dissuasion.
Confusing it with といっても (lowering the degree) → The JLPT often sets traps with this pair.
Using the polite form (です/ます) directly in the first clause → Not grammatically wrong, but the JLPT favors the plain form.
Missing the negation/adjustment in the second clause → The meaning of the pattern is easily lost.
911.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～から.
→ ～からといって means “just because…, you cannot conclude/act that way”; it negates a simplistic inference.
2) The second clause is usually a negation or a reminder/advice.
→ Common forms: ～からといって、…とは限らない／…わけではない.
3) Not used to state a direct reason.
→ If you are just stating an ordinary cause, use ～から／～ので.
meaning_vi: Means “just because of the reason ~”
examples: 1. ①　治ったからって
Just because you've recovered from the illness.
2. ②　好きじゃないからといって、野菜を食べないのは体に悪い。
Not eating vegetables just because you don't like them is bad for your health.
3. ➂　バスケットボールの選手だからって、背が高いわけではない。
Just because someone is a basketball player doesn't mean they are tall. meaning_vi: Just because of the reason　～, ～ ⏐ explain: Just because of a reason, however, even so, not necessarily (you cannot draw a conclusion or assert something based on that one reason alone)
「～からって」 is used in spoken language ⏐ examples: 1. 好きだからといって、同じ食品ばかり食べるのはよくない。
It's not good to eat only the same food just because you like it.
2. 日本に住んでいるからといって、日本語がしゃべれるようにはならない。
Just because you live in Japan doesn't mean you will become able to speak Japanese.

examples.jp: 約束したからには、必ず守るべきだ。
examples.tr: Once you've made a promise, you must keep it without fail.

examples.jp: 試合に出るからには、全力を尽くすつもりだ。
examples.tr: Since I'm taking part in the match, I intend to give it my all.

examples.jp: 留学するからには、しっかり成果を出したい。
examples.tr: Since I'm going to study abroad, I want to achieve solid results.

examples.jp: プロであるからには、結果で示さなければならない。
examples.tr: As a professional, you have to prove yourself through results.

examples.jp: ここまで来たからには、後には引けない。
examples.tr: Now that we've come this far, there's no turning back.

examples.jp: 受験するからには、合格するはずだ/に違いない。
examples.tr: Since they're taking the exam, they should pass / they're sure to pass.

912.explain:
Emphasizes a “commitment” or a “norm” after a prerequisite has happened or will happen.
The second clause often goes with: ～べきだ／～つもりだ／～てみせる／～ないわけにはいかない／～はずだ／～に違いない。
More formal than ～以上(は), ～上(は) in some contexts, but all three express “once…”.
V-たからには emphasizes that something has already happened; V-るからには can express determination before doing it.

• “Once…, then…”: states a strong premise that entails an obligation/determination/logical result.
• Two main nuances:

Obligation/determination (the speaker states/proposes a norm): やるからには最後までやり抜く。
Inevitable conjecture: 日本に来たからには、日本語はできるはずだ。

• Obligation/determination (the speaker states/proposes a norm): やるからには最後までやり抜く。
• Inevitable conjecture: 日本に来たからには、日本語はできるはずだ。
• The second clause usually contains a strong will/rule/expectation, not simply a statement of fact.

rows: やるからには<ruby>全力<rt>ぜんりょく</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>学生<rt>がくせい</rt></ruby>である<ruby>以上<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>、<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>本分<rt>ほんぶん</rt></ruby>だ。
Tied to an action already chosen/decided
<ruby>出場<rt>しゅつじょう</rt></ruby>する<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>悔<rt>く</rt></ruby>いのないように。
<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>いからといって<ruby>良<rt>よ</rt></ruby>いとは<ruby>限<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>らない。

mistakes: Second clause just states a fact → The nuance of obligation/determination is lost (misuse of the pattern).
Confusing it with からといって in sentences that negate a prejudice → Different function.
Missing a suitable option for the second clause (choosing an answer with no volition/norm) → A common N2 trap.
Using it with adjectives/nouns without である in formal writing → Unnatural/not standard.
912.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～以上（は）／～から.
→ ～からには means “once…, then…”; the second clause is usually an obligation/volition/determination.
2) The second clause usually has a nuance of obligation or responsibility.
→ If the second clause is just an ordinary description, this pattern usually does not fit.
3) Not used for light conditions.
→ For an ordinary “because/since”, use ～から／～ので.

examples.jp: 専門家から見ると、この計画には問題点が多い。
examples.tr: From an expert's point of view, this plan has a lot of problems.

examples.jp: データから見れば、景気は回復しつつある。
examples.tr: Judging from the data, the economy is gradually recovering.

examples.jp: 子どもの目から見ると、大人の世界は不思議だ。
examples.tr: Through a child's eyes, the adult world is a strange place.

examples.jp: 安全面から見ても、この橋の補修は急務だ。
examples.tr: From a safety standpoint as well, repairing this bridge is an urgent task.

examples.jp: 第三者の立場から見ると、双方に誤解がある。
examples.tr: From a third party's standpoint, there are misunderstandings on both sides.

examples.jp: 衛星写真から見ると、被害は想定以上だ。
examples.tr: Judging from the satellite photos, the damage is greater than expected.

913.explain:
Used when you want to make clear the “focus of the assessment” before stating a conclusion.
Suitable for both written and spoken language; moderately formal.
Not used to express benefit/relationship, i.e. personal feelings “for (someone)…” → prefer 〜にとって.
To emphasize conjecture, use 〜からすると; to emphasize the aspect/criterion of the statement, use 〜から言うと.
The conclusion after ～から見ると is usually a judgment, evaluation or inference, not a direct command.

～から見ると: “Seen from/if we consider (perspective/criterion/source of information)…, then…”. Expresses a judgment/comment based on a specific viewpoint or data.
• The focus is on the viewpoint/observation (visual/metaphorical). “見る” suggests a sense based on something that can be observed or interpreted.
• Often used with N indicating a source: データ・統計・専門家・第三者・子どもの目・外部・安全面・コスト面…
• Expresses relative objectivity; however, it is still the speaker's assessment based on the stated viewpoint.
• Variants: 見れば (supposition), 見ても (emphasizing “even considered from that…”).

rows: Considering/looking from the perspective of N
<ruby>専門<rt>せんもん</rt></ruby><ruby>家<rt>か</rt></ruby>から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ると、<ruby>妥当<rt>だとう</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>足跡<rt>あしあと</rt></ruby>からすると、<ruby>熊<rt>くま</rt></ruby>だ。
Emphasizes the criterion for the statement/evaluation
<ruby>品質<rt>ひんしつ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うと、Aが<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>私<rt>わたし</rt></ruby>にとって、<ruby>家族<rt>かぞく</rt></ruby>が<ruby>一番<rt>いちばん</rt></ruby>だ。
N + によれば/によると
Reports information, not an evaluative viewpoint
<ruby>天気<rt>てんき</rt></ruby><ruby>予報<rt>よほう</rt></ruby>によれば、<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Confusing it with 〜によれば/によると (reported source of information). から見ると is a judgment from a viewpoint, not “according to the forecast…”.
Using it for “for (someone)” (feelings) → incorrect. Correct form: 〜にとって.
Attaching it directly to a command: “専門家から見ると、やめろ” → crude; switch to an indirect recommendation.
JLPT: easily confused with からすると/から言うと. Look at the core verb: 見る=observation, 言う=statement/criterion, する=arriving at a conjecture.
913.notes:
• N is usually a specific “eye/standpoint”: 研究者・医者・利用者・会計の面・文化の視点.
• With N referring to things/data sources (地図・統計・記録), the nuance is “observing from the data”.
• Avoid overusing it with commands/volition; switching to ので/から is more natural. | Variants: ～から見れば・から見て(も)

914.meaning: In terms of…, from the standpoint of…

examples.jp: 値段から言うと、こちらの機種が一番お得だ。
examples.tr: In terms of price, this model is the best deal.

examples.jp: 品質から言えば、国産のほうが安心だ。
examples.tr: In terms of quality, domestic products are more reassuring.

examples.jp: 法律から言って、その行為は違法だ。
examples.tr: From a legal standpoint, that act is illegal.

examples.jp: 文法の点から言うと、この表現は不自然だ。
examples.tr: From a grammatical point of view, this expression is unnatural.

examples.jp: 経験から言って、準備は早いほどいい。
examples.tr: Speaking from experience, the earlier you prepare, the better.

examples.jp: 会社の立場から言えば、値上げは避けられない。
examples.tr: From the company's standpoint, a price increase is unavoidable.

914.explain:
Used when you want to “set a framework of criteria” before making a judgment.
Suitable for written language, speeches and reports; natural in the context of debate.
Do not confuse it with the meaning “say that” of言う; here it marks a criterion.
Often used with phrases like の点から言うと/見地から言うと to make it sound more standard.

～から言うと: “In terms of/as regards/if we talk about (criterion)…, then…”. Used when setting an evaluation criterion and then giving an assessment.
• N is usually a criterion: 値段・品質・安全・法律・文法・効率・デザイン・立場 等.
• Its nuance is more reasoned/normative than 〜から見ると; less intuitive.
• The variants から言えば/から言って change the rhythm of the sentence and the level of formality.

rows: <ruby>効率<rt>こうりつ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うと、Bが<ruby>良<rt>よ</rt></ruby>い。
Seen from the perspective of N
<ruby>外部<rt>がいぶ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ると、<ruby>複雑<rt>ふくざつ</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>症状<rt>しょうじょう</rt></ruby>からすると、<ruby>風邪<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>子供<rt>こども</rt></ruby>にとって、<ruby>睡眠<rt>すいみん</rt></ruby>は<ruby>重要<rt>じゅうよう</rt></ruby>。
Introduces a topic, not just a criterion
<ruby>環境<rt>かんきょう</rt></ruby>について、<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>そう。

mistakes: Confusing it with “Aと言うと” (when it comes to A). 〜から言うと means “in terms of…”, not “speaking of…”.
Using から言うと for the subject's feelings “for (someone)” → incorrect. You must use 〜にとって.
Combining it with a direct command sounds harsh; use a recommendation/evaluation instead of giving an order.
JLPT: distinguish から見ると/からすると/から言うと by the core verb (見る/する/言う).
914.notes:
• “経験から言って” is a very natural phrase, almost fixed in advice.
• In academic fields: 歴史学から言うと／統計学の観点から言うと make it more convincing.
• In presentations, several criteria are combined in parallel: 価格・性能・デザインの点から言うと、Aが最適だ。 | Variants: ～から言えば・から言って

examples.jp: デパートのドアが開くか開かないかのうちに、待っていた客たちはバーゲン会場に殺到した。
examples.tr: Almost the moment the department store doors opened, the waiting customers rushed to the sale area.

examples.jp: けがをしたところが治ったか治らないかのうちに、また同じところを切ってしまった。
examples.tr: My injury had barely healed when I cut the same spot again.

examples.jp: 始業ベルがあり終わるか終わらないかのうちに先生が教室に入ってきた。
examples.tr: The opening bell had hardly finished ringing when the teacher came into the classroom.

examples.jp: チャイムが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、学生たちは教室を飛び出した。
examples.tr: The moment the chime rang, the students dashed out of the classroom.

examples.jp: 彼は席に座るか座らないかのうちに、眠ってしまった。
examples.tr: He had barely sat down in his seat when he fell asleep.

examples.jp: 家に着くか着かないかのうちに、雨が降り出した。
examples.tr: I had just about reached home when it started to rain.

915.explain:
Emphasizes the suddenness and near simultaneity of two events.
Suitable for narration and description; the second clause usually does not express volition or advice.
The verb in the first clause should be a punctual verb (鳴る、着く、座る、開ける...).
More formal in style than ～とたん(に); somewhat written language.

• Meaning: “Just as / As soon as … then …”, “before … has even finished, … already …”.
• The time gap is extremely short; the later action happens almost simultaneously with the threshold of the first action.
• Used for sudden, quick events that are not under the speaker's volition (usually objective facts).
• The second clause is usually in the past; avoid commands or strong volition.

rows: Very instantaneous; repeats Vる/ Vない
<ruby>着<rt>つ</rt></ruby>くか<ruby>着<rt>つ</rt></ruby>かないかのうちに<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>
Often surprise; does not repeat V
<ruby>立<rt>た</rt></ruby>ったとたん、<ruby>倒<rt>たお</rt></ruby>れた
Very formal/archaic; not used in conversation
<ruby>着<rt>つ</rt></ruby>くや<ruby>否<rt>いな</rt></ruby>や、<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>した
～かと<ruby>思<rt>おも</rt></ruby>うと／～かと<ruby>思<rt>おも</rt></ruby>ったら
Subjective feeling; second clause is beyond one's volition
<ruby>降<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>ったかと<ruby>思<rt>おも</rt></ruby>うと、やんだ
Not necessarily instantaneous; does not repeat Vる/ない
<ruby>暗<rt>くらく</rt></ruby>くならないうちに<ruby>帰<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>る

mistakes: Not repeating the same verb in the affirmative form and the negative form: incorrect structure.
Using it with a second clause that expresses volition or a command: unnatural in exam questions.
Using a durative verb in the first clause (勉強するかしないかのうちに): lacks the momentary quality, less natural.
Confusing it with ～ないうちに (before): ～か～ないかのうちに is instantaneous, while ～ないうちに means “before”.
915.notes:
• This pattern creates the effect “before action A has even been confirmed as complete, B has already happened”.
• In narration, “の” can be dropped: ～か～ないかうちに (colloquial, but the standard form is still “のうちに”).
• The second clause is usually past, or present describing a quickly recurring habit in narrative writing.
• Not suitable for direct commands or volition in the second clause.

916.meaning:
～するのが難(むずか)しい、とても～できない
Hard to do

examples.jp: そのドラマの話はあまりに非現実的で、理解しがたいものだった。
examples.tr: The story of that drama was so unrealistic that it was hard to understand.

examples.jp: 子供にあんなことを言うなんて、本当に許しがたい。
examples.tr: Saying something like that to a child is truly unforgivable.

examples.jp: 彼女のような正直な人が嘘をつくとは信じがたい。
examples.tr: It's hard to believe that an honest person like her would lie.

examples.jp: 古くなっても、このかばんには愛着があって捨てがたい。
examples.tr: Even though this bag has gotten old, I'm attached to it and find it hard to throw away.

examples.jp: 耐え難い痛みの中で、救急車の到着を待った。
examples.tr: In unbearable pain, I waited for the ambulance to arrive.

examples.jp: 息子は留学という得難い経験をして、一回り成長したようだ。
examples.tr: My son seems to have grown a lot through the rare and precious experience of studying abroad.

916.explain: ◎ A written-language usage expressing that something is difficult to do.
916.notes:
meaning_vi: Hard to ～; cannot　～ ⏐ explain: Not used to mean being unable in terms of ability.
Formal sentence. ⏐ examples: 1. これは信じがたい話だが、事実である。
This is a hard-to-believe story, but it is true.
2. 人が人の命をうばうなんて、許しがたい。
For a person to take another person's life is unforgivable.

examples.jp: 家がお金持ちなだけに、彼女はもう車を持っている。
examples.tr: Precisely because her family is rich, she already has a car.

examples.jp: 年が年だけに、父は耳が遠くなってきた。
examples.tr: Given his age, my father has started to become hard of hearing.

examples.jp: キーパーがいいだけに、このチームから点を取るのは大変そうだ。
examples.tr: Because their goalkeeper is so good, it looks like it will be tough to score against this team.

examples.jp: 北欧の国々は、社会福祉が進んでいるだけに、自分が幸福だと感じている人の割合が高い。
examples.tr: Precisely because social welfare is so advanced in the Nordic countries, a high proportion of people feel that they are happy.

917.explain: ◎ An expression meaning "because ~, so naturally", used to present grounds when mentioning a natural result.

examples.jp: あんなまずい料理にお金を払うくらいなら、カップラーメンを食べたほうがいい。
examples.tr: Rather than pay money for food that bad, I'd be better off eating instant ramen.

examples.jp: 彼にあげるくらいなら、捨てたほうがましだよ。
examples.tr: I'd rather throw it away than give it to him.

examples.jp: 最近は、地方に転勤させられるくらいなら、会社を辞める、という若者が増えているそうだ。
examples.tr: I hear that more and more young people these days say they would quit their company rather than be transferred to a regional office.

examples.jp: あんな男に顔を上げるくらいなら、死んだほうがましだ。
examples.tr: I would rather die than bow my head to a man like that.

918.explain: ◎ Presents an option the speaker does not want, to show that they would make a different choice.

rows: Does not necessarily have the “rather” nuance; more neutral.
<ruby>歩<rt>ある</rt></ruby>くよりは、バスのほうがいい。
If it's A, then rather B
Close in meaning, written/rhetorical; むしろ emphasizes “rather”.
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くならむしろ<ruby>一人<rt>ひとり</rt></ruby>で<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>く。
Often follows ～くらいなら for emphasis.
<ruby>待<rt>ま</rt></ruby>つくらいなら、いっそ<ruby>帰<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>ろう。
Sound variant of くらいなら
<ruby>怒<rt>おこ</rt></ruby>られるぐらいなら、やらない。

mistakes: Making part B a fact that has already happened (“…already did …”) → wrong intent; this pattern states a choice/evaluation, not a narration.
Leaving out the evaluative phrase in part B (ましだ/ほうがいい) makes the sentence vague.
Confusing it with ～ほどなら (degree comparison) → different function.
Using it for a positive action in part A (no negative nuance) → makes the sentence less natural.
918.notes:
explain: Expresses a choice: “rather A than B”. A is an option that is not good but still acceptable, while B is worse.
examples: 1. 途中でやめるくらいなら、初めからやらないほうがいい。
If you're going to quit halfway, it's better not to do it at all from the start.
2. お金のためにいやな仕事をするくらいなら、貧しくてもいい。
I'd rather be poor than do a job I hate just for the money.
3. あいつに謝るくらいなら、死んだほうがましだ。
I'd rather die than apologize to him.
4. 「練習が辛くて泣くぐらいなら、やめてしまいなさい」
If practice is so hard that it makes you cry, you'd better quit.
meaning_vi: If I had to… I'd rather…
explain: Emphasizes a “rather… than…” attitude, with clear emotion, sometimes decisive.
Part A is a hypothetical situation that is hard to accept; part B is the less bad alternative.
Suitable for advice or mild warnings in conversation; not used for past events that are already over.
Often combined with まだ・いっそ to strengthen the nuance.
examples: 1. あんな人に頭を下げるくらいなら、辞めたほうがましだ。
If I had to bow my head to someone like that, I'd rather quit.
2. うそをつくくらいなら、黙っていたほうがいい。
If you'd have to lie, it's better to stay silent.
3. 渋滞で何時間も待つくらいなら、電車で行ったほうがましだ。
If I'd have to wait for hours in a traffic jam, I'd be better off going by train.
4. 苦手な肉を食べるくらいなら、サラダで十分だ。
If I'd have to eat meat I don't like, a salad is enough.
5. 彼と別れるくらいなら、遠距離恋愛のほうがいい。
If it means breaking up with him, a long-distance relationship is better.
6. あの店で深夜まで働くくらいなら、自分で商売を始めたほうがいい。
If I'd have to work until late at night at that shop, I'd be better off starting my own business.

919.meaning:
いかにも～そうだ（seems）
Indicates an emotional state, an air of
919.connection: Aい (drop い)・Na + げ / Vます + たげ

examples.jp: 彼女は、最近、彼からメールが来ないらしくて、何か、寂しげだった。
examples.tr: She apparently hasn't been getting emails from him lately, and she seemed somehow lonely.

examples.jp: 彼女はいつも、息子の学校の成績の話を自慢げに言う。
examples.tr: She always talks proudly about her son's grades at school.

examples.jp: 息子は得意げに１００点を取ったテストを差し出した。
examples.tr: My son triumphantly held out the test he had gotten 100 points on.

examples.jp: ハンバーガーショップは楽しげな若者たちでいっぱいだった。
examples.tr: The hamburger shop was full of young people who looked like they were having fun.

examples.jp: 学生は自信なさげ（/ありげ）に答えた。
examples.tr: The student answered without much confidence (/with apparent confidence).

examples.jp: 彼は何か言いたげな様子で立っていた。
examples.tr: He was standing there looking as if he wanted to say something.

919.explain:
◎ A written-language usage that expresses conjecture.

いかにも～そうだ（様態(ようたい)）
Indicates an emotional state, an air of
919.notes:
explain: Indicates a person's state of mind as perceived from outside. ⏐ examples: 1. あの人はさびしげな目をしている。
That person has lonely-looking eyes.
2. 彼は何か言いたげだった。
He looked as if he wanted to say something.

920.meaning:
（よく知(し)っている人等(ひとなど)）の性格(せいかく)や様子(ようす)から考(かんが)えると →話(はな)し手(て)の予想(よそう)判断(はんだん)等(など)
Because; presents the speaker's conjecture or judgment

examples.jp: 朝寝坊の彼のことだから、今日も遅れてくるだろう。
examples.tr: He's always oversleeping, so he'll probably be late again today.

examples.jp: 真面目な木村さんのことだから、約束は守るに違いない。
examples.tr: Knowing how serious Mr. Kimura is, he will surely keep his promise.

examples.jp: 母のことだから、いつも私のことを心配していると思う。
examples.tr: Knowing my mother, I think she is always worrying about me.

examples.jp: 田舎のことだから、派手なかっこうはしないほうがいい。
examples.tr: Since it's the countryside, you'd better not wear anything flashy.

examples.jp: 家族と仕事とどっちを取るか聞かれて、彼は迷うことなく家族と答えた。
examples.tr: When he was asked which he would choose, his family or his work, he answered “my family” without hesitation.

examples.jp: 彼女は５年間、一度も休むことなく、毎週ピアノ教室に通った。
examples.tr: For five years she went to piano lessons every week without missing a single one.

examples.jp: 彼らは試合に勝つために、1日も休むことなく練習に励んだ。
examples.tr: To win the match, they practiced hard without taking even one day off.

examples.jp: 彼は社長の地位を苦労することなく手に入れた。
examples.tr: He got the position of company president without any hardship.

examples.jp: 夫は毎年忘れることなく、結婚記念日に花を送ってくれる。
examples.tr: Every year my husband never forgets to send me flowers on our wedding anniversary.

examples.jp: 彼は最後まで諦めることなく戦った。
examples.tr: He fought to the very end without giving up.

921.explain:
Emphasizes “not at all” (stronger in degree than ないで/ずに); suited to objective, formal description.
Suitable for continuous/repeated actions; for a single event, ずに/ないで is more natural.
In casual speech, ないで/ずに is more common; ことなく sounds stiff/written.
Can be used with non-human subjects (rain, wind, traditions…).

• Expresses doing action B “without ever doing A”, emphasizing the continuous/thorough negation of A.
• Often used with verbs such as: 休む, 諦める, 迷う, とどまる, 振り返る, 止む, 絶える, ためらう.
• Formal, objective nuance; often used in narration, evaluation, writing that praises effort, or descriptions of natural phenomena.

rows: Do B without ever doing A
<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>むことなく<ruby>働<rt>はたら</rt></ruby>く
<ruby>朝<rt>あさ</rt></ruby>ご<ruby>飯<rt>はん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>食<rt>た</rt></ruby>べないで<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>かけた
More formal than ないで; flexible
<ruby>確認<rt>かくにん</rt></ruby>せずに<ruby>送信<rt>そうしん</rt></ruby>した
Written language, stiffer than ことなく
