examples.jp: 「掃除をしたはかりにしては汚れが目立ちますね。やり直したほうがいいですよ」
examples.tr: "For a place that's just been cleaned, the dirt really stands out. You'd better do it again."

965.explain:
Expresses an impression of something "unusual" based on the common standard of the group/condition that N indicates.
The second clause is a judgment/evaluation. Rarely used for commands/wishes.
Goes well with words for quantity/price/age to emphasize "compared with the norm":値段 にしては …,年齢 にしては …
More objective nuance than わりに(は) with a personal N; clearly emphasizes the "group standard".

• Used to state an evaluation contrary to expectations based on a standard N/V: "even though/compared with being…, …".
• The standard N is a general group/identity/condition (children, beginners, spring…).
• The second clause is usually a remark or subjective evaluation that is surprising compared with the standard.
• Different from のに: it does not express a disappointed cause-and-effect relationship, but a comparison with the "expected standard".

rows: Even though/compared with the expected standard
The standard is a general group/identity; clear surprise.
<ruby>初心者<rt>しょしんしゃ</rt></ruby>にしてはうまい。
The standard is subjective/personal; milder surprise.
<ruby>年齢<rt>ねんれい</rt></ruby>のわりに<ruby>若<rt>わか</rt></ruby>く<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>える。
Hypothetical concession, broad scope, not necessarily a group standard.
<ruby>安<rt>やす</rt></ruby>いにしても<ruby>品質<rt>ひんしつ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>大事<rt>だいじ</rt></ruby>だ。
Opposite meaning: the result matches expectations, usually praise.
<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>いだけあって<ruby>品質<rt>ひんしつ</rt></ruby>がいい。
Emphasizes the contradiction between reality and the speaker's expectations; strong emotion.

mistakes: Using it with commands/wishes: 子どもにしては早く寝なさい（unnatural). Use it for evaluations.
Confusing it with わりに(は): when the standard is an objective group (初心者, 子ども), prefer にしては.
Using it for obvious facts with no element of surprise → loses the "unusual" meaning.
Making N too vague: 彼にしては… but without information about the "standard" it will be hard to understand in the exam.
965.notes:
• Best used with objective standards (age, occupation, experience, season…); avoid vague standards that are hard to define.
• The second clause is usually an adjective/verb expressing evaluation: いい／悪い／多い／少ない／うまい／下手 など.
• With concrete figures: 1000円にしては…, 3ヶ月にしては… make the sentence objective and convincing.

examples.jp: 興味がないにしても、行くか行かないか、返事をしてほしい。
examples.tr: Even if you're not interested, I'd like you to reply whether you're going or not.

examples.jp: 社長にしても、彼を責めているんじゃないと思う。
examples.tr: I don't think even the company president is blaming him.

examples.jp: 謝るにしても、もう少しちゃんと謝るべきだ。
examples.tr: Even if you apologize, you should apologize a bit more properly.

examples.jp: 忙しいにしても、欠席の連絡をしてこないのはよくない。
examples.tr: Even if you're busy, it's not good not to let us know that you will be absent.

examples.jp: いくら忙しいにしても、睡眠は大事だ。
examples.tr: No matter how busy you are, sleep is important.

examples.jp: 行くにしても、準備してから行きなさい。
examples.tr: Even if you go, get ready before you go.

966.explain:
Combines well with emphatic words たとえ/いくら/どんなに.
The second clause is usually the speaker's evaluation/position.
V-たにしても is used when acknowledging something that has already happened; V-るにしても for a future supposition.
Compared with としても: slightly more formal/stiff; compared with にしろ/にせよ: softer.

• Concession: Even if X, Y (position unchanged).
• Acknowledging a fact: Even though X has happened, the conclusion is still Y.
• Evaluation by a standard: Even for/at the level of N, … (beyond/different from expectations).
• Listing: N1にしてもN2にしても: whether it is A or B, the conclusion is the same.

rows: <ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くとしても<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>する。
Formal/stiff; often followed by a command
<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しいにしろ<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>なさい。
Expresses deviation from expectations, not concession
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもにしては<ruby>上手<rt>じょうず</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>貧乏<rt>びんぼう</rt></ruby>であれ<ruby>金持<rt>かねも</rt></ruby>ちであれ。

mistakes: Confusing it with ～にしては (deviation from expectations) and ～としても (neutral supposition).
Dropping “だ/である” before にしても with N/Na in written language.
A direct command after にしても can sound harsh; consider the situation.
Use V-たにしても when the event has already happened; V-るにしても for a supposition.
966.notes:
• “Nにしても…” can be translated flexibly: “even… ”, “even if…”.
• In literature/speeches, “であるにしても” increases objectivity.
• The pairing can be extended to more than two elements: AにしてもBにしてもCにしても…

967.connection: V plain form + にせよ にしろ / N + (である) / Na + (である) / Aい

examples.jp: どんな相手にせよ、返事はした方がいい。
examples.tr: Whoever the other person is, you should reply.

examples.jp: いずれにせよ、今日はもう時間がないから明日にしよう。
examples.tr: Either way, we don't have any more time today, so let's leave it until tomorrow.

967.explain: ◎ An expression that presents a hypothetical condition, but the conclusion does not change.

968.meaning:
①～という理由(りゆう)で（書(か)き言葉(ことば)）
For the reason that, because | Due to…, because… (formal notices)

examples.jp: 本日のプログラムは、満席につき、受付を終了いたしました。
examples.tr: Today's program is fully booked, so we have stopped accepting registrations.

examples.jp: 現在、工事中につき、通行できません。
examples.tr: Construction work is currently in progress, so passage is not possible.

examples.jp: 出入り口につき、駐車禁止。（書き言葉）
examples.tr: Entrance/exit: no parking. (written language)

examples.jp: 本日は定休日につき、休ませていただきます。
examples.tr: We are closed today for our regular holiday.

examples.jp: 残高不足につき、引き落としできません。
examples.tr: Due to insufficient balance, the payment cannot be debited.

examples.jp: 割合
examples.tr: Ratio

968.explain: ◎ A written-language expression meaning "because of ~". Often used in notices.
968.notes:
explain: A stiff sentence style. Often used in formal situations or in business documents. ⏐ examples: 1. この機械はただ今調整中につき、ご使用になれません。
This machine is currently being adjusted, so it cannot be used.
2. 本日は祭日につき、休業させていただきます。
Today is a national holiday, so we will be closed.

examples.jp: こういうニュースを見るにつけ、政治家は信用できないと思う。
examples.tr: Whenever I see news like this, I think politicians can't be trusted.

examples.jp: 彼は何かにつけ、文句を言うから、困る。
examples.tr: He complains at every opportunity, which is a real problem.

examples.jp: 一生懸命勉強する子供たちを見るにつけ、この仕事をやっていて、本当によかったと思う。
examples.tr: Whenever I see children studying hard, I think it's really good that I'm doing this job.

examples.jp: あの客は何かにつけ文句を言ってくるから、本当に困る。
examples.tr: That customer complains about every little thing, so it's really troublesome.

969.explain: ◎ An expression indicating the cause that leads to some action or state of mind.
969.notes: As a fixed idiomatic expression, used in the forms 「何事につけ」 and 「何かにつけ」, meaning “in any case” and “every time there is some occasion,” respectively.

examples.jp: 年を取るにつれ、目が見えにくくなってきた。
examples.tr: As I've gotten older, my eyesight has gotten worse.

examples.jp: パソコンの普及につれ、漢字を正しく書けなくなったと感じる人が増えている。
examples.tr: With the spread of personal computers, more and more people feel they can no longer write kanji correctly.

970.explain: ◎ When one thing or state changes, another thing changes along with it.

examples.jp: 子供の数の減少にともない、学校の数も減っている。
examples.tr: Along with the decrease in the number of children, the number of schools is also decreasing.

examples.jp: 結婚にともない、引っ越すことになりました。
examples.tr: Because I'm getting married, I will be moving.

971.explain: ◎ An expression describing a change that arises as a result of some other change.
971.notes: An even more formal way of saying 「にともなって」.

examples.jp: 経済の回復にともなって、消費が増加している。
examples.tr: Along with the economic recovery, consumption is increasing.

examples.jp: 人口が増えるのにともなって、交通渋滞が深刻化した。
examples.tr: As the population grew, traffic congestion became more serious.

examples.jp: ダム建設に伴い、周辺環境が大きく変化した。
examples.tr: With the construction of the dam, the surrounding environment changed greatly.

examples.jp: 人事異動に伴う住所変更の手続きについてお知らせします。
examples.tr: We would like to inform you of the procedures for changing your address in connection with personnel transfers.

examples.jp: 景気悪化にともなって、採用計画を見直した。
examples.tr: With the economic downturn, we reviewed our hiring plans.

examples.jp: 駅の完成にともなって
examples.tr: With the completion of the station

972.explain:
Emphasizes relationships that are systemic/policy-related/social phenomena; suits a serious style.
The second clause is a result, effect, or countermeasure; avoid direct commands except in notices.
Often appears with academic vocabulary:変化,影響,増加,減少,実施,見直し,…

- Meaning 1 (simultaneous change): “Along with/at the same time as A, B also changes/continues.”
- Meaning 2 (accompaniment/consequence): “A brings about B (consequence/effect/measure).”
- More formal than ～につれて; can be used in formal spoken language, written language, and administrative notices.

rows: Formal; used for changes and accompanying consequences
<ruby>増加<rt>ぞうか</rt></ruby>にともなって<ruby>対策<rt>たいさく</rt></ruby>が<ruby>必要<rt>ひつよう</rt></ruby>。
Leans toward gradual change; less “measure/consequence” nuance
<ruby>気温<rt>きおん</rt></ruby>が<ruby>下<rt>さ</rt></ruby>がるにつれて<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>くなる。
<ruby>規則<rt>きそく</rt></ruby>にしたがって<ruby>処理<rt>しょり</rt></ruby>する。
Has both a simultaneous meaning and a correlated-change meaning; more neutral
<ruby>成長<rt>せいちょう</rt></ruby>とともに<ruby>責任<rt>せきにん</rt></ruby>が<ruby>重<rt>おも</rt></ruby>くなる。

mistakes: Using it for a single, instantaneous event → does not fit the “process/accompaniment” nuance.
Confusing the modifier function: “に伴う + N” must come before a noun.
JLPT trap when choosing between につれて and にともなって where the second clause is a “measure/effect” → prefer にともなって.
972.notes:
• “伴う” is a formal Sino-Japanese word; in headings/notices “に伴い/に伴う” is commonly used.
• If you want to emphasize a clear cause–result relationship, consider ため/ので; “にともなって” is neutral and describes an accompanying relationship.
• Often used in a nominalized passive form: N + に伴う + N (effects/measures/costs…).

973.meaning: Is precisely…, is nothing other than…

examples.jp: 目標が達成できたのは、周りの協力があったからにほかならない。
examples.tr: We were able to achieve our goal for no other reason than the cooperation of those around us.

examples.jp: コーチが彼に厳しく言うのも、期待の表れにほかならない。
examples.tr: The coach being strict with him is nothing other than a sign of high expectations.

examples.jp: 彼女は合格したのは努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.tr: Her passing is nothing other than the result of hard work.

examples.jp: 親が子どもを叱るのは、子どもを愛しているからにほかならない。
examples.tr: Parents scold their children precisely because they love them.

examples.jp: 新しい事業の成功は、社員全員の努力の賜物にほかならない。
examples.tr: The success of the new business is nothing other than the fruit of the efforts of all the employees.

examples.jp: 脳死は人間の死にほかならないとかんがえる人が増えた。
examples.tr: More and more people now think that brain death is nothing other than human death.

973.explain:
Used to emphasize the essence/truth/origin of something.
Strong, formal nuance; suitable for reports, essays, and speeches.
Often used with vocabulary of causal relationships:原因,結果,目的,事実,誤解,…

- Strong affirmation “is precisely …/is nothing other than …”, used to draw a conclusion about the essence/core cause.
- Often appears in official statements, argumentative writing, and press releases; a nuance of certainty and decisiveness.

rows: <ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>にほかならない。
<ruby>私<rt>わたし</rt></ruby>は<ruby>通訳<rt>つうやく</rt></ruby>にすぎない。
<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>こそ<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>の<ruby>鍵<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>だ。
～<ruby>以外<rt>いがい</rt></ruby>の<ruby>何<rt>なに</rt></ruby>ものでもない
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>行為<rt>こうい</rt></ruby>は<ruby>善意<rt>ぜんい</rt></ruby><ruby>以外<rt>いがい</rt></ruby>の<ruby>何<rt>なに</rt></ruby>ものでもない。

mistakes: Using it directly with an adjective (×嬉しいにほかならない) → convert it to a nominalization: 嬉しさにほかならない.
Using it when not yet certain/still conjecturing → contradicts the strong affirmative nuance.
Confusing it with ～にすぎない (opposite meaning): one elevates with strong affirmation, the other downplays the degree.
973.notes:
• The form “A は B にほかならない” is suitable for concluding a paragraph: redefining A as B.
• “…からにほかならない” emphasizes the sole reason; suitable for refuting rumors/speculation.
• Not used when the speaker is only making a vague conjecture; requires a firm stance or grounds. meaning_vi: is precisely, is nothing other than ～ ⏐ explain: Used when you want to make the assertion “there is nothing other than that”, “it is exactly that”
A stiff sentence style. ⏐ examples: 1. 合格したのは、彼の努力の結果にほかならない。
Passing the exam is nothing other than the result of his efforts.
2. 彼があなたをからかうのは、まさに愛情表現にほかならない。
His teasing you is nothing other than an expression of affection.

examples.jp: 長年英語を勉強しているにもかかわらず、なかなか上手く話せない。
examples.tr: Although I've been studying English for many years, I still can't speak it well.

examples.jp: けがをしているにもかかわらず、彼は今日も試合に出た。
examples.tr: Despite being injured, he played in the match again today.

examples.jp: 彼は熱が高いにもかかわらず、仕事に行った。
examples.tr: Although he had a high fever, he went to work.

examples.jp: 深夜にもかかわらず、大勢の人が病院に駆けつけた。
examples.tr: Despite the late hour, a large number of people rushed to the hospital.

examples.jp: このゲーム機は高価であるにもかかわらず、よく売れているそうだ。
examples.tr: I hear that this game console sells well despite being expensive.

examples.jp: 気を付けていたにもかかわらず、また失敗してしまった。
examples.tr: Although I was being careful, I failed again.

974.explain:
Formal/objective nuance: suitable for writing, presentations, and announcements.
Emphasizes a “paradoxical” result rather than the speaker's emotions (unlike ～のに, which often carries a nuance of annoyance/regret).
The first clause is a “fact/obvious condition” or a “general expectation”; information that is still conjecture should not be used.
The sentence can be split with “。それにもかかわらず、～。” for more emphasis.

Expresses “although/despite A, B (a result contrary to common sense/unexpected)”. Character: formal, more objective than ～のに. Emphasizes a strong contrast between the reality A and the result B.
• Implies “contrary to common sense, expectations, or obvious conditions”.
• Often appears in written language, news, reports, and speeches.
• Not (or very rarely) used to state wishes/give direct commands; suitable for describing facts and evaluations.

rows: Casual, strong emotion, common in speech
Objective, written language, emphasizes “contrary to expectation”
<ruby>警報<rt>けいほう</rt></ruby><ruby>発令<rt>はつれい</rt></ruby><ruby>中<rt>ちゅう</rt></ruby>にもかかわらず<ruby>外出<rt>がいしゅつ</rt></ruby>した。
<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているくせに<ruby>黙<rt>だま</rt></ruby>っている。
<ruby>失敗<rt>しっぱい</rt></ruby>した。それにもかかわらず<ruby>挑戦<rt>ちょうせん</rt></ruby>する。

mistakes: Using it with direct commands/suggestions makes the sentence awkward: avoid “にもかかわらず、来てください” in formal writing.
Dropping “である” after N/Aな in written language makes it less natural: “学生にもかかわらず” → should be “学生であるにもかかわらず”.
Confusing it with “のに”: exam questions often ask you to choose the pattern with the right nuance; official documents prefer “にもかかわらず”.
974.notes:
• With Aな/N, “である” makes the sentence natural and consistent with written style.
• Can be combined with statistical data or news headlines to increase formality.
• If you want to express personal emotions, consider using ～のに instead of ～にもかかわらず. explain: Used when you want to say that the result turned out different from what was expected from the reality of ～ ⏐ examples: 1. 雨にもかかわらず、大勢の人々が集まった。
A large number of people gathered despite the rain.
2. 見たにもかかわらず、彼は見なかったと言った。
Even though he saw it, he said he hadn't.

examples.jp: 合格に向けて、毎日、一生懸命勉強しています。
examples.tr: I'm studying hard every day toward passing the exam.

examples.jp: 解決に向けて、今日も話し合いが行われた。
examples.tr: Talks were held again today toward a resolution.

975.explain: ◎ Expresses the meaning "taking ~ as a target or purpose".
975.notes: Takes nouns expressing a place or direction and indicates the destination toward which something moves, the direction a person is facing, etc. As in ③, it can also be used as the predicate of a sentence.

976.meaning: Based on…, on the basis of…

examples.jp: アンケート結果に基づいて、商品開発をした。
examples.tr: We developed products based on the survey results.

examples.jp: この本は、教授が長年の研究に基づいて書いたものだ。
examples.tr: This book was written by the professor based on many years of research.

examples.jp: テストの結果に基づいて、クラスを決めます。
examples.tr: Classes will be decided based on the test results.

examples.jp: 計画に基づいて、来月から工事が始まる。
examples.tr: Based on the plan, construction will begin next month.

examples.jp: 最新の統計に基づいて政策を見直す。
examples.tr: The policy is being reviewed based on the latest statistics.

examples.jp: 会社は社内規定に基づいて処分を行った。
examples.tr: The company took disciplinary action based on its internal regulations.

976.explain:
Formal nuance; often found in administrative documents, laws, reports, and guidelines.
Nouns before「に基づいて」are usually:法律,規則,方針,計画, データ,統計,事実, マニュアル,基準, エビデンス.
Used when you need to emphasize that an action is reasonable/conforms to standards.
If you want to emphasize “following, staying close to a direction/criteria” during the process, consider 「～に沿って」.

～に基づいて expresses “based on, on the grounds of” an objective basis (data, facts, laws, standards, plans) for carrying out an action/making a decision/giving an evaluation.
• Focuses on the foundation/basis underlying the action.
• Often used with verbs such as: 判断する, 決定する, 設計する, 作成する, 評価する, 対応する.
• Different from ～をもとに: 「に基づいて」 emphasizes officialness, objectivity, and standards; 「をもとに」 can carry the nuance of “taking inspiration/material” to adapt or compile.
• Close to ～に則って/に即して (in accordance with norms and standards), but 「に基づいて」 emphasizes the “basis” more than “strict compliance”.
• Can also be used with a negative basis to advise against something: 感情に基づいて判断してはいけない。

rows: <ruby>統計<rt>とうけい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>基<rt>もと</rt></ruby>づいて<ruby>決<rt>き</rt></ruby>める
<ruby>小説<rt>しょうせつ</rt></ruby>をもとに<ruby>映画<rt>えいが</rt></ruby><ruby>化<rt>か</rt></ruby>する

Has 2 meanings: to follow; or a change in A causes B to change
<ruby>指示<rt>しじ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>従<rt>したが</rt></ruby>って<ruby>行動<rt>こうどう</rt></ruby>する

mistakes: Confusing it with ～をもとに: for “a movie based on a novel” → 「小説をもとに」 is more natural than 「に基づいて」.
Using it for “following a route” → use 「～に沿って」 instead of 「～に基づいて」.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に基づいて」 must be a noun.
The JLPT often asks you to choose among 「に基づいて／に沿って／をもとに」 based on context: laws/regulations → 「に基づいて」; routes/criteria → 「に沿って」; creating/compiling → 「をもとに」.
976.notes:
• Memory tip: 「基」= foundation, 「基づく」= based on a foundation.
• If the sentence emphasizes a source of inspiration or reference material → prefer 「～をもとに」.
• The linking form 「N に基づく/に基づいた N」 is very natural in report headings.
• In casual spoken language you may hear 「にもとづいて」 pronounced as plain kana. meaning_vi: Taking ～ as a basis, grounds ⏐ explain: Used in written language. ⏐ examples: 1. この工事は市の計画に基づいて進められます。
This construction work is being carried out based on the city's plan.
2. 長年の経験に基づき新入社員を教育する。
New employees are trained based on many years of experience.

examples.jp: 彼女は親の期待に応えて、いい会社に就職した。
examples.tr: She lived up to her parents' expectations and got a job at a good company.

examples.jp: お客様の要望に応えて、開店時間を３０分早めることにいたしました。
examples.tr: In response to our customers' requests, we have decided to open 30 minutes earlier.

examples.jp: お客様の声に応えて、営業時間を延長します。
examples.tr: In response to customer feedback, we will extend our business hours.

examples.jp: ファンの期待に応えて、名演技を見せた。
examples.tr: They gave a brilliant performance that lived up to the fans' expectations.

examples.jp: 市場の需要に応える新製品を開発した。
examples.tr: We developed a new product that meets market demand.

examples.jp: 要請に応え、自衛隊が派遣された。
examples.tr: In response to the request, the Self-Defense Forces were dispatched.

977.explain:
Positive nuance; often used with verbs expressing concrete actions:実施する,開催する,改善する,延長する,用意する,開発する.
Can be used in both spoken and written language; the form 「に応え」 has a written-language nuance.
The subject acts with volition and effort to respond.
To say “respond to cheers”, you often see:声援に応えて手を振る.

～に応えて expresses the action of “meeting, responding to” expectations, requests, appeals, needs, etc. from other people/society.
• The target is usually a wish/expectation/request from people or organizations: 期待, 要望, 依頼, 要請, リクエスト, 声援, ニーズ, 需要.
• Emphasizes the subject's effort to satisfy them in response.
• Different from ～に応じて: 「に応じて」 = “depending on/in accordance with (conditions)”, while 「に応えて」 = “in response to (a request/expectation)” from another party.

rows: Emphasizes the subject satisfying a request
<ruby>要望<rt>ようぼう</rt></ruby>に<ruby>応<rt>こた</rt></ruby>えて<ruby>増便<rt>ぞうびん</rt></ruby>する
Changes flexibly according to the situation
<ruby>人数<rt>にんずう</rt></ruby>に<ruby>応<rt>おう</rt></ruby>じて<ruby>席<rt>せき</rt></ruby>を<ruby>用意<rt>ようい</rt></ruby>する

“<ruby>答<rt>こた</rt></ruby>える” is used for questions/exercises
<ruby>質問<rt>しつもん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>答<rt>こた</rt></ruby>えてください
<ruby>方針<rt>ほうしん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>沿<rt>そ</rt></ruby>って<ruby>進<rt>すす</rt></ruby>める

mistakes: Confusing it with 「に応じて」. If the meaning is “depending on quantity/conditions” → use 「に応じて」, not 「に応えて」.
Using 「質問に応えて」 instead of 「質問に答えて」 → likely to be considered unnatural. Standard: 質問に答えて.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に応えて」 must be a noun.
JLPT collocation trap: 需要/期待/要望/声援 usually go with 「に応えて」; 人数/状況/年齢/収入 usually go with 「に応じて」.
977.notes:
• Kanji distinction: 応える (meet expectations) vs 答える (answer a question).
• Common phrases in the news: 「市民の要望に応えて～」「需要に応える～」.
• Polite negative in announcements: 「ご期待に応えることができません。」
meaning_vi: 相手(あいて)からの希望(きぼう)、要求(ようきゅう)、等(など)に応(おう)じて
To respond to
examples: 1. 選手たちは会場の声援にこたえて手を振った/大活躍した。
In response to the cheers from the venue, the athletes waved.
2. 学校は学生の用法にこたえ、図書館の利用時間を延長した。
The school extended the library's opening hours in response to the students' wishes.
3. きょうの晩ご飯は、子どもたちのリクエストに応えてハンバーグにした。
For dinner tonight, we had hamburger steak at the children's request.
4. 私は成績が悪く、親の期待に応えることができなかった。
My grades were poor, and I couldn't live up to my parents' expectations. meaning_vi: In response to, responding to… ⏐ explain: Responding to an action from outside. N is a noun indicating questions, expectations, wishes, etc.
Kanji: 応えて・応え・答える ⏐ examples: 1. 客の意見にこたえて、営業時間を延長する。
Extend business hours in response to customers' opinions.
2. 親の期待にこたえ、がんばった。
I worked hard to live up to my parents' expectations.

examples.jp: 収入に応じて納税額が決まる。
examples.tr: The amount of tax is determined according to income.

examples.jp: 人数に応じて席を増やします。
examples.tr: We will add more seats depending on the number of people.

examples.jp: 状況に応じ、対応策を変える。
examples.tr: We change our countermeasures depending on the situation.

examples.jp: 能力に応じたクラスを選べる。
examples.tr: You can choose a class suited to your ability.

examples.jp: 天候に応じて出発時間を調整します。
examples.tr: We will adjust the departure time depending on the weather.

examples.jp: お客様の希望に応じてカスタマイズ可能です。
examples.tr: It can be customized according to the customer's wishes.

978.explain:
Neutral-to-formal nuance, suitable for announcements, regulations, and service descriptions.
Used with verbs indicating change/adjustment:変わる,変える,決める,調整する,分ける,対応する.
To express “changing together” naturally over time/a process, you can also use 「～につれて／～に従って」.

～に応じて expresses change/adjustment to suit conditions, situations, quantities, degree, ability, etc.
• Often used when the result/measure is flexible according to the input criteria.
• Typical targets: 年齢, 能力, 状況, 希望, 人数, 収入, 需要, レベル, 天候, 予算.
• Different from ～によって (because of/depending on), 「に応じて」 emphasizes corresponding adjustment, not necessarily a cause.
• Different from ～に応えて: 「に応じて」 does not mean “responding to” someone's specific expectations/requests.

mistakes: Confusing it with 「に応えて」: if it is “someone's request/expectation” → use 「に応えて」, not 「に応じて」.
Using 「によって」 instead of 「に応じて」 loses the nuance of “flexible adjustment”.
Wrong part of speech: it attaches only to nouns.
JLPT collocation trap: 料金/課題/クラス/対応/調整 → often go with 「に応じて」.
978.notes:
• Memory tip: 「応」 = respond/cope → 「に応じて」 = “respond accordingly”.
• The linking form 「N に応じた N」 is very common in advertising/services: ご希望に応じたプラン.
• When the subject “accepts/responds” (agrees to take part), the verb 「応じる」 is used on its own: 募集に応じる＝apply.
meaning_vi: 変化(へんか)、耐用性(たいようせい)に合(あ)わせて
Depending on, in accordance with
examples: 1. 本校では学生のレベルに応じてクラス分けを行います。
At this school, classes are divided according to the students' level.

In line with the diversification of learning purposes, teaching methods and materials also need to be more carefully devised.

In an emergency, you need to deal flexibly with the situation.
4. 最近は電気製品もカラフルになり、好みに応じて色が選べる。
These days, electrical appliances have also become colorful, so you can choose a color according to your taste.
5. 当ホテルでは、お客様一人一人のニーズに応じたサービスを提供いたします。
At our hotel, we offer services that meet the needs of each guest.
6. 他からの働きかけに対してこたえる
7. ボランティアの募集に多くの若者が応じた。
Many young people responded to the call for volunteers.
8. 注文が殺到し、応じきれなくなった。
Orders flooded in, and we could no longer keep up with them.

examples.jp: そんな話、嘘に決まっている。
examples.tr: A story like that is bound to be a lie.

examples.jp: 初めてなら、緊張するに決まっている。
examples.tr: If it's your first time, of course you'll be nervous.

examples.jp: あの高級店は値段が高いに決まってる。
examples.tr: That high-end restaurant is bound to be expensive.

examples.jp: 彼は忙しいから、今日来られないに決まっている。
examples.tr: He's busy, so he definitely won't be able to come today.

examples.jp: この問題は難しくない？— いや、難しいに決まってるよ。
examples.tr: Isn't this problem hard? — No way, of course it's hard.

examples.jp: あの態度なら、誤解されるに決まっている。
examples.tr: With an attitude like that, you're bound to be misunderstood.

979.explain:
Often used in conversation; to be more polite, use 「～に決まっています」.
The colloquial contracted form is 「～に決まってる」, emphasized with 「じゃん／でしょ」.
Can sound pushy; be careful when speaking to superiors.
Can be used with the past to make a conjecture about the past: ～に決まっていた.

～に決まっている expresses a strong subjective judgment: “surely…, of course… (based on the speaker's conjecture/context/experience)”.
• Assertive nuance, sometimes implying criticism/asserting the obvious.
• Used with both affirmative and negative: ～ないに決まっている.
• Different from ～に違いない: 「に決まっている」 is more emotional and colloquial; 「に違いない」 is more formal and objective.
• Not used when the speaker already knows for sure from solid evidence (in that case, simply state the fact).

rows: <ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>勝<rt>か</rt></ruby>つに<ruby>決<rt>き</rt></ruby>まってる
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>医者<rt>いしゃ</rt></ruby>だに<ruby>違<rt>ちが</rt></ruby>いない
<ruby>事実<rt>じじつ</rt></ruby>だに<ruby>相違<rt>そうい</rt></ruby>ない
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>ができるわけがない

mistakes: Mechanically adding だ before に決まっている with N/な: 「学生だに決まっている」 is usually unnatural → 「学生に決まっている」.
Using it for an obvious, already known fact instead of a conjecture → redundant and inappropriate.
Confusing it with 「に違いない」 in formal written language: the JLPT usually chooses 「に違いない」 rather than 「に決まっている」.
The tone is too strong and impolite in business emails; use 「～に違いありません／～と思われます」 instead.
979.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～に違いない.
→ ～に決まっている is a very strong assertion, carrying the emotion “of course”.
2) Often used in spoken language, with a subjective nuance.
→ Can easily sound assertive, sometimes a bit pushy.
3) Not used when the degree of certainty is low.
→ If it is only “probably”, use ～だろう／～かもしれない.

examples.jp: この道は海岸線に沿って伸びている。
examples.tr: This road runs along the coastline.

examples.jp: マニュアルに沿って対応してください。
examples.tr: Please handle it according to the manual.

examples.jp: カリキュラムに沿い授業を進める。
examples.tr: Classes proceed according to the curriculum.

examples.jp: 会社の方針に沿った評価制度を導入した。
examples.tr: We introduced an evaluation system in line with company policy.

examples.jp: 川に沿う遊歩道が整備された。
examples.tr: A walking path along the river has been built.

examples.jp: 予算に沿って計画を見直す。
examples.tr: We will revise the plan in line with the budget.

980.explain:
Used to emphasize not deviating from guidelines/criteria/a path.
Common nouns:方針,規則,規定,目標,計画, マニュアル, カリキュラム,地図,境界線,川/道/線.
Suitable for guidelines/procedure documents; in geographical descriptions it has the literal meaning “along”.

～に沿って has two main layers of meaning:
• Along (literal meaning): going/moving along a road, riverbank, route, or boundary.
• Closely following (figurative meaning): carrying out work in line with an established policy, criteria, plan, guideline, or goal, avoiding deviation.
• Emphasizes adherence to a “guiding line/criteria”, unlike 「に基づいて」 (emphasizes an objective basis) and 「に応じて」 (emphasizes flexible adjustment).

rows: <ruby>方針<rt>ほうしん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>沿<rt>そ</rt></ruby>って<ruby>実施<rt>じっし</rt></ruby>する
データに<ruby>基<rt>もと</rt></ruby>づいて<ruby>判断<rt>はんだん</rt></ruby>する
<ruby>指示<rt>しじ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>従<rt>したが</rt></ruby>って<ruby>動<rt>うご</rt></ruby>く
～に<ruby>即<rt>そく</rt></ruby>して／に<ruby>則<rt>そく</rt></ruby>して
<ruby>実情<rt>じつじょう</rt></ruby>に<ruby>即<rt>そく</rt></ruby>して<ruby>見直<rt>みなお</rt></ruby>す
<ruby>相手<rt>あいて</rt></ruby>に<ruby>合<rt>あ</rt></ruby>わせて<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>す

mistakes: Confusing it with 「に基づいて」: if you need to emphasize “a scientific/data basis”, prefer 「に基づいて」.
Confusing it with 「に応じて」: 「に沿って」 does not express “changing flexibly depending on conditions”.
Using it with verbs of change over time such as 「増える/減る」 to express proportional change → 「につれて／に従って」 is more natural.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に沿って」 is a noun.
980.notes:
• Visualize it: draw “a line” and then follow along that line → 「に沿って」.
• In quality procedures, a common pair is: マニュアルに沿って（carry out）＋ 記録に基づいて（prove）.
• For places/roads, you can replace it with 「沿い（ぞい）」 as in 名詞＋沿いの道. explain: Expresses doing something according to, following, or conforming to something.
Kanji: 沿い ⏐ examples: 1. 資料に沿って、ご説明いたします。
I will explain following the materials.
2. お客様ひとりひとりのご希望に沿った旅行プランをお作りします。
We create travel plans in line with the wishes of each customer.

981.meaning:
きっと～だと思(おも)う（強(つよ)い確信(かくしん)）（書(か)き言葉(ことば)） ＝～違(ちが)いない（N3)
Without doubt, certainly

examples.jp: これだけの証拠がある以上、犯人はあの人の男に相違ないと思われる。
examples.tr: With this much evidence, it seems certain that the culprit is that man.

examples.jp: 双方が譲歩しなければ、交渉は決裂するに相違ない。
examples.tr: If neither side compromises, the negotiations will undoubtedly break down.

examples.jp: 今の状況が続けば今年の収支は赤字になるに相違なく、何らかの対策を立てる必要があります。
examples.tr: If the current situation continues, this year's balance will undoubtedly be in the red, so some kind of countermeasure is needed.

examples.jp: *「これは私のものに相違（/違い）ありません。
examples.tr: *This is undoubtedly mine.

examples.jp: 調べ結果、それはその時代にかかれた絵に相違ないそうです。
examples.tr: According to the investigation, it is undoubtedly a painting made in that period.

examples.jp:
〈裁判〉
A: ここに書かれていることは事実ですか。
B: はい、事実に相違ありません。
examples.tr:
〈Court〉
A: Is what is written here true?
B: Yes, it is true without a doubt.

981.notes:
Source taken from (Marugoto grammar_n2; the original grammar entry lacks に: ～相違ない).
Marugoto: similar to ～に違いない but stiffer and more formal; the form 相違ありません is used in documents and confirmation papers.

982.connection: V plain form + に過ぎない に過ぎません / N + (である) / Na + (である) / Aい

examples.jp: あの子はとてもしっかりしているけど、まだ高校生に過ぎない。
examples.tr: That kid is very mature, but is still just a high school student.

examples.jp: 彼はいろいろ言っているけど、言い訳をしているに過ぎない。
examples.tr: He says all sorts of things, but he's merely making excuses.

examples.jp: まだ１次試験を通ったにすぎません。これからが大変なんです。
examples.tr: I've only passed the first-round exam. The hard part starts now.

examples.jp: それは噂に過ぎない。
examples.tr: That's nothing more than a rumor.

examples.jp: 彼の成功は運が良かったに過ぎない。
examples.tr: His success was merely a matter of good luck.

examples.jp: このグラフは傾向を示すに過ぎない。
examples.tr: This graph merely shows a trend.

982.explain:
Usually placed at the end of a clause to conclude by downplaying: …に過ぎない。
Used in objective/argumentative writing; it avoids the sense of a direct attack more than ただの…だ.
Used with emphasizing words: ただ/単なる/所詮+ N + に過ぎない → strengthens the low evaluation.
Suitable for reports, academic writing, and news; it can also be used in conversation but sounds serious.

• Core meaning: asserts a small, limited degree/substance: “only… nothing more; not exceeding…”.
• Discourse implication: downplays importance, negates exaggeration/expectations.
• With figures: emphasizes that they are for reference only/not absolute (この数字は目安に過ぎない).
• More formal and objective nuance than だけだ; often used in writing, reports, and presentations.
• Not used to express obligation/rules; purely an evaluation of degree.

rows: More neutral and colloquial than に<ruby>過<rt>す</rt></ruby>ぎない
Often written entirely in kana in everyday texts
Expresses obligation due to having no choice; not an evaluation of degree
にすぎず（<ruby>連用<rt>れんよう</rt></ruby>）
<ruby>推測<rt>すいそく</rt></ruby>にすぎず、<ruby>証拠<rt>しょうこ</rt></ruby>はない。
ただの<ruby>偶然<rt>ぐうぜん</rt></ruby>だ。

mistakes: Confusing it with しかない: しかない = “have no choice but to”, while に過ぎない = “merely”.
Dropping である when formality is needed with Na/N: writing 重要だに過ぎない is unnatural → 重要であるに過ぎない.
Overusing it in casual speech makes the sentence sound distant; replace it with だけだ when you need to sound natural.
Wrong placement: この結果は仮説に過ぎない（correct）; 仮説過ぎない（incorrect).
982.notes:
• After a long clause, use であるに過ぎない to make the sentence sound formal and emphasize its rationality.
• In debates, it can be combined with たかが/所詮 to lower the value of the target: たかが噂に過ぎない。
• Be careful with the nuance toward the other person: it can easily be taken as belittling their effort/value.
meaning_vi: ただ～たけだ（程度(ていど)の低(ひく)さを強調(きょうちょう)）
Merely
examples: 1. その航空機事故で助かったのは、５００人中４人にすぎなかった。
Only 4 out of 500 people survived that plane crash.
2. 汚職事件が摘発されたが、あんなものは氷山一角にすぎないと思われない。
Although the corruption case was exposed, that is only the tip of the iceberg.
3. 彼女はロシア話ができるといっても、ちょっとした挨拶ができるにすぎない。
She says she can speak Russian, but she can only manage simple greetings.
4. 「お礼だなんて、とんでもない。当然の子をしたにすぎないんですから」
[No need to thank me, I only did what anyone should do]
──────
1. ①　５％以下にすぎない
Only 5% or less
2. ②　高校に進学しない人は、５％以下にすぎない。
People who do not go on to high school account for only 5% or less.
3. ③　彼のスピーチは長かったが、同じことを言っているにすぎなかった。
His speech was long, but he was only saying the same things. explain: Used to emphasize a low degree: “Only to that extent, no more.”
Formal sentence style. ⏐ examples: 1. 単なる言い間違いにすぎない。
It is simply nothing more than a slip of the tongue.
2. 簡単な日常英会話ができるにすぎない。
I can merely hold a simple everyday conversation in English.

examples.jp: これは、命にかかわる大変重要なことです。
examples.tr: This is an extremely important matter where lives are at stake.

examples.jp: 音楽に関わる仕事をしたいと思っています。
examples.tr: I'd like to have a job related to music.

983.notes: Expresses the meaning “to affect” or “to be related to.” ①～④ mean “to affect.” Nouns denoting things that can be affected, such as 「名誉、評判、生死、合否」, are used. ⑤～⑦ mean “to be related to” or “to have a connection with,” and nouns denoting “people,” “work,” “events,” etc. are used.（４２９）

984.meaning:
①～の場合(ばあい)は（不思議(ふしぎ)に）…だ（多(おお)くの場合(ばあい)は不満(ふまん)な気持(きも)ち）
Particularly... just when

examples.jp: 宿題をして来なかった日に限って先生に当てられる。
examples.tr: It's always on the day I haven't done my homework that the teacher calls on me.

examples.jp: 私がかさを持っていないときに限って雨が降るんだから！
examples.tr: It always rains precisely when I don't have an umbrella!

examples.jp: いつもは朝寝坊の夫がゴルフに行く日に限って早起きできるのは不思議だ。
examples.tr: It's strange that my husband, who usually oversleeps, manages to get up early only on the days he goes golfing.

examples.jp: 「だいじょうぶ、だいじょうぶ」と言う人に限って、なんかあったときには頼りにならないことが多い。
examples.tr: People who say “It's fine, it's fine” are often the very ones you can't rely on when something happens.

examples.jp: 信頼しているひとが～するはずがない
examples.tr: Someone you trust couldn't possibly do ~

examples.jp: あの山田さんに限って、無断欠勤するなて考えられない。何かあったに違いない。
examples.tr: I can't imagine Yamada, of all people, missing work without notice. Something must have happened.

985.meaning: Means “not limited to that scope, but extending to a wider scope”.

examples.jp: お申し込みは平日に限らず、土日でも受け付けております。
examples.tr: Applications are accepted not only on weekdays but also on Saturdays and Sundays.

examples.jp: 最近では夏に限らず冬でもアイスクリームがよく売れるようだ。
examples.tr: These days, ice cream seems to sell well not only in summer but in winter too.

examples.jp: * テレビゲームに夢中になるのは子どもに限らない。
examples.tr: * It is not only children who get absorbed in video games.

examples.jp: * 社長のやり方がおかしいと思っているのは、私に限るまい。
examples.tr: * I am surely not the only one who thinks the president's way of doing things is strange.

examples.jp: 日本に限らず
examples.tr: Not only in Japan

examples.jp: この小説は、日本に限らず、海外でも有名だ。
examples.tr: This novel is famous not only in Japan but also abroad.

985.explain: ◎ Expresses that something applies not only within that scope but within an even wider scope.
985.notes:
examples: 1. この食堂は、学生に限らず、誰でも利用できる。
This cafeteria can be used by anyone, not only students.
2. 今回に限らず、田中さんにはいつもお世話になっている。
Not only this time—Mr. Tanaka always helps me out.

986.meaning:
「～が一番いい・～がいちばんいい方法だ。」客観的な事実ではなくて、話者が主観的に言うときに使う。
~ is the best / is the best way.
This structure is used when the speaker wants to express their subjective impression rather than an objective fact. | Nothing beats…, the best thing is…

examples.jp: デザイナー募集。経験者に限る。
examples.tr: Designer wanted. Experienced applicants only.

examples.jp: ６５歳以上の方に限り無料です。
examples.tr: Free only for those aged 65 and over.

examples.jp: レポートはパソコンで書いたものに限ります。
examples.tr: Only reports written on a computer are accepted.

examples.jp: 夏休みに限って教室での飲食が認められている。
examples.tr: Eating and drinking in the classroom is permitted only during summer vacation.

examples.jp: 漢字を書く力が落ちているのは、若者に限ってことではない。
examples.tr: It is not only young people whose ability to write kanji is declining.

examples.jp: やっぱり映画は映画館で見るに限る。
examples.tr: Movies really are best watched in a movie theater.

986.notes: Used to assert that 「…が一番だ」 (“…is the best”). Often preceded by 「…なら／たら」.

examples.jp: ご利用に際して、身分証の提示が必要です。
examples.tr: Identification must be presented when using the service.

examples.jp: 契約を締結するに際して、内容を十分にご確認ください。
examples.tr: When concluding the contract, please check its contents thoroughly.

examples.jp: 入学するに際して、多くの方に支えられました。
examples.tr: When I entered school, I was supported by many people.

examples.jp: 赴任に際し、皆様にご挨拶申し上げます。
examples.tr: On taking up my new post, I would like to extend my greetings to you all.

examples.jp: 登録に際しまして、同意が必要となります。
examples.tr: Consent is required upon registration.

examples.jp: 入院に際して、いくつかの注意事項を説明された。
examples.tr: When I was admitted to the hospital, several precautions were explained to me.

987.explain:
Used in official documents, speeches, user guides, and contracts.
Following a Sino-Japanese noun, it creates a ceremonial nuance: ご利用に際して／開館に際して.
Accompanies requests, rules, and ceremonial expressions of thanks/apology.

• Establishes the point in time when an important event begins/takes place, to attach notes, thanks, or requests.
• More formal in nuance than ～とき, close to ～にあたって but leaning toward “the time it takes place”/ceremony.
• Often used with: 入学／卒業／ご利用／ご登録／契約／開業／赴任／受賞 など.
• Rarely used for unexpected negative incidents; if negative, consider the more neutral ～際に (さいに).

rows: Emphasizes the point in time of a ceremony/important event
<ruby>入社<rt>にゅうしゃ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>際<rt>さい</rt></ruby>して<ruby>挨拶<rt>あいさつ</rt></ruby>する。
<ruby>開業<rt>かいぎょう</rt></ruby>にあたって<ruby>計画<rt>けいかく</rt></ruby>を<ruby>練<rt>ね</rt></ruby>る。
<ruby>来日<rt>らいにち</rt></ruby>の<ruby>際<rt>さい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>ください。

mistakes: Using it for small everyday actions (毎朝起きるに際して…) → unnatural; use とき.
Confusing it with にあたって: exam questions often require choosing the appropriate nuance (preparation vs. ceremony).
Forgetting the polite variant in formal documents: you should use に際し／に際しまして.
987.notes:
• In speeches: “この場をお借りして” often goes with “就任に際し”.
• The polite variant “～に際しまして” is common in service/IT notices when displaying terms and conditions.
• For unexpected negative events (事故・災害), prefer “際に/とき”; “に際して” sounds dry and unnatural.
meaning_vi: On the occasion of…, at the time of/when… (formal)
examples: 1. ①　受験に際しては、必ず受験票を持参してください。
2. ②　〈大学の掲示板〉奨学金の申し込みに際して、以下のような条件があります。よく確かめた上で、申し込みをしてください。
meaning_vi: ～（特別(とくべつ)なこと）の前(まえ)に、～のときに
When
examples: 1. 就職に際して、多くの先輩にお世話になった。
When I got a job, I received a lot of help from many seniors.
2. 黒田氏はアメリカ大塗料来日際し、通訳を務めた。
Mr. Kuroda served as interpreter when the U.S. president came to Japan.
3. 海外駐在員を選ぶに際しては、仕事の能力だけではなく性格も考慮すべきだ。
When selecting staff to be posted overseas, one should consider not only their work ability but also their personality.
4. 「ここに入院に際しての注意事項が書いてありますから、読んでおいてください」
“The precautions for hospital admission are written here, so please read them beforehand.”
meaning_vi: When starting…, while…
explain: Means at the point of starting some special matter, or while that matter is in progress.
It is a solemn style. Formal, stiff language.
examples: 1. お申し込みに際しては、写真が必要となります。
A photo is required when applying.
2. A氏は日本を訪問するに際し、喜びを語った。
Mr. A spoke of his joy on the occasion of visiting Japan.

988.meaning: To do to the end, persevere…

examples.jp: 決めたことは最後までやりぬきなさい。
examples.tr: Whatever you have decided, see it through to the end.

examples.jp: 彼は初マラソンで42.195キロを走り抜いた。
examples.tr: He ran the full 42.195 km in his first marathon.

examples.jp: 考え抜いた末に、会社を辞めて独立することにした。
examples.tr: After thinking it through thoroughly, I decided to quit the company and go independent.

examples.jp: A氏は戦時下を生き抜き、戦後は祖国は復興に尽くした。
examples.tr: Mr. A survived the war years, and after the war he devoted himself to rebuilding his homeland.

examples.jp: 悩み/耐え/がんばり/困り＋ぬく
examples.tr: worry to the utmost / endure to the end / persevere to the end / be utterly at a loss

examples.jp: 苦しい時期を耐えぬいて、ようやく成功をつかんだ。
examples.tr: Having endured a difficult period to the end, I finally achieved success.

988.explain:
Used when you want to honor effort and will: has a positive, encouraging nuance.
Not used for instantaneous actions/actions lacking duration (×笑いぬく). Suitable for continuous/long-term actions.
Often appears in slogans, self-introductions, and inspirational writing: やりぬく力,最後までやりぬく.
The kanji抜く is often used in formal writing; kana ぬく is friendlier and softer.

• Expresses doing something “to the end, completely” through perseverance and overcoming difficulties: Vます + ぬく = do V to the end.
• Nuance: emphasizes a long process with many challenges; the speaker evaluates the effort highly.
• Unlike simple “完了/completion”, 〜ぬく implies persistent will and endurance (耐える、努力する、守る...).
• Often used with verbs expressing prolonged effort: 耐える・守る・戦う・走る・生きる・考える・やる・読み/書き（large amounts/difficult）.

rows: Do to the end, overcome difficulties
Focuses on the completed result, not necessarily involving difficulty
Emphasizes holding firm to a stance/action
<ruby>主義<rt>しゅぎ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>貫<rt>つらぬ</rt></ruby>き<ruby>通<rt>とお</rt></ruby>す
Leans toward pouring in all one's strength and heart
<ruby>患者<rt>かんじゃ</rt></ruby>のために<ruby>尽<rt>つ</rt></ruby>くす
Different meaning (intransitive verb), not a completion pattern

mistakes: Confusing it with “〜ぬ” (archaic negative: 行かぬ). “〜ぬく” is a completion/perseverance suffix, not a negative.
Using it with punctual verbs → unnatural: ×驚きぬく, ×気づきぬく.
Confusing the nuance with 〜きる: 〜きる = completion; 〜ぬく = completion after overcoming difficulties. The JLPT often asks you to distinguish them.
Forgetting to write the kanji: “抜く” is common in formal written language; however, kana “ぬく” is still correct.
988.notes:
• “考えぬいた末（すえ）に” is a common written-language phrase, expressing a process of careful thought before making a decision.
• “〜ぬく” can be used in the potential form if the base verb has a potential form: 耐えぬける is unnatural; use 耐えきれる? => For “able to endure”, 耐えきれる/耐え切れる is more natural.
• In PR/recruitment: “困難に立ち向かい、最後までやりぬく人材を求めます。”
explain: ◎ Not giving up, continuing to the end.
examples: 1. これが、彼らが考え抜いて出した結論だった。
This was the conclusion they reached after thinking it through thoroughly.
2. 途中で何度かあきらめかけたが、最後まで走り抜いた。
I almost gave up several times, but in the end I ran all the way.
──────
1. ①　初めてのマラソンは思ったん以上にきつかったけど、最後まで走り抜くことができて、大満足です。
2. ②　〈コーヒー店で〉選び抜かれた豆だけを使った最高級の味を香りをお楽しみください。 meaning_vi: To do everything completely and fully, through a whole process or action.
Emphasizes the sense of completion after enduring hardship. ⏐ examples: 1. 大変な仕事でも、やり抜く自信があります。
Even if the work is hard, I am confident I can see it through to the end.
2. 彼はあきらめずにゴールまで走り抜いた。
He didn't give up and ran all the way to the finish line.

examples.jp: 明日までに報告書を提出せねばならない。
examples.tr: The report must be submitted by tomorrow.

examples.jp: 我々は約束を守らねばならない。
examples.tr: We must keep our promises.

examples.jp: 何としてもこのプロジェクトを成功させねばならない。
examples.tr: We must make this project succeed, no matter what.

examples.jp: 被災地の支援を急がねばならない。
examples.tr: Support for the disaster-stricken areas must be provided urgently.

examples.jp: 規則は遵守せねばならぬ。
examples.tr: Rules must be observed.

989.explain:
Used in formal statements, pledges, regulatory documents, and political statements/speeches.
In natural conversation, consider using ～なきゃ/～なくちゃ/～ないと instead.
The subject is usually “I/we/an organization”; directed at the listener, it can easily feel like a command.

• Expresses strong obligation: rules, responsibilities, self-imposed duties.
• Formal/classical nuance, sounds stiffer than ～なければならない; somewhat literary/rhetorical in tone.
• In everyday spoken language it is usually replaced by ～なきゃ／～なくちゃ／～なければならない.

rows: <ruby>守<rt>まも</rt></ruby>らなければならない。
<ruby>守<rt>まも</rt></ruby>らなくてはならない。
<ruby>延期<rt>えんき</rt></ruby>せざるを<ruby>得<rt>え</rt></ruby>ない。

mistakes: Wrong conjugation with する: “しねばならない” → incorrect; it must be “せねばならない”.
Confusing the nuance with ざるを得ない: the latter means “reluctantly having no choice”, not an obligation based on rules.
Using it in casual conversation → sounds stiff/theatrical; use なきゃ/ないと instead.
The JLPT often tests recognition of 未然形: 書く→書かねばならない; 食べる→食べねばならない.
989.notes:
• In headlines/slogans: ～せねばならない creates a strong, concise rhythm.
• Masculine/old-fashioned colloquial contracted form: ～ねばならん (not formal).
• With “～ねば”, “ならない” can be omitted in a rallying style: 守らねば！ (strong, archaic nuance).

991.connection: V/A plain form + のではないか / N・Na + なのではないか

examples.jp: 将来、ロボットが介護をする時代になるのではないかと思う。
examples.tr: I think there may come a time in the future when robots provide nursing care.

examples.jp: 留学することについて、彼女はまだ迷っているんじゃないかなあ。
examples.tr: I wonder if she's still undecided about studying abroad.

991.explain: ◎ An expression of conjecture about something.
991.notes: Attaches to plain-style expressions and expresses the speaker's conjectural judgment, along the lines of 「はっきりそうだと断定はできないが、おそらく…ではないだろうか」 (“I can't say for certain that it is so, but perhaps…”). The speaker's degree of certainty is lower than with 「だろう」.

993.connection: V plain form + のも + (は)もっともだ / N + も

examples.jp: 約束を破られて、君が怒るのももっともだ。
examples.tr: Since your promise was broken, it's only natural that you're angry.

examples.jp: 初めての発表なら、緊張するのももっともだ。
examples.tr: If it's your first presentation, it's only natural to be nervous.

examples.jp: 徹夜続きだったのだから、彼がミスをしたのももっともだ。
examples.tr: He had been staying up all night for days on end, so it's no wonder he made a mistake.

examples.jp: 物価がこれだけ上がれば、不満が出るのももっともだ。
examples.tr: With prices rising this much, it's only natural that there is discontent.

examples.jp: 子どもなんだから、泣くのももっともだ。
examples.tr: It's just a child, so it's only natural that it cries.

993.explain:
Usually follows a part stating the reason (～から/～ので/状況説明).
Used for a second or third person; used about yourself it can sound like self-justification, but it is not wrong when reflecting on yourself.
Standard, somewhat objective nuance; suitable for reports/evaluations.

Expresses “(A) is understandable/reasonable/natural”. The speaker judges an action/emotion/state to be reasonable based on the stated circumstances. Sympathetic, justifying nuance.
• Often used for other people's emotions/behavior: 怒る・悲しむ・心配する…
• Unlike command/volition: not used to give orders, only to state a judgment.
• Emphasizes objectivity more than 「～のも無理はない」 (less inclined toward “can't be blamed”).

rows: Nothing strange about it/can't be blamed
Emphasizes that it is unavoidable, more emotional
<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しすぎて、<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れるのも<ruby>無理<rt>むり</rt></ruby>はない
<ruby>当然<rt>とうぜん</rt></ruby>だ / <ruby>当<rt>あ</rt></ruby>たり<ruby>前<rt>まえ</rt></ruby>だ
Direct and stronger; can sound judgmental
<ruby>失敗<rt>しっぱい</rt></ruby>して<ruby>落<rt>お</rt></ruby>ち<ruby>込<rt>こ</rt></ruby>むのは<ruby>当然<rt>とうぜん</rt></ruby>だ
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>怒<rt>おこ</rt></ruby>るのも<ruby>道理<rt>どうり</rt></ruby>だ

mistakes: Confusing it with 「もっとも」 (conjunction) → 「だ」 is needed to make it a -だ adjective.
Attaching it directly to na-adjectives/N without 「な/である」: you need Aなのも/Nなのも or であるのも.
Using it to criticize others sounds contradictory: this pattern is essentially about sympathy/reasonableness.
Changing the subject between the reason part and the main clause makes the reference ambiguous (keep it consistent).
993.notes:
• 「もっとも」 is also a conjunction meaning “however/that said”: もっとも、例外もある。 Do not confuse it with 「もっともだ」.
• The tense/modifier form can change: ～のももっともだった／～のももっともだろう to adjust tense/degree of certainty.
• The direct negative 「もっともではない」 is rarely used; it is usually replaced with another, softer pattern.

examples.jp: 理論の上では可能だが、実現は難しい。
examples.tr: It is possible in theory, but difficult to realize.

examples.jp: 地図の上では近いが、山道なので時間がかかる。
examples.tr: It is close on the map, but it takes time because it's a mountain road.

examples.jp: 書類の上では彼は正社員になっている。
examples.tr: On paper, he is a full-time employee.

examples.jp: 統計の上では景気は回復しているという結果だ。
examples.tr: According to the statistics, the economy is recovering.

examples.jp: 法律の上では差別は禁止されている。
examples.tr: Legally, discrimination is prohibited.

994.explain:
Usually followed by a second clause expressing a contrasting reality or adding context.
Style: neutral → formal; suitable for documents, reports, and news.
Not used to indicate a sequence in time/of actions (that is a different meaning of上で).

～の上では states a judgment “from the standpoint of A / according to A / on paper…”, emphasizing a theoretical perspective, documents, figures, or maps. Common implication: reality may differ (contrast between theory and reality).
• Semantic domain: 理論・記録・統計・法律・書類・地図・規則 など.
• Often used in contrasting pairs: Nの上では～が、実際は～／現場では～.
• Different from 「上で(うえで)＝after/in order to」; here it means “in terms of”.

rows: Neutral, does not imply a contrast with reality
<ruby>統計<rt>とうけい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>関<rt>かん</rt></ruby>しては<ruby>詳<rt>くわ</rt></ruby>しい
<ruby>研究<rt>けんきゅう</rt></ruby>において<ruby>重要<rt>じゅうよう</rt></ruby>だ
<ruby>確認<rt>かくにん</rt></ruby>した<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>提出<rt>ていしゅつ</rt></ruby>する
<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>する<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>大切<rt>たいせつ</rt></ruby>だ

mistakes: Confusing it with 「Vた上で」: exam questions often set traps to distinguish “in terms of” vs. “after”.
Omitting 「は」 after 「上で」 makes the meaning unclear; on the exam, choose 「上では」 for the meaning “on paper”.
Using it with nouns that cannot be an “aspect” (e.g., 人の上では) → unnatural.
994.notes:
• 「見かけの上では」「形式の上では」「制度の上では」 are phrases common in journalistic writing.
• In spoken language, 「上では」 can drop 「は」 and become 「上で」, but this is easily confused with the other meaning; keep 「は」 when writing.
• Precede it with a nominalized phrase to make the aspect clear: 実験結果の上では／理屈の上では…

examples.jp: 冗談はさておき、今後の方針について話しましょう。
examples.tr: Joking aside, let's talk about our future policy.

examples.jp: 結果が出るかどうかはさておき、まず行動に移すべきだ。
examples.tr: Setting aside whether it will produce results, we should first put it into action.

examples.jp: 値段はさておき、安全性を最優先に考える。
examples.tr: Price aside, safety is our top priority.

examples.jp: 彼の責任があるかないかはさておき、問題解決が先だ。
examples.tr: Setting aside whether or not he is responsible, solving the problem comes first.

examples.jp: デザインはさておき、機能面は申し分ない。
examples.tr: Design aside, the functionality is flawless.

examples.jp: 費用の問題はさておき、今一番行ってみたいところはどこですか。
examples.tr: Setting aside the question of cost, where would you most like to go right now?

995.explain:
Usually placed at the beginning of a sentence, as a signal of a transition/priority.
Used when there are two parallel criteria/topics but you want to focus on B.
Avoid applying it bluntly to a sensitive target, as it can come across as rude to the listener.

• “Setting aside/not discussing N for now, (let's) discuss/prioritize B.” Used for a topic shift to something more important/urgent.
• Nuance of actively steering the conversation/discussion; somewhat polite, leaning toward written language, meetings, and presentations.
• Different from ignoring something permanently: it is set aside “temporarily” and can be returned to later.

rows: Set topic N aside for now
Nuance of steering the conversation; more formal
<ruby>冗談<rt>じょうだん</rt></ruby>はさておき、<ruby>本題<rt>ほんだい</rt></ruby>へ
<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>た<ruby>目<rt>め</rt></ruby>はともかく、<ruby>味<rt>あじ</rt></ruby>はいい
Implies excluding N from the scope of evaluation
<ruby>休日<rt>きゅうじつ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>別<rt>べつ</rt></ruby>として、<ruby>毎日<rt>まいにち</rt></ruby><ruby>早起<rt>はやお</rt></ruby>きだ
Adverb, does not mark a topic

mistakes: Using it in place of absolute “exclusion” → wrong nuance. ～はさておき means “set aside for now”, not “unrelated”.
Failing to nominalize an interrogative clause: × 行けるかはさておき → ◯ 行けるかどうかはさておき.
Placing it after an overly long phrase loses its switching effect; it should be placed early, at the beginning of the sentence.
995.notes:
• Origin “措く/置く”: to put aside → a natural nuance of changing direction.
• In presentations, it can be followed by “まず/先に/本題に入る”.
• Easily combined with pairs of contrasting criteria: 値段vs品質, 感情vs事実, 理想vs現実.

996.meaning: Speaking of / when it comes to ~

examples.jp: 今年の目標はというと、とにかく全国大会で優勝することだ。
examples.tr: As for this year's goal, it's to win the national tournament, no matter what.

examples.jp: 彼女はというと、参加するかどうか、まだ決めていないようだ。
examples.tr: As for her, she doesn't seem to have decided yet whether she'll participate.

examples.jp: 昨日の夜、地震があったそうですね。私はというと、ぐっすり眠っていて、全然気がつきませんでしたけど。
examples.tr: I heard there was an earthquake last night. As for me, I was sound asleep and didn't notice it at all.

examples.jp: その頃、日本はというと、仏教が人々の間に広がりつつあった。
examples.tr: As for Japan at that time, Buddhism was spreading among the people.

996.explain: ◎ An expression that presents a topic, used especially when you want to raise an issue to draw everyone's attention to it.

examples.jp: 彼のレポートは、内容はもとより、字の間違いも多く、評価が低かった。
examples.tr: His report received a low evaluation: besides its content, it had many spelling mistakes.

examples.jp: このアニメは、子供はもとより大人も十分楽しめる。
examples.tr: This anime can be fully enjoyed not only by children but by adults as well.

examples.jp: 日本語はもとより、英語や中国語も話せる。
examples.tr: I can speak not only Japanese but also English and Chinese.

examples.jp: 安全はもとより、品質管理にも細心の注意を払っている。
examples.tr: We pay close attention not only to safety but also to quality control.

examples.jp: 彼は礼儀はもとより、時間も必ず守る。
examples.tr: He is not only polite but also always punctual.

examples.jp: 学生はもとより、地域の人々まで参加している。
examples.tr: Not only students but even local residents are taking part.

998.explain:
Used when you want to emphasize “A goes without saying, and B also…” to broaden the scope or raise the standard.
Serious, polite style; suitable for reports, articles, and official speeches.
The second clause should have も/まで/さえ to show the extension; avoid creating an “empty” sentence that only states that A is obvious without main information afterward.
Not used to emphasize everyday personal feelings; in casual conversation, ～はもちろん/～は言うまでもなく is more natural.

• Meaning 1: “Let alone…, needless to say…, of course…”, used to present A as obvious and then extend the scope to B, C (… as well).
• Meaning 2: “Not only A but even B/C …” with a nuance emphasizing the degree of inclusiveness, often accompanied by も/まで/さえ in the second clause.
• Feel: formal, leaning toward written language, announcements, and presentations; stronger than ～はもちろん in its “of course” sense.
• Syntax: Part A (before はもとより) is usually a noun. If it is a clause, it must be nominalized with の/こと.
• Logic: A is the basis/obvious → B is also satisfied/included → a general conclusion is stated.

rows: Of course A, and B also …
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>はもとより、<ruby>海外<rt>かいがい</rt></ruby>でも<ruby>人気<rt>にんき</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>英語<rt>えいご</rt></ruby>はもちろん、<ruby>仏語<rt>ふつご</rt></ruby>もできる。
Similar in meaning, often placed at the beginning of a sentence like an adverbial
<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うまでもなく<ruby>健康<rt>けんこう</rt></ruby>が<ruby>一番<rt>いちばん</rt></ruby>だ。
Far from A, actually B (contrary to expectation)
<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>めるどころか、<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しい。

mistakes: Using it with a verb but forgetting to nominalize: × 努力するはもとより → ○ 努力するのはもとより
Missing an extending particle in the second clause: × Aはもとより、B。 → use Bも/まで/さえ to make the extension clear.
Confusing it with ～はもちろん in terms of style: the JLPT often asks about the more formal nuance of ～はもとより.
Wrong order of degree: the “obvious” information must be placed before はもとより.
998.notes:
• Often combined with inclusive words: も・まで・さえ to increase the emphasis.
• “もとより” also has the lexical meaning “from the start/originally”, which differs from this grammar structure; distinguish them by the presence or absence of は.
• In administrative writing/advertising: “安全はもとより、環境にも配慮しています。” is a stock sentence type.
• The A–B order should follow the degree: A is more obvious than B. Reversing them makes it less natural. meaning_vi: Not only, let alone. ⏐ explain: Presents things considered obvious to express the meaning “not only that, but there are also more important or lesser matters”
Used in a serious style typical of written language. ⏐ examples: 1. うちには、車はもとより自転車もないんです。
At my house, there's not only no car but not even a bicycle.
2. レタスはサラダで食べるのはもとより、炒めてもおいしい。
Lettuce is not only good eaten in salads, but also tasty stir-fried.

999.connection: V plain form + ばかりか / N / Na + な / Aい

examples.jp: 彼の研究は、日本ばかりか、海外からも注目されている。
examples.tr: His research is attracting attention not only in Japan but also from overseas.

examples.jp: 昨日行った店はおいしくないばかりか値段も高くて、もう二度と行きたくない。
examples.tr: The restaurant I went to yesterday wasn't good, and on top of that it was expensive. I never want to go there again.

examples.jp: 親ばかりか、姉も、私の留学に反対した。
examples.tr: Not only my parents but also my older sister opposed my studying abroad.

examples.jp: お金がなくて、旅行に行けないばかりか、外食もできない。
examples.tr: I have no money, so not only can I not go on a trip, I can't even eat out.

examples.jp: 女王は美しいばかりか心も優しかった。
examples.tr: The queen was not only beautiful but also kind-hearted.

examples.jp: この野菜はビタミンが豊富な(/である）ばかりか、がんを予防する働きもする。
examples.tr: Not only is this vegetable rich in vitamins, it also helps prevent cancer.

999.explain:
◎ An expression showing surprise, "not only that," and bringing up something else.
◎ It has the same meaning as「～ばかりなく」, but this expression is usually used in written language.

rows: Not only A but also B
Neutral, less nuance of surprise than ～ばかりか
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>日本語<rt>にほんご</rt></ruby>だけでなく<ruby>英語<rt>えいご</rt></ruby>も<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>せる。
In addition to A, also B
Leans toward listing information, less emphasis
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>加<rt>くわ</rt></ruby>えて<ruby>風<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>も<ruby>強<rt>つよ</rt></ruby>い。
Not only A, but also B (very formal)
Written language, journalism; close synonym of ～ばかりか
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>学業<rt>がくぎょう</rt></ruby>のみならずスポーツも<ruby>優秀<rt>ゆうしゅう</rt></ruby>だ。
Not A, but on the contrary B
<ruby>楽<rt>らく</rt></ruby>どころか、かえって<ruby>大変<rt>たいへん</rt></ruby>だ。
そればかりか、<ruby>費用<rt>ひよう</rt></ruby>まで<ruby>払<rt>はら</rt></ruby>った。

mistakes: Dropping も in the second clause: you need ～も/まで/さえ for the correct nuance of "unexpected addition."
Reversing the degree: putting the stronger information in A and the weaker in B weakens the rhetorical effect.
Confusing it with ～だけでなく when the question calls for a nuance of "unexpected/more serious" → choose ～ばかりか.
Overusing it with two different subjects makes the sentence ambiguous; prefer the same subject.
999.notes:
meaning_vi: Not only… but also… | Not only…, but also
explain: Used when B is unexpected and stronger than A in its positive/negative degree.
The style leans toward writing and presentations; in speech, ～だけでなく/～に加えて are common.
To emphasize an extreme degree, use まで/さえ in the second clause: ～ばかりか～まで/さえ.
Keep the two clauses parallel in word type (N—N; clause—clause) so it sounds natural.
The subject usually stays the same in both clauses; if it changes, make it clear to avoid ambiguity.
examples: 1. 彼は日本語ばかりか、フランス語も話せる。
He can speak not only Japanese but also French.
2. この冬は寒いばかりか、雪も多かった。
This winter was not only cold but also had a lot of snow.
3. その店は値段が高いばかりか、店員の態度も悪い。
That shop is not only expensive, but the staff's attitude is bad too.
4. 彼女は歌ばかりか、ダンスもプロ並みだ。
She is at a professional level not only in singing but also in dancing.
5. 事故で車ばかりか、荷物も壊れてしまった。
In the accident, not only the car but also the luggage was damaged.
──────
1. 彼は日本語ばかりか、英語も話せる。
He can speak not only Japanese but also English.
2. この店は値段が高いばかりか、サービスも悪い。
This shop is not only expensive, but the service is bad too.
3. 大雨で試合ばかりか、授業も中止になった。
Because of the heavy rain, not only the game but also classes were canceled.
4. 彼女は歌ばかりか、踊りも上手だ。
She is good not only at singing but also at dancing.
5. そればかりか、交通費まで出してくれた。
Not only that, they even paid for my transportation.
6. 手伝ってくれないばかりか、文句まで言う。
Not only do they not help, they even complain.
meaning_vi: Not only…but also…
explain: Used to show that a thing or matter has an additional (bad) characteristic besides the one already known
Expresses annoyance, disappointment, dissatisfaction
examples: 1. あの店は、味が悪いばかりか、店員の態度もひどい。
At that shop, not only is the food bad, but the staff's attitude is terrible too
2. 私は、漢字ばかりか、まだひらがなも書けません。
I can't write not only kanji but even hiragana yet
meaning_vi: Not only ～, in addition…
explain: Expresses the meaning "not only ～ but also…"　Adds something of greater scope or degree.
Sentences of command or compulsion are almost never used after 「ばかりか／ばかりでなく」
examples: 1. あの人は、学校の成績がいいばかりかスボーツもできる。
That person not only has good grades at school but is also good at sports.
2. このあたりは、空気ばかりでなく水も汚染されている。
Around here, not only the air but also the water is polluted.

examples.jp: 他の人に秘密を話したばかりに、彼女を怒らせてしまった。
examples.tr: Just because I told someone else the secret, I ended up making her angry.

examples.jp: レポートの提出期限に遅れたばかりに、単位をもらえなかった。
examples.tr: Just because I missed the deadline for the report, I didn't get the credits.

examples.jp: 私が遅刻をしたばかりに皆に迷惑をかけてしまった。
examples.tr: Just because I was late, I ended up causing trouble for everyone.

examples.jp: 彼の一言を信じたばかりにひどい目にあった。
examples.tr: Just because I believed one thing he said, I had a terrible time.

examples.jp: 背が高いばかりにどこへいっても目立ってしまう。
examples.tr: Just because I'm tall, I stand out wherever I go.

examples.jp: 兄は無口なばかりによく冷たい人だと誤解されるようだ。
examples.tr: Just because my older brother is quiet, he often seems to be misunderstood as a cold person.

1000.explain:
Suits contexts of regret, justification and complaint.
With “V-たい＋ばかりに”: emphasizes an excessive motive; may imply self-blame.
Not used for a neutral, objective cause (in that case ～ために/ので is more natural).

• Just because… , …: A single cause leads to a result (often negative/regrettable). Implies resentment or regret.
• Just to… , …: Because of a single desire/motive, someone does an action (sometimes recklessly/not worth it).
• Evaluation: The speaker judges the cause as trivial or simple, yet it has major consequences.

rows: More neutral regarding “single cause”; ～ばかりに emphasizes “just because of that one reason”.
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>のせいで<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れた。
Neutral/objective; lacks the strong tone of regret of ～ばかりに.
<ruby>渋滞<rt>じゅうたい</rt></ruby>のために<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れた。
The result usually matches expectations; with ～ばかりに the result is usually bad/unexpected.
<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>しただけに<ruby>嬉<rt>うれ</rt></ruby>しい。
<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>りたいばかりに<ruby>聞<rt>ききだし</rt></ruby>き<ruby>出<rt></rt></ruby>した。

mistakes: Using it for a good result: unnatural. For “努力したばかりに合格した” you should use “おかげで/だけに”.
Confusing it with ～せいで: the JLPT tests the “single cause” nuance of ～ばかりに.
Form: with Aな/N in formal style you need “であるばかりに”; avoid “だばかりに”.
1000.notes:
• Written language prefers “N/Aである＋ばかりに” to raise formality.
• When the subject suffers harm: often used with ～てしまう／～ことになった to emphasize that it was unavoidable.
• Cause phrases of the “appearance” type can also be used: 見た目が地味なばかりに…
explain: Expresses regret that a bad result came about only because of that cause.
examples: 1. あの飛行機に乗ったばかりに、彼は死んだ。
Just because he got on that plane, he died.
2. 英語の先生が嫌いなばかりに、英語も嫌いになってしまった。
Just because I disliked my English teacher, I ended up disliking English too.

1001.connection: Vる + まい / Vます + まい (Group 2)

examples.jp: 人の忠告を聞こうとしない彼には、もう何も言うまい。
examples.tr: I won't say anything more to him, since he won't listen to anyone's advice.

examples.jp: もう甘いものは食べまいと思っても、ついつい食べてしまう。
examples.tr: Even when I think I won't eat sweets anymore, I end up eating them anyway.

examples.jp: 一気飲みなどというばかなこと二度とす（/する）まい。
examples.tr: I will never again do something as stupid as chugging a drink in one go.

examples.jp: 彼女は涙を見せまいとして横を向いた。
examples.tr: She turned her face away so as not to show her tears.

examples.jp: 彼は昨日とても具合が悪そうだったから、今日のスポーツ大会には来るまい。
examples.tr: He looked really unwell yesterday, so he probably won't come to today's sports meet.

examples.jp: この程度の雨なら、川が氾濫する恐れはあるまい。
examples.tr: With rain at this level, there's probably no danger of the river flooding.

1001.explain:
Formal, leaning toward written language, speeches and reports; in conversation, ～ないだろう／～ないと思う is usually used.
Negative volition usually goes with volitional verbs and has the speaker as subject.
With N/な: use であるまい to keep a serious tone.

• Negative conjecture: “probably not/unlikely to …” (= ～ないだろう). Written, formal, sometimes classical.
• Negative volition: “determined not to/will never …” when the speaker tells themselves, showing strong resolve.
• “～まいと（して）” means “trying not to …”. “～まいか” is used as a rhetorical question, emphasizing an affirmative expectation.

rows: Neutral, lacks the strong resolve of ～まい
Expresses an effort to avoid doing something

mistakes: Wrong Group 2 conjugation: × 食べるまい → ○ 食べまい（drop ます: 食べます → 食べ）
Using it in everyday conversation makes the sentence stiff; the JLPT often tests the natural replacement ～ないだろう.
Confusing the “volition” meaning with “conjecture”: use the context, subject and person to tell them apart.
Mistaking “すまい” for the polite form: it is actually an old variant of するまい.
1001.notes:
• In natural spoken language, switch to: きっと来ない／来ないと思う to avoid sounding stiff.
• “すまい” exists but is rarely used; “するまい” is more common.
• “あるまい” is used with ある (e.g., そんなことはあるまい = there's probably no such thing). meaning_vi: determined not to, intend not to ⏐ explain: Firmly wanting to give up ～ (expresses negative volition)
A formal expression used in written language.
The sentence is stiff.
⏐ examples: 1. あんなひどいところ、二度と行くまい。
A terrible place like that—I'm determined never to go there again.
2. 海外旅行では、絶対に買った水以外は飲むまいと思った。
When traveling abroad, I resolved never to drink any water other than water I had bought. explain: Expresses negative conjecture.
A formal expression used in written language.

1002.explain:
N/ V-る + ままに: “following/letting be”, may imply a lack of control or deliberately letting go.
V-た + ままに（しておく）/ そのままに: emphasizes maintaining a state; often used in instructions and operations.
In written language/formal expression, “言われるがままに/成り行きのままに” creates a nuance of being swept along.
Avoid overusing “ままに” when the meaning is purely “exactly as/identical to” → in that case “とおり（に）/どおり（に）” is more natural.

• Meaning 1: “Just as…, letting…, led by…” → emphasizes that the action happens following emotions, wishes or circumstances without resisting. Example: 感情のままに話す.
• Meaning 2: “Keeping a state unchanged” when used with V-た + ままにする/しておく or そのままに（しておく）. Example: ドアを開けたままにしておく.
• Difference in nuance:

V-るままに/Nのままに: going along, letting be (more or less a passive nuance of following emotions/circumstances).
V-たままに（しておく）: maintaining a state that has occurred → neutral or negative depending on the context.

• V-るままに/Nのままに: going along, letting be (more or less a passive nuance of following emotions/circumstances).
• V-たままに（しておく）: maintaining a state that has occurred → neutral or negative depending on the context.
• “〜がままに” is a variant with the nuance “exactly as told, being led”.

No need for 「に」 when only stating a state
<ruby>靴<rt>くつ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>履<rt>は</rt></ruby>いたまま<ruby>入<rt>はい</rt></ruby>るな
No implication of going along; reproduces something

mistakes: Confusing “〜ままに” with “〜とおりに”: when you want to say “exactly according to the instructions/standard” → とおりに/どおりに is more natural.
Missing “に” in the state-keeping structure with operation verbs: use “V-たままにしておく/にする”.
Using “V-るままに” for the neutral meaning “exactly as” → unnatural; switch to “とおりに”.
It may appear on JLPT N2-N1 with the nuance of “being swept along”: 言われるがままに＝passive, you need to recognize it.
1002.notes:
• “ありのままに” is a fixed phrase meaning “as it is, just as it naturally is”.
• “V-るがままに” is somewhat literary: 風の吹くがままに, 波の赴くがままに.
• For operating machines/procedures, “そのままにしておく” is safe and neutral; when describing attitudes/behavior, use “Nのままに/V-るままに”. | Meaning: doing as one is made to (causative sense) (Vられるまま(に))

1003.explain:
Placed right after the element being ignored:人目もかまわず, ルールもかまわず.
The nuance is usually negative or one of surprise; be careful when the subject is “I/we” to avoid putting yourself down.
Rarely used in direct command/request sentences.

• Expresses behavior of “not caring, paying no attention” to something one should care about (rules, people's eyes, weather, circumstances…).
• Usually carries the speaker's evaluation (surprise, criticism); rarely used for commands/the listener's volition.
• Different from “にもかかわらず”: “もかまわず” emphasizes that the agent actively ignores/doesn't care; “にもかかわらず” only shows a fact contrary to expectation and is more neutral.

1005.explain:
Used to state a view as a principle, not aimed directly at an individual like a command.
Usually takes a general subject (人は/子どもは/約束は…).
In conversation it sounds soft but still serious: it has a tone of “admonishing”.

• Admonishing, stating a moral/social rule: “one should not do…”.
• Stating a general judgment of impossibility: “cannot/is not something to…”.
• Objective, impersonal nuance; often used in written language and in statements of principle.

mistakes: Confusing it with てはいけない (direct prohibition) → wrong choice when the sentence states a general principle.
Confusing it with ないほうがいい (personal advice) → when the sentence has a general subject “人は…”, prefer ものではない/べきではない.
Using the past tense before ものではない: × したものではない → it must be V辞書形.
1005.notes:
• When criticizing a specific behavior of the other person, ものではない makes the sentence less harsh than てはいけない.
• Besides “should not”, many sentences are naturally translated as “is not something…”, “cannot…”.
• Often appears in JLPT questions to distinguish its nuance from べきではない/てはいけない.

1006.explain:
Usually used with potential verbs (戻れる、できる、会える…).
The second clause expresses the speaker's wish/intention/evaluation.
In the challenging usage, the second clause is usually ～てみろ／てごらん (strong/mild).
Standard/written in tone, not very colloquial except when used as a challenge.

• An almost unreal supposition (counterfactual/low probability): “if only one could…/I wish…”.
• Used to express a strong desire or regret, or to state a condition that is hard to meet.
• Challenging variant: a harsh/provoking nuance, usually in spoken language.

mistakes: Confusing it with ～たら (feasible) → wrong choice when the context is “unlikely/far-fetched”.
Confusing it with ～ようものなら (bad consequence) → look at the second clause: wish vs. warning.
Using it awkwardly with adjectives/nouns: this pattern is mainly used with verbs.
1006.notes:
• In translation: “if only…”, “if it were possible… then…”, “if you think you can, then go ahead and…”.
• The JLPT often tests the difference between ～ものなら (hard-to-realize supposition) and ～ようものなら (bad consequence).
• The implied subject is usually the speaker or the other person (in the challenging usage).

• More formal than ～が／～けれど(も); often used in writing, journalism and reports.
• The second clause is usually not a direct command/request, but a fact/evaluation.

Confusing it with のに (which has a nuance of reproach): test questions often set traps with emotion.

1008.explain:
Often used in sentences with a nuance of exclamation/complaint: ～やら～やらで、… / ～やら～やらして…
More than 2 items can be used, but 2 items are most common for a natural sentence rhythm.
Compared with ～たり～たり: ～やら～やら does not emphasize alternation; it is a mixed, disorderly listing.
In formal written language, consider replacing it with ～など／～や～など.

• Lists two (or more) examples among many similar things: “what with A and B…”.
• Suggests a sense of things being out of control, messy, or of mixed feelings; usually spoken.
• The two items are usually of the same kind of meaning or the same semantic field (cluttered things, a series of mishaps, conflicting emotions...).
• Implies “there is much more” beyond the items mentioned.

mistakes: Using it with a neutral nuance when no emotion is intended: choose ～など/～や～など instead of ～やら～やら.
Confusing it with ～だの～だの: if there is no strong criticism, avoid ～だの～だの.
Wrong word types: keep the items consistent in type/meaning where possible so the sentence is natural; excessive mixing is confusing.
JLPT: recognize a “messy/complaining” context to choose ～やら～やら instead of ～たり～たり.
1008.notes:
• “やら” was originally an old listing particle; in this pattern it is repeated to create rhythm and a nuance of “all sorts of things”.
• The forms “AやらBやらで～” and “AやらBやらして～” are very common in conversation.

1009.explain:
Used when other options have been considered but none are feasible.
Has a nuance of reluctance/unwillingness; do not use it when you want to emphasize an active decision (in that case use ～ことにする/～つもりだ).
In casual speech, ～しかない is more natural; formal written language uses ～よりほかない.
Usually comes at the end of a sentence or before a noun: ～よりほかない方法／選択肢.

• Expresses a situation with only one feasible solution: “have no choice but to / the only way is…”.
• Implies a lack of initiative, a sense of being forced by objective circumstances.
• More formal than ～しかない; works well in written language and public statements.

mistakes: Confusing it with “～つもりだ/ことにする”: if it is an active decision, do not use ～よりほかない.
Wrong form with nouns: × 努力よりほかない → ✔ 努力のほか（に）はない or Vるよりほかない.
Confusing it with ～ざるを得ない: both express reluctance, but ～ざるを得ない emphasizes “being forced”; ～よりほかない emphasizes “having no other option”.
JLPT: when the context has “他の方法がない/選択肢がない/致し方ない”, the answer leans toward ～よりほかない／～しかない／～ざるを得ない; pay attention to the formal nuance.
1009.notes:
• “より” strengthens the exclusive comparison: it rules out all other options, leaving only the option before “より”.
• Often used with words such as 状況, 事情, 現実, 選択肢, 方策 to create an argumentative style.
• In company announcements: 「やむを得ず値上げせざるを得ない／値上げするよりほかない」 – a formal nuance, asking for understanding.

1012.explain:
Formal; tends to be used in official documents/advertisements/announcements.
Usually expresses the “unrestricted scope” of a rule/condition.
Comes in the middle of a sentence and modifies the second clause; there is also the attributive form “Nを問わないN₂”.
With pairs of opposites (AかBか), it makes clear the meaning “regardless of whether A or B”.

• Regardless of/irrespective of N, what follows is still true/applies.
• Public, regulatory, slogan-like nuance: used a lot in announcements, recruitment and policies.
• Often used with classifying nouns: age, gender, nationality, weather, time, wealth, size…
• Different from “even if … still …”, which involves personal choice; this pattern states an objective scope of application.

rows: <ruby>国籍<rt>こくせき</rt></ruby>を<ruby>問<rt>と</rt></ruby>わず<ruby>採用<rt>さいよう</rt></ruby>
～に<ruby>関<rt>かか</rt></ruby>わらず／にかかわりなく
Close in meaning, used more widely, less formal
<ruby>天候<rt>てんこう</rt></ruby>に<ruby>関<rt>かか</rt></ruby>わらず<ruby>実施<rt>じっし</rt></ruby>
Emphasizes the relationship rather than distinction
<ruby>年齢<rt>ねんれい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>関係<rt>かんけい</rt></ruby>なく<ruby>楽<rt>たの</rt></ruby>しめる
Nuance of overcoming difficulties, not just “regardless of”
<ruby>風雨<rt>ふうう</rt></ruby>をものともせず<ruby>進<rt>すす</rt></ruby>む

mistakes: Confusing it with ～に関わらず: both are correct in many cases, but the JLPT often tests the formal nuance of ～を問わず.
Using it with long verb clauses: unnatural; prefer nouns/noun phrases.
Putting it in a command/volition sentence: pragmatically inappropriate.
1012.notes:
• The negative form “Nを問わないN₂” is common in job advertisements: 経験を問わない人材.
• Unnatural with direct volition/commands (do/don't) because of its objective, normative nuance.
• With nouns that do not have clear classification criteria, this pattern can be ambiguous – choose nouns with clear criteria. meaning_vi: Unrelated to ～ ⏐ explain: Indicates that the noun mentioned is unrelated to, has no influence on, and is not an issue for the following action. ⏐ examples: 1. 年齢を問わず多くの人々が集まった。
Many people gathered regardless of age.
2. 経験の有無を問わず、募集。
Recruiting regardless of whether you have experience or not.
3. 性別は問いません。
Gender does not matter.

examples.tr: Cigarettes are going up in price soon, so I've decided to take this as an opportunity to quit.

1013.explain: ◎ Expresses the meaning "a certain event or situation becomes the reason or cause".

examples.jp: 月曜日を除いて
examples.tr: Except for Monday
