1014.notes: Expresses the meaning “treating that as an exception”. It is written-language style; in spoken language, 「－をのぞけば」 or 「…のほかは」 is more often used.

1015.meaning: After…, when… (finish the first thing, then do the next)

examples.jp: 「家族と相談た上でご返事いたします」
examples.tr: "I will give you my answer after discussing it with my family."

examples.jp: 実物を見た上で、買うかどうか決めるつもりだ。
examples.tr: I'm going to decide whether to buy it after seeing the actual item.

examples.jp: 調べてみた上でなけらば、はっきりしたことは言えない。
examples.tr: Unless I look into it first, I can't say anything definite.

examples.jp: これは何度も話し合った上（で）の結論だ。
examples.tr: This is a conclusion reached after discussing it many times.

examples.jp: 「この書類にご記入の上、1番の窓口にお出しください」
examples.tr: "Please fill in this form and then submit it at counter No. 1."

examples.jp: 現地を視察した上で、最終判断を下します。
examples.tr: We will make a final decision after inspecting the site.

1015.explain:
Formal; common in instructions/forms/contracts.
Meaning “after”: the first clause must be truly completed; not used for unintentional actions or actions without a clear point of completion.
Meaning “when/in terms of”: often used with words indicating difficulties/conditions such as注意,工夫,問題,課題,重要,必要.

• Meaning 1 (V-た上で): “After … then …” emphasizes completion, deliberately preparing before the next action.
• Meaning 2 (V-る上で/Nの上で): “When/In the process of …” or “In terms of …” states a condition, a point to note/difficulty/something important when carrying out an action.
• Different from “上に/上は”: “上で” is about sequence (Meaning 1) or aspect/condition (Meaning 2), not addition/affirming determination.

rows: Emphasizes preparation before the next step
<ruby>検討<rt>けんとう</rt></ruby>した<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>決定<rt>けってい</rt></ruby>。
More neutral, everyday, no emphasis on preparation
<ruby>運用<rt>うんよう</rt></ruby>する<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>での<ruby>課題<rt>かだい</rt></ruby>。
Nにあたって/に<ruby>際<rt>さい</rt></ruby>して
<ruby>開業<rt>かいぎょう</rt></ruby>にあたって<ruby>挨拶<rt>あいさつ</rt></ruby>。
Marks place/field, no implication of sequence
<ruby>教育<rt>きょういく</rt></ruby>において<ruby>重要<rt>じゅうよう</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Using V-た上で for an action without a clear point of completion → unnatural.
Confusing “上で” with “上に” (not only…but also). Their functions are completely different.
Dropping “の” in “上でのN”: writing “上でN” is wrong; it must be “上でのN”.
Using “Nの上で” for a physical location “on the surface” → the meaning becomes “in terms of”, which can easily cause misunderstanding.
1015.notes:
• The phrase “～上でのN” is very common in instruction headings: 利用上の注意, 契約上の義務.
• With the meaning “after”, it often goes with verbs of evaluation/consideration: 検討する, 相談する, 確認する, 準備する.
• Meaning “in terms of”: can be replaced with “面で/観点で” in many contexts, but “上で” is more formal.

examples.tr: Now that I've taken it on, I will see it through responsibly.

examples.jp: 試合に出る上は、全力を尽くすべきだ。

examples.jp: 秘密が漏れた上は、対応を急がざるを得ない。

examples.jp: こうなった上は、警察に相談するしかない。
examples.tr: Now that things have come to this, the only option is to consult the police.

examples.jp: 学生である上は、本分を尽くすべきだ。
examples.tr: As a student, you should fulfill your duties.

1016.explain:
Sets an established point (a decision/current situation) and infers an inevitable consequence of a normative/rule-like kind.
Has a nuance of commitment/responsibility. Suitable for work contexts and official statements.
Avoid using it to directly make the listener do something: “…上は、～してください” is unnatural.

• Expresses the idea “now that … (naturally/will) …”. From an established situation, it infers an inevitable determination/obligation/measure.
• Serious nuance, more formal than “からには”. Often used in declarations/decisions.
• The second clause is rarely a request/desire addressed to the listener; it is mainly the speaker's volition, an inevitable judgment, or a general rule.

rows: <ruby>参加<rt>さんか</rt></ruby>する<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>全力<rt>ぜんりょく</rt></ruby>で。
More common, less formal; can be used with mild requests
<ruby>始<rt>はじ</rt></ruby>めたからには、<ruby>続<rt>つづ</rt></ruby>けろ。
Close in meaning; “<ruby>以上<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>は” is usually more spoken than “<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>は”
<ruby>約束<rt>やくそく</rt></ruby>した<ruby>以上<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>守<rt>まも</rt></ruby>る。
Softer spelling; the nuance stays the same

mistakes: Using it to make a direct request to the listener: “…上は、～してください” → unnatural; change to “以上、よろしくお願いします” or “からには”.
The first clause is not clearly “established” (only a possibility) → logical contradiction.
Confusing it with “上で” (sequence/aspect) and “上に” (addition). “上は” is a pattern of determination/inevitability.
1016.notes:
• Often accompanied by a normative conclusion: ～べきだ／～なければならない／～に違いない／～ものだ。
• “Nである上は” is less common than with verbs, but can be used when stating a position/state: 社員である上は…
• In speeches, it can be combined with “責任/覚悟/義務”: 受けた上は、責任を果たす。 explain: Expresses the reason: because ～, naturally ～. The second clause contains words expressing determination, advice, prohibition, etc.
Stiff sentence style. ⏐ examples: 1. キャプテンに選ばれた上は、がんばるしかない。
Now that I've been chosen as captain, I have no choice but to do my best.
2. 入学する上は卒業したい。
If I enter the school, I want to graduate.

examples.jp: 給料をもらっている以上、ちゃんと仕事をしなければならない。
examples.tr: As long as you are getting paid, you have to do your job properly.

examples.jp: 約束した以上、守る義務がある。
examples.tr: Now that I've promised, I have an obligation to keep my word.

1017.explain: ◎ Often used to indicate obligations, responsibilities, rules or common sense, expressing the idea "Since X, Y is only natural".
1017.notes:
explain: Expresses the feeling that one naturally must ～
[以上] is followed by obligation, prohibition, request, conjecture or a strong judgment.
（＝「上は」） ⏐ examples: 1. 試験を受ける以上、いい点を取りたい。
Since I'm taking the exam, I want to get a good score.
2. 日本に来た以上は、日本語ができるようになりたい。
Now that I've come to Japan, I want to become able to speak Japanese.

examples.tr: Those two getting married? That's impossible.

examples.jp: 難しすぎて、私のような凡人には理解し得ない。

examples.tr: Something unforeseeable happened this time, but everyone stayed calm.

examples.tr: I tried every method I could think of, but it didn't work.

examples.jp: しかたがない

～した後(あと)で最後(さいご)に
After, at the end of

examples.tr: After a long discussion, the plan was finally completed.

examples.tr: "This is a conclusion reached after careful thought, so there can be no changes.

examples.jp: いろいろ悩んだ末、会社をやめることにしました。
examples.tr: After much agonizing, I decided to quit the company.

1021.explain:
Written language; narrates a process leading to a decision/result.
“Vた末に” comes in the middle of a sentence; “Vた末、” comes at the beginning of a sentence as an adverbial.
Suggests a heavy/laborious process; not used for instantaneous events with no process.
The second clause is the final result, usually 〜ことにした／〜に至った／〜と決まった など.

rows: A result after a long process
<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>し<ruby>合<rt>あ</rt></ruby>った<ruby>末<rt>すえ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>合意<rt>ごうい</rt></ruby>。
A bad outcome after a long process
<ruby>迷<rt>まよ</rt></ruby>ったあげく、<ruby>機会<rt>きかい</rt></ruby>を<ruby>逃<rt>のが</rt></ruby>した。
Emphasizes cause and effect more, not necessarily long
<ruby>検査<rt>けんさ</rt></ruby>した<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>、<ruby>異常<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>なし。
<ruby>長時間<rt>ちょうじかん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>議論<rt>ぎろん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>末<rt>すえ</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Using it with instantaneous actions (見る・出会う) that have no process → unnatural. Use た結果/とき instead.
Confusing it with ～あげく: ～末 does not imply something bad; ～あげく usually has a negative outcome.
Choosing the wrong tense: it must be Vた + 末. Vる + 末 is not used.
Overusing it in everyday spoken language → sounds like written language; consider simplifying.
1021.notes:
meaning_vi: In the end…, ultimately…
examples: 1. 家族と何度も話し合った末に、留学を決めた。
After discussing it with my family many times, I finally decided to study abroad.
2. 長い交渉の末、ようやく契約にこぎつけた。
After long negotiations, we finally managed to sign the contract.
3. 悩んだ末、手術は受けないことにした。
After agonizing over it, I decided not to have the surgery.
4. 数か月にわたる捜索の末に、行方が判明した。
After months of searching, their whereabouts were finally found.
5. 検討を重ねた末、計画は白紙に戻された。
After repeated consideration, the plan was scrapped and returned to square one.
meaning_vi: After so much… finally… (～た末に)
meaning_vi: Long after ～
explain: After going through a certain process, in the end. Often used in written language, giving a stiff sentence style.
examples: 1. 悩んだ末、進学ではなく就職することにした。
After thinking it over carefully, I decided to get a job instead of continuing my studies.
2. 住民との話し合いの末、その建物の建設は中止となった。
After discussions with residents, construction of that building was halted.

1022.meaning: I humbly state that…, it is because… | As soon as…, depending on…

examples.jp: 父は来年ですが、うちには弟と妹がいます。私もアルバイトを減らしてもっと勉強したいと考えています。このようなわけでは奨学金を申請する次第です。
examples.tr: My father retires next year, but I have a younger brother and sister at home. I am also thinking of cutting back on my part-time job so I can study more. That is why I am applying for a scholarship.

examples.jp: その件について一応お耳には入れておこうと考え、お手紙を差し上げる次第です。
examples.tr: I thought I should at least let you know about that matter, and so I am writing you this letter.

examples.jp: 売り上げ予想とコストを考慮した結果、この製品の開発を断念した次第です。
examples.tr: After considering the sales forecast and the costs, we have decided to abandon the development of this product.

examples.jp: 担当者が不在のため、返信が遅れましたことをお詫び申し上げる次第です。
examples.tr: Because the person in charge was away, our reply was delayed, for which we sincerely apologize.

examples.jp: 諸事情により、予定を変更することになった次第です。
examples.tr: Due to various circumstances, it has been decided that the schedule will be changed.

examples.jp: 上記の理由から、今回は参加を見送る次第です。
examples.tr: For the reasons stated above, I will not be participating this time.

1022.explain:
Structure: Vます +次第、～
The second clause is usually a clause expressing the speaker's intention or action (contacting, notifying, starting…).
Context: written language/business, polite announcements; rarely used in casual conversation (replaced by ～たらすぐ/～たらすぐに).
Not used when the second clause is a general habit or an obvious fact with no sense of "immediately".

•
Meaning: "As soon as… then…", "once … is done, …". Emphasizes that the two actions follow each other immediately in time.

•
Scope of use: situations where you announce a plan or action that will be carried out as soon as the condition in the first clause is completed.

•
Nuance: formal; common in business emails, service announcements, and promises of action.

•
Meaning frame: [A completed] → (immediately) [do B]. The second clause rarely expresses a vague, prolonged state.

rows: Spoken, more neutral; no emphasis on a formal announcement nuance
<ruby>着<rt>つ</rt></ruby>いたらすぐ<ruby>電話<rt>でんわ</rt></ruby>して。
Different meaning: a condition that depends on a noun, not "as soon as"
<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>は<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby><ruby>次第<rt>しだい</rt></ruby>で<ruby>変<rt>か</rt></ruby>わる。
Different function: a sentence that explains or wraps up the content
<ruby>以上<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>、ご<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>した<ruby>次第<rt>しだい</rt></ruby>です。

mistakes: Wrong nuance: using it in casual conversation → sounds stiff and distant.
JLPT: tricks you with its role as a sentence ending compared with ～というわけです; asks you to choose the pattern that fits a business situation.
Wrong position: placed in the middle of a passage instead of at the end of the summarized content.
1022.notes:
• Often used with verbs signaling completion: 分かる・判明する・届く・到着する・準備ができる・確認する・決まり次第…
• In emails: "～が分かり次第、ご連絡申し上げます。" is a very common formula.
• On sentence rhythm: put a comma after 次第 to clearly separate the two clauses.
meaning_vi: ～したらすぐに過去形(かこけい)の文(ぶん)にはならない
Immediately after...
examples: 1. 「向こうに着きしだい、電話してください」
Please call me as soon as you get there.
2. 「皆さんがそろいしだい出発しましょう」
Let's leave as soon as everyone is here.
3. 次の会合は来月１日です。場所は決まり次第お知らせします。
The next meeting is on the 1st of next month. We will let you know the venue as soon as it is decided.

examples.jp: やり方次第でもう少し早くできると思う。
examples.tr: I think we could do it a bit faster depending on how we go about it.

examples.jp: 成績次第で給料は上がると言われた。
examples.tr: I was told that my salary would go up depending on my performance.

examples.jp: 努力次第で、人生は大きく変わる。
examples.tr: Depending on your effort, your life can change dramatically.

examples.jp: 説明の仕方次第では、相手の反応も良くなる。
examples.tr: Depending on how you explain it, the other person may react better too.

examples.jp: 資金次第で、計画の規模を調整します。
examples.tr: We will adjust the scale of the plan depending on the funds.

examples.jp: 天候次第では、イベントを屋内に切り替えます。
examples.tr: Depending on the weather, the event may be moved indoors.

1023.explain:
Structure: N +次第で／次第では／次第に
"次第で" states a relationship of dependence; "次第では" states a possibility in a particular case.
The second clause is usually a verb expressing change (変わる・左右される・決まる・調整する…).
Often used with general nouns:努力・考え方・状況・予算・天気・使い方・対応・方針…

•
Meaning: the result or outcome depends on the factor N (a condition, circumstance, way of doing something, point of view, etc.).

•
Focus: a conditional cause-and-effect relationship; things change according to N.

•
Nuance: neutral and logical; can be used in both spoken language and written language.

rows: Broader meaning; leans toward "by way of/thanks to/done by"
<ruby>国<rt>くに</rt></ruby>によって<ruby>文化<rt>ぶんか</rt></ruby>が<ruby>違<rt>ちが</rt></ruby>う。
More formal; common in stiff written texts
<ruby>成績<rt>せいせき</rt></ruby>いかんでは<ruby>進学<rt>しんがく</rt></ruby><ruby>不可<rt>ふか</rt></ruby>。
Different meaning: a time relationship, not dependence on a condition
<ruby>準備<rt>じゅんび</rt></ruby>ができ <ruby>次第<rt>しだい</rt></ruby><ruby>出発<rt>しゅっぱつ</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Wrong meaning: taking ～次第で as "as soon as" → confusing it with ～次第 (Vます+次第).
Wrong part of speech: putting a verb before 次第で → it must be noun + 次第で.
JLPT: often tests the distinction between ～によって／～いかんで（は）／～次第で in terms of formality.
1023.notes:
• N + 次第で emphasizes the decisive "lever": the factor N is the variable that governs the result.
• 次第では often goes with a clause stating a possible choice or option: 中止する／延期する／見送る…
• A natural contrasting pair: 「能力・努力・工夫」⇄「結果・成果・評価」. | Sentence-final form: ～次第だ (depends on)

1024.meaning:
①～であるば（仮定(かてい)、条件(じょうけん)）
Assumption, condition, as long as | Within the scope of…, as long as…

examples.jp: 私たちが黙っている限り、この秘密を人に知られることはない。
examples.tr: As long as we keep quiet, nobody will find out this secret.

examples.jp: 学生である限り、校則は守らなければならない。
examples.tr: As long as you are a student, you have to follow the school rules.

examples.jp: 大きなミスをしない限り、村山選手の優勝は間違いないでしょう。
examples.tr: As long as he doesn't make any big mistakes, Murayama will surely win.

examples.jp: 「よほどのことがない限り、出席します」
examples.tr: "Unless something serious comes up, I will attend."

1024.explain: ◎ An expression of limitation meaning " if the condition is met", " within that scope".

examples.jp: まじめに働き続ける限りは、クビになることはない。

1025.explain: ◎ Expresses the idea "if a certain condition is satisfied".

1026.connection: V volitional form + か + Vる・Vます + まいか

examples.jp: パーティーに出席しようか、しまいか、まだ迷っている。
examples.tr: I still can't decide whether to attend the party or not.

1026.explain: ◎ Expresses hesitation about whether or not to do an action.
1026.notes:
Taken from (Speed Master); fuller 接続 (まいか attaches to Vる or Vます depending on the verb group). meaning_vi: whether to ～ or not ⏐ explain: Used in written language.
Formal sentence. ⏐ examples: 1. 本当のことを話そうか話すまいか迷った、結局全部話した。
I hesitated over whether to tell the truth or not, but in the end I told everything.
2. 食べたいけど、太りたくないし、食べようか食べまいか考えているところです。
I want to eat it, but I don't want to gain weight, so I'm thinking about whether to eat it or not.

examples.jp: 今日は朝から会議ずくめだ。
examples.tr: Today it's been nothing but meetings since the morning.

examples.jp: 彼は全身黒ずくめの格好をしている。
examples.tr: He is dressed in black from head to toe.

examples.jp: この投資話はいいことずくめに聞こえるが、注意が必要だ。
examples.tr: This investment offer sounds like nothing but good things, but you need to be careful.

examples.jp: 新制度は規則ずくめで息が詰まる。
examples.tr: The new system is nothing but rules, and it's suffocating.

examples.jp: 今週は仕事ずくめで、休む暇もない。
examples.tr: This week has been nothing but work, and I haven't had time to rest.

examples.jp: 彼のスピーチは自慢話ずくめでうんざりした。
examples.tr: His speech was nothing but bragging, and I got sick of it.

1027.explain:
Attaches directly after a noun; often used with の when it modifies another noun:黒ずくめの男.
Used for a sense of "all one color" or "densely packed" rather than simply quantity.
Often used in advertising and journalism to emphasize "completeness".

• "All/full of/covered entirely by …": emphasizes singleness, uniformity, all one color.
• Often used with colors, repeated events, rules, and things that are entirely good or bad.
• Nuance: can be positive (いいことずくめ) or negative (苦情ずくめ／規則ずくめ).
• Different from づくし: ずくめ = one kind covering everything; づくし = "all kinds within one theme".

rows: <ruby>間違<rt>まちが</rt></ruby>いだらけのレポート。
Covered all over (with a substance), negative
All dishes/all kinds within a theme
<ruby>野菜<rt>やさい</rt></ruby>づくしのコース。

mistakes: Used with a verb: ×勉強ずくめする → correct: 勉強ずくめの日々.
Confused with づくし: ずくめ = one color; づくし = all kinds within one theme.
Using ずくめ for dirt or for being covered in a substance is the wrong nuance → use まみれ.
1027.notes:
• Fixed color phrases: 黒ずくめ／白ずくめ（all black/all white）.
• With prolonged events: ～三日間ずくめで（nothing but … for 3 days）.
• Avoid using it for objects covered in dirty material → まみれ is more suitable.

examples.jp: 会議は大阪にて行います。
examples.tr: The meeting will be held in Osaka.

examples.tr: We will send you the details by email.

examples.tr: Exchanges at our store require a receipt.

1028.explain:
Degree of formality: high; used in announcements, invitations, event posters, and internal documents.
Spoken replacements: で/に (place/point in time) and で/により (means).
Often used with:開催・実施・受け付ける・行う・終了・販売・配布・連絡・案内.
Position: mid-sentence (NにてV), or at the beginning of a sentence in fixed phrases (これにて、以上にて...).
Avoid it in everyday conversation; prefer で/に to sound natural.

• Indicates the place where something happens: equivalent to で in spoken language. Example: 東京にて開催する。
• Indicates the ending/starting point in time (announcements): 10時にて終了。
• Indicates means/method: 電話にてお問い合わせください。 (equivalent to で/により)
• Formal nuance; used a lot in announcements, correspondence, and corporate/government documents.
• Not used for the destination of movement (× 東京にて行く), but for the place where an event or action takes place.
• Compared with において: において is more academic/general; にて leans toward practical announcements (events, sales, reception...)

rows: Natural, less formal than にて
<ruby>会議<rt>かいぎ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>大阪<rt>おおさか</rt></ruby>で<ruby>行<rt>おこな</rt></ruby>う。
<ruby>教育<rt>きょういく</rt></ruby>において<ruby>重要<rt>じゅうよう</rt></ruby>だ。
Emphasizes the agent/cause; にて leans toward formal means
<ruby>電話<rt>でんわ</rt></ruby>により<ruby>受<rt>う</rt></ruby>け<ruby>付<rt>つ</rt></ruby>ける。
As of the end of, by means of
More formal when saying "ends as of ..."
<ruby>本日<rt>ほんじつ</rt></ruby>をもって<ruby>終了<rt>しゅうりょう</rt></ruby>。
Fixed phrase for closing a speech
これにて<ruby>閉会<rt>へいかい</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Wrongly used for a destination: × 東京にて行く → ◯ 東京にて開催する／東京へ行く。
Overusing it in everyday conversation makes sentences stiff; change it to で/に.
Confused with において in abstract scope: 教育にて × → 教育において。
Point in time: 10時にて終了 (announcement) is natural; in speech, 10時で終了 is usually used.
1028.notes:
• Very frequent in documents: event posters, business emails, store announcements.
• "NにてのN" is mostly seen in writing; in speech it usually becomes "NでのN".
• Not combined with verbs of motion indicating a destination (行く・来る) in the destination sense.
• Polite expressions that often go with it: 〜いたします、〜しております、〜させていただきます。 explain: Often used on notice boards or in letters…
Formal sentence. ⏐ examples: 1. 現地にて解散となります。
We will disperse on site.
2. 電話カメールにてご連絡ください。
Please contact me by email or phone.
3. 京都にて　洋子より（*旅先からのハガキの最後などでよく使う）
From Yoko, in Kyoto.

examples.jp: このプロジェクトの成否は、資金調達のいかんだ。
examples.tr: The success or failure of this project depends on fundraising.

examples.jp: 進学できるかどうかは、期末試験の結果のいかんだ。
examples.tr: Whether I can go on to the next level of school depends on the results of the final exams.

examples.jp: 採用は人物と適性のいかんだ。
examples.tr: Hiring depends on the person's character and aptitude.

examples.jp: 交渉継続の可否は、相手側の回答のいかんだ。
examples.tr: Whether the negotiations continue depends on the other party's response.

1029.explain:
Often used in affirmative sentences that set rules or give an overall evaluation.
Not used in everyday casual speech; replaced by "〜による/〜次第だ".
Suitable when you want to single out the "deciding factor" in an objective way.

• "~のいかんだ" = "depends on ~ / is decided by ~".
• Emphasizes that N is the factor that determines result X. Highly formal; often seen in official documents.
• "いかん" is a Sino-Japanese noun (如何) meaning "degree/condition/state (how good or bad)".
• Only combines with nouns (努力・資金・成否・態度・結果・審査 等). Does not attach directly to adjectives/verbs.

rows: Very formal; states a deciding relationship
<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>のいかんだ
Due to, because of, depending on
<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>は<ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>による
<ruby>合格<rt>ごうかく</rt></ruby>は<ruby>君<rt>きみ</rt></ruby><ruby>次第<rt>しだい</rt></ruby>だ
Sets a condition to state a consequence
<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>のいかんでは<ruby>処分<rt>しょぶん</rt></ruby>も
N のいかんにかかわらず
<ruby>年齢<rt>ねんれい</rt></ruby>のいかんにかかわらず

mistakes: Used directly with an adjective/verb: ×速いのいかんだ → 速さのいかんだ (convert to a noun).
Using it in casual conversation sounds stiff and unnatural; use による/次第だ instead.
Confusing its function with "では/によっては" (conditional variants) → "のいかんだ" only states a general relationship of dependence.
1029.notes:
• "いかん" often goes with abstract nouns: 成否・可否・結果・状況・態度・出来（でき）など.
• Because it is highly formal, it suits announcements, regulations, and contracts.
• In legal/administrative discourse, "〜のいかんにかかわらず／問わず" appears very often.

examples.jp: 砂糖のない紅茶をください。
examples.tr: Tea without sugar, please.

examples.jp: 人影のない公園で本を読んだ。
examples.tr: I read a book in a park with no one around.

examples.jp: 根拠のない批判に惑わされるな。
examples.tr: Don't be misled by groundless criticism.

examples.jp: 前例のない挑戦だ。
examples.tr: It is an unprecedented challenge.

examples.jp: 予告のない訪問はご遠慮ください。
examples.tr: Please refrain from visiting without prior notice.

1030.explain:
Put N1 before のない to emphasize "what is lacking".
More formal than "N1抜きのN2" (N1 intentionally left out) and "N1なしのN2" (without N1 in general).
Often used in legal documents, announcements, and academic writing.

• Modifier form: "N2 that has no N1", "N2 not accompanied by N1", equivalent to "N2 without N1".
• Expresses absence (of something material or abstract: 根拠, 前例, 予告, 音, 人影…).
• More formal/written than ～なしの/～抜きの in some contexts.

rows: <ruby>根拠<rt>こんきょ</rt></ruby>のない<ruby>噂<rt>うわさ</rt></ruby>
<ruby>砂糖<rt>さとう</rt></ruby>なしのコーヒー
アルコール<ruby>抜<rt>ぬ</rt></ruby>きのパーティー

mistakes: Wrong order: ×ないのN → correct: NのないN.
Mixed up with なしの/抜きの: なしの is neutral, 抜きの emphasizes "intentional removal".
Using のない with a verb → incorrect: the concept must be nominalized (例: 許可のない撮影).
JLPT: choose correctly when saying "groundless/unprecedented": 根拠のない／前例のない are common answers.
1030.notes:
• N1 is a noun; if it is a quality expressed by a na-adjective or い-adjective, it is usually nominalized: 可能性のない, 安全性のない.
• Common phrases: 前置きのない, 合意のない, 許可のない, 音のない（無音の）.
• In formal headlines, "前例のない" is very common to emphasize that something is unprecedented.

examples.jp: 東京をはじめとして、各地で桜が見頃を迎えている。
examples.tr: Starting with Tokyo, cherry blossoms are reaching full bloom in many places.

examples.jp: 社長をはじめとして、多くの関係者が出席した。
examples.tr: Many people involved attended, starting with the company president.

examples.jp: 日本をはじめとして、アジアの国々で高く評価されている。
examples.tr: It is highly regarded in Asian countries, Japan first and foremost.

examples.jp: 小学生をはじめとして、幅広い年齢層に人気だ。
examples.tr: It is popular with a wide range of age groups, starting with elementary school children.

examples.jp: 環境問題は、身近な節電をはじめとして、できることが多い。
examples.tr: When it comes to environmental problems, there is a lot we can do, starting with saving electricity in our daily lives.

1031.explain:
Placed at the beginning of a sentence to lead into a broader scope.
More formal than "〜をはじめ," but with the same basic meaning; choose according to the context.
N must be a typical/representative member of a larger set.
Often used with nouns for place names, job titles, groups of people, and items.

• "Starting with N, including others of the same kind."
• Emphasizes the starting point/typical case (N) and then extends to a broader scope.
• Style of official information: speeches, reports, news articles.

rows: Noun modifier "including N first and foremost ..."
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>をはじめとする<ruby>国々<rt>くにぐに</rt></ruby>
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>などで<ruby>人気<rt>にんき</rt></ruby>
Written language, emphasizes "the leader"; strong nuance
<ruby>社長<rt>しゃちょう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>筆頭<rt>ひっとう</rt></ruby>に〜

mistakes: Confused with "〜をはじめに(して)": that one indicates a sequence, "starting with ... first".
Used when there is no broader scope: × 社長をはじめとして、社長が来た。
Choosing a non-representative subject: using an N that is too small or isolated is unnatural.
1031.notes:
• In local news reports: 地名 + をはじめとして/に is very common.
• When N is a superior (社長・校長), it creates a respectful, polite nuance.
• Not used for a complete listing; implies there are many other members. meaning_vi: First and foremost, ～ ⏐ explain: Gives one main example, then lists other similar examples. ⏐ examples: 1. 会議には中国をはじめ、アジアの国々が参加した。
Asian countries, starting with China, took part in the conference.
2. わが国では、野球をはじめとして、サッカーやテニスなど、様々なスポーツがさかんである。
In our country, many sports are popular, starting with baseball, as well as soccer and tennis.

examples.jp: 日本をはじめとするアジアの国々が参加した。
examples.tr: Asian countries, led by Japan, took part.

examples.jp: 社長をはじめとする役員の出席が決まった。
examples.tr: It has been decided that the executives, starting with the president, will attend.

examples.jp: スマートフォンをはじめとする携帯端末の需要が伸びている。
examples.tr: Demand for mobile devices, such as smartphones, is growing.

examples.jp: 京都をはじめとする関西の観光地は春に賑わう。
examples.tr: Tourist spots in the Kansai region, such as Kyoto, are bustling in spring.

examples.jp: 数学をはじめとする理系科目が得意だ。
examples.tr: I'm good at science subjects, especially math.

examples.jp: WHOをはじめとする国際機関が声明を出した。
examples.tr: International organizations, including the WHO, issued a statement.

1032.explain:
Placed right before the head noun N2 to modify it directly.
Formal tone; suitable for informational, academic, and journalistic texts.
Make sure there is a set relationship: N1 is a member of the set N2.
Not used when N2 has only one member; it must be a group/set.

• Used like an attributive adjective to describe a set N2 in which N1 is the representative/leading member.
• Formal nuance; often appears in articles, presentations, and reports.
• N1 and N2 must belong to the same semantic field (the same kind): country–countries, person–group of people, product–products...

rows: Does not directly modify a noun
Links clauses; not a noun modifier
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>をはじめとして、〜
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>といった<ruby>国々<rt>くにぐに</rt></ruby>
Nを<ruby>中心<rt>ちゅうしん</rt></ruby>とするN
Emphasizes the "center", not necessarily a representative example
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>中心<rt>ちゅうしん</rt></ruby>とするプロジェクト

mistakes: Wrong category relationship: × 日本をはじめとするヨーロッパ → Japan is not part of Europe.
N2 is not a set: × 日本をはじめとする文化 → N2 should be a countable set: 文化圏／文化行事.
Confused with "〜をはじめに(して)": a pattern about the order of actions, with a completely different meaning.
1032.notes:
• Headline pattern: 「N1をはじめとするN2、〜」 is very common.
• Often combined with words denoting a set: 国々／関係者／製品群／都市／機関／科目.
• A long complement can be inserted after N2 and the sentence still stays formal and coherent.

examples.jp: 環境問題をめぐる国際会議が開かれた。
examples.tr: An international conference on environmental issues was held.

examples.jp: 遺産をめぐる家族間の争いは長期化している。
examples.tr: The family dispute over the inheritance has dragged on.

examples.jp: 人事をめぐる社内の噂が絶えない。
examples.tr: Rumors within the company about personnel matters never stop.

examples.jp: 教育改革をめぐる世論は二分している。
examples.tr: Public opinion on education reform is split in two.

examples.jp: 安全保障をめぐる与野党の論戦が続いた。
examples.tr: The debate between the ruling and opposition parties over national security continued.

examples.jp: 史実をめぐる解釈の違いが表面化した。
examples.tr: Differences in the interpretation of historical facts have come to the surface.

1033.explain:
Placed right before the head noun to sum up the content "surrounding N".
Formal and concise; favored in administrative documents, journalism, and academic writing.
Suitable when you want to emphasize multiple sides or a conflict of interests/opinions.
Not used as a predicate: ×「この問題をめぐる。」→ you must write 「この問題をめぐって議論している。」

• Modifies the following noun, meaning "related to / surrounding (the issue N)" with a nuance of controversy, opposition, multiple parties.
• Creates concise noun phrases suited to titles and headlines: ～をめぐる論争／～をめぐる対立／～をめぐる疑惑.
• Scope of use: politics, society, economics, law, academia, organizations.

rows: <ruby>予算<rt>よさん</rt></ruby>をめぐる<ruby>対立<rt>たいりつ</rt></ruby>
<ruby>計画<rt>けいかく</rt></ruby>についての<ruby>説明<rt>せつめい</rt></ruby>
<ruby>規則<rt>きそく</rt></ruby>に<ruby>関<rt>かん</rt></ruby>する<ruby>通知<rt>つうち</rt></ruby>
Nを<ruby>中心<rt>ちゅうしん</rt></ruby>としたN
<ruby>若者<rt>わかもの</rt></ruby>を<ruby>中心<rt>ちゅうしん</rt></ruby>とした<ruby>活動<rt>かつどう</rt></ruby>
Same meaning; used with a predicate
<ruby>憲法<rt>けんぽう</rt></ruby>をめぐって<ruby>議論<rt>ぎろん</rt></ruby>が<ruby>続<rt>つづ</rt></ruby>く

mistakes: Using ～をめぐる as a predicate: ×「問題をめぐる。」→ grammatically incorrect.
Confusing it with ～についてのN: JLPT questions test the nuance of "controversy/opposition". If there are keywords like 対立/論争/賛否 → choose ～をめぐる.
Using it for small, personal topics → sounds exaggerated and unnatural.
Missing the noun after ～をめぐる: there must always be an N right after it (mandatory modifier).
1033.notes:
• Contracted form for headlines: 「Nをめぐる混乱」「Nをめぐる疑惑」 keeps the sentence short and informative.
• Several modifiers can be stacked: 「資源開発をめぐる国際的な政治的対立」, but use restraint so it does not become hard to read.
• Often used with adjectives: 深刻な/複雑な/激しい + NをめぐるN.

1034.connection: いつまで + V plain form + のやら

examples.jp: いつまでこの不況が続くのやら。
examples.tr: I wonder how long this recession will last.

examples.jp: いつまで待てばいいのやら、連絡が来ない。
examples.tr: I wonder how long I'm supposed to wait. No word has come.

examples.jp: いつまで我慢すればいいのやら。
examples.tr: I wonder how long I'll have to put up with this.

examples.jp: いつまで物価上昇が続くのやら、先が見えない。
examples.tr: Who knows how long prices will keep rising. There's no end in sight.

examples.jp: あの子はいつまで反抗期なのやら。
examples.tr: I wonder how long that child will be in this rebellious phase.

1034.explain:
Used when the speaker wonders to themselves about something hard to predict, with emotion attached.
Not used to question the person you are talking to; for a real question, use いつまで～か／いつまで～のですか .
Placed at the end of a sentence; the plain form comes before のやら. With na-adjectives/N, use なのやら .

いつまで～のやら expresses a feeling of uncertainty, worry, or lament: "I wonder how long…". It is a rhetorical question that does not require an answer.
• Nuance: emotion (worry, lament, weariness, helplessness), leaning toward monologue.
• Often used in light written language, diaries, and monologues; rarely used to ask other people directly.
• The sentence can end with a period or a question mark depending on style; grammatically it is a rhetorical question.

rows: いつまで<ruby>続<rt>つづ</rt></ruby>くのやら
いつまで<ruby>待<rt>ま</rt></ruby>つか<ruby>教<rt>おし</rt></ruby>えて
いつまで<ruby>続<rt>つづ</rt></ruby>くのだろうか

mistakes: Using です/ます right before のやら is incorrect: say 高いのやら, not 高いですのやら.
Using it to question other people sounds rude; the JLPT often tests distinguishing it from ～か/～のですか.
Confusing it with the listing pattern ～やら～やら (a completely different function).
1034.notes:
• のやら is more literary than のかな; it fits narration of a character's state of mind.
• Modal words can be inserted before のやら: 一体／果たして／全く to emphasize bewilderment.
• With なのやら, don't forget the な for na-adjectives/nouns.

1035.connection: どうにか(して) + V potential form ない + ものか

examples.jp: この渋滞、どうにかならないものか。
examples.tr: Isn't there something that can be done about this traffic jam?

examples.jp: 予算は厳しいが、品質だけはどうにか落とさないものか。
examples.tr: The budget is tight, but isn't there some way to at least not lower the quality?

examples.jp: 部長にどうにか時間を作ってもらえないものか。
examples.tr: Couldn't we somehow get the department manager to make some time for us?

examples.jp: この問題、専門家の力でどうにか解決できないものだろうか。
examples.tr: I wonder if this problem couldn't somehow be solved with the help of experts.

examples.jp: 事故が多すぎる。対策をどうにか急げないものか。
examples.tr: There are far too many accidents. Can't the countermeasures somehow be sped up?

1035.explain:
Used when the speaker feels pressed and wants to change a bad situation; usually a shared or work-related problem.
More formal with ないものだろうか; blunt and somewhat harsh with ないものか.
Often combined with degree words such as "どうにか/なんとか/せめて". "どうにか" is neutral; "なんとか" is more colloquial.
The one carrying out the action is usually not just the speaker; it implies the need to "find a way".
Not used for small direct requests; used for things that are difficult or have been tried without success.

- Expresses a strong desire: "Isn't there (some way) to…?", "Is there any way to…?". Often used when the matter is difficult or beyond the speaker's control.
- The nuance is complaint/regret + hope of finding a solution. The degree of longing is higher than ordinary patterns for asking opinions.
- Used with: verbs in the potential form (できる/られる), or てもらう (hoping to have someone else do it). The fixed phrase どうにかならないものか emphasizes "isn't there any way to manage?".
- "ものか" here is a particle that emphasizes a rhetorical question; it can be replaced by "ものだろうか" to soften the frustration.

rows: Strong desire: "isn't there a way to…?"
<ruby>解決<rt>かいけつ</rt></ruby>できないだろうか
Not an interrogative grammar point; often used with ないものか
なんとかならないものか
Aimed at the listener; small, casual matters
<ruby>手伝<rt>てつだ</rt></ruby>ってくれないかな
どうにかならないものか
<ruby>渋滞<rt>じゅうたい</rt></ruby>、どうにかならないものか

mistakes: Using it for easy/trivial matters → sounds too serious. Use ～てくれない？ instead of ～ないものか.
Confusing the agent: this pattern does not emphasize "I will do it" but "there is a way/someone/some condition to…".
Dropping the "potential" of the verb: prefer V-られない/できない. Example: ×増やさないものか → better: 増やせないものか.
Confusing it with a simple negative: ～ないものか is a question expressing desire, not a statement that "it is not…".
In exams, the polite answer is usually ～ないものだろうか in formal contexts (official documents, proposals).
1035.notes:
- "どうにか" and "なんとか" are mostly interchangeable; "どうにか" sounds neutral/written, "なんとか" is colloquial and more emotional.
- Polite/written forms: ～ないものだろうか ＞ ～ないだろうか ＞ ～ないものか (strong). Choose according to the relationship and context.
- せめて can be added to narrow the scope of the wish: せめて納期だけでも守れないものだろうか。

1036.meaning:
～だけ（書(か)き言葉(ことば)）
Only

examples.jp: 野球の全国大会に出場できるのは１県に1枚のみだ。
examples.tr: Only one slot per prefecture is allowed to compete in the national baseball tournament.

examples.jp: 今はただ、父が無事であるよう、祈るのみです。
examples.tr: All I can do now is pray that my father is safe.

examples.jp: 指導者はまだ厳しいのみではいけない。それでは若者はついてこないだろう。
examples.tr: A leader must not be merely strict. Otherwise, young people won't follow.

examples.jp: 最近はペーパーテストのみではなく、面接も行こう大学が増えた。
examples.tr: Recently, more universities are holding interviews, not just paper tests.

examples.jp: 彼はただ人を殺したのみか（＝ばかりか）、その罪を人に着せようとした。
examples.tr: Not only did he kill someone, he also tried to pin the crime on someone else.

examples.jp: * T大学合格には、ただ努力あるのみ！
examples.tr: * To pass the T University entrance exam, all it takes is hard work!

1037.meaning: If (by any chance)… then… (serious consequences will follow)

examples.jp: うちの犬は、外で少しでも音がしようものなら。すごい勢いで吠える。
examples.tr: If there's even the slightest sound outside, our dog barks furiously.

examples.jp:
A: レポート、大変だよね。思わず、ネットから誰かの論文を借りたくなる。
B: 気持ちはわかる。でも、そんなことをしようものなら、絶対、単位をもらえないよ。
examples.tr:
A: This report is tough, isn't it? I'm tempted to just borrow someone's paper from the internet.
B: I know how you feel. But if you did something like that, you'd definitely not get the credits.

1037.notes: A somewhat exaggerated way of stating a condition, expressing the meaning "if by any chance such a thing were to happen." It is normally followed by content saying that "a serious situation will arise." (５９８)

1038.meaning:
Let's… together! (a call to action, rallying; formal) | 一緒(いっしょ)に～しよう（他社(たしゃ)への呼(よ)びかけ）
Do… together

examples.jp: せっかくここまで来たんだから、思い切り楽しもうじゃありませんか。
examples.tr: We've come all this way, so why don't we enjoy ourselves to the fullest?

examples.jp: ＜文章＞人それぞれ悩みはある。しかし、考えているだけでは悩みは解決しない。苦しくても一歩ずつ前に進もうではないか。
examples.tr: ＜Written text＞Everyone has their own worries. But just thinking about them won't solve them. Even if it is hard, let us move forward one step at a time.

1038.notes:
explain: Expresses a strong call to action or a strong will; often used by men.
Formal sentence style.
⏐ examples: 1. 今日はお祝いだ。みんなで飲もうではないか。
Today is a celebration. Let's all drink together!
2. だれもやらないなら、ぼくがやってみようじゃないか。
If nobody else will do it, then I'll give it a try myself.

examples.jp: 彼は日本語が下手だ。おまけに、英語も話せない。
examples.tr: He's bad at Japanese. On top of that, he can't speak English either.

examples.jp: この店は高い。おまけに、サービスも悪い。
examples.tr: This shop is expensive. On top of that, the service is bad too.

examples.jp: 今日は朝から雨。おまけに、傘を忘れた。
examples.tr: It's been raining since this morning. And to top it off, I forgot my umbrella.

examples.jp: 彼は仕事が遅い。おまけに、間違いが多い。
examples.tr: He's slow at work. On top of that, he makes lots of mistakes.

examples.jp: 風邪をひいている。おまけに、熱まで出てきた。
examples.tr: I have a cold. And on top of that, I've even started running a fever.

1039.explain:
Position : At the beginning of clause B, following a complete sentence or clause A.
Nuance : Carries strong emotion, usually dissatisfaction or complaint; but it can also be used in a positive sense.
Style : Casual, colloquial; rarely used in formal written language or theses.
When used in a positive sense, the nuance is cheerful and humorous:彼は優しい。 おまけに、ハンサムだ。

•
Expresses addition: B is additional information to A, making the situation better or (usually) worse.

•
Emotional nuance: Often used when the speaker wants to complain, reproach, or emphasize that something is "unlucky, annoying, piling on".

•
Equivalent meaning in English: "On top of that…", "In addition…", "And that's not all…".

• Rarely used in formal writing; mainly appears in conversation, spoken language, stories, and casual writing.

rows: <ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。 おまけに<ruby>風<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>もある。
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。 その<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby><ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>まで<ruby>降<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>ってきた。
Presents an argument; less emotional than おまけに.
<ruby>安<rt>やす</rt></ruby>い。 しかも<ruby>品質<rt>ひんしつ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>良<rt>よ</rt></ruby>い。
Colloquial, lighter than おまけに.
<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しい。 それに<ruby>眠<rt>ねむ</rt></ruby>い。

mistakes: Confusing it with それに: それに is neutral, whereas おまけに carries a strong emotional nuance.
Using it in formal writing → inappropriate; use その上 or さらに instead.
Using it when A and B do not point in the same direction → illogical (おまけに is used when B adds information in the same direction as A).
Omitting the comma in written language: you should write "おまけに、～"。
1039.notes:
• Often used when listing successive unfavorable conditions to create a "one bad thing after another" effect.
• In casual conversation, it can be replaced by "しかもさ" or "それにしてもさ" depending on the degree of emotion.
• Positive uses also occur but are rarer and have a playful nuance. explain: Used in spoken language. A word more commonly used in speech than 「しかも」 ⏐ examples: 1. 日本の夏は暑いし、おまけに湿気も多いです。
Summers in Japan are hot, and on top of that, very humid.
2. あのそば屋は高いしまずい。おまけにサービスも悪い。
That soba shop is expensive and the food is bad. On top of that, the service is poor.

examples.jp: このパソコンは軽い。しかも、バッテリーが長持ちする。
examples.tr: This computer is light. What's more, the battery lasts a long time.

examples.jp: 彼は若い。しかも経験が豊富だ。
examples.tr: He is young. Moreover, he has a wealth of experience.

examples.jp: 渋滞している。しかも事故まで起きた。
examples.tr: There's a traffic jam. On top of that, there's even been an accident.

examples.jp: この店は味がいい。しかも値段が手頃だ。
examples.tr: The food at this restaurant is good. What's more, the prices are reasonable.

examples.jp: 雨が強い。しかも風速がどんどん上がっている。
examples.tr: The rain is heavy. What's more, the wind speed keeps rising.

1040.explain:
Used when you want to emphasize that the additional information is "significant/surprising".
Suitable for argumentative writing, presentations, and advertising.
Placed at the beginning of the sentence S2; it can also be placed mid-sentence to connect two attributes of the same subject.
Avoid using it to introduce a request/command; it sounds forced.
Often used together with まで・さえ to widen the scope.

しかも: "moreover, besides, on top of that"; emphasizes that S2 is an additional element that is surprising/noteworthy, raising the evaluation in the same direction as S1.
• Intensifying effect: S2 makes the impression stronger (better or worse).
• Style: neutral to formal; can be used in reports/articles.
• Does not express a cause-and-effect relationship; it is only emphatic addition.

rows: <ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。おまけに<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>まで。
<ruby>便利<rt>べんり</rt></ruby>だ。そのうえ<ruby>安全<rt>あんぜん</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しい。それに<ruby>眠<rt>ねむ</rt></ruby>い。
<ruby>売上<rt>うりあげ</rt></ruby>がさらに10%<ruby>伸<rt>の</rt></ruby>びた。

mistakes: Using it for a cause-and-effect relationship: ×「雨だ。しかも、試合を中止した」→ use それで/したがって instead.
Mixing it up with そのうえ/それに: questions asking you to choose a conjunction require a degree of emphasis ⇒ しかも is the answer when S2 is "more striking".
Using it with a command/suggestion sounds forced: ×「しかも、来てください」.
The direction of evaluation must be consistent (positive + positive or negative + negative) to be natural.
1040.notes:
• In rhetoric, the sequence "まず… 次に… しかも…" creates a sense of escalating argument.
• "しかも" can follow a semicolon or comma in literary writing for a stronger rhythm.
• Tip: if you want to sound more "persuasive" than それに, choose しかも. explain: Used when adding another thing or matter to a certain thing or matter. ⏐ examples: 1. 彼女は美人で頭がいい。しかも性格もいい。
She is beautiful and smart. What's more, she has a good personality.
2. 先日泊まったホテルは、古くて高かった。しかもサービスが悪かったので、もう二度と行かない。
The hotel I stayed at the other day was old and expensive. What's more, the service was bad, so I'm never going there again.

examples.jp: 台風が接近中だ。したがって、本日のイベントは中止とする。
examples.tr: A typhoon is approaching. Therefore, today's event is canceled.

examples.jp: コストが上昇した。したがって、価格改定が必要だ。
examples.tr: Costs have risen. Therefore, a price revision is necessary.

examples.jp: 証拠が不十分である。したがって、有罪とは言えない。
examples.tr: The evidence is insufficient. Therefore, it cannot be said that the defendant is guilty.

examples.jp: 需要が急拡大した。したがって、増産を検討する。
examples.tr: Demand has expanded rapidly. Therefore, we will consider increasing production.

examples.jp: この装置は老朽化している。したがって、更新を推奨する。
examples.tr: This equipment has become old and worn. Therefore, we recommend replacing it.

1041.explain:
Formal style; suitable for reports, announcements, and academic presentations.
Position: at the beginning of the sentence stating the conclusion; usually followed by a comma.
Should not be used before personal, direct commands/requests.
Often appears in argument sequences: まず/第一に →次に → したがって /結論.

したがって: "therefore/so/accordingly". States a conclusion or inevitable consequence based on the premise just mentioned. Often used in academic texts, reports, and official announcements.
• Highly logical, with little emotional nuance.
• S2 is usually a judgment, conclusion, policy, or objective resulting state.
• Unnatural when followed by a personal request or a direct command.

rows: <ruby>熱<rt>ねつ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>た。それで、<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>んだ。
Written language; emphasizes the reason rather than a logical conclusion.
<ruby>渋滞<rt>じゅうたい</rt></ruby>。そのため、<ruby>遅刻<rt>ちこく</rt></ruby>した。
Very academic/literary; stronger than したがって.
<ruby>証拠<rt>しょうこ</rt></ruby><ruby>不十分<rt>ふじゅうぶん</rt></ruby>、ゆえに<ruby>無罪<rt>むざい</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Using it before a personal request: ×「したがって、来てください」→ use ですので/それで instead.
Confusing it with そのため/それで: for sentences with academic, logical reasoning → したがって; for everyday sentences with a natural result → それで.
Mixing it up with the meaning "in accordance with": check whether an object + に comes before it (規則に従って = a different pattern from the conjunction).
1041.notes:
• Distinguish "従って" (conjunction: therefore) from "規則に従って" (meaning "in accordance with"). They look the same but function differently.
• In formal speeches there is a keigo variant "したがいまして" (rarely used in standard writing, but heard in ceremonial speech).
• Tip: if the sentence is a conclusion about a policy/regulation, したがって is usually a good choice. explain: Expresses that the following matter occurs as a natural result of the conditions in the preceding sentence.
Used in formal sentences. ⏐ examples: 1. 彼はまじめて誠実な人だ。したがってみんなから信頼されている。
He is a serious and sincere person. Therefore, he is trusted by everyone.
2. 教授は急用で来られません。したがって講義は中止です。
The professor cannot come due to urgent business. Therefore, the lecture is canceled.

examples.jp: 部屋が寒かった。そこで、暖房をつけた。
examples.tr: The room was cold. So I turned on the heater.

examples.jp: バスが来なかった。そこで、タクシーで行くことにした。
examples.tr: The bus didn't come. So I decided to take a taxi.

examples.jp: レポートの締め切りが近い。そこで、今夜は徹夜するつもりだ。
examples.tr: The report deadline is close. So I plan to stay up all night tonight.

examples.jp: パソコンが壊れてしまった。そこで、新しいのを買うことにした。
examples.tr: My computer broke. So I decided to buy a new one.

examples.jp: この問題は難しい。そこで、先生に相談してみよう。
examples.tr: This problem is difficult. So let's try asking the teacher.

1042.explain:
Position : Always at the beginning of the second clause, after a period or comma.
Suitable context : When B is an intentional action to resolve the situation in A.
Style : Reasoned and logical – often used in writing, storytelling, and reports.
Nuance : Polite and neutral; not as colloquial as それでさ, nor as formal as従って.

•
Expresses an action/solution based on the preceding situation: A is the circumstance or problem → B is the action taken to deal with or respond to it.

•
Natural translations: "So…", "Therefore…", "That's why…".

•
Emphasizes reasonableness and the speaker's deliberate conclusion: Unlike "そして", which just connects, "そこで" shows a shift to action.

•
Often used in storytelling, reports, and descriptions of how a problem was solved.

rows: Emphasizes an action to solve the problem.
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。 そこでコートを<ruby>着<rt>き</rt></ruby>た。
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。 それで<ruby>風邪<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>をひいた。
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>い。 だから<ruby>嫌<rt>いや</rt></ruby>なんだ。
The result happens immediately, often unexpectedly.
ドアを<ruby>開<rt>あ</rt></ruby>けた。 すると<ruby>猫<rt>ねこ</rt></ruby>がいた。

mistakes: Confusing it with それで: それで only states a natural result; そこで emphasizes an intentional action.
Using it for an unexpected result: Incorrect. In this case, use すると.
Illogical when A is not a problem/situation: そこで requires A to provide a reason for carrying out B.
Omitting the comma after そこで in formal written language → you should write: "そこで、…"。
1042.notes:
• Often appears in JLPT reading comprehension when explaining a solution or the steps for dealing with a problem.
• Often used in logical presentations, scientific reports, and talks: problem → solution.
• Not used when B is an emotion or an unexpected result (use すると in that case). explain: Used when developing a story. A conjunction indicating that the following sentence presents a way of solving, a suggestion, or a request. ⏐ examples: 1. 明日は車が混むらしい。そこで我々は朝早く出発するつもりだ。
I hear the roads will be crowded tomorrow. So we plan to leave early in the morning.
2. 「今度アメリカに旅行します。そこでお願いがあるのですが．．．。」
I'm going on a trip to America soon. So I have a favor to ask…

examples.jp: 一生懸命勉強した。それなのに、試験に落ちてしまった。
examples.tr: I studied really hard. And yet I failed the exam.

examples.jp: 雨が降っていた。それなのに、彼は傘を持っていなかった。
examples.tr: It was raining. And yet he didn't have an umbrella.

examples.jp: 彼女は約束した。それなのに、来なかった。
examples.tr: She promised. And yet she didn't come.

examples.jp: この店は人気だ。それなのに、今日は客が少ない。
examples.tr: This shop is popular. And yet there are few customers today.

examples.jp: 努力すればできるよって言った。それなのに、手を抜いたんだね。
examples.tr: I told you that you could do it if you tried. And yet you slacked off, didn't you?

1043.explain:
Position: Always at the beginning of the second clause, after a period or comma.
Used when you want to emphasize an emotion: disappointment, indignation, reproach, surprise.
It is not simply a result like それで, nor just “even so” like それでも; it means “it should have been different, but…”.
Often used in spoken language, conversation, or emotional narrative writing.

•
Expresses strong contrast with expectations: Clause B goes completely against what should have followed from clause A.

•
Clear emotional nuance: Usually carries feelings of reproach, surprise, disappointment, or resentment.

•
Natural translations: “And yet…”, “But…”, “Even so…”.

• Difference from それでも: それなのに emphasizes stronger emotion and a clearer contrast.

rows: <ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>した。 それなのに<ruby>負<rt>ま</rt></ruby>けた。
Acknowledges A, then B still happens (less emotional).
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>だ。 それでも<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>く。
Colloquial; no emphasis on emotion or strong contrast.
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>きたい。 でも<ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しい。
A result completely contrary to expectation, with a feeling of “oh no!”.
<ruby>勝<rt>か</rt></ruby>つと<ruby>思<rt>おも</rt></ruby>った。 ところが<ruby>負<rt>ま</rt></ruby>けた。

mistakes: Confusing it with それでも: それでも = “even so, still…”, while それなのに = “and yet…” (emphasizes disappointment).
Using it when the two sentences have no contrasting relationship is incorrect.
Using it in very formal writing is inappropriate; replace it with しかしながら or とはいえ.
Omitting the comma in written language → it should be written “それなのに、…”。
1043.notes:
• Common in everyday conversation, anime and manga when a character expresses emotion.
• Works well in narrative writing when you want to emphasize the conflict between expectation and reality.
• Often translated as “And yet…”, “But…”, “Even so…”. meaning_vi: But, and yet ～ ⏐ explain: Expresses an unexpected result. ⏐ examples: 1. この時計は高かった。それなのにすぐに壊れた。
This watch was expensive. And yet it broke right away.
2. 一生懸命勉強している。それなのに成績はよくならない。
I'm studying hard. And yet my grades aren't improving.

examples.jp: 参加は無料。ただし、事前登録が必要だ。
examples.tr: Participation is free. However, advance registration is required.

examples.jp: 喫煙可。ただし、指定の場所に限る。
examples.tr: Smoking permitted. However, only in designated areas.

examples.jp: 契約は自動更新とする。ただし、両者の合意により変更できる。
examples.tr: The contract will be renewed automatically. However, it may be changed by agreement of both parties.

examples.jp: 学割を適用します。ただし、学生証の提示が条件です。
examples.tr: We will apply the student discount. However, you must present your student ID.

examples.jp: この薬は成人向け。ただし、妊娠中の方は医師に相談のこと。
examples.tr: This medicine is for adults. However, pregnant women should consult a doctor.

1044.explain:
Always at the beginning of the sentence that follows, followed by a comma: “ただし、…”.
Suitable for setting the scope/conditions of application, not for emotional argument.
In company documents, なお adds information, while ただし sets a condition/exception.

• Establishes an exception/additional condition that restricts the previous sentence.
• Highly prescriptive; stiffer and more formal in nuance than ただ or でも.
• S2 often contains conditional wording: ～に限る／～を除く／～場合は／要～／原則として…など.

rows: <ruby>無料<rt>むりょう</rt></ruby>。ただし、<ruby>会員<rt>かいいん</rt></ruby>のみ。
<ruby>便利<rt>べんり</rt></ruby>だ。ただ、<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>い。
<ruby>賛成<rt>さんせい</rt></ruby><ruby>多数<rt>たすう</rt></ruby>。しかし、<ruby>不満<rt>ふまん</rt></ruby>もある。
<ruby>受付<rt>うけつけ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>9時<rt>きゅうじ</rt></ruby>。なお、<ruby>土日<rt>どにち</rt></ruby>は<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>み。
<ruby>祝日<rt>しゅくじつ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>除<rt>のぞ</rt></ruby>く<ruby>平日<rt>へいじつ</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Using ただし for contrasting personal opinions → unnatural; use しかし/でも/ただ instead.
S2 lacks a prescriptive element (no condition/limitation) → wrong choice in reading questions.
Confusing なお with ただし: なお only adds information and imposes no restriction.
JLPT questions often set the trap “無料。なお、事前登録が必要だ。” → the nuance is not quite right; the answer is usually ただし.
1044.notes:
• “ただし書き” is the “hedging” clause in regulations; it usually follows a declarative main clause.
• In polite emails you can use: ただし、〜となります／〜が必要となります。
• When S2 is a safety warning, ただし helps the reader notice its importance immediately.

examples.jp: このプランは安い。ただ、データ容量が少ない。
examples.tr: This plan is cheap. The only thing is, the data allowance is small.

examples.jp: 明日は出勤しなくていい。ただ、午前中に報告書を提出しておいて。
examples.tr: You don't need to come to work tomorrow. Just make sure to submit the report in the morning, though.

examples.jp: この薬はよく効く。ただ、眠くなることがある。
examples.tr: This medicine works well. However, it can make you drowsy.

examples.jp: 今日は晴れる予報だ。ただ、午後から風が強くなるらしい。
examples.tr: The forecast says it will be sunny today. However, the wind is apparently going to get stronger in the afternoon.

examples.jp: この本は読みやすい。ただ、専門用語が多い。
examples.tr: This book is easy to read. The only thing is, it has a lot of technical terms.

1045.explain:
Placed at the beginning of the sentence that follows, followed by a comma: “ただ、…”.
S2 is usually an additional condition, an exception, or a safety note.
Neutral and moderately polite; can be used in everyday work emails.
Avoid using ただ for rigid regulations/legal clauses (use ただし in that case).

• Restrictive addition: S2 states a condition, exception, drawback, or note regarding the information in S1.
• Strength: softer than しかし, more neutral than でも; not as formal as ただし.
• Nuance: “S1 is true, it's just that / however S2”. It does not negate S1 but adjusts expectations.
• Context: usable in both spoken and written language; suitable for explanations, negotiations, and stating accompanying conditions.

rows: Soft; fine in both spoken and written language
<ruby>安<rt>やす</rt></ruby>い。ただ、<ruby>質<rt>しつ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>普通<rt>ふつう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>賛成<rt>さんせい</rt></ruby><ruby>多数<rt>たすう</rt></ruby>。しかし、<ruby>課題<rt>かだい</rt></ruby>は<ruby>残<rt>のこ</rt></ruby>る。
Strongly colloquial, rarely used in serious writing
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>きたい。でも、<ruby>時間<rt>じかん</rt></ruby>がない。
Used for regulations and formal conditions
<ruby>無料<rt>むりょう</rt></ruby>。ただし、<ruby>学生<rt>がくせい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>限<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>る。
Written language; concession followed by a counterpoint
<ruby>簡単<rt>かんたん</rt></ruby>だ。とはいえ、<ruby>注意<rt>ちゅうい</rt></ruby>は<ruby>必要<rt>ひつよう</rt></ruby>だ。

mistakes: Confusing ただ with ただし: questions about regulations/clauses call for ただし, not ただ.
Missing comma after ただ: it should be written “ただ、…”.
Rigid machine-like translation as “however” in every context: for mild requests, translate as “it's just that / but”.
Choosing しかし when a strong counterargument is needed; ただ is a milder level.
1045.notes:
• In presentations, ただ helps “soften the blow” when bringing up a drawback after praise.
• Placing ただ between two short sentences saves words compared with けれども/とはいえ while still sounding natural.
• Do not confuse it with ただ = “only/just”: ただ一つ (only one), ただの冗談 (just a joke).

examples.jp: 経費を削減した。だが、赤字は解消していない。
examples.tr: We cut expenses. But the deficit has not been eliminated.

examples.jp: 彼は若い。だが、経験は豊富だ。
examples.tr: He is young. But he has a wealth of experience.

examples.jp: 全力で走った。だが、追いつけなかった。
examples.tr: I ran as fast as I could. But I couldn't catch up.

examples.jp: 提案は斬新だ。だが、実現性に乏しい。
examples.tr: The proposal is innovative. But it lacks feasibility.

examples.jp: 雨はやんだ。だが、路面は依然として滑りやすい。
examples.tr: The rain has stopped. But the road surface is still slippery.

1046.explain:
Used to move on to a clearly contrasting clause, keeping the style strong and concise.
Suits narration, argument, and exposition. In polite conversation, しかし/でも/けれども are usually used.
Can stand at the beginning of a paragraph/beginning of a sentence to create a decisive rhythm.

• Meaning: “But/However”. A logical contrastive link, with a written-language, decisive nuance.
• Nuance: masculine, strongly assertive; often seen in essays, expository texts, and journalistic/narrative style.
• Neutrality: less emotional than それなのに; more forceful than しかし in tone (not necessarily in logic).

rows: Neutral and more general; less “sharp” than だが
<ruby>急<rt>いそい</rt></ruby>いだ。しかし<ruby>間<rt>ま</rt></ruby>に<ruby>合<rt>あ</rt></ruby>わず。
Implies resentment/surprise; だが is more neutral
<ruby>約束<rt>やくそく</rt></ruby>。それなのに<ruby>来<rt>こ</rt></ruby>ない。
<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>いけれども<ruby>必要<rt>ひつよう</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Confusing the conjunction “だが” with “〜だ + が” within one sentence: questions may set a trap about sentence-component analysis. A period before だが signals that it is a conjunction.
Using だが in polite conversation with customers → sounds rough; choose しかし/けれども.
Using だが for a concessive “still do it” relationship → off in nuance (use それでも instead).
1046.notes:
• だが is an independent conjunction, different from “〜だ + が” (copula + contrastive particle) within a sentence. Although they look the same, their functions differ.
• In advertising/entertainment style, “だがしかし” is used for exaggeration and rhythm.
• Using だが many times in a row can make the text stiff; alternate it with しかし/一方/ところが depending on the argument. explain: A stiff way of saying　「しかし」　「けれども」. ⏐ examples: 1. これは難しい挑戦だ。だが失敗を恐れてはいけない。
This is a difficult challenge. But we must not be afraid of failure.
2. 生活は貧しい。だが幸せだ。
Life is poor. But I'm happy.

examples.jp: 会議は10時からです。ちなみに、場所は第3会議室です。
examples.tr: The meeting starts at 10. By the way, it will be held in Meeting Room 3.

examples.jp: この店は評判がいい。ちなみに、オーナーは元プロ選手だ。
examples.tr: This restaurant has a good reputation. Incidentally, the owner is a former professional athlete.

examples.jp: このソフトは無料。ちなみに、有料版もある。
examples.tr: This software is free. By the way, there is also a paid version.

examples.jp: 彼は大阪出身だ。ちなみに、方言はあまり出ない。
examples.tr: He is from Osaka. Incidentally, he doesn't have much of an accent.

examples.jp: 来週は出張です。ちなみに、金曜は在宅勤務にします。
examples.tr: I'm on a business trip next week. By the way, I'll be working from home on Friday.

1047.explain:
Placed at the beginning of a sentence (a new one), followed by a comma: “ちなみに、…”.
It gives additional information, not a “condition/exception” and not a “conclusion”.
In formal writing, なお replaces ちなみに when a stiffer style is wanted.

• “By the way / incidentally”: provides useful side information that does not determine the main flow.
• Keeps the connection to the topic; it should not change the topic abruptly like ところで.
• Often used in presentations, emails and conversation to insert an interesting/related fact.

rows: Does not change the topic abruptly
<ruby>締切<rt>しめきり</rt></ruby>は<ruby>金曜<rt>きんよう</rt></ruby>。ちなみに、<ruby>土曜<rt>どよう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>休<rt>やす</rt></ruby>み。
Switches to a new topic, changes direction
ところで、<ruby>週末<rt>しゅうまつ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>予定<rt>よてい</rt></ruby>は？
While doing A, also do B
<ruby>買<rt>か</rt></ruby>い<ruby>物<rt>もの</rt></ruby>ついでに<ruby>切符<rt>きっぷ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>買<rt>か</rt></ruby>う。
<ruby>受付<rt>うけつけ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>9時<rt>きゅうじ</rt></ruby>。なお、<ruby>午後<rt>ごご</rt></ruby>は<ruby>休止<rt>きゅうし</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Using ちなみに to introduce a binding condition → wrong function; ただし must be used.
Confusing it with ところで: questions testing the topic usually require ところで for a sharp shift.
Inserting ちなみに too often confuses the flow; in writing, the answer is sometimes なお (more formal).
1047.notes:
• Use ちなみに to slip in a “fun fact” and make a talk lively, but don't overuse it and dilute the main flow.
• In polite emails: “ちなみにですが、〜をご存じでしょうか。” opens a topic gently.
• If the added information is a condition/exception, switch to ただし/なお for the right nuance. explain: Used to add a small piece of information to the previous sentence (a). ⏐ examples: 1. 最近は、ペットを飼う家が増えているようです。ちなみに、うちにも犬が１ 匹とネコが２ 匹います。
It seems that more and more households have pets these days. By the way, we have one dog and two cats at our house too.
2. 燃えるゴミは月曜日と木曜日、燃えないゴミは金曜日に出してください。ちなみに資源ごみの収集日は第３水曜日です。
Please put out burnable garbage on Mondays and Thursdays and non-burnable garbage on Fridays. By the way, recyclables are collected on the third Wednesday of the month.

examples.jp: 本日は臨時休館です。なお、明日は通常どおり開館します。
examples.tr: We are temporarily closed today. Please note that we will open as usual tomorrow.

examples.jp: 応募はオンラインのみ受け付けます。なお、郵送での応募はできません。
examples.tr: Applications are accepted online only. Please note that applications cannot be submitted by mail.

examples.jp: 参加費は1,000円です。なお、学生は無料です。
examples.tr: The participation fee is 1,000 yen. Note that it is free for students.

examples.jp: 資料を添付しました。なお、詳細は3ページをご参照ください。
examples.tr: I have attached the materials. For details, please refer to page 3.

examples.jp: 受付は17時まで。なお土日は休み。
examples.tr: Reception until 5 p.m. Closed on Saturdays and Sundays.

1048.explain:
Placed at the beginning of the sentence in B; always followed by a comma to separate the content.
Neutral-to-formal tone; suited to official documents, rarely used in casual conversation (replaced by それで/それから/あと).
When it means a “mild exception”, it is weaker than ただし and lacks the strong counterargument nuance of しかし.
Often used with instructional verbs: ご確認ください／ご注意ください／お問い合わせください.

• Adding information: Adds related details, often important to the reader.
• Note/reminder: Shifts to a tone of instruction, warning, or additional rules.
• Correction/exception: States a special case without negating the previous content.
• Nuance: Formal; typical of announcements, administrative documents, manuals, and work emails.

rows: Not the conjunction “なお”; different meaning
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>いからなおさら<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>きたくない。

mistakes: Using なお in casual conversation → sounds stiff; use それで/それから/あと.
Confusing なお with ただし: なお is not strong enough to set a binding condition.
Confusing it with なおさら (all the more) → different part of speech and meaning.
Omitting the comma after なお makes the sentence hard to read; in JLPT reading questions, the comma helps identify the structure.
1048.notes:
• In headings/signs, the subject and particles can be omitted: なお、入場は一方通行.
• The kanji 尚 is often used in formal writing; on computers/forms you may see it written entirely in kanji.
• In emails, “なお” often comes right before a sentence containing a keigo verb requesting an action. explain: Used when adding something to the conversation. It does not necessarily have to be related to the previous sentence.
2
「今日はこれで終わります。 なお 次回の日時は・・・」 We'll finish here for today. In addition, the date and time of the next session is…

examples.jp: 彼の提案には賛成だ。もっとも、予算内でできるならだが。
examples.tr: I agree with his proposal. Mind you, that's only if it can be done within the budget.

examples.jp: 日本に留学したい。もっとも、親が許せばだけど。
examples.tr: I want to study abroad in Japan. That is, if my parents allow it.

examples.jp: このカメラは性能がいい。もっとも、値段も高いけどね。
examples.tr: This camera performs well. Mind you, it's expensive too.

examples.jp: 試験は簡単だったと思う。もっとも、合格できたかどうかは別だけど。
examples.tr: I think the exam was easy. Whether I passed or not is another matter, though.

examples.jp: 行かないと言った。もっとも、気が変わるかもしれないけど。
examples.tr: I said I wouldn't go. Then again, I might change my mind.

1049.explain:
Placed at the beginning of clause B to correct or supplement clause A.
It does not completely negate A, but softens the statement or adds a condition.
Nuance: Polite and reasoned, somewhat written, as if “making the statement more precise”.
Not strongly emotional like それなのに or それでも; leans toward reasoning and supplementing.

•
Used to add supplementary information, an exception, or to adjust the statement in the preceding clause.

• Close in meaning to “However / Even so / That said…”.
•
Clause B does not completely negate clause A, but only limits it or corrects it to be more precise.

• Often used in written language, mildly formal spoken language, and logical presentation.

rows: Adds an exception/condition without completely negating the previous idea.
<ruby>便利<rt>べんり</rt></ruby>だ。 もっとも、<ruby>高<rt>たか</rt></ruby>いが。
B shows an action/determination that overcomes A.
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>だ。 それでも<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>く。
Disappointment; B strongly contradicts the expectation from A.
<ruby>約束<rt>やくそく</rt></ruby>した。 それなのに<ruby>来<rt>こ</rt></ruby>なかった。
Argumentative, strongly negating; used in formal written language.
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>来<rt>く</rt></ruby>ると<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>った。 しかし<ruby>来<rt>こ</rt></ruby>なかった。

mistakes: Confusing it with それでも: それでも = doing B anyway even though A is an obstacle; もっとも = only adds an exception or condition.
Using it in strongly emotional contexts such as complaining → unnatural; use それなのに・でも instead.
Omitting clause A: もっとも always builds on preceding information.
Omitting the comma: in written language, write “もっとも、～”。
1049.notes:
• Appears very often in JLPT reading passages when the author states the main point and then adjusts it with もっとも to be precise or to add an exception.
• Can be translated flexibly: “However”, “That said…”, “Of course…”, “The only thing is…”.
• Usually comes after a period or comma, or can be written as: 「～。 もっとも～。」. explain: Used when supplementing the previous sentence by adding an exception or condition. ⏐ examples: 1. 検査の前夜から飲食禁止です。もっとも水は飲んでもかまいません。
You may not eat or drink from the night before the examination. That said, drinking water is fine.
2. 全員が参加しなければなりません。もっとも病気の場合の別です。
Everyone must participate. That said, cases of illness are an exception.

examples.jp: いろいろ考えた。要するに、やってみるしかない。
examples.tr: I thought about it from every angle. In short, there's nothing to do but give it a try.

examples.jp: 彼は忙しいし、興味もないらしい。要するに、来ないってことだ。
examples.tr: He's busy, and apparently he's not interested either. In short, he isn't coming.

examples.jp: 説明が長くなったけど、要するに、この機械はもう使えない。
examples.tr: My explanation got long, but in short, this machine can't be used anymore.

examples.jp: あれこれ理由を言っていたけど、要するに、行きたくないんでしょ？
examples.tr: You gave all sorts of reasons, but basically, you just don't want to go, right?

examples.jp: この仕事は難しいし時間もかかる。要するに、覚悟が必要だ。
examples.tr: This job is difficult and takes time. In short, you need to be prepared for it.

1050.explain:
Placed at the beginning of clause B to draw out the essence/core of clause A.
Nuance: Objective/neutral, or sometimes a little cold and blunt.
Often used when the speaker wants to conclude quickly, or feels the listener is rambling.
Appears often in spoken language, presentations, reports, and JLPT reading tests.

•
Summarizes and concludes the preceding content briefly and concisely.

•
Expresses the main point or essence of a matter after a long or detailed explanation.

•
Natural translations: “In short…”, “In other words…”, “Basically…”, “In the end…”.

• Often used in explanations, presentations, logical conversation, or to emphasize a personal opinion.

rows: States a brief conclusion after a detailed explanation.
Restates the same information in a different way.
<ruby>日本語<rt>にほんご</rt></ruby>、 つまり、<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>言葉<rt>ことば</rt></ruby>。
Emphasizes the final result after a process.
<ruby>結局<rt>けっきょく</rt></ruby>、<ruby>来<rt>こ</rt></ruby>なかった。
More colloquial; close in meaning to <ruby>要<rt>よう</rt></ruby>するに.
<ruby>要<rt>よう</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>時間<rt>じかん</rt></ruby>がない。

mistakes: Confusing it with つまり: つまり = restating information in a different way; 要するに = drawing a conclusion.
Using it when there is no content yet to summarize → unnatural.
Using it in very formal writing such as a thesis → use “結論としては…, 要するに…” or other academic expressions.
Omitting the comma/、 after 要するに in written language is non-standard.
1050.notes:
• Usually placed after a period or comma: 「～。 要するに、～。」
• Common in expository texts when the author wants to emphasize the result or the core point.
• Can sound a little sarcastic in conversation: “要するにさ、君はやりたくないんでしょ？” meaning_vi: To put it briefly, in short ～ ⏐ explain: Means explaining the previous sentence in a simple way. ⏐ examples: 1. 試合に大負けした。要するに、相手のチームと力の差があったということだ。
We lost the match badly. In short, there was a gap in ability between us and the other team.
2. 彼は一度も入賞しなかった。要するに、才能がなかったということだ。
He never once won a prize. In short, he had no talent.

1051.meaning:
～すぎた結果(けっか)→（-）の結果(けっか)
Because of an extreme degree, an excessive result

examples.jp: 緊張のあまり気分が悪くなった。
examples.tr: I was so nervous that I started to feel sick.

examples.jp: 母は心配のあまり病気になってしまった。
examples.tr: My mother worried so much that she fell ill.

examples.jp: 現代の日本には、体系を気にするあまり過激なダイエットをする女性がいる。
examples.tr: In Japan today, there are women who are so concerned about their figure that they go on extreme diets.

examples.jp: 日本では経済成長を急ぐあまりに、環境破壊が急激に進んだ。
examples.tr: In its rush for economic growth, Japan saw environmental destruction advance rapidly.

examples.jp: ゲームに熱中していたあまり、父が帰ってきたことに気がつかなかった。
examples.tr: I was so absorbed in my game that I didn't notice my father had come home.

examples.jp: *あまりに寒くて（=寒さのあまり）息ができなかった。
examples.tr: *It was so cold that I couldn't breathe (= because of the extreme cold, I couldn't breathe).

1051.notes: Attaches to nouns and verbs expressing emotions or states to show that their degree is extreme; the second half describes an undesirable result that happened because of it.

examples.jp: 支払い方法は現金、あるいはクレジットカードをご利用いただけます。
examples.tr: You may pay in cash or by credit card.

examples.jp: 参加は明日、あるいは来週でも構いません。
examples.tr: You can join tomorrow or even next week.

examples.jp: 対面か、あるいはオンラインか、どちらにしますか。
examples.tr: Which would you prefer, in person or online?

examples.jp: あるいは、原因は設定ミスかもしれない。
examples.tr: Perhaps the cause is a configuration error.

examples.jp: 資料は日本語、あるいは英語で提出してください。
examples.tr: Please submit the documents in Japanese or English.

1052.explain:
The form “N、あるいは N” is common in formal announcements and instructions.
At the beginning of a sentence, “あるいは、...” carries a polite nuance of conjecture.
In alternative questions, それとも is preferred; “Xか、あるいはYか” is emphatic/written.

- A conjunction/adverb meaning “or; or else; perhaps”.
- Formal nuance, suitable for official documents, regulations, and technical descriptions.
- With “か”: use the frame “Xか、あるいはYか” to emphasize two mutually exclusive possibilities.

rows: Formal; close to あるいは

mistakes: Wrong particle combination: (x) A あるいは B か → (o) A か、あるいは B か.
Using あるいは in a plain question sounds stiff; それとも is preferred.
Confusing the nuance with または/もしくは: at the beginning of a sentence, あるいは can express conjecture.
1052.notes:
• When listing more than 2 items, you can say: A、B、あるいはC のいずれか.
• “あるいは” can stand mid-sentence with commas before and after to separate ideas clearly.
• In technical specifications, “または” and “もしくは/あるいは” sometimes differ in scope; follow the document's conventions. explain: A choice between two things or two sides.
A stiff way of saying　「または」 ⏐ examples: 1. ファックス、あるいはメールでお知らせください。
Please let us know by fax or email.
2. 来週の火曜日の午後はどうですか。あるいは水曜日の午前でもかまいませんが・・・。
How about next Tuesday afternoon? Or Wednesday morning would also be fine…

1053.meaning: at least ～, it could be worse
1053.connection: V plain form + だけましだ / N + である / Na / Aい

examples.jp: 君は仕事があるだけましだよ。俺は首になってしまった。
examples.tr: At least you still have a job. I got fired.

examples.jp: 給料が減ったけれど、首にならないだけましだ。
examples.tr: My salary was cut, but at least I didn't get fired.

examples.jp: 僕のアパートは、狭くて高いけれど、便利なだけましだ。
examples.tr: My apartment is small and expensive, but at least it's convenient.

1053.explain: Expresses that although a situation is not very good, the fact that it is at that level and not worse is already quite fortunate.

1054.meaning: No sooner… than…; just when you think…, …

examples.jp: この時期は、晴れていたかと思うと、急に降り出すことがあるから、傘を持っていったら？
examples.tr: At this time of year, just when you think it's sunny, it can suddenly start raining, so why not take an umbrella?

examples.jp: 日曜なのに、お父さん、忙しそうだね。さっき戻ったかと思うと、また出かけて行った。
examples.tr: Dad seems busy even though it's Sunday. He came back a moment ago, and then went straight out again.

examples.jp: 子どもから高齢者に至るまで楽しめるイベントです。
examples.tr: This is an event that everyone from children to the elderly can enjoy.

examples.jp: 企画から販売に至るまで一貫して社内で行う。
examples.tr: Everything from planning to sales is handled in-house from start to finish.

examples.jp: 春から冬に至るまで観光客が絶えない。
examples.tr: From spring all the way to winter, there is never a shortage of tourists.

examples.jp: 生活必需品からぜいたく品に至るまで幅広く扱う。
examples.tr: We handle a wide range of goods, from daily necessities to luxury items.

examples.jp: 都市部から離島に至るまでネットワークを整備した。
examples.tr: We built a network reaching from urban areas all the way to remote islands.

1055.explain:
Used in written language, presentations, and descriptions of services/products/targets.
N2 is usually the extreme point or a representative example of the other end of the range.
Placed before a main clause describing an all-encompassing action: 〜に至るまで + V.
Not used for step-by-step concrete physical distance; used for a general scope.
Emphasizes comprehensiveness: goes with words like幅広く,一貫して, あらゆる.

～から～に至るまで means “from ... all the way to ...”, emphasizing a scope that stretches from the starting point to the end point, usually with a formal nuance; used in explanations, reports, and advertising.
• Creates a feeling of “covering everything”, “reaching even the extreme/periphery”.
• Often used when N2 is a surprising or distant extreme, or to emphasize comprehensiveness.
• Compared with ～から～まで: more formal, with a stronger “all the way to” nuance.
• “至る” is a verb meaning “to reach (a level/point)”, used in the linking form “に至るまで”.

rows: Less formal; does not stress “all the way to”
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもから<ruby>大人<rt>おとな</rt></ruby>まで
Stresses a vague range, not just two extremes
<ruby>朝<rt>あさ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>昼<rt>ひる</rt></ruby>にかけて
To lead to, to reach (a result/point)
A concluding verb, not a scope construction
<ruby>交渉<rt>こうしょう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>決裂<rt>けつれつ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>至<rt>いた</rt></ruby>る
Covering everything from A all the way to B
<ruby>商品<rt>しょうひん</rt></ruby>からサービスに<ruby>至<rt>いた</rt></ruby>るまで

mistakes: Confusing it with ～まで: without “に至る”, the formal/comprehensive nuance is lost.
Choosing an illogical A–B pair (not two extremes) makes the sentence lose its emphatic force.
JLPT: a trap is replacing it with ～から～にかけて; if the question wants “all the way to the extreme” → choose ～に至るまで.
Using it with verbs/modifiers: it must be N + に至るまで; V does not attach directly to に至るまで.
1055.notes:
• Choose an N1 and N2 that are opposite or far apart for good rhythm.
• When listing more than two, use “N1からN2、N3に至るまで”.
• In marketing: “企画から運用に至るまでワンストップで提供”.
• In academic writing: “古代から近代に至るまでの変遷”.

1056.connection: V volitional form + か + Vる + まいか

examples.jp: 彼に本当のことを話そうか話すまいか、ずっと悩んでいる。
examples.tr: I've been agonizing over whether or not to tell him the truth.

examples.jp: 就職するか進学するまいか、親と相談して決めるつもりだ。
examples.tr: I plan to talk it over with my parents and decide whether to get a job or not go on to further study.

examples.jp: 今買おうか買うまいか迷っているうちに、売り切れてしまった。
examples.tr: While I was hesitating over whether or not to buy it now, it sold out.

examples.jp: 帰国しようかするまいか、最後まで決めかねた。
examples.tr: Right up to the end, I couldn't decide whether or not to return to my country.

examples.jp: 会議に出ようか出るまいか考えている。
examples.tr: I'm thinking about whether or not to attend the meeting.

1056.explain:
Used to emphasize the process of hesitation; suitable for essays and narration.
Goes well with verbs related to decisions:決める,迷う,悩む,考える.
This phrase is usually followed by a result/development: ～か～まいか、結局～／～と考えた。
With する: both するまいか and すまいか are seen; するまいか is preferred in modern Japanese.

• Expresses hesitation between two choices, “to do or not to do”.
• More formal than VるかVないか; has a written/speech-like tone.
• The subject is usually the speaker or the decision-maker; describes the process of deliberation.
• Sometimes used to set up the hesitation before a decision: ～か～まいか、結局…

rows: <ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>こうか<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くまいか<ruby>迷<rt>まよ</rt></ruby>う
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くか<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>かないか<ruby>決<rt>き</rt></ruby>める
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>降<rt>くだ</rt></ruby>ろうが<ruby>降<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>るまいが<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>く
Nominalized clause; does not stress hesitation
<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くかどうか<ruby>分<rt>わ</rt></ruby>からない
<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うべきか<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うべきでないか

mistakes: Wrong form: the second part must be “Vる＋まいか” (or Vまいか with ichidan verbs), not “ないか”.
Confusing it with ～ようが～まいが (regardless) leads to the wrong meaning.
Using it in casual speech sounds stiff; the JLPT likes to test the formal nuance of this pattern.
Using different verbs in the two clauses: the same verb must be used to create the correct correspondence.
1056.notes:
• “まい” is an old-fashioned negative volitional form; today it mainly survives in this formula and in ～まいと思う.
• In spoken language, VるかVないか is usually used instead to sound more natural.
• In titles/literature, this pattern creates a symmetrical rhythm and adds emphasis.

1057.connection: Vます(drop ます) + がい (やりがい・生きがい)

examples.jp: このプロジェクトは学びがいがある。
examples.tr: This project is worth learning from.

examples.jp: 子どもが成長すると、育てがいを感じる。
examples.tr: As children grow up, you feel that raising them was worth the effort.

examples.jp: 並んだわりに味が普通で、待ちがいがなかった。
examples.tr: Despite the long line, the taste was ordinary, so it wasn't worth the wait.

examples.jp: 歴史好きには読みがいのある資料だ。
examples.tr: These are materials well worth reading for history lovers.

1057.explain:
Can take an object complement: ～をV-ます + がいがある（実習生を教えがいがある）.
Not used with purely stative verbs/verbs with no clear output.

- Emotional focus: the speaker “feels it was worth the effort”.
- Suitable for spoken language, job advertisements, and sharing experiences.

rows: <ruby>努力<rt>どりょく</rt></ruby>の<ruby>甲斐<rt>かい</rt></ruby>があった
Used when logical argument is needed
<ruby>投資<rt>とうし</rt></ruby>する<ruby>価値<rt>かち</rt></ruby>がある

mistakes: Dropping “が” after がい: “やりがいある” → unnatural; should be “やりがいがある”.
Using it with verbs that produce no result: for example, “あるがい” is incorrect.
Confusing it with 甲斐があって: that is a result clause after the action is done; ～がいがある is a general evaluation.
1057.notes:
• Many words combine naturally: 教えがい／鍛えがい／挑みがい／撮りがい／見がい／味わいがい.
• “見がい” exists, but “見ごたえ” is more common to express “worth seeing”. examples: 1. やりがいのある仕事
Work worth doing
2. 教えがいのある生徒
A student worth teaching

1058.connection: Nが + Vられる（spontaneous・potential: 感じられる・思い出される）

examples.jp: 彼の発言には誠意が感じられる。
examples.tr: Sincerity can be felt in what he says.

examples.jp: この作品から作者の葛藤がうかがわれる。
examples.tr: The author's inner conflict can be glimpsed in this work.

examples.jp: 春になると、故郷の景色が思い出される。
examples.tr: When spring comes, the scenery of my hometown comes back to me.

examples.jp: 現場ではいくつかの安全上の問題が見受けられる。
