• The structure is often written entirely in kanji for extra formality: 撮影禁止／撮影斯くの如し 等; however, べからず is still historically common.
• In classical literature/speeches, べからず can be used figuratively: 恐れるべからず (do not fear), but this usage is almost never seen in modern Japanese.

examples.jp: 生産性を高めるべく、新しいシステムを導入した。
examples.tr: A new system was introduced in order to raise productivity.

examples.jp: 顧客満足度を向上させるべく、アンケート調査を実施する。
examples.tr: A questionnaire survey will be conducted in order to improve customer satisfaction.

examples.jp: 留学すべく、奨学金の情報を集めている。
examples.tr: I'm gathering information on scholarships in order to study abroad.

examples.jp: 渋滞を緩和するべく、通勤時間をずらす。
examples.tr: We stagger commuting hours in order to ease traffic congestion.

examples.jp: 地域活性化を図るべく、イベントが企画された。
examples.tr: An event was planned with the aim of revitalizing the region.

examples.jp: 彼は自己分析を深めるべく、日記をつけ始めた。
examples.tr: He started keeping a diary in order to deepen his self-analysis.

1380.explain:
Puts the “purpose” at the beginning of the sentence: [Purpose] + べく、[Action]. Creates a formal, coherent style.
Not used with direct commands/requests: ×時間を守るべく、早く来てください → use ために/ように instead.
Not used when the two clauses have different subjects; with a different subject, use ために or ように.
Combines naturally with:実施する,取り組む,図る,導入する,開始する,強化する,設置する,改善する.

• Meaning: “To/in order to V; with the purpose of V”. Used before the main clause expressing an action aimed at achieving goal V.
• Formal nuance, often found in reports, news and planning documents: 〜すべく、〜を目指す/実施する/開始する/取り組む.
• Subject restriction: as a rule, the same agent carries out the purpose and the main action (like ために; unlike ように, which is used for goals of ability/results beyond one's control).

rows: <ruby>合格<rt>ごうかく</rt></ruby>すべく<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>する。
<ruby>合格<rt>ごうかく</rt></ruby>するために<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>する。
Used for goals beyond one's control, often with なる/できる
<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れないように<ruby>目覚<rt>めざ</rt></ruby>ましをかける。
<ruby>起<rt>お</rt></ruby>こるべくして<ruby>起<rt>お</rt></ruby>こった。
Idiom from なる + べく, a different meaning

mistakes: Using it when the subjects differ: × 学生を増やすべく、大学は奨学金が設けられた → use ために; or adjust the subjects so they match.
Using it for direct commands/requests: pragmatically inappropriate (use ために/ように/てもらう).
Confusing it with べくもない (there is no way…): this is a different pattern, not “purpose”.
1380.notes:
• With サ変 nouns, “N + するべく/すべく” is very natural: 改善すべく, 検討すべく, 強化すべく.
• In headlines/plans, べく comes right after the goal: コスト削減すべく新体制へ.
• Chains of purpose: より良い社会を実現すべく、〜に取り組む/〜を推進する: common in policy writing.

examples.jp: 当時の記録は失われ、真相は今となっては知るべくもない。
examples.tr: The records from that time have been lost, so there is no way of knowing the truth now.

examples.jp: この資金力では大企業に太刀打ちするべくもない。
examples.tr: With this level of funding, there is no way we can compete with large corporations.

examples.jp: 私の実力は彼とは比べるべくもない。
examples.tr: My ability cannot even be compared with his.

examples.jp: この景気で昇給など望むべくもない。
examples.tr: In this economy, a pay raise is out of the question.

examples.jp: 詳細は機密で、外部の者には知るべくもない。
examples.tr: The details are confidential, so outsiders cannot possibly know them.

1381.explain:
Mainly used in written language, essays and newspapers. In conversation, it is usually replaced by とても〜ない／どうにもならない.
Often accompanied by phrases that emphasize hopelessness:今となっては, この状況では, そもそも,元より.
The first clause usually presents the circumstances that make the action impossible; the second clause is ～るべくもない.
Not used for advice or commands; it is the speaker's objective judgment.

• Expresses impossibility: "cannot possibly…", "there is no way to…". The speaker judges that something cannot be done/achieved because of circumstances, information or ability.
• Often used with verbs of cognition/evaluation such as 知る・理解する・想像する・望む・期待する, or as 比べるべくもない when there is a large gap in a comparison.
• Formal, rational nuance; suited to written language and analytical writing. Close to "どうしようもない/不可能だ" but more objective and calm.
• It is a strong negation of feasibility, not simply "should not" (unlike ～べきではない).

rows: Similar meaning but neutral and more conversational.
<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby><ruby>先<rt>さき</rt></ruby>がないので、<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>らせようがない。
Negates possibility but leans toward emotion.
あの<ruby>人<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>が<ruby>負<rt>ま</rt></ruby>けるわけがない。
Different axis of meaning: "should not" vs "cannot".
そんな<ruby>言<rt>いいかた</rt></ruby>い<ruby>方<rt></rt></ruby>はすべきではない。
Conversational; ～<ruby>比<rt>くら</rt></ruby>べるべくもない is written language.
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>才能<rt>さいのう</rt></ruby>は<ruby>私<rt>わたし</rt></ruby>とは<ruby>比<rt>くら</rt></ruby>べものにならない。

mistakes: Confusing it with ～べきではない (should not). Tip: ～べくもない = impossibility; ～べきではない = morality/advice.
Using it too much in natural spoken language sounds forced. In conversation, replace it with ～ようがない/無理だ.
The JLPT often sets traps with "AはBと比べるべくもない" vs "AはBに比べるべくもない". Using と or は～と… is natural; に is incorrect.
Commands/volition are not used after ～べくもない.
1381.notes:
• "べく" comes from the continuative form of "べし" (possibility/worthiness); in this pattern it becomes a negation of feasibility, "～べくもない".
• Appears often in newspaper commentary, novels and academic texts.
• "想像するべくもない" is used, but "想像に難くない" is a different pattern meaning "it is not hard to imagine". Do not confuse them.

examples.jp: 受験者は身分証を常時携帯するものとする。
examples.tr: Examinees shall carry their identification at all times.

examples.jp: 申請は電子メールで行うものとする。
examples.tr: Applications shall be submitted by email.

examples.jp: 開始時刻を過ぎた入室は認めないものとする。
examples.tr: Entry after the starting time shall not be permitted.

examples.jp: 本規則に違反した者は、処分の対象とするものとする。
examples.tr: Anyone who violates these rules shall be subject to disciplinary action.

examples.jp: 交通費は申請者が負担するものとする。
examples.tr: Transportation costs shall be borne by the applicant.

1382.explain:
Used in regulations, contracts and official notices. Avoid it in everyday conversation.
Often used with regulatory nouns:本規程／本学／当社／当委員会／第○条など.
Combined with ただし、但し書き to state exceptions: ただし、緊急時はこの限りではない。
V-ない + ものとする can be used to prohibit/prevent an action.

• Normative language: "(we/the regulations) stipulate that…", equivalent to "shall" in legal English.
• The subject is usually omitted; those it applies to are "受験者／参加者／申請者／本学／本契約 など".
• Stiff, objective nuance; does not express personal volition at the time of speaking.
• Often appears in clauses of provisions: 条・項・但し書き etc.

rows: Softer; used in internal notices/formal conversation.
<ruby>来月<rt>らいげつ</rt></ruby>から<ruby>値上<rt>ねあ</rt></ruby>げすることとする。
Has several meanings; in legal texts often used as N + とする.
<ruby>提出<rt>ていしゅつ</rt></ruby><ruby>期限<rt>きげん</rt></ruby>は<ruby>金曜<rt>きんよう</rt></ruby>とする。
General in nature, no regulatory force.
<ruby>約束<rt>やくそく</rt></ruby>は<ruby>守<rt>まも</rt></ruby>るものだ。
<ruby>欠席<rt>けっせき</rt></ruby>は<ruby>辞退<rt>じたい</rt></ruby>とみなす。

mistakes: Using it in everyday conversation sounds stiff and funny.
Confusing it with ～とみなす: "regard as" ≠ "shall/is stipulated to".
Wrong agent: normative sentences usually do not state "I/we"; use the organization's name, or it is omitted.
The JLPT often sets traps with polite choices: for a strict regulation → choose ～るものとする, not ～ことにする (a personal decision).
1382.notes:
• The structure "ものとする" makes the text more normative and limits vague interpretation.
• In contracts, it often accompanies definitions: 用語の定義は別紙に定めるものとする。
• In softer announcements, companies often use ～こととする to sound friendlier.

examples.jp: ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。
examples.tr: The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.

examples.jp: 彼はドアを開けるや否や、大声で謝った。
examples.tr: As soon as he opened the door, he apologized loudly.

examples.jp: 駅に着くや否や、彼女は電話をかけた。
examples.tr: The moment she arrived at the station, she made a phone call.

examples.jp: 彼の顔を見るや否や、母は涙ぐんだ。
examples.tr: The moment she saw his face, his mother's eyes filled with tears.

examples.jp: 試合開始のホイッスルが鳴るや否や、両チームは攻め込んだ。
examples.tr: As soon as the whistle blew to start the match, both teams went on the attack.

1383.explain:
The second clause is something that happens instantly (with no delay): ～た／～たのだ/～出した など.
Avoid commands/suggestions/the speaker's volition in the second clause.
Works well in literary descriptions or news to create a sense of urgency.
Often used with verbs of instantaneous action:立つ・出る・開く・鳴る・見る.

• Expresses two events in sequence that are almost simultaneous: "as soon as … then … immediately".
• Narrative, formal nuance; used a lot in written language, books and newspapers, and in describing sudden events.
• The subjects of the two clauses are usually the same person/thing; if they differ, this must be clear and natural in context.
• Not used to express repeated habits; it refers to a one-time, instantaneous event.

rows: More conversational; the second clause is not the subject's volitional act.
<ruby>立<rt>た</rt></ruby>ち<ruby>上<rt>あ</rt></ruby>がったとたん、めまいがした。
Emphasizes overlapping time; used in both written language and conversation.
<ruby>授業<rt>じゅぎょう</rt></ruby>が<ruby>終<rt>お</rt></ruby>わるか<ruby>終<rt>お</rt></ruby>わらないかのうちに<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>て<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>った。
Written language; the subject is usually the same person; the second clause is often an unexpected action.
<ruby>帰<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>るなり<ruby>寝<rt>ね</rt></ruby>てしまった。
Formal/literary; not used with commands/the speaker's volition.
<ruby>着<rt>つ</rt></ruby>くや<ruby>否<rt>いな</rt></ruby>や、<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>した。

mistakes: Using a command/suggestion in the second clause is incorrect: ×着くや否や、連絡してください。
Using it for repeated habits is inappropriate. This pattern describes a one-time event.
Wrong tense: V-る is required before や否や; V-た is not used.
Exam questions often set traps with ～たとたん／～か～ないかのうちに: note the formal nuance and the strong "immediacy" of ～や否や.
1383.notes:
• "否" is read いな; in everyday writing the whole phrase is often written in kana as "やいなや" for readability.
• Compared with ～とすぐ, ～や否や is more formal and dramatic.
• In news/incident reports, it helps create a fast pace and a narrative that emphasizes the point in time.

examples.jp: 注意しても聞かず、期限も守らず、会社に損害まで与える始末だ。
examples.tr: He doesn't listen when warned, doesn't meet deadlines, and has even caused the company losses.

examples.jp: ギャンブルにのめり込み、借金する始末だ。
examples.tr: He got so hooked on gambling that he ended up borrowing money.

examples.jp: 風邪を放っておいたら、入院する始末だ。
examples.tr: I ignored my cold, and I ended up in the hospital.

examples.jp: 約束を何度も破り、友人に見放される始末だ。
examples.tr: He broke his promises again and again, and ended up being abandoned by his friends.

examples.jp: 無駄遣いが続き、貯金がゼロになる始末だ。
examples.tr: The wasteful spending went on until his savings were down to zero.

1384.explain:
Placed at the end of a passage/sentence to sum up a bad outcome.
The first clause lists accumulated actions/problems; they can be linked with ～し、～し、… or ～て、～て、…
Not used when the result is positive. If it is neutral/good, use ～結果／～末に.
In spoken language, まったく／本当に can be added to strengthen the critical nuance.

• Expresses a bad outcome after a series of problems: "to the point that…", "in the end…".
• Carries the speaker's criticism/negative dissatisfaction; not used for good results.
• Often accompanied by words such as ついには・とうとう・あげく・結局 to emphasize "in the end".

rows: Emphasizes a long process before a bad result; more neutral in terms of personal criticism.
Neutral; the result can be good or bad.
<ruby>議論<rt>ぎろん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>末<rt>すえ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>合意<rt>ごうい</rt></ruby>した。
<ruby>検査<rt>けんさ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>、<ruby>異常<rt>いじょう</rt></ruby>なし。
Expressive; does not specifically describe an accumulated chain like ～<ruby>始末<rt>しまつ</rt></ruby>だ.
<ruby>大切<rt>たいせつ</rt></ruby>な<ruby>書類<rt>しょるい</rt></ruby>をなくしてしまった。

mistakes: Using it for a good result is incorrect: ×努力した結果、合格する始末だ → use 合格した.
Exams often set traps with ～あげく／～末に: if a critical nuance condemning someone's attitude is needed → choose ～始末だ.
Form: V-る + 始末だ; V-た is not used directly before 始末だ.
Without a preceding chain of circumstances, the sentence sounds forced. There should be a listing before concluding with ～始末だ.
1384.notes:
• "始末" originally means "settling/outcome"; in this pattern it leans toward "a bad, blameworthy outcome".
• Often appears in commentary criticizing attitudes/awareness: 管理が杜撰で～という始末だ。
• Can take a contracted form before a noun/phrase: ～という始末 (drop だ when the sentence continues).
meaning: In the end, it came to this… (bad outcome: 始末だ)

examples.jp: 彼は物事を大げさに言う嫌いがある。
examples.tr: He has a tendency to exaggerate things.

examples.jp: 日本のメディアは話題を煽り立てる嫌いがある。
examples.tr: The Japanese media tend to stir up sensationalism.

examples.jp: この計画はコストを軽視する嫌いがある。
examples.tr: This plan tends to make light of costs.

examples.jp: 専門家は難解な用語を使い過ぎる嫌いがある。
examples.tr: Experts tend to use too much difficult jargon.

examples.jp: 私は結果より手順にこだわる嫌いがあると自覚している。
examples.tr: I am aware that I tend to be more particular about procedures than results.

1385.explain:
Situations: reports, academic comments, mild criticism.
Nuance: formal and distant; avoid using it directly to the listener's face.
Tense: mainly the general present; the past is less common but can be used to talk about an earlier period.
It is rarely combined directly with the negative; to soften it, use an adverb of degree instead of a negative.

～る嫌いがある expresses "having a tendency/leaning toward (a bad habit)", with a mildly critical, formal nuance that leans toward written language.
• Often used for habits and repeated tendencies, with a moderately negative evaluation.
• The subject can be an individual, a group of people, an organization, a policy, a document, etc.
• Often accompanied by adverbs of degree such as やや・少々・いささか・多少 to soften it.
• Not used for praise/positive things; for neutral cases use 傾向がある.

rows: <ruby>言<rt>いいわけ</rt></ruby>い<ruby>訳<rt></rt></ruby>に<ruby>走<rt>はし</rt></ruby>る<ruby>嫌<rt>きら</rt></ruby>いがある
<ruby>消費<rt>しょうひ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>増<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>える<ruby>傾向<rt>けいこう</rt></ruby>がある
Describes repeated habits; closer to spoken language

mistakes: Confusing it with "Aが嫌いだ (dislike A)": completely different meaning and function.
Using it directly with an i-adjective is incorrect: you do not say 真面目な嫌いがある; change it to a verb or noun + の.
Using it to praise is unnatural: this pattern implies criticism; for praise use 傾向がある or another expression.
Using it in casual conversation sounds stiff; the JLPT favors written contexts/objective judgments.
1385.notes:
• "嫌い" here is a Sino-Japanese noun meaning "tendency/bias", not "dislike".
• When talking about yourself to remain polite and modest, this pattern is suitable in self-evaluations.
• Often combined with evaluative phrases: 形式に流れる嫌いがある／数字に偏る嫌いがある／結論を急ぐ嫌いがある.

examples.jp: この件を任せられるのは、彼をおいて他にない。
examples.tr: The only person who can be entrusted with this matter is him.

examples.jp: 次の主将は、山田をおいて他に考えられない。
examples.tr: I can't think of anyone other than Yamada as the next captain.

examples.jp: 日本文化に精通している指導者は、田中先生をおいてはいない。
examples.tr: There is no instructor other than Professor Tanaka who is so well versed in Japanese culture.

examples.jp: この町で最高の寿司は、ここをおいて他にない。
examples.tr: The best sushi in this town is here and nowhere else.

examples.jp: 最終候補は、この案をおいてほかにない。
examples.tr: The final candidate can be none other than this plan.

1386.explain:
Formal; often used in speeches, nominations, advertising and expert judgments.
Suitable when you want to emphasize uniqueness/being the best; avoid using it carelessly so as not to exaggerate.
他に/ほかに can be added for emphasis; "～ない" is required for the meaning.

• Asserts uniqueness: "apart from N, there is no other option".
• Nuance of high evaluation/praise and absolute trust; used in formal statements and promotion.
• Often used with nouns referring to people, organizations, places, means, or the best/only option.
• The second clause is always negative: ～ない／いない／考えられない／見当たらない.

rows: <ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>をおいて<ruby>他<rt>た</rt></ruby>にない
Neutral, little nuance of high regard
<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby><ruby>以外<rt>いがい</rt></ruby>にいない
<ruby>夏<rt>なつ</rt></ruby>はビールに<ruby>限<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>る

mistakes: Dropping "ない" in the second clause → wrong meaning. A negative is always required.
Using it for ordinary things → does not fit the nuance of "unique/outstanding".
Confusing it with ～しかない: the JLPT tests the difference between "uniqueness as an evaluation" and "no other choice".
1386.notes:
• When praising a person/organization, this pattern creates strong credibility in CVs, PR and speeches.
• Not used for trivial obvious facts; use it when there are clear criteria for comparison.
• Accompanied by negative verbs rich in nuance: 見当たらない／思い当たらない／他に類を見ない.

1387.meaning: Taking… as the point in time

examples.jp: 本日をもって退職いたします。
examples.tr: I will be resigning as of today.

examples.jp: 結果はメールをもってご連絡いたします。
examples.tr: We will inform you of the results by email.

examples.jp: これをもって会議を終了します。
examples.tr: With this, we will close the meeting.

examples.jp: 本書をもって保証書に代えます。
examples.tr: This document shall serve in place of a warranty certificate.

examples.jp: 熱意をもって業務に取り組む。
examples.tr: Approach one's work with enthusiasm.

examples.jp: 彼の努力をもってしても、達成は難しかった。
examples.tr: Even with all his effort, it was hard to achieve.

1387.explain:
Very formal; used a lot in administrative and business documents and speeches.
When used in the meaning "point in time", it often goes with announcements of closing/opening, appointments and endings.
Meaning "by means of": abstract nouns/designating nouns are preferred (書面、文書、メール、愛、誠意、熱意、誠心誠意).

• Means/method: "by/through/thanks to" in official documents, notices and contracts.
• Point in time when something takes effect: "as of/until", to declare a start/end.
• Standard/treatment: determines what is regarded as…
• Be careful to distinguish it from ～をもってしても (a different pattern with a strong concessive meaning).

rows: <ruby>書面<rt>しょめん</rt></ruby>をもって<ruby>通知<rt>つうち</rt></ruby>
メールにより<ruby>連絡<rt>れんらく</rt></ruby>
これをもちまして<ruby>閉会<rt>へいかい</rt></ruby>といたします
<ruby>全力<rt>ぜんりょく</rt></ruby>をもってしても<ruby>無理<rt>むり</rt></ruby>だ

mistakes: Confusing ～をもって with ～によって in spoken sentences → sounds stiff or too bookish.
Using ～をもって when the subject is the speaker in ordinary conversation → unnatural; replace with ～で/～で.
Confusing it with ～をもってしても: the JLPT often sets traps where しても requires a negative sentence.
1387.notes:
• The kanji 以て is also seen in archaic/symbolic writing: ～を以て（＝をもって）.
• "身をもって" is an idiom: 自ら体験して (experiencing it oneself).
• In ceremonies, "これをもちまして" is a very natural way to open/close a speech.

examples.jp: このサービスは高トラフィックを前提にしてインフラを構築している。
examples.tr: This service has built its infrastructure on the premise of high traffic.

examples.jp: 少人数を前提にカリキュラムを組み直した。
examples.tr: We restructured the curriculum on the premise of small class sizes.

examples.jp: 両社の連携を前提にしたスケジュールだ。
examples.tr: This schedule is premised on cooperation between the two companies.

examples.jp: マスク着用を前提にしてイベントを開催します。
examples.tr: The event will be held on the premise that masks are worn.

examples.jp: 将来的な拡張を前提にデータベースを設計した。
examples.tr: The database was designed on the premise of future expansion.

1388.explain:
Combined with nouns related to operating conditions:利用・需要・前提人数・連携・拡張性・予算・安全基準.
Often goes with concrete actions:設計する・見直す・構築する・実施する・運用する.
"Implementation/operation-oriented" nuance; natural in field reports.

• Sets a concrete practical/implementation premise and carries out actions/design/adjustments based on it.
• Practical nuance, closer to the field than ～を前提として (which is normative/documentary).
• Common in IT, operations, service design and implementation planning.

rows: <ruby>少<rt>しょう</rt></ruby><ruby>人数<rt>にんずう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>運営<rt>うんえい</rt></ruby>
<ruby>信頼<rt>しんらい</rt></ruby><ruby>継続<rt>けいぞく</rt></ruby>を<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>として
Not necessarily an "assumption taken as true".
<ruby>規格<rt>きかく</rt></ruby>に<ruby>基<rt>もと</rt></ruby>づいて<ruby>設計<rt>せっけい</rt></ruby>
<ruby>需要<rt>じゅよう</rt></ruby>が<ruby>増<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>えるという<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>で

mistakes: Confusing its nuance with ～を前提として: exam questions ask you to choose the form that fits the context (normative vs operational).
Putting a long clause directly into ～を前提にして makes it heavy; use という前提で.
Vague premise: a concrete noun is needed; avoid an N that is too general to be measured.
1388.notes:
• Use "当面/仮に/想定上" to emphasize that the premise is temporary: 当面Xを前提に運用する。
• In design, there is the pair "前提" vs "制約": 前提 (assumption) and 制約 (constraint) should be kept separate in descriptions.
• When the premise changes, an action should accompany it: 前提変更に伴い、設計を見直す。

examples.jp: 就職を境に、彼は地元を離れた。
examples.tr: When he got a job, he left his hometown.

examples.jp: 事故を境に、会社の安全基準が厳格化された。
examples.tr: Since the accident, the company's safety standards have been tightened.

examples.jp: この道を境に、東側は住宅地、西側は商業地だ。
examples.tr: This road is the boundary: the east side is residential and the west side is commercial.

examples.jp: 1997年を境にして、規制が大きく変わった。
examples.tr: From 1997 on, the regulations changed greatly.

examples.jp: 大震災を境に、防災意識が高まった。
examples.tr: Since the great earthquake, awareness of disaster prevention has increased.

examples.jp: これを境に、チームは連勝を続けた。
examples.tr: From this point on, the team kept winning.

1389.explain:
Nouns used as the dividing point:年/年度/時点/出来事(結婚・出産・事故・震災)/地物(川・道・山脈・県境).
Often goes with verbs of change/shift:変わる・転じる・一変する・分かれる・境する.
Objective, descriptive nuance; suitable for reports, history, geography and statistics.

• "Taking N as the dividing point/boundary": indicates a clear before–after division in time or in space.
• In time: an event/point in time marks a turning point or a change in tendency.
• In space: an object/road/border serves as the boundary dividing areas.
• Emotionally neutral; different from ～を機に (deliberately taking an opportunity) or ～を限りに (ending).

rows: <ruby>事故<rt>じこ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>境<rt>さかい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>変化<rt>へんか</rt></ruby>
Implies deliberately using the occasion to do something.
<ruby>結婚<rt>けっこん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>機<rt>き</rt></ruby>に<ruby>禁煙<rt>きんえん</rt></ruby>
Indicates a time from a past point until now, does not emphasize a "boundary of change".
<ruby>卒業<rt>そつぎょう</rt></ruby><ruby>以来<rt>いらい</rt></ruby><ruby>会<rt>あ</rt></ruby>っていない
Stop at the end of N
<ruby>今季<rt>こんき</rt></ruby>を<ruby>限<rt>かぎ</rt></ruby>りに<ruby>引退<rt>いんたい</rt></ruby>
Used for a series of events that follow.
<ruby>東京<rt>とうきょう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>皮切<rt>かわき</rt></ruby>りに<ruby>全国<rt>ぜんこく</rt></ruby><ruby>巡回<rt>じゅんかい</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Confusing it with ～を機に: exams often set traps with the "intentional" nuance (機). ～を境に is an objective description of a result.
Using it with nouns that are not a concrete dividing point/boundary sounds forced: prefer clear events/points in time.
Placing the subject badly makes the sentence ambiguous: make clear what the "before–after change" applies to.
1389.notes:
• "境" originally means "boundary". The figurative time meaning is very common in statistics/sociology.
• To clearly emphasize "before–after", use a contrasting structure: N を境に、前は～、後は～。
• In geography/administration, it goes with the verbs 分ける/区切る/接する to describe boundaries.

examples.jp: 結婚を機にして、貯金を本格的に始めた。
examples.tr: With my marriage as the occasion, I started saving seriously.

examples.jp: 不具合発生を機に、品質管理体制を強化した。
examples.tr: Taking the defect incident as an opportunity, we strengthened our quality control system.

examples.jp: 異動を機にして、新しい分野に挑戦したい。
examples.tr: I want to use my transfer as a chance to take on a new field.

examples.jp: これを機に、部屋を片付けよう。
examples.tr: Let's take this opportunity to tidy up the room.

examples.jp: 大地震を機に、防災意識が高まった。
examples.tr: The major earthquake raised awareness of disaster prevention.

1390.explain:
Usually placed at the beginning of the sentence to introduce the reason for a change.
Goes well with verbs such as:見直す・切り替える・導入する・開始する・改定する.
Semi-formal style; suits company documents and announcements, but can also be used in everyday life.

• Takes the occasion/turning point N to start something new or to change a policy or lifestyle.
• Expresses an active, deliberate intention; usually has a positive/improving character.
• Can be used with a negative event if what follows is a corrective or reform measure.

rows: Turning point, taking the occasion to change
<ruby>出産<rt>しゅっさん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>機<rt>き</rt></ruby>に<ruby>在宅<rt>ざいたく</rt></ruby><ruby>勤務<rt>きんむ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>切替<rt>きりかえ</rt></ruby>。
Casual; the trigger can be small
<ruby>友人<rt>ゆうじん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>助言<rt>じょげん</rt></ruby>をきっかけに<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>不況<rt>ふきょう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>契機<rt>けいき</rt></ruby>に<ruby>改革<rt>かいかく</rt></ruby>。
Neutral, less emphasis on a turning point
<ruby>来日<rt>らいにち</rt></ruby>の<ruby>機会<rt>きかい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>観光<rt>かんこう</rt></ruby>。

mistakes: Used before a verb clause: incorrect; it needs an event noun.
Expressing a natural, unintended consequence: consider ～ため／～結果 instead.
Confused with ～をきっかけに: exams often test the nuance of formality and scale.
1390.notes:
• Using “これを機に” in a work email tactfully suggests a change without being too pushy.
• Do not overuse it for trivial matters; the nuance of “機” should be reserved for significant changes.

examples.jp: 大阪公演を皮切りに、全国ツアーがスタートする。
examples.tr: Starting with the Osaka performance, the nationwide tour will get underway.

examples.jp: 関西地区を皮切りに、新サービスの提供を始める。
examples.tr: Starting with the Kansai area, we will begin offering the new service.

examples.jp: この受賞を皮切りに、依頼が相次いだ。
examples.tr: Starting with this award, requests poured in one after another.

examples.jp: 春のキャンペーンを皮切りに、年間を通じて各種イベントを展開する。
examples.tr: Kicking off with the spring campaign, various events will be held throughout the year.

examples.jp: 記者発表を皮切りに、SNSでの話題が広がった。
examples.tr: Starting with the press conference, the topic spread across social media.

1391.explain:
Moderately formal; suits planning documents and news.
The input should be an event/place noun that can serve as a “starting point”.
What follows should express continuation/spread; avoid describing a single, isolated action.

• States the opening point of a series of similar events/activities that follow.
• Emphasizes planning/spread across space or time.
• Often used in the context of organizations, products, performing arts and community campaigns.

rows: <ruby>名古屋<rt>なごや</rt></ruby>を<ruby>皮切<rt>かわき</rt></ruby>りに<ruby>展開<rt>てんかい</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>札幌<rt>さっぽろ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>皮切<rt>かわき</rt></ruby>りにして<ruby>開催<rt>かいさい</rt></ruby>。
No emphasis on a time sequence; emphasizes inclusion
<ruby>京都<rt>きょうと</rt></ruby>を<ruby>初<rt>はじ</rt></ruby>めとして<ruby>多<rt>おお</rt></ruby>くの<ruby>名所<rt>めいしょ</rt></ruby>。
More casual; also used for individuals
<ruby>読書<rt>どくしょ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>手始<rt>てはじ</rt></ruby>めに<ruby>学<rt>まな</rt></ruby>び<ruby>直<rt>なお</rt></ruby>す。

mistakes: Attached to a one-off action with no continuation: unnatural.
Confusing “kickoff” with “turning point”: exams like to trick you between 皮切り and 機.
Used before a noun that is not an event/place (e.g. 能力、気持ち): does not fit.
1391.notes:
• Effective in résumés/PR: 「海外展開を皮切りに、売上が拡大」.
• In event news, combine with round/phase markers: 第1弾、第1期.

examples.jp: 札幌を皮切りにして、全国で巡回展が行われる。
examples.tr: Starting in Sapporo, a traveling exhibition will be held across the country.

examples.jp: この講演を皮切りにして、連続セミナーを月一回のペースで実施する。
examples.tr: Starting with this lecture, we will hold a series of seminars once a month.

examples.jp: ドラマの放送を皮切りにして、関連商品のコラボが次々と発表された。
examples.tr: Starting with the broadcast of the drama, tie-ins with related products were announced one after another.

examples.jp: 新店舗の開店を皮切りにして、東北地域への進出を加速させる。
examples.tr: Starting with the opening of a new store, we will accelerate our expansion into the Tohoku region.

examples.jp: 沖縄を皮切りにして、全国一斉清掃キャンペーンがスタートする。
examples.tr: Starting in Okinawa, a simultaneous nationwide cleanup campaign will be launched.

1392.explain:
Formal; preferred in planning documents, proposals and announcements.
Placed at the end of an adverbial clause, linking smoothly to the main predicate.
What follows must express continuation/expansion; avoid ending abruptly.

• Equivalent to ～を皮切りに: “starting with N as the kickoff”, followed by a series of similar activities.
• “して” makes its adverbial role toward the main predicate clear; often used in official documents, plans and announcements.
• Suitable when followed by verbs of step-by-step rollout: 開始する・展開する・導入する・実施する...

rows: <ruby>東京<rt>とうきょう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>皮切<rt>かわき</rt></ruby>りにツアー。
When a formal rhythm and a clear link to the predicate are needed
<ruby>大阪<rt>おおさか</rt></ruby>を<ruby>皮切<rt>かわき</rt></ruby>りにして<ruby>展開<rt>てんかい</rt></ruby>する。
<ruby>整理<rt>せいり</rt></ruby><ruby>整頓<rt>せいとん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>手始<rt>てはじ</rt></ruby>めに<ruby>改善<rt>かいぜん</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>春<rt>はる</rt></ruby>に<ruby>始<rt>はじ</rt></ruby>まり<ruby>秋<rt>あき</rt></ruby>に<ruby>終<rt>お</rt></ruby>わる。

mistakes: Used when no series follows: unnatural.
Confusing the nuance with ～を機に: exams often test “series” vs “turning point”.
Input is not a clear event/place noun: error-prone.
1392.notes:
• The “して” form helps long, multi-clause sentences keep a coherent rhythm in administrative writing.
• Goes well with expressions of frequency/roadmap: 順次・段階的に・第一弾・第1期など.

1393.connection: N + (の) + 前提で / V plain form + 前提で

examples.jp: 来期に人員を増やす前提で予算を組む。
examples.tr: We draw up the budget on the premise that staff will be increased next term.

examples.jp: 大会が予定通り開催されるという前提で準備を進める。
examples.tr: We are proceeding with preparations on the assumption that the tournament will be held as scheduled.

examples.jp: 既存システムを活用する前提で設計した。
examples.tr: It was designed on the premise of using the existing system.

examples.jp: 日本に長期滞在する前提で話を進めましょう。
examples.tr: Let's continue the discussion on the premise that you will stay in Japan long-term.

examples.jp: 全員が合意するという前提で契約を作成した。
examples.tr: The contract was drawn up on the assumption that everyone would agree.

1393.explain:
Used when establishing a prerequisite for a plan/design/process.
Suits business, legal and technical writing; also natural in conversation when discussing plans.
Often used with:進める,設計する,作成する,組む,試算する,想定する,検討する.

• “On the premise/assumption that …”, then the action/design/plan that follows is carried out.
• The premise is treated as a necessary condition; if the premise changes, what follows may no longer be valid.
• Nuance of planning, business, legal matters and research; more formal than つもりで (subjective intention).

rows: Used with a clause; planning nuance
<ruby>参加<rt>さんか</rt></ruby>する<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>で
N を<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>に／として
More natural when N is a noun
<ruby>安全<rt>あんぜん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>前提<rt>ぜんてい</rt></ruby>に
<ruby>引<rt>ひ</rt></ruby>っ<ruby>越<rt>こ</rt></ruby>すつもりで<ruby>片付<rt>かたづ</rt></ruby>ける
A supposition for reasoning, not applied by default
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>だとしたら<ruby>延期<rt>えんき</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Incorrect with a noun: × 安全を前提で → ◯ 安全を前提に/として.
Confused with つもりで (intention) → ～前提で is a “mandatory condition”, not just an intention.
JLPT often tests substitution: ～前提で vs ～としたら vs ～場合は; note the “applied by default” character of ～前提で.
1393.notes:
• “前提” is a foundational condition; in technical documents it often appears as “前提条件”.
• “～前提での + N” is used, but “～を前提とした + N” is more formal/better.
• If the premise is uncertain, consider “想定で/想定のもとで” to loosen the constraint.

examples.jp: 公共の場でのその発言は、失礼極まりない。
examples.tr: That remark in a public place is extremely rude.

examples.jp: 素人が単独で登頂を試みるのは危険極まりない。
examples.tr: For an amateur to attempt to reach the summit alone is extremely dangerous.

examples.jp: この手続きは不便極まりないので、早急に見直すべきだ。
examples.tr: This procedure is extremely inconvenient, so it should be reviewed as soon as possible.

examples.jp: 結果は残念極まりないものだった。
examples.tr: The result was utterly regrettable.

examples.jp: 彼の厚顔無恥ぶりは非常識極まりない。
examples.tr: His shamelessness is utterly lacking in common sense.

examples.jp: この上ない喜びで、嬉しいこと極まりない。
examples.tr: It is a joy beyond compare; I am happy beyond words.

1394.explain:
Emphasizes a strong subjective judgment, often to reproach/criticize.
Stiff, formal style; in conversation it is usually replaced by ほんとうに／とても／めっちゃ…
Can come before a noun to highlight its bad quality:失礼極まりない態度.

- Meaning: “extremely/to the utmost”, emphasizing a strong emotional judgment (usually negative: rude, dangerous, foolish…).
• Formal, written-language nuance; stronger than とても/非常に, close to “excessively/unacceptably”.
• Often used with fixed word sets: 失礼／不便／危険／不快／残念／愚か＋極まりない.
• Can also be used with positive words (嬉しいこと極まりない), but this is rare and literary.

rows: この<ruby>上<rt>うえ</rt></ruby>ない<ruby>幸<rt>しあわ</rt></ruby>せ
Neutral adverb; no strong judgmental nuance
<ruby>極<rt>きわ</rt></ruby>めて<ruby>重要<rt>じゅうよう</rt></ruby>だ
Close in meaning but leans toward describing a state that has reached the extreme; <ruby>極<rt>きわ</rt></ruby>まりない emphasizes judgment
<ruby>失礼<rt>しつれい</rt></ruby><ruby>極<rt>きわ</rt></ruby>まる<ruby>態度<rt>たいど</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Using it with a neutral adjective sounds forced (× 綺麗極まりない). Choose words with a strong/evaluative nuance.
Confused with 極めて（adverb） in vocabulary questions; pay attention to the grammatical function.
Dropping “こと” with an i-adjective: × 嬉しい極まりない → should be: 嬉しいこと極まりない.
Wrong nuance: 極まりない usually carries reproach; using it in the wrong context sounds rude.
1394.notes:
• Reading: 極まりない（きわまりない）.
• Natural collocations: 失礼／危険／不便／不快／無責任／不謹慎／愚か＋極まりない.
• For even greater formality, you can switch to ～の極み／遺憾の意など.

examples.jp: 公共の場でのあの態度は非常識極まる。
examples.tr: That attitude in a public place is utterly lacking in common sense.

examples.jp: そんなことを言うなんて失礼極まる。
examples.tr: Saying something like that is extremely rude.

examples.jp: 資金計画が甘すぎて、危険極まった投資だ。
examples.tr: The financial plan is far too careless; it is an extremely dangerous investment.

examples.jp: 彼の発想は愚劣極まりない。
examples.tr: His ideas are foolish beyond words.

examples.jp: この対応は不快極まるものだ。
examples.tr: This response is extremely unpleasant.

1395.explain:
Do not add an adverb of degree (とても、極めて) before極まる.
Mainly used with na-adjectives and nouns describing qualities; i-adjectives usually switch to another form (極めて + Adj).
A strong judgment that can sound harsh; consider the social context.

- Indicates the utmost degree of a quality (usually negative): “extremely/… to the extreme”.
- Used when the speaker makes a strong judgment; common in written language and commentary.
- Goes well with Sino-Japanese words carrying an evaluative nuance: 失礼, 無礼, 非常識, 危険, 愚劣, 不便, 不快...

rows: <ruby>危険<rt>きけん</rt></ruby><ruby>極<rt>きわ</rt></ruby>まりない
Used with N; also has a positive meaning
<ruby>極<rt>きわ</rt></ruby>めて<ruby>不適切<rt>ふてきせつ</rt></ruby>

mistakes: Used with an i-adjective: (x) 速い極まる → (o) 極めて速い / 迅速の極み.
Adding an adverb of degree before 極まる is redundant: (x) とても失礼極まる.
Wrong nuance: 極まる/極まりない are usually negative; の極み can be positive.
1395.notes:
• Many fixed collocations; using it otherwise sounds forced: 失礼極まる/極まりない, 危険極まりない, 非常識極まる.
• Reading: きわまる. Distinguish it from きわめる (transitive verb).
• In newspaper headlines/court rulings: often used to add weight to a judgment.

examples.jp: 説明が足りないので、誤解が生じた。
examples.tr: The explanation was insufficient, so a misunderstanding arose.

examples.jp: 成功するには、まだ練習が足りない。
examples.tr: To succeed, you still don't practice enough.

examples.jp: その批判は検討に足りない。
examples.tr: That criticism is not worth considering.

examples.jp: 彼は信用するに足りないと判断された。
examples.tr: He was judged not worthy of trust.

examples.jp: そんな噂は取るに足りない。
examples.tr: Rumors like that are not worth worrying about.

1396.explain:
Use が to mark what is lacking; use は for contrast/topic.
～にはNが足りない states the criterion/goal clearly; a standard expression in reports/evaluations.
～に足りない is judgmental; often used with Sino-Japanese nouns.

- Basic meaning: lacking, not enough (time, money, people, ability...).
- The structure “～に足りない”: an evaluation that something is not worth doing (検討・信頼・議論...).
- Nuance: “Nが足りない” is neutral; “Nに足りない” is formal and critical.

rows: <ruby>人手<rt>ひとで</rt></ruby>が<ruby>不足<rt>ふそく</rt></ruby>する

mistakes: Confusing “Nが足りない” (lacking in quantity) with “Nに足りない” (not worth it).
Using verbs arbitrarily with “～に足りない”: prefer standard collocations (検討・信頼・注目...).
Wrong particle: (x) 合格するに点数が足りない → (o) 合格するには点数が足りない.
1396.notes:
• “頭が足りない” disparages someone's intelligence; be careful with the context.
• “足りない” vs “足らない”: a difference in style; the meaning is the same.
• “取るに足りない” is a common set phrase, equivalent to 些細だ/大したことはない.

examples.jp: この調査は議論に足るサンプル数を確保している。
examples.tr: This survey has secured a sample size sufficient for discussion.

examples.jp: 彼は信頼に足るパートナーだ。
examples.tr: He is a partner worthy of trust.

examples.jp: 最新の報告は参考に足る内容だ。
examples.tr: The latest report has content worth referring to.

examples.jp: その現象は注目に足ると言える。
examples.tr: That phenomenon can be said to be worthy of attention.

examples.jp: この状況は懸念するに足る。
examples.tr: This situation gives sufficient cause for concern.

1397.explain:
The most natural combinations:信頼・信用・検討・議論・注目・参考・称賛・懸念/危惧+ に足る.
Usually comes before a noun to make clear the worthiness of that N.
Not used to mean “enough in quantity” (use足りる).

- Confirms that the target has enough value/standing for an evaluative act (trust, consideration, attention...).
- Usually attaches to Sino-Japanese abstract nouns; formal, rational nuance.
- Widely used in research reports, business documents and specialist media.

rows: <ruby>信頼<rt>しんらい</rt></ruby>に<ruby>足<rt>た</rt></ruby>る<ruby>証拠<rt>しょうこ</rt></ruby>
<ruby>称賛<rt>しょうさん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>値<rt>あたい</rt></ruby>する
<ruby>一見<rt>いっけん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>価値<rt>かち</rt></ruby>がある
<ruby>検討<rt>けんとう</rt></ruby>に<ruby>足<rt>た</rt></ruby>りない

mistakes: Used for quantity: (x) お金に足る → (o) お金が足りる.
Wrong collocation: (x) 楽しいに足る → use 価値がある/面白い instead of ～に足る.
Confusing the direction of evaluation: ～に足る (positive) ↔ ～に足りない (negative).
1397.notes:
• V-るに足る is used selectively; prefer verbs that nominalize naturally (信用する・懸念する・危惧する).
• In academic titles, “～に足る証拠/根拠” is a very common phrase.
• The potential form 足りる also appears as a modifier: 信頼に足りるN（equivalent to に足る in many contexts）.
Not to be lumped together with ～たる～ (): a different point.

examples.jp: 一人になって、家族がいかに大切かが分かった。

examples.tr: My grandfather kept working right up until the day he died.

1443.meaning: Even after it has come to… (に至っても)

examples.jp: この期に至っても、彼はまだ嘘をついている。
examples.tr: Even at this stage, he is still lying.

examples.jp: 倒産に至っても、社長は責任を認めなかった。
examples.tr: Even when it came to bankruptcy, the president did not admit responsibility.

examples.jp: 試合当日に至っても、メンバーは決まらなかった。
examples.tr: Even on the day of the match, the lineup had not been decided.

1444.meaning: As for…, when it comes to… (に至っては)

examples.jp: 数学は苦手で、物理に至っては全く分からない。
examples.tr: I'm bad at math, and when it comes to physics, I don't understand it at all.

examples.jp: 兄は無口だが、弟に至っては一言も話さない。
examples.tr: My older brother is quiet, but my younger brother doesn't say a single word.

examples.jp: 祖父に至っては、スマホに触ろうともしない。
examples.tr: As for my grandfather, he won't even try to touch a smartphone.

1445.meaning: In the hands of…, when up against… (にかかっては)

examples.jp: 彼にかかっては、どんな難問も簡単に見える。
examples.tr: In his hands, even the hardest problem looks easy.

examples.jp: 母にかかっては、どんな言い訳も通用しない。
examples.tr: With my mother, no excuse works.

examples.jp: 彼女にかかれば、古い服もおしゃれに変身する。
examples.tr: In her hands, even old clothes are transformed into something stylish.

1446.meaning: Using… as an excuse, on the pretext of… (にかこつけて)

examples.jp: 彼は出張にかこつけて、観光を楽しんでいる。
examples.tr: He is using his business trip as an excuse to enjoy sightseeing.

examples.jp: 病気にかこつけて、会議を欠席した。
examples.tr: I used illness as an excuse to miss the meeting.

examples.jp: 何かにかこつけては、彼女に会いに行った。
examples.tr: Using one excuse or another, I would go to see her.

1447.meaning: Being absorbed in… (and neglecting other things: にかまけて)

examples.jp: 仕事にかまけて、家族との時間を忘れていた。
examples.tr: Wrapped up in work, I had forgotten about time with my family.

examples.jp: 遊びにかまけて、宿題をやっていない。
examples.tr: I've been so busy playing that I haven't done my homework.

examples.jp: 忙しさにかまけて、連絡が遅れてすみません。
examples.tr: I'm sorry for the late reply; I've been caught up in how busy I am.

1448.meaning: Related to…, associated with… (にまつわる)

examples.jp: この寺にまつわる伝説を聞いた。
examples.tr: I heard a legend associated with this temple.

examples.jp: お金にまつわるトラブルが多い。
examples.tr: There are many problems related to money.

examples.jp: その指輪にまつわる悲しい話がある。
examples.tr: There is a sad story connected with that ring.

1449.meaning: In accordance with…, in conformity with… (rules: に則って)

examples.jp: 規則に則って処分を決める。
examples.tr: The penalty will be decided in accordance with the rules.

examples.jp: 伝統に則って儀式が行われた。
examples.tr: The ceremony was held in accordance with tradition.

examples.jp: 法律に則って手続きを進めてください。
examples.tr: Please proceed with the procedures in accordance with the law.

1450.meaning: Cannot bear to…, not have the heart to… (に忍びない)

examples.jp: 思い出の品を捨てるに忍びない。
examples.tr: I can't bring myself to throw away things that hold memories.

examples.jp: 彼の落ち込む姿は見るに忍びない。
examples.tr: I can't bear to see him so depressed.

examples.jp: まだ使えるものを処分するに忍びない。
examples.tr: I don't have the heart to get rid of things that can still be used.

1451.meaning: Worth…, sufficient to… (に足る/に足りる)

examples.jp: 彼は信頼するに足る人物だ。
examples.tr: He is a person worthy of trust.

examples.jp: 満足するに足る結果が得られた。
examples.tr: We obtained results that were satisfactory enough.

examples.jp: それは議論に足る問題ではない。
examples.tr: That is not an issue worth discussing.

1452.meaning: In light of…, based on… (に照らして)

examples.jp: 過去の例に照らして判断する。
examples.tr: We make a judgment in light of past cases.

examples.jp: 法律に照らして、その行為は違法だ。
examples.tr: In light of the law, that act is illegal.

examples.jp: 経験に照らして言えば、この計画は難しい。
examples.tr: Speaking from experience, this plan is difficult.

1453.meaning: …is unreasonable, it is hardly possible to… (には無理がある)

examples.jp: 一日で全部終わらせるには無理がある。
examples.tr: It is unrealistic to finish everything in one day.

examples.jp: その説明には無理がある。
examples.tr: That explanation is far-fetched.

examples.jp: この人数で店を回すには無理がある。
examples.tr: Running the shop with this number of people is too much to ask.

1454.meaning: …there should be a limit to… (にもほどがある)

examples.jp: 冗談にもほどがある。
examples.tr: A joke can only go so far.

examples.jp: 失礼にもほどがある。
examples.tr: That's rude beyond belief.

examples.jp: 人に頼るにもほどがあるよ。
examples.tr: There's a limit to how much you can rely on other people.

1455.meaning: There is no need to…, it is not worth… (には当たらない)

examples.jp: 彼が優勝しても、驚くには当たらない。
examples.tr: Even if he wins the championship, it's nothing to be surprised about.

examples.jp: その程度のミスなら、非難するには当たらない。
examples.tr: A mistake of that degree is not worth criticizing.

examples.jp: 感謝されるには当たりません。当然のことをしただけです。
examples.tr: There's no need to thank me. I only did what was natural.

examples.jp: その料理の辛いのなんのって、涙が出たよ。
examples.tr: That dish was so spicy, it brought tears to my eyes.

examples.jp: 驚いたのなんのって、声も出なかった。
examples.tr: I was so shocked, I couldn't even make a sound.

examples.jp: 眠いのなんのって、目を開けているのがやっとだ。
examples.tr: I'm so sleepy that it's all I can do to keep my eyes open.

1458.meaning: With… approaching, on the eve of… (を控えて)

examples.jp: 試験を控えて、彼は毎晩遅くまで勉強している。
examples.tr: With the exam coming up, he studies late into the night every evening.

examples.jp: 結婚式を来週に控えて、準備に追われている。
examples.tr: With the wedding next week, I'm swamped with preparations.

examples.jp: 出発を明日に控えて、眠れそうにない。
examples.tr: With my departure tomorrow, I don't think I'll be able to sleep.

1459.meaning: Taking advantage of… (をいいことに)

examples.jp: 親がいないのをいいことに、子どもたちは騒ぎ放題だ。
examples.tr: Taking advantage of their parents being away, the children are running wild.

examples.jp: 彼は彼女の優しさをいいことに、彼女を利用している。
examples.tr: He is taking advantage of her kindness and using her.

examples.jp: 相手が黙っているのをいいことに、言いたい放題だった。
examples.tr: Taking advantage of the other person's silence, he said whatever he liked.

1460.meaning: Regardless of…, without regard for… (を顧みず)

examples.jp: 彼は危険を顧みず、川に飛び込んだ。
examples.tr: Disregarding the danger, he jumped into the river.

examples.jp: 家庭を顧みず、仕事ばかりしてきた。
examples.tr: I have done nothing but work, neglecting my family.

examples.jp: 医師たちは身の危険をも顧みず、治療を続けた。
examples.tr: The doctors continued treatment without regard even for their own safety.

1461.meaning: Combining the purpose of… (を兼ねて)

examples.jp: 散歩を兼ねて、買い物に行った。
examples.tr: I went shopping, which also served as a walk.

examples.jp: 新年会を兼ねて、彼の歓迎会を開いた。
examples.tr: We held a welcome party for him that doubled as a New Year party.

examples.jp: 勉強も兼ねて、日本のドラマを見ている。
examples.tr: I watch Japanese dramas, partly as study.

1462.meaning: Taking the opportunity of…, using… as a turning point (を機に)
1462.connection: V (plain form) + の + を機に / N

examples.jp: 結婚を機に、たばこをやめた。
examples.tr: I quit smoking when I got married.

examples.jp: 引っ越しを機に、いらない物を全部処分した。
examples.tr: I took the opportunity of moving house to get rid of everything I didn't need.

examples.jp: 病気になったのを機に、生活を見直した。
examples.tr: Getting sick prompted me to reconsider my lifestyle.

1463.meaning: No one/nothing else but… (をおいて～ない)

examples.jp: この役ができるのは、彼をおいてほかにいない。
examples.tr: There is no one but him who can play this role.

examples.jp: リーダーは彼女をおいて考えられない。
examples.tr: I can't imagine anyone other than her as the leader.

examples.jp: 頼れるのは君をおいてほかにない。
examples.tr: You are the only one I can rely on.

examples.jp: 彼は病気を押して、試合に出場した。
examples.tr: He played in the match despite being ill.

examples.jp: 周囲の反対を押し切って、二人は結婚した。
examples.tr: The two of them got married in the face of opposition from everyone around them.

examples.jp: 家族の反対を押して、留学を決めた。
examples.tr: I decided to study abroad despite my family's objections.

1465.meaning: Since… (a major turning point: を境に)

examples.jp: その事件を境に、二人の関係は変わった。
examples.tr: That incident changed the relationship between the two of them.

examples.jp: 40歳を境に、体力の衰えを感じるようになった。
examples.tr: Since turning 40, I have begun to feel my physical strength declining.

examples.jp: 引っ越しを境にして、彼とは会っていない。
examples.tr: I haven't seen him since I moved.

1466.meaning: To feel…, to experience… (辛い思いをする)

examples.jp: 電車で恥ずかしい思いをした。
examples.tr: I had an embarrassing experience on the train.

examples.jp: 子どものころ、寂しい思いをして育った。
examples.tr: As a child, I grew up feeling lonely.

examples.jp: 二度と怖い思いをしたくない。
examples.tr: I never want to go through anything that frightening again.

1467.connection: およそ + Quantity / およそ + N

examples.jp: 駅までおよそ20分かかる。
examples.tr: It takes about 20 minutes to get to the station.

examples.jp: その話はおよそ現実的ではない。
examples.tr: That story is not realistic at all.

examples.jp: およそ勉強というものは、続けることが大切だ。
examples.tr: When it comes to studying in general, what matters is keeping at it.

1468.meaning: As if…, just as though… (さも)
1468.connection: さも + [sentence/clause] + (そうに/そうな) [sentence/clause] + (ように/ような)

examples.jp: 彼はさも自分の手柄のように話した。
examples.tr: He talked as if it were his own achievement.

examples.jp: 猫はさも気持ちよさそうに眠っている。
examples.tr: The cat is sleeping, looking ever so comfortable.

examples.jp: 彼女はさも驚いたような顔をした。
examples.tr: She made a face as if she were really surprised.

1469.connection: [sentence/clause] 1 + さもないと さもなければ + [sentence/clause] 2

examples.jp: 早く出発しなさい。さもないと遅れるよ。
examples.tr: Leave now. Otherwise you'll be late.

examples.jp: 静かにしなさい。さもないと外に出てもらいます。
examples.tr: Be quiet. Otherwise I'll have to ask you to leave.

examples.jp: 今すぐ謝ったほうがいい。さもなければ、彼は許してくれないだろう。
examples.tr: You'd better apologize right now. Otherwise, he probably won't forgive you.

1470.meaning: To miss the chance to…, to fail to… (V+そびれる)

examples.jp: タイミングを逃して、お礼を言いそびれた。
examples.tr: I missed the right moment and never got to say thank you.

examples.jp: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べそびれた。
examples.tr: I was so busy that I missed lunch.

examples.jp: 聞きそびれたことがあるので、また連絡します。
examples.tr: There's something I didn't get a chance to ask, so I'll contact you again.

1471.meaning: To fail to…, to do… wrong (損なう/損ねる)

examples.jp: 寝坊して、電車に乗り損なった。
examples.tr: I overslept and missed the train.

examples.jp: 言い方を間違えて、彼の機嫌を損ねてしまった。
examples.tr: I phrased it badly and ended up offending him.

examples.jp: 書き損じたはがきは交換できます。
examples.tr: Postcards with writing mistakes can be exchanged.

1472.meaning: There is no way to… (術がない)

examples.jp: 連絡先が分からず、彼に知らせる術がない。
examples.tr: I don't know his contact details, so I have no way to let him know.

examples.jp: 当時はこの病気を治す術がなかった。
examples.tr: At that time, there was no way to cure this disease.

examples.jp: 真実を確かめる術がない。
examples.tr: There is no way to confirm the truth.

1473.meaning: At the very moment… (unintentional: た弾みに/た拍子に)

examples.jp: 転んだ弾みに、めがねが飛んでしまった。
examples.tr: When I fell, my glasses went flying.

examples.jp: 立ち上がった拍子に、頭をぶつけた。
examples.tr: As I stood up, I hit my head.

examples.jp: ドアを閉めた弾みに、指をはさんでしまった。
examples.tr: As I shut the door, I caught my finger in it.

1474.meaning: To treat as having…, to consider as… (たことにする)

examples.jp: 今の話は聞かなかったことにしよう。
examples.tr: Let's pretend we didn't hear what was just said.

examples.jp: その約束はなかったことにしてください。
examples.tr: Please consider that promise as never having been made.

examples.jp: 書類上は、会議は行われたことになっている。
examples.tr: On paper, the meeting is recorded as having taken place.

1475.meaning: Had no intention of… (たつもりはない)

examples.jp: あなたを傷つけたつもりはない。
examples.tr: I didn't mean to hurt you.

examples.jp: うそをついたつもりはありません。
examples.tr: I had no intention of lying.

examples.jp: 命令したつもりはなかったのに、そう聞こえたらしい。
examples.tr: I didn't mean it as an order, but apparently that's how it sounded.

1476.meaning: All one can do is…, there is nothing to do but… (ただ～のみだ)

examples.jp: 準備は終わった。あとはただ結果を待つのみだ。
examples.tr: The preparations are done. All that's left is to wait for the results.

examples.jp: 言い訳はしない。ただ謝るのみだ。
examples.tr: I won't make excuses. All I can do is apologize.

examples.jp: ここまで来たら、ただ前進あるのみだ。
examples.tr: Having come this far, there is nothing to do but press forward.

1477.meaning: It has never once happened that…, never… (ためしがない)

examples.jp: 彼が時間どおりに来たためしがない。
examples.tr: He has never once arrived on time.

examples.jp: この計画がうまくいったためしがない。
examples.tr: This plan has never gone well.

examples.jp: 弟は約束を守ったためしがない。
examples.tr: My younger brother has never kept a promise.

1478.meaning: If…, would have… (counterfactual supposition: たら～ところだ)
1478.connection: たら ば なら + [sentence/clause] + V plain form + ところだ

examples.jp: あと5分遅かったら、電車に乗り遅れたところだ。
examples.tr: If I had been five minutes later, I would have missed the train.

examples.jp: 君が教えてくれなかったら、大失敗するところだった。
examples.tr: If you hadn't told me, I would have made a huge mistake.

examples.jp: 保険に入っていなければ、大変なことになっていたところだ。
examples.tr: If I hadn't had insurance, I would have been in serious trouble.

1479.meaning: As a…, one must… (one's position: たる者)

examples.jp: 教師たるもの、学生の手本となるべきだ。
examples.tr: A teacher should set an example for students.

examples.jp: リーダーたるもの、簡単に諦めてはいけない。
examples.tr: A leader must not give up easily.

examples.jp: 政治家たる者、国民の声を聞くべきだ。
examples.tr: A politician should listen to the voice of the people.

1480.meaning: …is only natural, ought to… (てしかるべきだ)

examples.jp: 彼の功績はもっと評価されてしかるべきだ。
examples.tr: His achievements ought to be valued more highly.

examples.jp: この問題は国会で議論されてしかるべきだ。
examples.tr: This issue ought to be debated in the Diet.

examples.jp: 謝罪があってしかるべきではないか。
examples.tr: Shouldn't there be an apology?

1481.meaning: It is not something that can be settled just by… (て済むことではない)

examples.jp: これは謝って済むことではない。
examples.tr: This isn't something that can be settled with an apology.

examples.jp: お金で済むことではない。
examples.tr: This isn't something money can solve.

examples.jp: 「知らなかった」で済むことではありません。
examples.tr: Saying "I didn't know" doesn't make it all right.

1482.meaning: Even if you…, it won't help (てもどうにもならない)

examples.jp: 今さら後悔してもどうにもならない。
examples.tr: There's no use regretting it now.

examples.jp: 一人で悩んでいてもどうにもならないよ。
examples.tr: Worrying about it on your own won't get you anywhere.

examples.jp: 泣いてもどうなるものでもない。
examples.tr: Crying won't solve anything.

1483.meaning: If you…, don't blame me (warning: ても知らない)

examples.jp: そんなに食べると、おなかを壊しても知らないよ。
examples.tr: If you eat that much and get a stomachache, don't blame me.

examples.jp: 遅くまで遊んでいて、明日起きられなくても知らないから。
examples.tr: If you stay out late and can't get up tomorrow, it's your own fault.

examples.jp: 忠告を聞かないなら、失敗しても知らないよ。
examples.tr: If you won't listen to advice, don't come to me when you fail.

1484.meaning: As if to say… (とばかりに)

examples.jp: 彼は「帰れ」とばかりに、ドアを指さした。
examples.tr: He pointed at the door as if to say, "Get out."

examples.jp: 今がチャンスとばかりに、彼女は発言した。
examples.tr: She spoke up as if to say, "Now's my chance."

examples.jp: 犬は遊んでほしいとばかりに、しっぽを振っている。
examples.tr: The dog is wagging its tail as if to say it wants to play.

1485.meaning: It could be said that… (と言えなくもない)
1485.connection: V plain form + と言えなくもない / N + (だ/である) / Na + (だ/である) / Aい

examples.jp: 彼の意見にも一理あると言えなくもない。
examples.tr: You could say his opinion has a point too.

examples.jp: この値段なら安いと言えなくもない。
examples.tr: At this price, you could say it's cheap.

examples.jp: 責任は私にあると言えなくもない。
examples.tr: It could be said that the responsibility lies with me.

1486.meaning: As soon as one sees that…, immediately… (と見るや)
1486.connection: V plain form + とみるや

examples.jp: 客が来ないと見るや、店はすぐ値下げを始めた。
examples.tr: As soon as it saw that no customers were coming, the store immediately started cutting prices.

examples.jp: 形勢が不利と見るや、彼は作戦を変えた。
examples.tr: As soon as he saw the situation was unfavorable, he changed his strategy.

examples.jp: チャンスと見るや、彼女は一気に攻めた。
examples.tr: The moment she saw her chance, she went all out on the attack.

1487.meaning: All too easily…, tend to… (ともすれば)

examples.jp: 一人暮らしは、ともすれば生活が不規則になりがちだ。
examples.tr: When you live alone, your daily routine all too easily becomes irregular.

examples.jp: 忙しいと、ともすれば健康をおろそかにしがちだ。
examples.tr: When people are busy, they tend to neglect their health.

examples.jp: ともすれば忘れがちだが、感謝の気持ちは大切だ。
examples.tr: It is easy to forget, but gratitude is important.

1488.meaning: For someone like… to do such a thing (としたことが)

examples.jp: 私としたことが、大事な書類を忘れてしまった。
examples.tr: How could I, of all people, forget such important documents?

examples.jp: 慎重な彼としたことが、こんなミスをするとは。
examples.tr: To think that someone as careful as he is would make a mistake like this.

examples.jp: プロとしたことが、基本を間違えるなんて。
examples.tr: For a professional to get the basics wrong!

1489.meaning: Instantly, on the spur of the moment (とっさに)

examples.jp: 車が来たので、とっさに飛びのいた。
examples.tr: A car was coming, so I instantly jumped out of the way.

examples.jp: 名前を聞かれて、とっさに答えられなかった。
examples.tr: When asked my name, I couldn't answer on the spot.

examples.jp: とっさの判断が命を救った。
examples.tr: A split-second decision saved a life.

examples.jp: 親とて、子どものすべてを知っているわけではない。
examples.tr: Even parents don't know everything about their children.

examples.jp: 専門家とて、間違えることはある。
examples.tr: Even experts make mistakes sometimes.

examples.jp: 社長とて、規則には従わなければならない。
examples.tr: Even the company president has to follow the rules.

1491.meaning: Completely different from…, a complete change from… (とは打って変わって)

examples.jp: 昨日の雨とは打って変わって、今日は快晴だ。
examples.tr: Unlike yesterday's rain, today is perfectly clear.

examples.jp: いつもの態度とは打って変わって、彼は真剣だった。
examples.tr: In stark contrast to his usual attitude, he was serious.

examples.jp: 先月とはうってかわり、売り上げが伸びている。
examples.tr: In complete contrast to last month, sales are rising.

examples.jp: 彼はその町を知り尽くしている。
examples.tr: He knows that town inside out.

examples.jp: 火事で家財を焼き尽くしてしまった。
examples.tr: The fire burned all the household belongings to the ground.

examples.jp: 言葉では言い尽くせないほど感謝している。
examples.tr: I am more grateful than words can express.

1493.meaning: I told you… (reproach: ってば/ったら)
1493.connection: [sentence/clause] + ってば ったら / N + (だ) Na + (だ)

examples.jp: もう分かったってば。何度も言わないで。
examples.tr: I said I get it already. Stop saying it over and over.

examples.jp: お母さんったら、また私の話を聞いていない。
examples.tr: Oh, Mom, you're not listening to me again.

examples.jp: 行くってば。ちょっと待ってよ。
examples.tr: I said I'm going. Just wait a second.

1494.meaning: Doesn't count as…, hardly deserves to be called… (うちに入らない)
1494.connection: V plain form + うちに(は)入らない / N + の / Na / Aい

examples.jp: この程度の雨は、雨のうちに入らない。
examples.tr: Rain like this hardly counts as rain.

examples.jp: 3か月の勉強では、勉強したうちに入らない。
examples.tr: Three months of studying doesn't count as having studied.

examples.jp: あれくらいの辛さは、辛いうちに入らないよ。
examples.tr: That level of spiciness doesn't even count as spicy.

1495.meaning: Neglecting…, putting… aside (をそっちのけで)

examples.jp: 息子は宿題をそっちのけで、ゲームをしている。
examples.tr: My son is ignoring his homework and playing video games.

examples.jp: 彼は仕事はそっちのけで、趣味に夢中だ。
examples.tr: He neglects his work and is absorbed in his hobbies.

examples.jp: 会議の議題をそっちのけで、雑談が続いた。
examples.tr: The meeting agenda was pushed aside, and the small talk went on and on.

1496.meaning: What with… and… (negative listing: わ～わで)
1496.connection: V plain form + わ + V plain form + わ(で) / Aいわ + Aいわ(で) / Naだわ + Naだわ(で)

examples.jp: 財布はなくすわ、雨には降られるわで、最悪の一日だった。
examples.tr: What with losing my wallet and getting caught in the rain, it was the worst day ever.

examples.jp: 電車は遅れるわ、会議には遅刻するわで、散々だった。
examples.tr: What with the train being delayed and being late for the meeting, it was a disaster.

examples.jp: 子どもは泣くわ、電話は鳴るわで、大変だった。
examples.tr: What with the kids crying and the phone ringing, it was chaos.

examples.jp: ドアを開けるや否や、猫が飛び出してきた。
examples.tr: The moment I opened the door, the cat came darting out.

examples.jp: 彼はベッドに入るや否や、眠ってしまった。
examples.tr: He fell asleep the moment he got into bed.

examples.jp: その商品は発売されるや否や、売り切れた。
examples.tr: That product sold out as soon as it was released.

1498.connection: やれ + N + だ(の) + やれ + N + だ(の) + と / [sentence/clause] + [sentence/clause]

examples.jp: やれ残業だ、やれ休日出勤だと、最近は休む暇もない。
examples.tr: What with overtime and working on my days off, I haven't had a moment to rest lately.

examples.jp: 母はやれ勉強しろ、やれ部屋を片付けろとうるさい。
examples.tr: My mother keeps nagging me: study, clean up your room.

examples.jp: やれ頭が痛いだの、やれ疲れただのと、彼は文句ばかりだ。
examples.tr: He does nothing but complain: he has a headache, he's tired.

1499.meaning: No matter how… (ようが/ようと)
1499.connection: V (V volitional form) + が と(も) / N + だろう/であろう / Na + だろう/であろう / Aい + かろう

examples.jp: 人に何を言われようが、気にしない。
examples.tr: No matter what people say, I don't care.

examples.jp: どんなに高かろうが、必要なものは買う。
examples.tr: No matter how expensive it is, I'll buy what I need.

examples.jp: 雨だろうと、試合は行われる。
examples.tr: Even if it rains, the match will be held.

1500.connection: V (V volitional form) + が と(も) / N + だろう/であろう / Na + だろう/であろう / Aい + かろう

examples.jp: 泣こうがわめこうが、決定は変わらない。
examples.tr: Whether you cry or scream, the decision won't change.

examples.jp: 雨が降ろうが風が吹こうが、毎日走っている。
examples.tr: Rain or wind, I run every day.

examples.jp: 反対されようが笑われようが、私はやる。
examples.tr: Whether people oppose me or laugh at me, I'm going to do it.

1501.meaning: Depending on how one… (ようによっては)

examples.jp: 考えようによっては、失敗もいい経験だ。
examples.tr: Depending on how you look at it, failure is also a good experience.

examples.jp: この絵は見ようによっては、人の顔にも見える。
examples.tr: Depending on how you look at it, this picture also looks like a human face.

examples.jp: 使いようによっては、この道具はとても便利だ。
examples.tr: Depending on how you use it, this tool can be very handy.

1502.meaning: Whether or not… (ようと～まいと)
1502.connection: V (V volitional form) + と + V + まいと が + V + まいが / How to use まい るV -> Vるまい / V ます まい うV -> Vるまい くる -> こまい / くるまい する -> しまい / すまい / するまい

examples.jp: 雨が降ろうと降るまいと、予定どおり出発する。
examples.tr: Whether it rains or not, we'll leave as planned.

examples.jp: 彼が来ようと来まいと、会議は始める。
examples.tr: Whether he comes or not, we'll start the meeting.

examples.jp: 人が信じようが信じまいが、これは事実だ。
examples.tr: Whether people believe it or not, this is a fact.

1503.meaning: …, you know; …, OK (male speech sentence-final particle, emphasis: ぞ/ぜ)

examples.jp: さあ、行くぞ。
examples.tr: All right, let's go!

examples.jp: 遅れると置いていくぜ。
examples.tr: If you're late, I'm leaving without you.

examples.jp: これは大事な試合だぞ。
examples.tr: This is an important match, you know.

1504.meaning: To the end, persistently, absolutely (あくまでも)

examples.jp: これはあくまでも私個人の意見です。
examples.tr: This is purely my own personal opinion.

examples.jp: 彼はあくまでも無実を主張した。
examples.tr: He persistently maintained his innocence.

examples.jp: あくまでも計画どおりに進めます。
examples.tr: We will proceed exactly according to plan, no matter what.

1505.meaning: Truly…, really looks very… (いかにも)

examples.jp: 彼はいかにも学者らしい話し方をする。
examples.tr: He talks just like a scholar.

examples.jp: いかにも高そうな時計をしている。
examples.tr: They're wearing a watch that looks really expensive.

examples.jp: いかにも残念そうな顔をしていた。
examples.tr: They looked truly disappointed.

examples.jp: もはや手遅れだ。
examples.tr: It's already too late.

examples.jp: その技術はもはや古い。
examples.tr: That technology is already outdated.

examples.jp: もはや彼を止められる者はいない。
examples.tr: There is no longer anyone who can stop him.

1507.meaning: How…!, What a…! (exclamation: なんという/なんて)

examples.jp: なんという美しい景色だろう。
examples.tr: What a beautiful view!

examples.jp: なんて優しい人なんだろう。
examples.tr: What a kind person!

examples.jp: なんということをしてくれたんだ。
examples.tr: What on earth have you done!

examples.jp: 一人での子育ては、さぞ大変だったでしょう。
examples.tr: Raising a child on your own must have been very hard.

examples.jp: 合格の知らせに、ご両親はさぞかし喜んだことでしょう。
examples.tr: Your parents must have been overjoyed at the news that you passed.

examples.jp: 山の上はさぞ寒いだろう。
examples.tr: It must be very cold at the top of the mountain.

examples.jp: 今年の夏はとりわけ暑い。
examples.tr: This summer is especially hot.

examples.jp: 彼は語学、とりわけ発音が得意だ。
examples.tr: He is good at languages, especially pronunciation.

examples.jp: とりわけ印象に残ったのは、最後の場面だ。
examples.tr: What made the strongest impression on me was the last scene.

1510.meaning: If luck is on your side…, with any luck… (hoping for a chance)

examples.jp: あわよくば優勝したいと思っている。
examples.tr: With any luck, I'd like to win the championship.

examples.jp: あわよくば彼女に会えるかもしれないと、パーティーに出た。
examples.tr: I went to the party thinking that, with any luck, I might get to see her.

examples.jp: あわよくばただで手に入れようとするなんて、ずうずうしい。
examples.tr: Trying to get it for free if you can get away with it — how shameless.

examples.jp: 理由のいかんにかかわらず、暴力は許されない。
examples.tr: Violence cannot be tolerated, whatever the reason.

examples.jp: 結果のいかんによらず、全力を尽くしたことに意味がある。
examples.tr: Regardless of the result, there is meaning in having given it your all.

examples.jp: 経験のいかんにかかわらず、応募できます。
examples.tr: Anyone can apply, regardless of experience.

1512.meaning: Probably…, surely… (archaic form of だろう: 良かろう)
1512.connection: Aい (drop い) + かろう (良かろう)

examples.jp: それで良かろう。
examples.tr: That should be fine.

examples.jp: 一人で行くのは危なかろう。
examples.tr: Going alone would probably be dangerous.

examples.jp: 冬の海はさぞ寒かろう。
examples.tr: The sea in winter must be very cold.

1513.meaning: Go ahead and… (command to an inferior; dramatic/novel style)

examples.jp: 悔しかったら、かかってくるがいい。
examples.tr: If you're so frustrated, go ahead and come at me.

examples.jp: 行きたければ、行くがいい。
examples.tr: If you want to go, then go.

examples.jp: 笑いたい者は笑うがいい。
examples.tr: Let those who want to laugh, laugh.

1514.meaning: Leaving things as they are… (着たなりで寝る)

examples.jp: 彼はコートを着たなりで寝てしまった。
examples.tr: He fell asleep with his coat still on.

examples.jp: 靴をはいたなりで部屋に入らないで。
examples.tr: Don't come into the room with your shoes still on.

examples.jp: 電気をつけたなりで出かけてしまった。
examples.tr: I went out and left the light on.

examples.jp: 富士山から見た朝日の美しさといったら、言葉にできないほどだった。
examples.tr: The beauty of the sunrise seen from Mt. Fuji was beyond words.

examples.jp: その時の恥ずかしさといったらなかった。
examples.tr: The embarrassment I felt then was indescribable.

examples.jp: 彼の部屋の汚さといったら、足の踏み場もないほどだ。
examples.tr: His room is so messy that there's nowhere to set foot.

1516.meaning: Should I call it… or… (hesitating over how to put it)
1516.connection: [expression A] + といおうか、[expression B] + といおうか

examples.jp: 彼は正直といおうか、単純といおうか、思ったことをすぐ口にする。
examples.tr: He's honest, or maybe simple — he says whatever he thinks right away.

examples.jp: 大胆といおうか、無謀といおうか、彼の計画には驚いた。
examples.tr: Bold or reckless, I'm not sure which, but his plan surprised me.

examples.jp: うれしいといおうか、恥ずかしいといおうか、複雑な気持ちだ。
examples.tr: I'm happy, or maybe embarrassed — I have mixed feelings.

1517.meaning: If…, then (it has its own difficulties/way)
1517.connection: NならNで / VたらVたで（repeating the same word）

examples.jp: 狭いなら狭いで、工夫すれば住みやすくなる。
examples.tr: If it's small, well, it's small — but with a little ingenuity it becomes easy to live in.

examples.jp: お金がないならないで、何とかなるものだ。
examples.tr: If you don't have money, you don't have money — somehow things work out.

examples.jp: 暇になったらなったで、何をしていいか分からない。
examples.tr: Now that I have free time, I don't know what to do with it.

examples.jp: 優勝者の名に恥じない見事な演技だった。
examples.tr: It was a splendid performance, worthy of a champion.

examples.jp: 母校の名に恥じないよう、努力します。
examples.tr: I will work hard so as to live up to the name of my alma mater.

examples.jp: 自分の良心に恥じない生き方をしたい。
examples.tr: I want to live a life I would not be ashamed of before my own conscience.

examples.jp: あいつ、俺の金を盗みやがった。
examples.tr: That bastard stole my money.

examples.jp: こんな時間に電話してきやがって。
examples.tr: Calling me at this hour, damn it.

examples.jp: 雨、また降ってきやがった。
examples.tr: Damn rain, it's started again.

1520.meaning: To force (someone) to…, leaving no choice

examples.jp: 台風は住民に避難を余儀なくさせた。
examples.tr: The typhoon forced residents to evacuate.

examples.jp: 資金不足が計画の変更を余儀なくさせた。
examples.tr: A lack of funds forced a change in the plan.

examples.jp: 不況が多くの店に閉店を余儀なくさせている。
examples.tr: The recession is forcing many shops to close.

1521.meaning: Having a hidden story, having one's own reasons (訳あり商品)
1521.connection: 訳あり + の + N / 訳あって + [sentence/clause]

examples.jp: この店では訳あり商品を安く売っている。
examples.tr: This store sells "special-reason" goods (slightly flawed, leftover stock, etc.) cheaply.

examples.jp: 二人は訳ありの関係らしい。
examples.tr: Those two seem to have some kind of complicated relationship.

examples.jp: 訳あって、今は実家に住んでいます。
examples.tr: For personal reasons, I'm living at my parents' home now.

1522.meaning: Whether … or not … (expresses that two contrasting possibilities do not change the result)

1523.meaning: Extremely, intensely, to the max, completely (colloquial emphatic prefix 「ガン」; e.g. ガン見 = to stare hard)

1524.meaning: To do (something) for a person/animal of lower status than oneself; also used to show irritation, deliberately doing something the other person dislikes

examples.jp: 子供に新しい自転車を買ってやったら、翌日盗まれてしまった。
examples.tr: I bought my child a new bicycle, and it was stolen the very next day.

examples.jp: 東京の弟に、今年もふるさとの名物を送ってやった。
examples.tr: This year again, I sent my younger brother in Tokyo some specialties from our hometown.

examples.jp: 犬を広い公園で放してやったら、うれしそうに走り回っていた。
examples.tr: When I let the dog off the leash in the big park, it ran around looking happy.

examples.jp: こんな給料の安い会社、いつでも辞めてやる。
examples.tr: A company with pay this low — I'll quit any time I feel like it.

examples.jp:
Ａ: 荷物、重かったら持ってやるよ。
Ｂ: あ、いい、大丈夫。
examples.tr:
A: If your bag is heavy, I'll carry it for you.
B: Oh, no, it's fine.

examples.jp:
Ａ: あんたなんか死ねばいいのよ。
Ｂ: そんなに言うんなら、ほんとに死んでやる。
examples.tr:
A: Someone like you should just drop dead.
B: If you're going to say that, I really will die, just to show you.

1524.explain: Expresses that the speaker (or someone on the speaker's side) does something for the sake of a person of lower status than the speaker, or for an animal. As in 5. and 6., it is sometimes also used as an expression of anger, meaning to do something the other person dislikes. For someone on an equal footing with the speaker, 「Ｖ－てあげる」 is used. (２８６)

1525.meaning: …that, saying that… (modifies a noun of speech/thought; formal written language)

examples.jp: 恩師から結婚式には出席できないとの返事を受け取った。
examples.tr: I received a reply from my former teacher saying that he could not attend the wedding.

examples.jp: 学生から、留学するため、一年休学させてほしいとの希望が出されている。
examples.tr: A student has expressed the wish to take a year's leave of absence in order to study abroad.

examples.jp: この件については、次回の審議に回してはどうかとの議長の提案に全員賛成した。
examples.tr: On this matter, everyone agreed with the chair's proposal that it be referred to the next deliberation.

examples.jp: 来月から一年間、札幌の支社に出向せよとの辞令を受けた。
examples.tr: I received an official order to transfer to the Sapporo branch for one year starting next month.

examples.jp: 文部大臣は、学校教育を改善するためには、高等教育機関の入学試験制度の抜本的改革が必要だとの見解を述べた。
examples.tr: The Minister of Education stated the view that, in order to improve school education, a radical reform of the entrance examination system of higher education institutions is necessary.

1525.explain:
A clause expressing the content of speech or thought modifies a noun; used in a formal style. For Ｎ, nouns related to speech acts such as 「手紙、返事、依頼、提案、警告、命令」, or to thinking such as 「意見、見解、考え、希望」, are used. It is used when talking about other people's statements or thoughts; when expressing the speaker's own thoughts, 「という」 rather than 「との」 is normally used, as in the following example.
*（例） 私は夫婦別姓を合法化すべきだという意見をもっている。

examples.jp: パソコンとは、個人で使える小型のコンピュータのことだ。
examples.tr: A pasokon is a small computer that an individual can use.

examples.jp: 蓮華とは蓮の花のことだ。
examples.tr: Renge means the lotus flower.

examples.jp: ２１世紀の日本で求められる福祉の形態とはどのようなものだろうか。
examples.tr: What kind of welfare system will be required in 21st-century Japan?

examples.jp: 「普遍的」とは、どんな場合にも広く一般的に当てはまるという意味だ。
examples.tr: "Universal" means applying broadly and generally in every case.

examples.jp: 私にとって家族とは一体何なのだろうか。
examples.tr: What on earth is family to me?

1526.explain: Takes a noun and is used to state what its meaning, nature or content is like. It is used to state an essential characteristic in forms such as 「とは…ものだ」, or to define the meaning or content of a word or phrase in forms such as …とは…のことだ／意味だ」「…とは…ということだ／意味だ」. It is a written-language expression; in spoken language 「Ｎというのは」 is more common.

1527.meaning: It's not that … not (…); somewhat feeling that way

examples.jp: 自分にも悪い点があったことは認めないでもない。
examples.tr: I do, to some extent, admit that I was partly at fault too.

examples.jp: 考えてみれば、彼の意見ももっともだという気がしないでもない。
examples.tr: Come to think of it, I kind of feel that his opinion makes sense too.

examples.jp:
Ａ: 納豆はお好きですか。
Ｂ: 食べないでもないですが、あまり好きじゃありません。
examples.tr:
A: Do you like natto?
B: It's not that I don't eat it, but I don't like it very much.

examples.jp:
Ａ: ねえ、行きましょうよ。
Ｂ: そんなに言うなら行かないでもないけど。
examples.tr:
A: Come on, let's go.
B: Well, if you insist, I might go.

1527.explain: Attaches to the negative form of a verb and expresses that such an action or perception can sometimes hold true. When verbs related to thought or perception such as 「言う、考える、思う、認める、感じる、気がする」 are used, it means "somehow I get that feeling."

1528.meaning: If it were …, it would be acceptable, but …
1528.connection: N + ならまだしも / plain form + ならまだしも

1529.meaning: Expresses something that does not match expectations

examples.jp: 彼は苦境にあっても、まげずに頑張っている。
examples.tr: Even in difficult circumstances, he keeps working hard without giving in.

examples.jp: 暖かい家庭の中にあっても、彼女の心は満たされなかった。
examples.tr: Even in a warm family, her heart was not fulfilled.

examples.jp: 母は死の間際にあっても、子供達の幸福を願い続けた。
examples.tr: Even on her deathbed, my mother kept wishing for her children's happiness.

1529.explain: Takes a noun and means "even though placed in the situation expressed there." It is followed by something that differs from what would be expected to happen in that situation. Written language.

1530.meaning: For (that person), from (that person's) point of view

examples.jp: 今何の歌がはやっているかなんて、私にしてみればどうでもいいことだ。それよりもっと大切なことが山ほどある。
examples.tr: Which songs are popular right now doesn't matter at all to me. There are tons of more important things than that.

examples.jp: 長い間使っていなかった古いコンピュータをあげたのだが、彼女にしてみればとてもありがたかったらしく、何度も何度もお礼を言われた。
examples.tr: I gave her an old computer I hadn't used for a long time, and it seems she was very grateful for it — she thanked me again and again.

examples.jp: 私は軽い気持ちで話していたのだが、あの人にしてみれば大きな問題だったのだろう。彼は落ち込んで誰とも口をきかなくなってしまった。
examples.tr: I was talking casually, but for him it was probably a big problem. He became depressed and stopped talking to anyone.

examples.jp: 母にしてみれば、大切に育ててきた息子が突然家を出ていったのだから、たいそうショックだろうが、私は親離れしようとしている弟に声援を送りたい気持ちだった。
examples.tr: For my mother, it must have been a great shock since the son she had raised so lovingly suddenly left home, but I felt like cheering on my younger brother, who was trying to become independent from our parents.

1530.explain: Attaches to a noun referring to a person and means "for that person." Used when you want to say that the person has a different view compared to others. 「…にしてみたら」 can also be used. (４３９)

1531.meaning: Being convinced/assuming that … (but in reality it is not so)

examples.jp: スキーはむずかしいものと思っていたが、やってみたら、簡単だった。
examples.tr: I had assumed skiing was difficult, but when I tried it, it was easy.

examples.jp: 間違いはもう全部直したものと思っていたら、まだ少しあると言われた。
examples.tr: I was sure I had corrected all the mistakes, but I was told there were still a few.

examples.jp: あしたはストで休みになるものと思っていたから、授業の準備は全然しなかった。
examples.tr: I assumed there'd be no class tomorrow because of the strike, so I didn't prepare for class at all.

examples.jp: 古典なんて退屈なものと思っていたが、読んでみたら、意外におもしろかった。
examples.tr: I had assumed the classics were boring, but when I read them, they were surprisingly interesting.

examples.jp: 吉田さんは来ないものと思って、５人分の食事しか作らなかった。
examples.tr: Assuming that Mr. Yoshida wasn't coming, I made food for only 5 people.

1531.explain: Expresses the speaker's assumption. Normally used when the speaker had believed something to be true, but in reality it was not.

1532.meaning: What with … and … (emphatic listing, with a nuance of complaint)

1533.meaning: Cannot keep (…) any longer (urgent situation); cannot just sit idly and …

examples.jp: 時間がないから、遅れて来る人を待ってはいられない。すぐ始めよう。
examples.tr: We don't have time, so we can't wait for the people who are coming late. Let's start right away.

examples.jp: あしたは試験だから、こんなところでのんびり遊んではいられない。
examples.tr: The exam is tomorrow, so I can't be lazing around here having fun.

examples.jp: 今晩はお客が何人か来るし、テニスなんかしてはいられない。早く買い物に行かなければならない。
examples.tr: Some guests are coming tonight, so I can't be playing tennis or anything. I have to go shopping soon.

examples.jp: 今うちの商品はよく売れているが、うかうかしてはいられない。新しい製品がどんどん出てくるからだ。
examples.tr: Our products are selling well now, but we can't afford to be complacent, because new products keep coming out one after another.

examples.jp: この事態を傍観してはいられない。
examples.tr: We cannot just stand by and watch this situation.

examples.jp: スキーのシーズンが始まると、わたしはじっとしてはいられない。
examples.tr: When the ski season starts, I just can't sit still.

1533.explain: Expresses that, because the situation is urgent, one must not continue doing such a thing, or that one wants to take action quickly. Often used with adverbs such as 「のんびり」, 「うかうか」 and 「じっと」. (２６３)

1534.meaning: Cannot help but (…); cannot stop oneself from (…)

examples.jp: こんな悲しい話を聞いたら、泣かないではいられない。
examples.tr: Hearing such a sad story, you can't help but cry.

examples.jp: 言わないほうがよいことは分かっているが、話さないではいられなかった。
examples.tr: I knew it was better not to say it, but I couldn't help talking about it.

examples.jp: あの映画を見たら、誰だって感動しないではいられないだろう。
examples.tr: Anyone who sees that movie would probably be moved.

examples.jp: 子供のことでは、日々悩まされないではいられない。
examples.tr: When it comes to my children, I can't help worrying every day.

1534.explain: Follows the negative form of a verb and expresses that one cannot hold something back by willpower and does it naturally. Used with verbs that express human actions or movements of thought and emotion, such as 「泣く」, 「思う」 and 「感動する」. It implies that the speaker regards this as "only natural". In written language it also becomes 「…せずにはいられない」. (３７１)

examples.jp: 山田にしても佐藤にしても、この仕事に向いているとはいえない。
examples.tr: Whether it's Yamada or Sato, neither can be said to be suited to this job.

examples.jp: 犬にしても猫にしてもこのマンションではペットを飼ってはいけないことになっている。
examples.tr: Whether it's a dog or a cat, keeping pets is not allowed in this apartment building.

examples.jp: 当選にしても落選にしても、今回の選挙に立候補したことは大いに意味があった。
examples.tr: Whether elected or defeated, running in this election was very meaningful.

examples.jp: 行くにしても行かないにしても、一応準備だけはしておきなさい。
examples.tr: Whether you go or not, at least get ready just in case.

examples.jp: 勝つにしても負けるにしても、正々堂々と戦いたい。
examples.tr: Win or lose, I want to fight fair and square.

examples.jp: 勝ったにしても負けたにしても、よく頑張ったとほめてやりたい。
examples.tr: Whether they won or lost, I want to praise them for doing their best.

1535.explain: Takes up two things of the same kind, or two opposing things, and expresses the meaning "in either case".

examples.jp: 山でのキャンプ生活は電気もガスもないが、不便なのもまた楽しい。
examples.tr: Camping life in the mountains has no electricity or gas, but the inconvenience is also part of the fun.

examples.jp: 暑いのも困るが寒いのもまたたいへんだ。
examples.tr: Hot weather is a nuisance, but cold weather is just as hard.

examples.jp: 晴れた日の散歩は楽しい。しかし、雨にぬれながら歩くのもまた風情があっていいものだ。
examples.tr: Walking on a sunny day is enjoyable. But walking while getting wet in the rain also has its own charm.

examples.jp: 天才といえども、彼もまた人の子だ。うれしいときもあれば悲しいときもある。
examples.tr: Genius though he may be, he too is only human. He has happy times and sad times.

1538.explain: Means "in the same way". As in 1. ～3., it expresses that something is the same as what was stated before. 4. means "he, a genius, is the same as an ordinary person".

1539.connection: plain form + とは + 考えられない

1541.meaning: (A) is precisely (the content describing A); (A) means … / (A) that is, …

1542.meaning: Whether … or not … (the result is the same)

examples.jp: 今回のレポートは出しても出さなくても、成績には全く影響ありません。
examples.tr: Whether you submit this report or not, it will have no effect at all on your grade.

examples.jp: 全員が参加してもしなくても、一応人数分の席を確保しておきます。
examples.tr: Whether everyone participates or not, I'll reserve a seat for each person just in case.

examples.jp: １日ぐらいなら、食べても食ベなくても、体重はたいして変化しない。
examples.tr: If it's only for about a day, whether you eat or not, your weight won't change much.

1542.explain: Using a form like 「…してもしなくても」, lists conditions in an affirmative–negative relationship and expresses that the result does not change in either case.

1543.meaning: To be (…) — the written/formal form of 「だ・です」

examples.jp: あんなにひどい言い方をすることもあるまいに。
examples.tr: There was no need to say it so harshly.

examples.jp: あの程度のことで、大の大人が泣くこともあるまい。
examples.tr: A grown adult surely needn't cry over something that minor.

examples.jp: 電話か手紙で用は足りるのだから、わざわざ行くほどのこともあるまい。
examples.tr: A phone call or a letter will take care of it, so there's probably no need to go all the way there.

1544.explain: Used to state a critical judgment that an action is inappropriate, or a judgment that an action is unnecessary. It is a stiff, written-language expression; in spoken language, 「Ｖ－ることもないだろう」 is used more often.

1545.meaning: The thing/person that … is … (emphasizes the chosen part)
1545.connection: [plain form]のは ～ N/[plain form] + のほうだ

examples.jp: あの人、山田さんなんじゃない？
examples.tr: That person, isn't that Mr. Yamada?

examples.jp: ほら、顔があかくなった。あなた山田さんが好きなんじゃないの？
examples.tr: Look, you're blushing. You like Yamada, don't you?

examples.jp: それ、いいんじゃない？悪くないと思うよ。
examples.tr: That's pretty good, isn't it? I don't think it's bad.
